a.definitionEn: the blood group whose red cells carry the A antigen
a.sentence: There is a dog in my house.

abandon.definitionEn: to leave somebody, especially somebody you are responsible for, with no intention of returning
abandon.sentence: The patient decided to abandon the treatment due to severe side effects.
abandon.sentenceTrans: 由于严重的副作用，患者决定放弃治疗。
abandon.mnemonic: ab去 + ban被命令 + don表名词 → 一直被别人命令，放弃自我 → abandon抛弃，放弃

ability.definitionEn: the fact that somebody/something is able to do something; a level of skill or intelligence
ability.sentence: He has the ability to run on water.

able.definition: 能够……的，可以...的；有能力的
able.definitionEn: (used as a modal verb) to have the skill, intelligence, opportunity, etc. needed to do something
able.sentence: Now he is able to walk without the help of crutches.
able.sentenceTrans: 现在他能够脱离拐杖走路了。

abnormal.definitionEn: different from what is usual or expected, especially in a way that is worrying, harmful or not wanted
abnormal.sentence: This potato has an abnormal shape.
abnormal.sentenceTrans: 这个土豆的形状很不正常。
abnormal.mnemonic: ab相反，变坏，离去 + normal正常的 → abnormal反常的

aboard.definition: 在（交通工具）上；  prep.在（交通工具）上
aboard.definitionEn: on or onto a ship, plane, bus or train
aboard.sentence: In Thailand, some women cook meals aboard their boats.
aboard.sentenceTrans: 在泰国，一些女性经常在船上做饭。
aboard.mnemonic: a在...上面 + board木板 -> aboard在（交通工具）上

abolish.definitionEn: to officially end a law, a system or an institution
abolish.sentence: In the mid 1800s, slavery was abolished in most states of America.
abolish.sentenceTrans: 19世纪中期，美国大多数州废除了奴隶制。
abolish.mnemonic: abol消除 + ish动词后缀 → abolish废除

abolition.definitionEn: the act of officially ending or stopping something :the act of abolishing something
abolition.sentence: The abolition of slavery was a significant historical event.
abolition.sentenceTrans: 奴隶制的废除是一个重要的历史事件。
abolition.mnemonic: aboli(sh)废除 + tion名词后缀 → abolition 废除

about.definition: 附近，大约，转向，左右，周围
about.definitionEn: on the subject of somebody/something; in connection with somebody/something; used to describe the purpose or an aspect of something; busy with something; doing something
about.sentenceTrans: 这口红的售价大约是220元。
about.mnemonic: a在...上面 + bo位于，靠近 + ut在...外面 → 某事物的各个方面 → about附近，周围，有关

above.definition: 在……之上；在…… 上方；  adv.在……上面，上文中，上述；  adj.上面的，上述的
above.definitionEn: at or to a higher place or position than something/somebody
above.sentence: The bird is flying above the water.
above.mnemonic: a在...上面 + bo位于，靠近 + ve高 → above在...之上

abroad.definitionEn: in or to a foreign country
abroad.sentence: The two Asian students study abroad together.
abroad.sentenceTrans: 这两个亚洲学生一起出国留学。
abroad.mnemonic: a去，到 + broad宽的，广阔的 -> 去广阔的地方 -> abroad到国外

abrupt.definitionEn: sudden and unexpected, often in an unpleasant way
abrupt.sentence: An abrupt gust of wind suddenly turned his umbrella inside out.
abrupt.sentenceTrans: 一阵突如其来的大风把他的雨伞都吹翻了。
abrupt.mnemonic: ab分离，脱离 + rupt裂，破坏 → abrupt不连贯的，突然的

absence.definitionEn: the fact of somebody being away from a place where they are usually expected to be; the occasion or period of time when somebody is away
absence.sentence: None of the classmates know the reason for his absence.
absence.sentenceTrans: 同学们都不知道他缺席的原因。
absence.mnemonic: ab远离的 + sen(t)出现 + ce名词后缀 → 没有出现 → absence缺席

absent.definition: 缺席的，不在场的；  v.不参加；缺席
absent.definitionEn: not in a place because of illness, etc.; not present in something; showing that you are not really looking at or thinking about what is happening around you
absent.sentence: My PE teacher is always absent, but my math teacher has perfect attendance.
absent.sentenceTrans: 体育老师总是不在，数学老师却从不缺席。
absent.mnemonic: ab远离的 + sent出现 → 没有出现 → absent缺席的

absent-minded.definitionEn: Not paying attention and easily forgetting things.

absolute.sentence: Marx thought that motion is absolute, while stillness is relative.
absolute.sentenceTrans: 马克思认为运动是绝对的，而静止是相对的。
absolute.mnemonic: ab离开 + solute松开，分离 → 不会放手的 → absolute绝对的

absolutely.definitionEn: used to emphasize that something is completely true
absolutely.sentence: The ad said the product was absolutely guaranteed to work.
absolutely.sentenceTrans: 广告说这个产品是保证绝对有效的。
absolutely.mnemonic: ab不 ＋ solute松开 ＋ ly...地 → 不松开地 → absolutely绝对地

absorb.definition: 吸收；理解，掌握；吸引……的注意
absorb.definitionEn: to take in a liquid, gas or other substance from the surface or space around
absorb.sentence: Plants absorb water from the soil.
absorb.sentenceTrans: 植物从土壤中吸收水分。
absorb.mnemonic: ab离开 + sorb吸收 → absorb吸收到

abstract.definition: 抽象的；  n.摘要；  v.提取（读作/ˈæbˌstrækt/）
abstract.definitionEn: based on general ideas and not on any particular real person, thing or situation; (of art) not representing people or things in a realistic way, but expressing the artist’s ideas about them; existing in thought or as an idea but not having a physical reality
abstract.sentence: Abstract art is often difficult to understand.
abstract.sentenceTrans: 抽象艺术通常让人难以理解。
abstract.mnemonic: abs向外 + tract拉 → abstract提取，抽象

abundant.definitionEn: existing in large quantities; more than enough
abundant.sentence: Fish are abundant in the pond.
abundant.mnemonic: ab一再 + und波动 + ant...的 → 波浪一多就溢出了 → abundant丰富的

abuse.definition: 滥用（读作/əˈbjuz/）；虐待；辱骂；  n.滥用；虐待；辱骂（读作/əˈbjus/）
abuse.definitionEn: unfair, cruel or violent treatment of somebody
abuse.sentence: The man often abuses drugs, so he looks very tired.
abuse.sentenceTrans: 这个人经常滥用药物，所以看起来很累。
abuse.mnemonic: ab离开 + use使用 → abuse滥用

abusive.definitionEn: rude and offensive; causing another person mental or physical harm
abusive.sentence: She became abusive when she was drunk.
abusive.sentenceTrans: 她喝醉酒后就开始辱骂人。
abusive.mnemonic: abus(e)滥用 + ive形容词后缀 → abusive 滥用的

academic.definition: 学术的；学院的；  n.学者；高等院校教师
academic.definitionEn: connected with education, especially studying in schools and universities
academic.sentence: This academic meeting has both students and professors.
academic.sentenceTrans: 这次学术会议有学生也有教授。
academic.mnemonic: academ学术 + ic……的 → 学院的;学术的;学究的

accelerate.definitionEn: (of a vehicle or person) to start to go faster
accelerate.sentence: The pilot needs to accelerate the aircraft to reach the required takeoff speed.
accelerate.sentenceTrans: 飞行员需要加速飞机以达到所需的起飞速度。
accelerate.mnemonic: ac去 + celer迅速 + ate动词后缀 → accelerate加速

accent.definition: 口音，腔调；重音符号；  v.强调（读作/ækˈsɛnt/）
accent.definitionEn: a way of pronouncing the words that shows which country, area or social class a person comes from
accent.sentence: The word 'tomato' is pronounced differently in British and American accents.
accent.sentenceTrans: '番茄'在英式口音和美式口音中的发音不同。
accent.mnemonic: ac=ad去，向 + cent唱歌 → 说话像唱歌 → accent口音；重音

accept.definition: 接受（所提供或给予的物品）；同意做；接纳，认可
accept.definitionEn: to take willingly something that is offered; to say ‘yes’ to an offer, invitation, etc.
accept.sentence: Thank you — I accept your lovely gift with pleasure!
accept.sentenceTrans: 谢谢你，我非常高兴地接受你送的可爱的礼物!
accept.mnemonic: ac一再 + cept拿 → accept接受，承认

acceptance.definitionEn: the act or process of accepting; the state of being accepted or acceptable
acceptance.sentence: Clapping can be a sign of acceptance.
acceptance.sentenceTrans: 鼓掌可以是一种表示接纳的标志。

access.definition: 进入；接触；通道，入口；  v.进入，使用，获取；接近
access.definitionEn: a way of entering or reaching a place
access.sentence: The ramp gives access to disabled people.
access.sentenceTrans: 这个斜坡可以让残障人士通行。
access.mnemonic: ac一再 + cess=go行走 → 接近；入口

accessible.definition: 可进入的；可接近的，可到达的；可使用的
accessible.definitionEn: that can be reached, entered, used, etc. by somebody who has problems walking
accessible.sentence: The secret garden is only accessible with the secret key.
accessible.sentenceTrans: 这个秘密花园要用秘密钥匙才能进入。
accessible.mnemonic: ac一再 + cess=行走 + ible形容词后缀，能…的 → accessible能接触到的

accident.definition: 不测，事故，意外事件；意外遭遇
accident.definitionEn: an unpleasant event, especially in a vehicle, that happens unexpectedly and causes injury or damage
accident.sentence: An accident happened, and then the egg was broken.
accident.sentenceTrans: 鸡蛋意外摔倒，然后碎了。
accident.mnemonic: ac强调 + cid降下 + ent为名词词尾 → 偶然降临的事 → accident偶然的事，意外

acclaim.definition: 欢呼，赞扬，称赞；  v.欢呼，喝彩
acclaim.definitionEn: to praise or welcome somebody/something publicly
acclaim.sentence: She was highly acclaimed for her wonderful performance.
acclaim.sentenceTrans: 她因自己出色的成绩受到了高度称赞。
acclaim.mnemonic: ac去 + claim呼喊 → acclaim喝彩，赞扬

accommodate.definitionEn: to provide enough space for somebody/something
accommodate.sentence: The hostel accommodates travellers from all over the world.
accommodate.sentenceTrans: 这家青年旅舍为来自全球各地的游客提供住宿。
accommodate.mnemonic: ac使 + commodate适应 → accommodate使适应，容纳

accommodation.definition: 住处，停留处；工作场所；住宿，膳宿
accommodation.definitionEn: somewhere to live or stay, often also providing food or other services
accommodation.sentence: Her accommodation during her travel is a nice hotel.
accommodation.sentenceTrans: 她旅行期间的住处是一间不错的酒店。
accommodation.mnemonic: accommodat(e)使适应，容纳 + ion名词后缀 → accommodation住所

accompany.definitionEn: to happen or appear with something else; to travel or go somewhere with somebody;
accompany.sentence: I always accompany my children to their school.
accompany.sentenceTrans: 我总是陪着我的孩子去学校。

accomplish.definitionEn: to succeed in doing or completing something
accomplish.sentenceTrans: 她完成了自己的减肥目标。
accomplish.mnemonic: ac使 + complish填满 → 已经填满的 → accomplish完成

accomplishment.definitionEn: something done, achieved, or accomplished successfully
accomplishment.sentence: His winning the Nobel Prize for Literature was a great accomplishment.
accomplishment.sentenceTrans: 他获得诺贝尔文学奖是一项极大的成就。
accomplishment.mnemonic: ac 一再 + complish=complete 造成... + ment 表示行为、行为的过程或结果 → n. 成就；完成；技艺，技能

according.definitionEn: (followed by `to') as reported or stated by
according.sentence: According to the map, we should go this way.
according.sentenceTrans: 根据地图来看，我们应该走这边。

according to.definitionEn: as stated or reported by somebody/something; following, agreeing with or depending on something
according to.sentence: According to the law, you are guilty.
according to.sentenceTrans: 根据法律，你的罪名成立。

account.definition: 账目，账户；描述；叙述；  v.做出说明（或解释）；占（一定数量或比例）
account.definitionEn: an arrangement that somebody has with a bank, etc. to keep money there, take some out, etc.
account.sentence: I have no money in my bank account.
account.sentenceTrans: 我的银行账户里没有钱。
account.mnemonic: ac去 +count计算 → 去计算 → account算账，账目

accumulate.definitionEn: to gradually get more and more of something over a period of time
accumulate.sentence: Long-term exposure to air pollutants may cause toxins to accumulate in the lungs.
accumulate.sentenceTrans: 长期接触空气污染物可能导致毒素在肺部积累。
accumulate.mnemonic: ac(ad)=to, towards 朝着；靠近 + cumul堆积 + ate使 → 朝着……堆积 → accumulate积累

accumulation.definitionEn: the process of gradually increasing or getting more and more of something over a period of time
accumulation.sentence: The accumulation of coins took a lot of time.
accumulation.sentenceTrans: 硬币的累积需要很长时间。
accumulation.mnemonic: accumulat积累 + ion名词后缀 → accumulation积累

accuracy.definitionEn: the state of being exact or correct; the ability to do something skilfully without making mistakes
accuracy.sentence: She is a professional archer who always shoots with high accuracy.
accuracy.sentenceTrans: 她是一名职业射箭手，总是射得很准。
accuracy.mnemonic: accura=accurate准确的 + cy名词后缀 → accuracy准确度

accurate.definitionEn: an accurate throw, shot, weapon, etc. hits or reaches the thing that it was aimed at; conforming exactly or almost exactly to fact or to a standard or performing with total accuracy
accurate.sentence: I never miss my target because my aim is so accurate.
accurate.sentenceTrans: 我从未脱靶，因为我瞄得很准。
accurate.mnemonic: ac加强语气 + cur关心 + ate形容词词尾 → 去关注、关心，不马虎大意 → accurate准确的；精确的

accusation.definitionEn: a statement saying that you think a person is guilty of doing something wrong, especially of committing a crime; the fact of accusing somebody
accusation.sentence: The accusations from different people make him lower his head in shame.
accusation.sentenceTrans: 来自不同人的指责让他羞愧地低下了头。
accusation.mnemonic: accus(e) 指责 + ation名词后缀 → accusation指责

accuse.definitionEn: to say that somebody has done something wrong or is guilty of something
accuse.sentence: They accused each other of being wrong.
accuse.sentenceTrans: 他们相互指责对方做错了。
accuse.mnemonic: ac=ad有关 + cuse起因；诉讼 → accuse指控

accustomed.definitionEn: familiar with something and accepting it as normal or usual
accustomed.sentence: He got accustomed to the food after 10 years of living here.
accustomed.sentenceTrans: 在这里住了十年之后，他习惯了这里的食物。
accustomed.mnemonic: ac加强意义 + custom习惯 + ed形容词后缀 → accustomed习惯的

ache.definitionEn: (often in compounds) a continuous feeling of pain in a part of the body
ache.sentence: Mark had an ache in his back.

achieve.definition: 实现，（尤指凭长期努力）达到（某目标）
achieve.definitionEn: to succeed in reaching a particular goal, status or standard, especially by making an effort for a long time; to succeed in doing something or causing something to happen; to be successful
achieve.sentence: She managed to achieve great success in her career.
achieve.sentenceTrans: 她成功地在职业生涯中取得了巨大的成就。
achieve.mnemonic: ad去 + chieve=chief头 → 到头，达到 → achieve完成，达到

achievement.definitionEn: a thing that somebody has done successfully, especially using their own effort and skill
achievement.sentence: He is known for his great achievements in the sport of tennis.
achievement.sentenceTrans: 他在网球运动上的成就令人瞩目。
achievement.mnemonic: achieve达成 + ment表示行为、行为的过程或结果 → achievement成就；实现

acknowledge.definitionEn: to tell somebody that you have received something that they sent to you
acknowledge.sentence: The boy acknowledged breaking the glass.
acknowledge.sentenceTrans: 小男孩承认自己打碎了杯子。
acknowledge.mnemonic: ac使 + knowledge了解 → acknowledge承认，认知

acquaint.definitionEn: to make somebody/yourself familiar with or aware of something
acquaint.sentence: I am trying to get acquainted with my new colleague.
acquaint.mnemonic: ac使 + quaint知道 → acquaint使认识，使熟悉

acquaintance.definitionEn: a person that you know but who is not a close friend
acquaintance.sentence: He met an old acquaintance at his friend's wedding.
acquaintance.sentenceTrans: 他在朋友的婚礼上遇见了一位老熟人。
acquaintance.mnemonic: acquaint熟悉 + ance名词后缀 → acquaintance认识，熟人

acquire.definition: （通过努力、能力）获得；学到；得到
acquire.definitionEn: to gain something by your own efforts, ability or behaviour
acquire.sentence: The little boy acquired knowledge of the universe from observing.
acquire.sentenceTrans: 小男孩通过观察学到了关于宇宙的知识。
acquire.mnemonic: ac加强 + quir寻求，询问 + e → acquire取得，学到

acquisition.definitionEn: the act of getting something, especially knowledge, a skill, etc.
acquisition.sentence: We study for the acquisition of knowledge.
acquisition.sentenceTrans: 我们为了获得知识而读书。
acquisition.mnemonic: ac加强 + quis询问 + ition名词后缀 → 通过询问得到 → 获得；增添的人(或物)

act.definition: 表演，扮演；行动；  n.行为，行动；（戏剧、歌剧等的）一幕；法案
act.definitionEn: perform an action, or work out or perform (an action)
act.sentence: The girl will act the part of princess in the play.
act.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩将在剧中扮演公主的角色。

action.definitionEn: the process of doing something in order to make something happen or to deal with a situation; a thing that somebody does; the way a part of the body moves or functions; the mechanical parts of a piano, gun, clock, etc. or the way the parts move
action.sentence: It is a polite action to offer your seat to old people.
action.sentenceTrans: 给老人让座是一种有礼貌的行为。
action.mnemonic: act行动 + ion表行为，情况 → action行为

active.definitionEn: always busy doing things, especially physical activities; doing something regularly; functioning;
active.sentence: Students should take an active approach to studying.
active.sentenceTrans: 学生们应该采取积极有效的学习方法。
active.mnemonic: act行动 + ive有…...性质的 → active积极的

activity.definitionEn: a thing that you do for interest or pleasure, or in order to achieve a particular aim
activity.mnemonic: act行动，做 + ivity名词后缀 → 活动 → activity活动

actor.definitionEn: a person who performs on the stage, on television or in films/movies, especially as a profession
actor.sentence: The actor is rehearsing his lines.
actor.sentenceTrans: 这位演员正在排练他的台词。
actor.mnemonic: act表演 + or名词后缀：人 → actor演员

actress.definitionEn: a woman who performs on the stage, on television or in films/movies, especially as a profession
actress.sentence: The actress is practising her line on the stage.
actress.sentenceTrans: 这位女演员正在舞台上练习她的台词。
actress.mnemonic: act表演 + ress女性 → actress女演员

actual.definitionEn: used to emphasize something that is real or exists in fact
actual.sentence: I refused the red packet, but the actual fact was that I wanted it.
actual.sentenceTrans: 我拒绝了那个红包，但事实上我想要它。
actual.mnemonic: act行动 + ual形容词后缀 → actual现实的，现行的

actually.definition: 实际上；事实上；竟然（表示惊讶）
actually.sentence: Mary may appear to be reading, but actually she is thinking about food.
actually.sentenceTrans: 玛丽看起来像是在看书，但实际上，她正想着食物。

adapt.definitionEn: to change something in order to make it suitable for a new use or situation
adapt.sentence: This animal changes its color to adapt to its new surroundings.
adapt.sentenceTrans: 这只动物为适应新环境改变自身的颜色。
adapt.mnemonic: ad朝向 + apt适应 → adapt使适合

add.definitionEn: to put (something) with another thing or group of things
add.sentence: Add some milk to the bowl.
add.mnemonic: ad往，到 + d给予 → add加，增加

addition.definitionEn: the process of adding two or more numbers together to find their total
addition.sentence: Simple addition is the easiest part of math class.
addition.sentenceTrans: 简单加法是数学课中最容易的部分。
addition.mnemonic: add加 + ition名词后缀 → addition附加，附加物

additional.definitionEn: more than was first mentioned or is usual
additional.sentence: He had to pay an additional charge for the overweight luggage.
additional.sentenceTrans: 他得为超重的行李支付额外的费用。
additional.mnemonic: add加上 + ition名词后缀 + al形容词后缀 → additional附加的，追加的

address.definition: 地址，住址；致辞；  v.写姓名地址；向……讲话
address.definitionEn: details of where somebody lives or works and where letters, etc. can be sent
address.sentence: You must write down the address before sending a letter.
address.sentenceTrans: 寄信之前你必须写上地址。

adequate.definition: 足够的，充分的；尚可的，过得去的
adequate.definitionEn: enough in quantity, or good enough in quality, for a particular purpose or need
adequate.sentence: The meal would not feed a family, but it was adequate for two.
adequate.sentenceTrans: 这一餐不够一家人吃，但够两个人的量。
adequate.mnemonic: ad加强意义 + equ相等 + ate…的 → 与所要求的相等 → adequate足够的

adhere.sentence: I used glue to adhere the poster to the wall.
adhere.sentenceTrans: 我用胶水把海报贴在墙上。
adhere.mnemonic: ad做…，加强… + here粘 → 粘在一起 → 坚持

adjective.definitionEn: a word that describes a person or thing, for example big, red and clever in a big house, red wine and a clever idea
adjective.sentence: We use adjectives to describe things.
adjective.sentenceTrans: 我们用形容词来描述物体。
adjective.mnemonic: ad向，朝 + ject扔 + ive形容词后缀 → 扔上去的，附加上去的 → adjective形容词

adjust.definitionEn: to change something slightly to make it more suitable for a new set of conditions or to make it work better
adjust.sentence: It's too hot in the room; I'll adjust the temperature.
adjust.sentenceTrans: 房间里太热了，我调节一下温度。
adjust.mnemonic: ad做…，加强… + just正确 → 弄正确 → 调整

administer.definitionEn: to manage and organize the affairs of a company, an organization, a country, etc.
administer.sentence: His job as manager is to administer many departments within the company.
administer.sentenceTrans: 作为经理，他的工作是管理公司内部的许多部门。
administer.mnemonic: ad去，往 + minister服务，参加 → administer管理，执行

administration.definitionEn: the activities that relate to running a company, school, or other organization; the people who plan, organize and run a business, an institution, etc.; the government of a country, especially the US; the act of giving a job to somebody
administration.sentence: She works in the university's administration office.
administration.sentenceTrans: 她在大学的行政办公室里工作。
administration.mnemonic: ad表加强 + ministr管理 + ation名词后缀 → 行政，管理 → administration管理

administrative.definitionEn: connected with organizing the work of a business or an institution
administrative.sentence: She was busy with administrative work all day.
administrative.sentenceTrans: 她一整天都忙于行政工作。
administrative.mnemonic: ad一再 + ministr=minister招待 + ative有……作用的 → adj. 管理的，行政的

admire.definitionEn: to respect somebody for what they have done or to respect their qualities
admire.sentence: The little girl admires this boxer and sees her as a model.
admire.sentenceTrans: 小女孩崇拜这位拳击手并将她视为榜样。
admire.mnemonic: ad关于 + mire感到惊讶 → admire钦佩

admission.definitionEn: the act of accepting somebody into an institution, organization, etc.; the right to enter a place or to join an institution or organization
admission.sentence: Children can gain admission to primary school at the age of 6.
admission.sentenceTrans: 孩子要到6岁才能上小学。
admission.mnemonic: ad向.... + mission放开；发送 → admission承认，允许进入

admit.definitionEn: to say that you have done something wrong or illegal
admit.sentence: The boy admitted that he broke the vase.
admit.sentenceTrans: 小男孩承认是他弄碎了花瓶。
admit.mnemonic: ad去，往 + mit送，放出 → 送来 → admit许可进入

adolescent.definition: 青少年；  adj.青少年的；青春期的
adolescent.definitionEn: in the process of developing from a child into an adult
adolescent.mnemonic: adolesc进入青春期 + ent表示具有……性质的，关于……的 → 青春期的,青少年的

adopt.definitionEn: to take somebody else’s child into your family and become its legal parent(s)
adopt.sentence: The couple adopted a child from the orphanage.
adopt.sentenceTrans: 这对夫妻从孤儿院收养了一个孩子。
adopt.mnemonic: ad做…，加强… + opt选择 → 选出来 → adopt采纳，收养

adult.definition: 成年人，成年动物；  adj.成年的；成年人的；（内容）色情的
adult.definitionEn: a fully grown person who is legally responsible for their actions
adult.sentence: An adult is a person who is 18 years old or over.
adult.sentenceTrans: 成年人的年龄大于或等于18岁。
adult.mnemonic: ad(to)去 + ul成长 + t → adult成人

advance.definition: 预先；进步，进展；  v.提前；前进；发展，进步；  adj.预先的，事先的
advance.definitionEn: done or given before something is going to happen
advance.sentence: He finished his homework in advance.
advance.mnemonic: ab（从、离开）+ ante（前面的、在前方）→ 拉丁语 abante → 古法语 avance（b变v，ante 变 ance）→ 英语误变 ad 得 advance（向前推进、提升）

advanced.definitionEn: (of a course of study) at a high or difficult level
advanced.sentence: The robot is so advanced that it can cook all kinds of meals.
advanced.sentenceTrans: 这个机器人很先进，能做各式各样的饭菜。
advanced.mnemonic: advanc前进 + ed……的 → 往前进的 → advanced先进的，高级的

advantage.definitionEn: a thing that helps you to be better or more successful than other people
advantage.sentence: The man with the rocket gets a huge advantage.
advantage.sentenceTrans: 坐着火箭的人占了很大的优势。

adventure.definitionEn: an unusual, exciting or dangerous experience, journey or series of events
adventure.sentence: The boy went on an adventure in the jungle.
adventure.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩去丛林里冒险了。
adventure.mnemonic: ad做…，加强… + venture冒险 → adventure冒险

advertise.definitionEn: to tell the public about a product or a service in order to encourage people to buy or to use it
advertise.sentence: This rich man is advertising breakfast cereal.
advertise.sentenceTrans: 富翁史密斯在为这款早餐麦片打广告。
advertise.mnemonic: ad再 + vert转变 + ise使…… → 转变客户想法 → advertise为……做广告

advertisement.definitionEn: a notice, picture or film telling people about a product, job or service
advertisement.sentence: This advertisement is used to promote a new product.
advertisement.sentenceTrans: 这则广告的目的是推广新产品。
advertisement.mnemonic: advertise做广告 + ment表名词 → advertisement广告

advertiser.definitionEn: an advertiser is a person or company that pays for a product, event, or job to be advertised online, in a newspaper, on television, or on a poster
advertiser.sentenceTrans: 他是一个有影响力的广告人。
advertiser.mnemonic: ad加强 + vert转 + is名词后缀 + er表示人 → 使顾客注意力转移到商品上的人 → advertiser广告客户；刊登广告的人

advice.definitionEn: an opinion or a suggestion about what somebody should do in a particular situation
advice.sentence: The doctor is giving her some good advice.
advice.sentenceTrans: 医生正给予她一些好的建议。

advisable.sentence: It's advisable to eat more vegetables if you want to keep fit.
advisable.sentenceTrans: 如果你想保持健康，多吃蔬菜是明智的选择。
advisable.mnemonic: advis=advise建议的 + able …的 → 可以参照的 → 可取的；明智的

advise.definitionEn: to give somebody help and information on a subject that you know a lot about
advise.sentence: My friend advised me to use this app when I failed the English exam.
advise.sentenceTrans: 当我的英语考试不及格时，我的朋友建议我用这个应用程序。
advise.mnemonic: ad朝向 + vise看见 → 看向某人 → （向某人）建议，劝告

adviser.sentence: The adviser is giving advice on the company's development.
adviser.sentenceTrans: 顾问正在对公司的发展提出建议。

advisor.definitionEn: a person who gives advice, especially somebody who knows a lot about a particular subject
advisor.sentence: Our financial advisor helps us with our money plans.
advisor.sentenceTrans: 我们的理财顾问帮助我们制定财务计划。

advocate.definition: 提倡，主张；  n.提倡者；拥护者；辩护律师
advocate.sentence: Experts advocate a healthy diet and regular exercise.
advocate.sentenceTrans: 专家提倡健康的饮食和规律的锻炼。
advocate.mnemonic: ad朝向 + voc喊叫 + ate动词词尾 → advocate提倡；鼓吹

affair.definition: 事情，事务；私通，风流韵事
affair.definitionEn: events that are of public interest or political importance
affair.sentence: The CEO is handling some commercial affairs.
affair.sentenceTrans: 这位总裁正在处理一些商务事宜。

affect.definitionEn: to produce a change in somebody/something; (of a disease) to attack somebody or a part of the body; to make somebody become ill/sick; to make somebody have strong feelings of sadness, pity, etc.
affect.sentence: Secondhand smoking may affect people's health.
affect.sentenceTrans: 吸二手烟会影响人的健康。
affect.mnemonic: af加强 + fect做，制作 → 做得让人加强印象 → affect影响；感动

affection.definitionEn: a person’s feelings of love; the feeling of liking or loving somebody/something very much and caring about them
affection.sentence: The girl sent her mother a card and flowers to show her deep affection.
affection.sentenceTrans: 女孩送了妈妈一张卡片和鲜花来表达自己对她深深的感情。
affection.mnemonic: affect情感上深深打动 + ion为名词后缀 → affection喜爱

afford.definitionEn: (usually used with can, could or be able to, especially in negative sentences or questions) to have enough money or time to be able to buy or to do something
afford.sentence: Finally, I can afford this car.
afford.sentenceTrans: 我终于买得起这辆车了。

affordable.definitionEn: cheap enough that people can afford to buy it or pay it
affordable.sentence: He is thinking about whether a bicycle is affordable for him.
affordable.sentenceTrans: 他正在考虑是否买得起一辆自行车。
affordable.mnemonic: afford负担 + able有能力的 → affordable负担得起的，能承受的

afraid.sentence: The dog looks afraid of the man.
afraid.sentenceTrans: 这只狗看上去害怕这个男人。
afraid.mnemonic: af走出，在...之外 + raid友善，爱 → 远离好的情绪 → afraid害怕的

after.definition: 后来，以后；  prep.【数】在...之后
after.definitionEn: later than something; following something in time
after.sentenceTrans: 他们从此过上了幸福的生活。
after.mnemonic: af=of离开 + ter后缀 → after在...之后

afternoon.definitionEn: the part of the day from 12 midday until about 6 o’clock
afternoon.sentence: I have to go back to work in the afternoon.
afternoon.sentenceTrans: 下午我不得不回去工作。
afternoon.mnemonic: after之后 + noon中午 → 中午之后 → afternoon午后，下午

afterward.definitionEn: at a later time; after an event that has already been mentioned
afterward.sentence: Afterward, please clean up your dog's poop.
afterward.sentenceTrans: 随后，请清洁你家狗狗的便便。
afterward.mnemonic: after以后 + ward向...的 → afterward之后

afterwards.definitionEn: at a later or succeeding time
afterwards.sentence: They had a romantic dinner and decided to watch a movie afterwards.
afterwards.sentenceTrans: 他们吃了一顿浪漫的晚餐，然后决定去看电影。
afterwards.mnemonic: after随后 + ward向…后 + s表副词 → afterwards后来；然后

again.definitionEn: one more time; on another occasion
again.sentence: It looks like it will rain again.
again.mnemonic: a在 + gain相反，相对 → 在相反的方向，回到此前位置 → again又，再次

against.definition: 反对；对（着），逆；违反；靠近，倚在；紧靠，碰，撞
against.sentence: We should all stand against animal cruelty!
against.sentenceTrans: 我们都应该抵制虐待动物的行为！

age.definitionEn: the number of years that a person has lived or a thing has existed; a particular period of a person’s life; a particular period of history
age.sentence: He started playing the piano at an early age.

agency.definition: 代理机构；(政府的)局，处；服务机构
agency.definitionEn: a business or an organization that provides a particular service especially on behalf of other businesses or organizations; a government department that provides a particular service
agency.sentence: It's more convenient to buy tickets from a ticket agency.
agency.sentenceTrans: 从车票代售点买票更方便。
agency.mnemonic: ag做，代理做 + ency表示机构或状态 → 代理处

agenda.definitionEn: a list of items to be discussed at a meeting
agenda.sentence: "There are many items that need to be discussed on the agenda", she said.
agenda.sentenceTrans: “议程上有许多事情需要讨论。”安迪说道。
agenda.mnemonic: ag做，代理做 + enda表示复数 → 做的事情 → agenda议事日程

agent.definition: 代理商，代理人；特工；动因；药剂
agent.definitionEn: a person whose job is to act for, or manage the affairs of, other people in business, politics, etc.; a person whose job is to arrange work for an actor, musician, sports player, etc. or to find somebody who will publish a writer’s work
agent.sentence: There are some real estate agents waiting for customers at the subway entrance.
agent.sentenceTrans: 一些房产中介在地铁口等待顾客。
agent.mnemonic: ag做，代理做 + ent表人或物 → 代理人 → agent作用因素；代理人

aggression.definitionEn: angry or violent behavior or feelings
aggression.sentence: A war of aggression started by aliens is very common in movies.
aggression.sentenceTrans: 外星人发动侵略战争的情节在电影中很常见。
aggression.mnemonic: ag一再 + gress走 + ion名词后缀 → 一再往前走 → 进攻，侵略

aggressive.definition: 有侵略性的；有攻击性的；积极进取的
aggressive.definitionEn: angry, and behaving in a threatening way; ready to attack
aggressive.sentence: I was terrified by this aggressive dog.
aggressive.sentenceTrans: 我被这只攻击性很强的狗吓到了。
aggressive.mnemonic: ag朝，向 + gress行走 + ive形容词词尾 → 侵略的；进取的

ago.definitionEn: used in expressions of time with the simple past tense to show how far in the past something happened
ago.sentence: I started going to school a few years ago.

agony.sentence: The man is in agony after hearing the bad news.
agony.sentenceTrans: 在听到这个坏消息之后，这个人陷入了极大的痛苦中。
agony.mnemonic: agon挣扎 + y表名词 → agony痛苦

agree.definitionEn: to have the same opinion as somebody; to say that you have the same opinion
agree.sentence: She agreed to go shopping with her friend.
agree.sentenceTrans: 她同意和朋友一起去购物。
agree.mnemonic: a=ad去 + gree支持，欢迎 → agree同意

agreement.definition: 一致，相合；同意；一致意见；协议，协定
agreement.definitionEn: an arrangement, a promise or a contract made with somebody
agreement.sentence: We reached an agreement on this idea.
agreement.sentenceTrans: 我们就这个想法达成一致。

agricultural.definitionEn: connected with the science or practice of farming
agricultural.sentence: Technological advancements have improved agricultural efficiency.
agricultural.sentenceTrans: 科技进步提高了农业生产的效率。
agricultural.mnemonic: agri田地，农业 + cult培养 + ur=ure表名词 + al形容词后缀 → 农业的，农艺的，农学的

agriculture.definitionEn: the science or occupation of farming
agriculture.sentence: Farmers rely on agriculture to make a living.
agriculture.mnemonic: agri田地 + cult耕种 + ure表名词 → 在田地里耕作 → agriculture农业

ahead.definitionEn: further forward in space or time; in front
ahead.sentence: I am running ahead of the rest of the group.
ahead.sentenceTrans: 跑步的时候，我领先于小组的其他人。
ahead.mnemonic: a副词前缀 + head头 → ahead在前，提前

aid.definition: 帮助；援助，帮助；  v.援助，帮助
aid.definitionEn: help that is given to a person
aid.sentence: The blind man walks with the aid of a guide dog.
aid.sentenceTrans: 那个盲人在导盲犬的帮助下走路。

aim.definition: 目的；目标；  v.瞄准，对准；力求达到，力争做到
aim.definitionEn: to point or direct a weapon, a shot, a kick, etc. at somebody/something
aim.sentence: His aim of exercising is to get more muscles.
aim.sentenceTrans: 他健身的目的是让自己练出更多肌肉。

air.definition: 空气；天空，空中；神态，样子；  v.通风；  v.晾干
air.definitionEn: the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth and that we breathe; the space above the ground or that is around things;  the particular feeling or impression that is given by somebody/something; the way somebody does something; (often used in the title of a piece of music) a tune
air.sentence: Could you blow some air into the balloons?
air.sentenceTrans: 你能给这个气球吹点气吗？

air-conditioner.sentence: The air-conditioner keeps the room cool during the hot summer days.
air-conditioner.sentenceTrans: 空调在炎热夏季使房间保持凉爽。

air-conditioning.sentence: The man is fixing the air-conditioning.
air-conditioning.sentenceTrans: 那个男人正在修理空调。

aircraft.definitionEn: any vehicle that can fly and carry goods or passengers
aircraft.sentence: Aircraft are meant to be in the sky.
aircraft.mnemonic: air空气 + craft技艺 → aircraft飞行器

airline.definitionEn: a company that provides regular flights to take passengers and goods to different places
airline.sentence: The plane of this airline has some red paint at the bottom.
airline.sentenceTrans: 这个航空公司的飞机底部有一些红色的油漆。
airline.mnemonic: air空气，空运 + line直线 → airline航空系统，航线

airplane.definitionEn: a flying vehicle with wings and one or more engines
airplane.sentence: You can go through the clouds by taking airplanes. It feels so amazing!
airplane.sentenceTrans: 坐飞机可以穿过云层，那感觉太神奇了！
airplane.mnemonic: air空气 + plane飞机 → airplane飞机

airport.definitionEn: a place where planes land and take off
airport.sentence: The plane landed at the airport.
airport.mnemonic: air空气，空中 + port港口 → airport机场，航空站

alarm.definition: 警报器，警报；  v.使惊恐，使忧虑
alarm.definitionEn: a device that warns people of a particular danger; a loud noise or a signal that warns people of danger or of a problem
alarm.sentence: He switched off the fire alarm.
alarm.mnemonic: a=to朝着，去 + l=the + arm武器 → 拿起武器，准备战斗 → alarm警报

alcohol.definition: 酒；酒精，乙醇；含酒精饮品
alcohol.definitionEn: a clear liquid that has a strong smell, that is used in some medicines and other products, and that is the substance in liquors (such as beer, wine, or whiskey) that can make a person drunk
alcohol.sentence: I avoid alcohol because it weakens my judgment.
alcohol.sentenceTrans: 我不喝酒，因为它会削弱我的判断力。

alert.definition: 警惕的；  v.向……报警，使警惕；  n.警报
alert.definitionEn: to warn somebody about a dangerous or urgent situation
alert.sentence: The cat is alert when guarding its fish.
alert.sentenceTrans: 喵星人在守卫自己的鱼的时候是很警觉的。
alert.mnemonic: al=ab加强 + ert直 → alert警惕的

alien.definition: 外星人；外国人；  adj.外国的；陌生的
alien.sentence: Do you ever think that aliens could be our friends?
alien.sentenceTrans: 你有没有想过外星人可能是我们的朋友？
alien.mnemonic: ali其他的，改变状态 + en表形容词或名词 → 其他地方的 → alien外国的，外国人的，外来的

alike.definition: 相同的，类似的；相像的；  adv.相像地，相似地
alike.sentence: Their haircut is the only reason why they look alike.
alike.sentenceTrans: 宋小宝和贝克汉姆的同款发型是他们唯一的相似之处。ㄟ( ▔, ▔ )ㄏ
alike.mnemonic: a加强意义 + like相像 → alike相同的（地）

alive.definition: 活着的，在世；活跃的，有生气的
alive.sentence: His beating heart shows that he is alive.
alive.sentenceTrans: 跳动的心脏表明他还活着。

all.definitionEn: (used with plural nouns. The noun may have the, this, that, my, her, his, etc. in front of it, or a number.) the whole number of
all.sentence: My girl friends and I all went shopping.
all.sentenceTrans: 我和女性朋友们都去购物了。

allow.definition: 允许，准许，许可；承认；同意
allow.definitionEn: to let somebody/something do something; to let something happen or be done
allow.sentence: The green light allows you to go.
allow.mnemonic: al=ad去，向 + low表扬 → allow允许

allowance.definitionEn: a small amount of money that is regularly given to children by their parents; an amount of money that can be earned or received before you start paying tax
allowance.sentence: He has an allowance of 3,000 dollars every month.
allowance.mnemonic: allow分配；发津贴 + ance行为，性质 → allowance津贴

almost.sentenceTrans: 他差一点就挖到钻石了。

alone.definitionEn: without help from anyone or anything else; and nothing or no one else
alone.sentence: Seesaws are not very fun when you're alone.
alone.sentenceTrans: 当你孤身一人时，跷跷板就不那么有趣了。
alone.mnemonic: al全部的，完全的 + one一个 → alone单独的

along.definitionEn: in a line matching the length or direction of (something)
along.sentence: She walked along the road for a long time.
along.mnemonic: a加强 + long长 → 向两边延长 → along沿着

alongside.definition: 在旁边，和……并排；和……一起，和......同时
alongside.definitionEn: next to or at the side of somebody/something
alongside.sentence: The prisoners are sitting alongside each other on the benches.
alongside.sentenceTrans: 杨树林和他的两个狱友并排坐在长凳上。（都坐牢了还不忘耍酷）
alongside.mnemonic: along沿着 + side……的一边 → 沿着……的边 → alongside在旁边

aloud.definitionEn: in a way that can be clearly heard
aloud.sentence: The boy is wearing earphones and singing aloud.
aloud.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩正戴着耳机，大声地唱歌。
aloud.mnemonic: a加强意义 + loud大声 → 高声地

alphabet.definitionEn: a set of letters or symbols in a fixed order used for writing a language

already.definitionEn: before now or before a particular time in the past
already.sentence: The concert has already started at 7 o'clock, hurry up!
already.sentenceTrans: 演唱会七点就已经开始了，快点啊！
already.mnemonic: al=all全部的 + ready准备好的 → already已经

also.definitionEn: (not used with negative verbs) in addition; too
also.sentence: She is also drinking his juice.

alter.definitionEn: to become different; to make somebody/something different
alter.mnemonic: alter其他的 → 变成〔其它的）→ alter变更，改变

alternate.definition: 交替的，间隔的；  v.（使）交替，（使）轮流；  n.代替者
alternate.definitionEn: (of two things) happening or following one after the other regularly; if something happens on alternate days, nights, etc. it happens on one day, etc. but not on the next
alternate.sentence: This is a week of alternate sunshine and rain.
alternate.mnemonic: altern其他的，改变状态 + ate表示做、造成 → 交替的，轮流的；间隔的

alternative.definitionEn: that can be used instead of something else
alternative.sentence: She provides an alternative choice for the girl who wants to buy a diamond ring.
alternative.sentenceTrans: 她给那个想买钻戒的女生提供了另一种选择。
alternative.mnemonic: altern另外的 + ative形容词/名词后缀 → alternative替换的，替换物

although.definitionEn: used to mean ‘but’ or ‘however’ when you are commenting on a statement
although.sentence: Although it is a rainy day, the girl is still having fun.
although.sentenceTrans: 尽管这是一个雨天，小姑娘还是玩得很开心。

altitude.definitionEn: the height above sea level; a place that is high above sea level
altitude.sentence: At this altitude it would be dangerous to fall off.
altitude.sentenceTrans: 在这种高度下跌落很危险。
altitude.mnemonic: alt高 + itude表抽象名词 → altitude高度

altogether.definition: 总共，一共；总而言之；完全
altogether.definitionEn: used to give a total number or amount
altogether.sentence: These gifts cost me 1,000 dollars altogether.
altogether.sentenceTrans: 这些礼物总共花了我1000美元。

always.definitionEn: at all times; on every occasion
always.mnemonic: al全部 + ways方式 → 全部都是这个方式 → 总是

am.definition: 是（动词be的第一人称形式）
am.definitionEn: the first person singular of the present tense of be

amaze.definitionEn: to surprise and sometimes confuse (someone) very much; to fill (someone) with wonder
amaze.sentence: The contents on the phone amazed both men greatly.
amaze.sentenceTrans: 手机上的内容让这两个人都大吃一惊。
amaze.mnemonic: a表加强 + maze迷宫 → 像进了迷宫一样 → amaze使诧异

amazing.definition: 令人惊奇的，令人惊喜的
amazing.definitionEn: very surprising, especially in a way that makes you feel pleasure or admiration
amazing.mnemonic: amaz=amaze惊异 + ing形容词后缀 → amazing令人惊异的

ambassador.definitionEn: an official who lives in a foreign country as the senior representative there of his or her own country
ambassador.sentence: "Our country wishes to have peace." said the ambassador.
ambassador.sentenceTrans: “我们国家渴望和平。”大使说道。
ambassador.mnemonic: amb围绕 + ass驱动，拉出 + a + dor名词后缀，做...的人 → ambassador大使，代表

ambiguous.definitionEn: unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way; having more than one possible meaning
ambiguous.sentence: This ambiguous image can have multiple meanings.
ambiguous.sentenceTrans: 这个模棱两可的图像会有很多含义。
ambiguous.mnemonic: ambi两者都 + guous...的 → 模棱两可的

ambition.definitionEn: the desire or determination to be successful, rich, powerful, etc.; something that you want to do or achieve very much
ambition.sentence: This powerful man's political ambition was to unify the three kingdoms.
ambition.sentenceTrans: 这个有权势的男人的政治野心是一统三国。
ambition.mnemonic: amb大 + it行走 + ion名词后缀 → 走大步 → ambition雄心，志向

ambitious.definitionEn: determined to be successful, rich, powerful, etc.
ambitious.sentence: The boy is ambitious and wants to be a successful businessman one day.
ambitious.sentenceTrans: 男孩很有抱负，未来想成为一个成功的商人。
ambitious.mnemonic: amb大 + it行走 + ious形容词后缀 → 大步向前走的 → ambitious有雄心的

ambulance.definitionEn: a vehicle used for taking hurt or sick people to the hospital especially in emergencies
ambulance.sentence: The ambulance sent the patient to the hospital.
ambulance.sentenceTrans: 救护车把病人送到了医院。
ambulance.mnemonic: ambul行走，走路 ＋ ance名词后缀 → 走的东西 → ambulance救护车，流动医院

among.definitionEn: surrounded by somebody/something; in the middle of somebody/something
among.sentence: There is an apple among the other fruits.
among.sentenceTrans: 这个苹果在这些水果之中。
among.mnemonic: a在...上 + mong揉捏，合身 → among处于...中，在...中间

amount.definitionEn: (used especially with uncountable nouns) a quantity of something
amount.sentence: The amount of sugar in this product is 28g.
amount.sentenceTrans: 这一产品中糖的总量是28克。
amount.mnemonic: a去，往 + mount山顶 → 去山顶 → amount总计

ample.definitionEn: enough or more than enough; (of a person’s figure) large, often in an attractive way
ample.sentence: We're lucky to have an ample amount of food to eat.
ample.sentenceTrans: 我们非常幸运能吃到这么多食物。
ample.mnemonic: ampl大，宽 + e → 很大，很宽 → ample富足的；宽敞的

amuse.definition: 使人发笑；（提供）娱乐，消遣；逗乐；娱乐
amuse.definitionEn: to make somebody laugh or smile; to make time pass pleasantly for somebody/yourself
amuse.sentence: Their talk show amused the audience.
amuse.sentenceTrans: 他们的脱口秀把观众逗乐了。
amuse.mnemonic: a使 + muse娱乐 → amuse娱乐，使发笑

amusement.definitionEn: a game, an activity, etc. that provides entertainment and pleasure
amusement.sentence: We had a good time in the amusement park.
amusement.sentenceTrans: 我们在游乐园玩得很开心。
amusement.mnemonic: amuse娱乐 + ment表名词 → amusement娱乐，消遣

an.sentence: There is an apple on the plate.

analyse.definitionEn: consider it carefully or use statistical methods in order to fully understand it
analyse.sentence: Knowing how to analyse the stock market, he made a lot of money.
analyse.sentenceTrans: 因为他知道如何分析股票市场，所以他挣了不少钱。

analysis.definitionEn: the detailed study or examination of something in order to understand more about it; the result of the study
analysis.sentence: Could you write up an analysis of how the market is moving this week?
analysis.sentenceTrans: 你能写一篇关于这周市场走势的分析报告吗？
analysis.mnemonic: ana完全，彻底地 + lysis解开，分开 → 彻底分开来（观察） → analysis分析

analyst.definitionEn: a person whose job involves examining facts or materials in order to give an opinion on them
analyst.sentence: The analyst is explaining the trend of the stock market.
analyst.sentenceTrans: 分析员正在解说股市走向。
analyst.mnemonic: ana分开 + lyst裂开，分解 → 分解 → analyst分析者

analyze.definitionEn: to examine the nature or structure of something, especially by separating it into its parts, in order to understand or explain it
analyze.sentence: Let's analyze the pattern of these shapes together, kids.
analyze.sentenceTrans: 让我们一起分析这些形状的规律吧孩子们。
analyze.mnemonic: ana完全 + lyze解开 → 完全解开 → analyze分析

ancestor.definitionEn: a person in your family who lived a long time ago
ancestor.sentence: It's said that the ancestors of whales may have had four limbs.
ancestor.sentenceTrans: 据说鲸鱼的祖先可能有四肢。
ancestor.mnemonic: an=ante前，先 + cest=cess行走，前进 + or表人 → 走在前面的人 → ancestor祖先

ancient.definition: 古代的；古老的；  n.古代人
ancient.definitionEn: belonging to a period of history that is thousands of years in the past; very old; having existed for a very long time; the people who lived in ancient times, especially the Egyptians, Greeks and Romans
ancient.sentence: These ancient statues are over 2,000 years old.
ancient.sentenceTrans: 这些古代雕像有2 000多年的历史。
ancient.mnemonic: anci古老 + ent……的 → ancient古代的

and.sentence: She and I are both confused.

angel.definitionEn: a spirit who is believed to be a servant of God, and is sent by God to deliver a message or perform a task. Angels are often shown dressed in white, with wings.
angel.sentence: Every child is an angel to their parents.
angel.sentenceTrans: 每个孩子都是父母的天使。

anger.definitionEn: the strong feeling that you have when something has happened that you think is bad and unfair
anger.sentence: The man was stuck in traffic, fuming with anger.
anger.sentenceTrans: 这名男子被堵在路上，怒火中烧。

angry.definitionEn: having strong feelings about something that you dislike very much or about an unfair situation
angry.sentence: The phone call makes him very angry.
angry.sentenceTrans: 这通电话让他非常生气。
angry.mnemonic: angr痛苦 + y表形容词 → angry愤怒的

animal.definitionEn: a living thing that is not a human being or plant
animal.sentence: There are many kinds of animals on the Earth.
animal.sentenceTrans: 地球上的动物种类繁多。

anniversary.definitionEn: a date that is an exact number of years after the date of an important or special event
anniversary.sentence: He gave his wife a diamond ring on their tenth anniversary.
anniversary.sentenceTrans: 在结婚十周年之际，他送给老婆一枚钻戒。
anniversary.mnemonic: anni=ann年 + vers转 + ary名词后缀 → 一年的转弯处一次 → anniversary周年纪念日

announce.definitionEn: to make (something) known in a public or formal way; to officially tell people about (something); to indicate beforehand; to give information about something in a public place, especially through a loudspeaker
announce.sentence: Her album was announced as the winner.
announce.sentenceTrans: 她的专辑被宣布为获奖作品。
announce.mnemonic: an加强意义 + nounce通知 → announce通告

announcement.definitionEn: a spoken or written statement that informs people about something; the act of publicly informing people about something
announcement.sentence: She makes an announcement with a loudspeaker.
announcement.mnemonic: an给予 + nounce讲话，说出 + ment名词后缀 → 通告

annoy.definitionEn: to cause (someone) to feel slightly angry
annoy.sentence: Talking on your phone during a movie is likely to annoy others.
annoy.sentenceTrans: 在看电影的时候打电话很可能会惹怒其他人。

annoyed.sentence: I am really annoyed with my roommate's snoring.
annoyed.sentenceTrans: 我真的被室友的鼾声搞得很烦。
annoyed.mnemonic: annoy烦人 + ed形容词后缀 → annoyed恼怒的

annual.definition: 年度的，一年一次的；  n.年鉴；年刊
annual.definitionEn: happening or done once every year; relating to a period of one year
annual.sentence: Our company has seen a rise in annual revenues in recent years.
annual.sentenceTrans: 近年来，我们公司的年收入不断增加。
annual.mnemonic: ann一年 + ual…的 → annual一年一度的

another.definitionEn: one more; an extra thing or person
another.sentence: You have another way to the train station if you are in a traffic jam.
another.sentenceTrans: 如果你遇到交通堵塞，你可以选择另一条路线前往火车站。

answer.definition: 回答，答复；答案；  v.回答，答复
answer.definitionEn: to say, write or do something as a reaction to a question or situation
answer.sentence: I didn't know the answer to the last question.
answer.sentenceTrans: 我不知道最后一个问题的答案。
answer.mnemonic: an在...前面 + swer断言，发誓 → 给出肯定的声明 → answer回答，答复

anticipate.sentence: I anticipate him winning the first prize as he is really great!
anticipate.sentenceTrans: 我期待他能得第一，因为他真的很棒！
anticipate.mnemonic: anti前面 + cip抓 + ate动词后缀 → 开始抓 → anticipate预料；预期的

anticipation.definitionEn: a feeling of excitement about something (usually something good) that is going to happen
anticipation.sentence: She is full of anticipation—her baby is almost due.
anticipation.sentenceTrans: 她充满了期待，因为她的宝贝就要出世了。
anticipation.mnemonic: anti反对 + cip拿、抓 + ation名词后缀 → 提前抓住 → anticipation预期，预料

anxiety.definitionEn: the state of feeling nervous or worried that something bad is going to happen
anxiety.sentence: His unfinished homework is causing him anxiety.
anxiety.sentenceTrans: 作业没写完使他焦虑不安。
anxiety.mnemonic: anxi焦虑 + e + ty名词后缀 → anxiety焦虑

anxious.definition: 焦虑的，不安的；渴望的；急切的
anxious.definitionEn: feeling worried or nervous; causing anxiety; showing anxiety
anxious.sentence: The boy is anxious about the exam.
anxious.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩对考试感到焦虑。
anxious.mnemonic: anxi焦虑 + ous形容词后缀 → anxious焦虑的

any.definitionEn: used with uncountable or plural nouns in negative sentences and questions, after if or whether, and after some verbs such as prevent, ban, forbid, etc. to refer to an amount or a number of something, however large or small
any.sentence: You can ride any of these bikes.
any.sentenceTrans: 你可以骑这些自行车里的任何一辆。

anybody.definition: 随便哪个人；任何人；  n.重要人物
anybody.definitionEn: any person at all; it does not matter who
anybody.sentence: He is taller than anybody else present.
anybody.sentenceTrans: 他比在场的其他任何人都高。
anybody.mnemonic: any任何 + body身体 → anybody任何人

anyhow.definition: 不论用何种方法，无论如何
anyhow.sentence: Someone has to wash the dishes anyhow, so I'll do it.
anyhow.sentenceTrans: 反正得有人洗碗，那就我洗吧。
anyhow.mnemonic: any无论 + how怎么 → 无论如何 → anyhow无论如何

anyone.definitionEn: used instead of someone in negative sentences and in questions after if/whether, and after verbs such as prevent, forbid, avoid, etc.; any person at all; it does not matter who; (in negative sentences) an important person
anyone.sentence: It's very discouraging for anyone to be out of a job.
anyone.sentenceTrans: 对于任何人来说，失业都是非常令人沮丧的。
anyone.mnemonic: any任何 + one一个 → anyone任何一个

anything.sentence: Welcome! Is there anything I can help you with?
anything.sentenceTrans: 欢迎光临！请问有什么可以帮您的吗？
anything.mnemonic: any任何 + thing事物 → anything任何东西

anyway.definitionEn: no matter what else occurs, without considering anything else
anyway.sentence: It doesn't matter; they all go to the same place anyway.
anyway.sentenceTrans: 没关系，所有路无论如何都通向一个地方。
anyway.mnemonic: any无论 + way方式 → anyway无论如何

anywhere.definitionEn: in, at or to any place, when it does not matter where
anywhere.sentence: You can connect to the internet from anywhere in the world.
anywhere.sentenceTrans: 你可以从世界上的任何地方连接到互联网。
anywhere.mnemonic: any任何 + where哪里 → anywhere无论何处

apart.definition: 分离地，分开地；  adj.分隔的，拆开的，撇开的
apart.definitionEn: separated by a distance, of space or time; not together; separate or separately
apart.sentence: They set one man apart from the rest.
apart.sentenceTrans: 他们把一个人与其他人分开了。
apart.mnemonic: a=ad去，向 + part授予，分配 → apart分离，分开

apartment.definitionEn: a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor of a building; a set of rooms used for a holiday/vacation
apartment.sentence: We have rented an apartment; time to buy some furniture.
apartment.sentenceTrans: 我们租了一套公寓，现在该去买些家具了。
apartment.mnemonic: apart分离的，分开的 + ment名词后缀 → 楼房分隔开住的地方 → 一套公寓房间

apologise.definitionEn: to say that you are sorry for doing something wrong or causing a problem
apologise.sentence: I should apologise to my friend for what I did.
apologise.sentenceTrans: 我应该为我的所作所为向我朋友道歉。
apologise.mnemonic: apo离开 + log演说 + ise → 表动词退后一步说 → apologise道歉

apologize.definitionEn: to say that you are sorry for doing something wrong or causing a problem
apologize.sentence: The cat apologized to its owner for breaking the vase.
apologize.sentenceTrans: 这只猫为打碎花瓶而向主人认错。

apology.definitionEn: a word or statement saying sorry for something that has been done wrong or that causes a problem; information that you cannot go to a meeting or must leave early
apology.sentence: He is making an apology to his boss.
apology.mnemonic: apo离开 + logy说话 → 退后一步说 → apology道歉

apparent.definition: 显然的；表面上的，貌似（真实）的
apparent.sentence: It's apparent that the boy is taller than the girl.
apparent.sentenceTrans: 很明显，那个男孩比女孩高。
apparent.mnemonic: ap加强意义 + par看见 + ent…的 → 能看见的 → apparent清晰易见的；显然的

apparently.sentence: Apparently, this chair is too small for the elephant.
apparently.sentenceTrans: 对大象来说，这把椅子显然太小了。

appeal.definition: 请求；呼吁；有吸引力；上诉
appeal.definitionEn: to make a serious and urgent request
appeal.sentence: They appealed to everyone to help protect the environment.
appeal.sentenceTrans: 他们请求大家一起保护环境。
appeal.mnemonic: ap=ad去，向 + peal促使，推进 → appeal呼吁；上诉

appear.definition: 出现，呈现，露面；  link-v.显得，似乎
appear.definitionEn: to become visible; to begin to be seen
appear.sentence: She appeared on stage as a surprise guest at the concert.
appear.sentenceTrans: 她作为演唱会嘉宾突然出现在舞台上。
appear.mnemonic: ap再 + pear看见 → 看见 → appear出现，显露

appearance.definition: 外貌，外表；出现，公开露面
appearance.definitionEn: the way that somebody/something looks on the outside; what somebody/something seems to be
appearance.sentence: She is checking her appearance in the mirror.
appearance.sentenceTrans: 她正在对着镜子检查自己的外表。
appearance.mnemonic: appear出现，显露 + ance性质，状况 → 显露出的性质 → appearance外貌

appendix.definitionEn: a small bag of tissue that is attached to the large intestine. In humans, the appendix has no clear function.
appendix.sentence: There is no appendix in this notebook.

appetite.sentence: I had a very healthy appetite and finished the whole meal.
appetite.sentenceTrans: 我的胃口很好，吃光了整顿饭。
appetite.mnemonic: ap加强动作 + pet追寻，寻求 + ite表名词 → 一再追求 → appetite胃口，欲望

applaud.definitionEn: to show your approval of somebody/something by clapping your hands
applaud.mnemonic: ap使 + plaud鼓掌 → applaud鼓掌；喝彩

applause.definitionEn: the noise made by a group of people clapping their hands and sometimes shouting to show their approval or enjoyment
applause.sentence: The cat praised herself with a round of applause.
applause.mnemonic: ap一再 + plause=plaud赞扬 → 一再赞扬 → applause掌声

apple.definitionEn: a round fruit with shiny red or green skin and firm white flesh
apple.sentence: I had an apple for breakfast today.
apple.sentenceTrans: 我今天早餐吃了一个苹果。

appliance.definition: 家用电器，器具；器具，器械
appliance.definitionEn: a machine that is designed to do a particular thing in the home, such as preparing food, heating or cleaning
appliance.sentence: I spent all my money on domestic appliances, like TVs and refrigerators.
appliance.sentenceTrans: 我把所有钱都花在像电视和冰箱这种家用电器上了。
appliance.mnemonic: apply适用 + ance表名词 → appliance家用电器，应用

applicable.definitionEn: capable of being applied; relevant or appropriate.
applicable.sentence: This license is applicable only to the Software.
applicable.sentenceTrans: 本许可仅适用于该软件。
applicable.mnemonic: ap一再+plic重叠、折叠+able能... → applicable适用的

applicant.definitionEn: a person who makes a formal request for something (= applies for it), especially for a job, a place at a college or university, etc.
applicant.sentence: The applicants are waiting outside before the interview.
applicant.sentenceTrans: 面试之前，申请人在外面等候。

application.definitionEn: a program designed to do a particular job; a piece of software
application.sentence: I download many applications on my cellphone.
application.sentenceTrans: 我在手机上下载了许多应用程序。
application.mnemonic: apply放置到=应用 + cation表名词 → application应用，运用

apply.definitionEn: to put or spread something such as paint, cream, etc. onto a surface; to ask formally for something (such as a job, admission to a school, a loan, etc.) usually in writing
apply.sentence: Don't forget to apply sunscreen if you spend time out in the sun.
apply.sentenceTrans: 如果你要长时间待在太阳下，一定别忘记涂防晒霜。
apply.mnemonic: ap去 + ply应用 → 去运用起来 → apply申请，应用

appoint.definitionEn: to choose (someone) to have a particular job; to give (someone) a position or duty
appoint.sentence: My boss has appointed me to manage this project.
appoint.sentenceTrans: 我的老板已任命我来管理这个项目。
appoint.mnemonic: ap加强 + point指 → appoint指定；任命

appreciate.definitionEn: to recognize the good qualities of somebody/something
appreciate.sentence: Grandma appreciated the gift on her birthday.
appreciate.sentenceTrans: 外婆为她生日那天收到的礼物表示感谢。
appreciate.mnemonic: ap一再 + preci价值 + ate动词后缀 → 一再给价 → appreciate欣赏

appreciation.definition: 鉴赏，欣赏；感激；理解，了解
appreciation.definitionEn: pleasure that you have when you recognize and enjoy the good qualities of somebody/something; a piece of writing or a speech in which the strengths and weaknesses of somebody/something, especially an artist or a work of art, are discussed and judged
appreciation.sentence: Appreciation of art is a skill that needs to be nurtured.
appreciation.sentenceTrans: 艺术鉴赏是一种需要培养的技能。
appreciation.mnemonic: ap一再 + preci价值 + ation名词后缀，表示行为 → 一再估价 → 评价，鉴赏，欣赏

approach.definition: 靠近；接近；着手处理；  n.接近；途径；方法
approach.definitionEn: to come near to somebody/something in distance or time
approach.sentence: The ship is approaching the shore at a high speed.
approach.sentenceTrans: 这艘船正以很快的速度靠近岸边。
approach.mnemonic: ap一再 + proach接近 → approach接近

appropriate.definition: 合适的，适当的；  v.挪用；拨款；私占
appropriate.definitionEn: suitable, acceptable or correct for the particular circumstances
appropriate.sentence: Slippers are not appropriate​ for a job interview.
appropriate.sentenceTrans: 拖鞋不适合在求职面试时穿。
appropriate.mnemonic: ap=ad到 + propri正确的 + ate形容词后缀 → appropriate合适的，适当的

appropriately.sentence: Dress up appropriately for different occasions.
appropriately.sentenceTrans: 要根据不同场合穿合适的衣服。
appropriately.mnemonic: ap一再+propri恰当+ate形容词后缀+ly...地→适当地；合适的；相称地

approval.definitionEn: agreement to, or permission for something, especially a plan or request
approval.sentence: The doctor gives me his approval to leave the hospital.
approval.mnemonic: ap一再 + prov证明 + al名词后缀 → 赞成

approve.definition: 正式核准，称许；赞成；满意
approve.definitionEn: to think that somebody/something is good, acceptable or suitable; to officially agree to a plan, request, etc.; to say that something is good enough to be used or is correct
approve.sentence: They all approve of my good performance.
approve.sentenceTrans: 他们都称许我良好的表现。
approve.mnemonic: ap加强 + prove证明 → approve承认，赞成

approximate.definition: 近似的（读作/əˈprɑːksəmət/）；  v.接近，近似（读作/əˈprɑksəmeɪt/）
approximate.definitionEn: almost correct or accurate, but not completely so
approximate.sentence: The approximate value of this car is 3,000 dollars.
approximate.mnemonic: ap不断 + proxim接近 + ate表动词 → 不断靠近 → approximate接近的，近似的

approximately.definitionEn: used to show that something is almost, but not completely, accurate or correct
approximately.mnemonic: ap引申 + proxim接近 + ate形容词后缀 + ly...地 → approximately大约，近似地；近于

april.definitionEn: the fourth month of the year, between March and May
april.sentence: Everything turns green in April as a result of all the rain it brings.
april.sentenceTrans: 四月带来了充沛的雨水，令万物呈现一派绿意。

arbitrary.definition: 随意的，任性的，随心所欲的；霸道的，专制的，蛮横的；主观的，武断的
arbitrary.definitionEn: (of an action, a decision, a rule, etc.) not seeming to be based on a reason, system or plan and sometimes seeming unfair
arbitrary.sentence: Tossing a coin is a rather arbitrary method of making a choice.
arbitrary.sentenceTrans: 靠抛硬币来做选择实在是太随便了。
arbitrary.mnemonic: arbitr判断 + ary……的 → 做出自己的判断 → arbitrary武断的

arbitration.definitionEn: the official process of settling an argument or a disagreement by somebody who is not involved
arbitration.sentence: The two companies agreed to resolve their dispute through arbitration.
arbitration.sentenceTrans: 两家公司同意通过仲裁解决他们的争端。

architect.definitionEn: a person whose job is designing buildings
architect.sentence: The architect is looking at a model of the building he designed.
architect.sentenceTrans: 这位建筑师正在看他设计的建筑模型。
architect.mnemonic: archi表示统治，主要的 + tect表示建筑 → 统治〔建筑〕的人 → architect建筑师

architecture.definition: 建筑学；建筑风格，建筑设计
architecture.definitionEn: the art and study of designing buildings; the design or style of a building or buildings
architecture.sentence: Our professor is explaining the theory of architecture in class.
architecture.sentenceTrans: 我们的教授正在课堂上讲解建筑学理论。
architecture.mnemonic: archi主要 + tect建造 +ure名词后缀 → 主要做造房 → architecture建筑学

area.definitionEn: a piece of land or part of a building that is used for a particular activity; a particular part of a town, a country, a region, or the world
area.sentence: The area of the office is about 40 square meters.
area.sentenceTrans: 办公室的面积大约是40平方米。

argue.definition: 争论；主张，认为；表明（原因等）
argue.definitionEn: to speak angrily to somebody because you disagree with them
argue.sentence: The workers are arguing about a problem.
argue.sentenceTrans: 员工们在争论一个问题。

argument.definition: 争吵，争论，争辩；论据，论点
argument.definitionEn: a conversation or discussion in which two or more people disagree, often angrily
argument.sentence: The girl had an argument with her boyfriend about the video game.
argument.sentenceTrans: 女孩和她的男朋友因为电子游戏争吵。
argument.mnemonic: argu(e)争论 + ment名词后缀 → argument争论，辩论

arise.definitionEn: to get out of bed; to stand up
arise.sentence: He arises at 7 a.m. every morning.
arise.mnemonic: a加强意义 + rise升起 → arise起来，升起

arm.definition: 手臂；上肢；  v.武装，装备
arm.definitionEn: either one of the two long body parts that join the top of your body at the shoulder and that end at the hand or wrist
arm.sentence: She is showing how strong her arm is.
arm.sentenceTrans: 她正在展示她那强壮的手臂。

army.definitionEn: a large organized group of soldiers who are trained to fight on land
army.sentence: The army is standing on the grass.
army.sentenceTrans: 这支军队正站在草地上。
army.mnemonic: arm武器，装甲 + y表名词 → 有武器、装甲的人 → army陆军，军队

around.definition: 周围，环绕；大约，四处；  prep.环绕，围绕，在……周围
around.definitionEn: surrounding somebody/something; on each side of something; on, to or from the other side of somebody/something
around.sentence: I stand up and look around.
around.mnemonic: a古英语前缀 + round圆圈 → around大约，四处

arouse.sentence: Being aroused from sleep is the beginning of his day.
arouse.sentenceTrans: 从梦中醒来是他一天的开始。
arouse.mnemonic: a在...的 + rouse唤醒 → arouse唤起

arrange.definitionEn: to put something in a particular order; to make something neat or attractive
arrange.sentence: They are arranging the coming event.
arrange.sentenceTrans: 他们正在筹备即将举行的活动。
arrange.mnemonic: ar使 + range排列 → 使排列好 → arrange安排

arrangement.definitionEn: the way things are done or organized
arrangement.sentence: Here are my important arrangements for today.
arrangement.sentenceTrans: 这些是我今天的重要安排。
arrangement.mnemonic: arrange安排 + ment名词后缀 → arrangement排列，布置

arrest.definition: 逮捕，拘留；  v.逮捕，拘留；吸引
arrest.definitionEn: if the police arrest somebody, the person is taken to a police station and kept there because the police believe they may be guilty of a crime
arrest.sentence: He was arrested for breaking the law.
arrest.sentenceTrans: 他因为犯法被抓起来了。
arrest.mnemonic: ar一再 + rest休息 → 不让动 → arrest逮捕，阻止

arrival.definitionEn: the act of coming to or reaching a place; the act of arriving
arrival.sentence: Passengers on the platform are waiting for the train's arrival.
arrival.sentenceTrans: 站台上的乘客正在等候火车到站。
arrival.mnemonic: arriv(e)到达 + al名词后缀 → arrival到达

arrive.definitionEn: to get to a place, especially at the end of a journey
arrive.sentence: She arrived at the airport on time.
arrive.mnemonic: ar一再 + rive河 → 到达河边 → 达到目标 → arrive到达

arrow.definitionEn: a thin stick with a sharp point at one end, which is shot from a bow
arrow.sentence: An arrow has a sharp point at one end and feathers on the other.
arrow.sentenceTrans: 箭的一端是尖的，另一端是羽毛。

art.definitionEn: the use of the imagination to express ideas or feelings, particularly in painting, drawing or sculpture
art.sentence: Painting and dance are forms of art.
art.sentenceTrans: 绘画和舞蹈都是艺术的表现形式。

article.definition: （报刊上的）文章，论文，报道；物品；条款；冠词
article.definitionEn: a piece of writing about a particular subject in a newspaper or magazine
article.sentence: She is reading the article in the newspaper.
article.sentenceTrans: 她正在阅读报纸上的文章。
article.mnemonic: art技巧，艺术 + icle东西 → 用技巧做出的东西 → article物品，文章

artificial.definition: 人造的，仿造的；人工的；假的
artificial.definitionEn: made or produced to copy something natural; not real; created by people; not happening naturally; not what it appears to be
artificial.sentence: Even with an artificial leg, he can still beat you in a race.
artificial.sentenceTrans: 尽管有一条假肢，他依然可以跑赢你。
artificial.mnemonic: artific技巧 + ial形容词后缀 → 用技巧做出的 → artificial人工的；矫揉造作的

artist.definitionEn: a person who creates works of art, especially paintings or drawings; a professional entertainer such as a singer, a dancer or an actor
artist.sentence: The artist is spraying colors on the wall.
artist.sentenceTrans: 这个艺术家在朝墙上喷涂颜料。
artist.mnemonic: art艺术 + ist表示从事某种职业的人 → artist艺术家，画家

as.definition: 和……一样；  prep.作为，当做；像，如同
as.definitionEn: used to say that something happens in the same way
as.sentence: Our actions look as consistent as each other's!
as.sentenceTrans: 我们的动作看起来很一致。

ash.definitionEn: the grey or black powder that is left after something, especially tobacco, wood or coal, has burnt
ash.sentence: These backpackers left nothing here but a pile of ashes.
ash.sentenceTrans: 这些背包客只在这儿留下一堆灰烬。

ashamed.definitionEn: feeling shame or embarrassment about somebody/something or because of something you have done
ashamed.sentence: The cat felt ashamed that it was caught when eating the goldfish.
ashamed.sentenceTrans: 这只猫很羞愧，因为它偷吃金鱼的时候被人发现了。
ashamed.mnemonic: a加强 + sham(e)羞耻 + ed形容词后缀 → ashamed感到羞愧的

aside.definitionEn: to one side; out of the way
aside.sentence: Cars all step aside to let the ambulance pass.
aside.sentenceTrans: 汽车们纷纷退让到一边，让救护车通过。
aside.mnemonic: a在…的 + side旁边 → 在旁边 → aside在边上

ask.definitionEn: to say or write something in the form of a question, in order to get information
ask.sentence: The man is asking a stranger for directions.
ask.sentenceTrans: 这个男人正在向陌生人问路。

asleep.sentence: This boy fell asleep in his stepfather's arms. How lovely!
asleep.sentenceTrans: 曼尼在杰的怀里睡着了，多有爱啊！
asleep.mnemonic: a表强调 + sleep睡觉 → asleep睡着的

aspect.definition: （问题等的）方面；外表，面貌；方位，方向
aspect.definitionEn: a particular part or feature of a situation, an idea, a problem, etc.; a way in which it may be considered
aspect.sentence: The students are recording every aspect of the plant's growth.
aspect.sentenceTrans: 学生们正在记录这株植物生长的各个方面。
aspect.mnemonic: a来，临近 + spect看 → 看的东西 → aspect外表，容貌，形势，方面

aspire.definitionEn: to have a strong desire to achieve or to become something
aspire.sentence: She aspires to be a firefighter and serve the people.
aspire.sentenceTrans: 她立志成为一名消防员，为人民服务。
aspire.mnemonic: a加强 + spir呼吸 + e强调 → 看到渴望的东西加强呼吸 → aspire渴望

assemble.definitionEn: to come together as a group; to bring people or things together as a group
assemble.sentence: The family assembled in the living room for a family photo.
assemble.sentenceTrans: 家庭成员为了拍这张照片在客厅集合。
assemble.mnemonic: as不断 + semble相类似，一样 → 不断使东西相同 → 组装东西 → assemble集合；装配

assert.definitionEn: to state clearly and firmly that something is true
assert.sentence: They both assert their opposing opinions, and I have no idea whom I should believe.
assert.sentenceTrans: 他们公说公有理，婆说婆有理，而我完全不知道该信谁。
assert.mnemonic: as加强 + sert加入，插入 → 强行插入观点 → assert断言

assertion.definitionEn: a statement saying that you strongly believe something to be true
assertion.sentence: He made an assertion that aliens exist.
assertion.mnemonic: as加强 + sert加入，插入 + ion名词后缀 → 加入讨论 → assertion声明；主张

assertive.definitionEn: expressing opinions or desires strongly and with confidence, so that people take notice
assertive.sentence: In the negotiation, it's crucial to be assertive when stating our bottom line.
assertive.sentenceTrans: 在谈判中，明确表述我们的底线时展现出坚定自信至关重要。
assertive.mnemonic: as加强 + sert加入，插入 + ive...的 → assertive断言的；确定的

assess.definitionEn: to make a judgement about the nature or quality of somebody/something; to calculate the amount or value of something
assess.sentence: The doctor needs to assess the patient’s symptoms before making a diagnosis.
assess.sentenceTrans: 医生需要在做出诊断前评估病人的症状。
assess.mnemonic: ad=as有关 + sess坐 -> 文职人员都是坐着的 -> 评估

assessment.definitionEn: an opinion or a judgement about somebody/something that has been thought about very carefully
assessment.sentence: "My assessment is that you are in good health," said the doctor.
assessment.sentenceTrans: “根据我的评估，你的身体很健康。”医生说。
assessment.mnemonic: assess评定 + ment表示行为、行为的过程或结果 → assessment（为征税对财产所作的）估价

asset.definition: 财产，资产；有价值的人或物
asset.definitionEn: a thing of value, especially property, that a person or company owns, which can be used or sold to pay debts; a person or thing that is valuable or useful to somebody/something
asset.sentence: My house is an important part of my assets.
asset.sentenceTrans: 我的房子是我的财产中重要的一部分。
asset.mnemonic: as朝，向，去 + set足够 → asset财产

assign.definitionEn: to give out as a job or responsibility; to give somebody something that they can use, or some work or responsibility
assign.sentence: Our teacher assigned us lots of homework.
assign.sentenceTrans: 我们的老师给我们布置了许多家庭作业。
assign.mnemonic: as一再 + sign记号 → 不断给人标记号 → assign指定；分配

assignment.definitionEn: a task or piece of work that somebody is given to do, usually as part of their job or studies
assignment.sentence: My teacher gave me a lot of assignments for the weekend.
assignment.sentenceTrans: 老师给我布置了很多周末的家庭作业。
assignment.mnemonic: assign分配 + ment名词后缀 → assignment（课外）作业

assimilation.definitionEn: people of different backgrounds come to see themselves as part of a larger national family.
assimilation.sentence: Assimilation is the process when a group comes to resemble those of another.
assimilation.sentenceTrans: 同化是一个群体变得与另一个群体相似的过程。

assist.definitionEn: to give support or help; to make it easier for someone to do something or for something to happen
assist.sentence: They assisted each other to the top of the mountain.
assist.sentenceTrans: 他们互相帮助，登上了山顶。
assist.mnemonic: as一再 ＋ sist站 → 站过来 → assist帮助

assistance.sentence: I climbed up the hill with the assistance of my friend.
assistance.sentenceTrans: 在我朋友的帮助下，我爬上了山。
assistance.mnemonic: assist帮助 + ance名词后缀 → assistance援助

assistant.definition: 助理，助手；  adj.助理的，辅助的
assistant.definitionEn: a person who helps or supports somebody, usually in their job
assistant.sentence: The businessman has an assistant to help him with his work every day.
assistant.sentenceTrans: 这个商人有一名每天协助他工作的助理。
assistant.mnemonic: assist援助 + ant名词后缀 → 帮助之人 → assistant助手，助理

associate.definition: 与某人交往；联系；  n.同事，合作人；  adj.副的
associate.definitionEn: to make a connection between people or things in your mind
associate.sentence: Nowadays, people like to associate with others online.
associate.sentenceTrans: 如今，人们喜欢在网上与别人交往。
associate.mnemonic: as去 + soci联合 + ate表动词  → 结成团队 → associate联合

association.definition: 协会，联盟；联想；联系，关联
association.definitionEn: an official group of people who have joined together for a particular purpose
association.sentence: The association members wanted to attract new people to join them.
association.sentenceTrans: 社团成员们想吸引更多的人加入他们。
association.mnemonic: as加强 + soci社会 + at(e)使… + ion表名词 → associate结成社会=联合 + ion表名词 → association联合

assume.definition: 猜想；认为；接受；  v.采取
assume.definitionEn: to think or accept that something is true but without having proof of it
assume.sentence: I assumed that the red team would win.
assume.mnemonic: as加强 + sume拿取 → 主动拿起 → assume承担

assure.definitionEn: to tell somebody that something is definitely true or is definitely going to happen, especially when they have doubts about it
assure.sentence: I can assure you that the dog will be well cared for.
assure.sentenceTrans: 我可以向你保证，狗会得到很好的照顾。
assure.mnemonic: as一再 + sure确定 → 一再确定 → assure肯定，确信

astonish.sentence: The opponent's harsh words astonished him.
astonish.mnemonic: as=ex表强调 + ton打雷 + ish表动词 → astonish使吃惊

astronaut.definitionEn: a person whose job involves travelling and working in a spacecraft
astronaut.sentence: I would love to be an astronaut and go to space.
astronaut.sentenceTrans: 我想成为一名宇航员进入太空。
astronaut.mnemonic: astro星际 + naut航行员 → 宇航员

at.definition: 在（地点），于，向，对准，在……方面
at.definitionEn: used to say where something/somebody is or where something happens; used to say where somebody works or studies

athlete.definitionEn: a person who competes in sports; a person who is good at sports and physical exercise
athlete.sentence: He was a great athlete who ran really fast.
athlete.sentenceTrans: 他以前是一名优秀的运动员，跑得非常快。
athlete.mnemonic: athl比赛 + ete → 参加体育比赛的专业人士 → athlete运动员

atmosphere.definitionEn: the mixture of gases that surrounds the earth
atmosphere.sentence: The Earth's atmosphere absorbs part of the sun's energy.
atmosphere.sentenceTrans: 地球大气层吸收太阳的部分能量。
atmosphere.mnemonic: atmo蒸汽 + sphere范围 → 大气层；空；气氛

attach.definition: 贴上，使依附；把……固定，把……附（在……上）；缚；认为...有重要性；附加；赋予
attach.definitionEn: to fasten or join one thing to another
attach.sentence: The card player has several pieces of paper to attach to his face.
attach.sentenceTrans: 这个打牌的人有好多张纸条要贴在他的脸上。
attach.mnemonic: at=ad 去 + tach 固定，栓→ 去固定 → attach附上，使附属，使依恋

attachment.definitionEn: a document that you send to somebody using email
attachment.sentence: I have sent my resume as an attachment.
attachment.sentenceTrans: 我以附件的形式发送了简历。
attachment.mnemonic: attach附加 + ment表名词 → 附属物

attack.definition: 攻击，进攻，袭击；毁坏；  n.疾病发作
attack.definitionEn: to use violence to try to hurt or kill somebody; to use weapons, such as guns and bombs against an enemy in a war, etc.; to criticize somebody/something severely
attack.sentence: The soldiers attacked the enemy during the war.
attack.sentenceTrans: 在战争中，战士们对敌人发起了攻击。

attain.definitionEn: to succeed in getting something, usually after a lot of effort
attain.sentence: I finally attained my driving license!
attain.mnemonic: at一再 + tain拿住 → attain获得；达到

attainable.definitionEn: capable of being attained or accomplished
attainable.sentence: The attainable profits can be maximized by reducing operational costs.
attainable.sentenceTrans: 通过降低运营成本，可以实现最大化的利润。

attainment.definitionEn: the state or condition of having gotten or done something difficult :the act of attaining something
attainment.sentence: Landing on the moon is now very possible attainment.
attainment.sentenceTrans: 现在，人们有可能登上月球了。
attainment.mnemonic: attain获得+ment表名词→获得的成就 → 成就，造诣

attempt.definition: 试图，尝试；  n.试图，尝试；企图
attempt.definitionEn: to make an effort or try to do something, especially something difficult
attempt.sentence: The cat attempts to catch that fish.
attempt.sentenceTrans: 那只猫咪试图抓到那条鱼。
attempt.mnemonic: at表强调 + tempt尝试 → 一再尝试 → attempt尝试，企图

attend.definition: 护理，照顾；处理；参加；注意
attend.definitionEn: to be with somebody and help them
attend.sentence: A nurse is attending to the newborn baby.
attend.sentenceTrans: 一位护士正在照顾新生的宝宝。
attend.mnemonic: at=ad，to + tend延伸 → 把思维延伸到 → 关注，引申为期待某人到达，后来又引申为到达 → attend出席

attendance.definitionEn: the act of being present at a place, for example at school
attendance.sentence: The register kept a record of people's attendances at the conference.
attendance.sentenceTrans: 登记簿记录了人们出席会议的情况。

attendant.definition: 服务员，侍者，随从；  adj.伴随的，随之而产生的
attendant.definitionEn: a person whose job is to serve or help people in a public place; a person who takes care of and lives or travels with an important person or a sick or disabled person
attendant.sentence: The gas attendant is filling up the car for the customer.
attendant.sentenceTrans: 这个加油站服务员正在为顾客的汽车加油。
attendant.mnemonic: attend照料 + ant名词后缀  → 照料的人  → 服务员，随从

attention.definitionEn: the act of listening to, looking at or thinking about something/somebody carefully; interest that people show in somebody/something; things that somebody does to try to please you or to show their interest in you; special care, action or treatment
attention.sentence: Only one student in the class was paying attention to what the teacher was saying.
attention.sentenceTrans: 班上只有一个学生在专心听老师讲课。
attention.mnemonic: attent关注 + ion名词后缀 → attention注意力

attitude.definitionEn: the way that you behave towards somebody/something that shows how you think and feel; the way that you think and feel about somebody/something
attitude.sentence: A positive attitude is what you need to solve problems.
attitude.sentenceTrans: 你需要以积极的态度来解决问题。
attitude.mnemonic: att=apr倾向 + itude后缀，构成抽象名词 → attitude态度

attract.definitionEn: if you are attracted by something, it interests you and makes you want it; if you are attracted by somebody, you like or admire them; to make somebody/something come somewhere or take part in something; to make people have a particular reaction
attract.sentence: This vibrant flower attracts a butterfly.
attract.sentenceTrans: 这朵鲜艳的花吸引了一只蝴蝶。
attract.mnemonic: at一再 + tract拉 → 拉过来 → attract吸引

attraction.definitionEn: a feeling of liking somebody, especially sexually; a force that pulls things towards each other; a feature, quality or person that makes something seem interesting and enjoyable, and worth having; an interesting or enjoyable place to go or thing to do
attraction.sentence: The park's attraction is enhanced by its beautiful gardens.
attraction.sentenceTrans: 公园因其美丽的花园而更具吸引力。
attraction.mnemonic: attract吸引 + ion表名词 → attraction吸引力

attractive.definitionEn: (of a thing or a place) pleasant; (of a person) pleasant to look at, especially in a sexual way
attractive.sentence: With such a low price, the hotel room is really attractive.
attractive.sentenceTrans: 这个旅馆房间价格如此低廉，真的很吸引人。
attractive.mnemonic: at加强 + tract拉 + ive...的 → attract拉过来=吸引 + ive...的 → attractive引人注目的

attribute.definition: 把……归因于，把……归咎于（读作/əˈtrɪbjut/）；  n.属性；特征；定语
attribute.definitionEn: to say or believe that something is the result of a particular thing
attribute.sentence: Success can be attributed to hard work and a bit of luck.
attribute.sentenceTrans: 成功都可以归因于努力的奋斗和些许的运气。

auction.definitionEn: a public event at which things are sold to the person who offers the most money for them
auction.sentence: I hold an auction to sell my house because I am broke.
auction.sentenceTrans: 我举办了一个拍卖会来卖掉我的房子，因为我破产了。
auction.mnemonic: auct=aug抬高，增加 + ion表名词 → auction拍卖

audience.definitionEn: the group of people who have gathered to watch or listen to something (a play, concert, somebody speaking, etc.)
audience.sentence: The audience in the conference hall stayed quiet during his speech.
audience.sentenceTrans: 他讲话时，会议厅里的听众都很安静。
audience.mnemonic: audi听 + ence表名词 → 听众，观众，读者

august.definitionEn: the 8th month of the year, between July and September

aunt.definitionEn: the sister of your father or mother or the wife of your uncle
aunt.sentence: This aunt enjoys tea very much.

authentic.definition: 真正的；真实的；真品的，真迹的；可靠的
authentic.definitionEn: known to be real and genuine and not a copy
authentic.sentence: This diamond isn't fake-I'm sure it's authentic.
authentic.sentenceTrans: 这颗钻石不是假的——我敢保证它是真的！
authentic.mnemonic: auth=author作者 + entic形容词后缀 → authentic真的，真正的

author.definitionEn: a person who writes books or the person who wrote a particular book
author.sentence: Lu Xun is the author of this book.
author.mnemonic: auth增加，创造 + or表人 → 创作的人 → author作者，作家

authorisation.definitionEn: a document giving an official instruction or command
authorisation.sentence: Those who decide to pull out because of US sanctions will need to be granted authorisation from the European commission, without which they face the risk of being sued by EU member states.
authorisation.sentenceTrans: 那些因美国制裁而决定撤出的人需要获得欧洲委员会的授权，否则他们将面临被欧盟成员国起诉的风险。

authorise.definitionEn: give or delegate power or authority to
authorise.sentence: He is authorised to log in the account.
authorise.sentenceTrans: 他被授权登录这个账户。

authority.definition: 权威，威信；权威人士；权力，职权；当局，官方
authority.definitionEn: the people or an organization who have the power to make decisions or who have a particular area of responsibility in a country or region; the power to give orders to people
authority.sentence: The authority declared that catmint would be banned completely in three months.
authority.sentenceTrans: 当局宣称猫薄荷将在三个月后被全面禁止。
authority.mnemonic: auth使增加；创造 + or施动者后缀 +ity名词后缀 → authority权力；权威

authorization.definitionEn: a document giving an official instruction or command
authorization.sentence: You need authorization to enter this area.
authorization.sentenceTrans: 你需要得到授权才能进入这个区域。

authorize.definitionEn: to give official permission for something, or for somebody to do something
authorize.sentence: The emperor authorized this document with a stamp.
authorize.sentenceTrans: 皇帝加印批准了这个文件。
authorize.mnemonic: auth授权 + or人 + ize动词后缀 → authorize授权，批准

automatic.definitionEn: (of a machine, device, etc.) having controls that work without needing a person to operate them
automatic.sentence: The automatic production line improves the working efficiency greatly.
automatic.sentenceTrans: 自动化生产线大大地提高了工作效率。
automatic.mnemonic: autom=auto，autom自动 + atic有…性质的 → automatic自动的，机械的

automobile.definitionEn: a vehicle used for carrying passengers on streets and roads; a car
automobile.sentence: This green automobile is for sale. Let's take a look.
automobile.sentenceTrans: 这辆绿色的汽车正在出售，我们去看看吧。
automobile.mnemonic: auto自己 + mobile移动的 → automobile汽车

autonomy.definition: 人身自由；自治；自治权；自主权
autonomy.definitionEn: the ability to act and make decisions without being controlled by anyone else
