clockwise.sentenceTrans: 那个男人以顺时针方向在花园里散步。
clockwise.mnemonic: clock时钟 + wise方向，状态 → clockwise顺时针的

close.definition: 关闭，合上；  adj.亲密的；  adv.（空间或时间上）接近地，靠近地
close.definitionEn: to put something into a position so that it covers an opening; to get into this position
close.sentence: The man is closing the door.

cloth.definitionEn: material made by weaving or knitting cotton, wool, silk, etc.
cloth.sentence: The shop sells different kinds of cloth.
cloth.sentenceTrans: 这家商店出售各式各样的布料。

clothe.definitionEn: to dress somebody/yourself; to provide clothes for somebody to wear

clothes.definitionEn: the things that people wear to cover their bodies and that are usually made from cloth
clothes.sentence: I hung the clothes on the washing line.
clothes.sentenceTrans: 我把衣服挂在了晾衣绳上。

cloud.definitionEn: a white or gray mass in the sky that is made of many very small drops of water
cloud.sentence: There was only one cloud in the middle of the blue sky.

cloudy.definitionEn: having many clouds in the sky
cloudy.sentence: It's cloudy today, so you can't see the sun.
cloudy.sentenceTrans: 今天多云，所以你看不见太阳。

club.definition: 社团，俱乐部；  v.用棍棒打
club.definitionEn: (especially in compounds) a group of people who meet together regularly, for a particular activity, sport, etc.
club.sentence: You should join a club to do exercise.
club.sentenceTrans: 你应该加入个俱乐部来进行锻炼。

clue.definitionEn: an object, a piece of evidence or some information that helps the police solve a crime
clue.sentence: The paw print is a big clue in the case.
clue.sentenceTrans: 爪印是此案的一个关键线索。

coach.definition: 教练；长途汽车；旅客车厢；  v.训练，指导
coach.definitionEn: a person who trains a person or team in sport
coach.sentence: The volleyball coach is talking to her team members.
coach.sentenceTrans: 这位排球教练正在和她的队员们交谈。

coal.definitionEn: a black or brownish-black hard substance within the earth that is used as a fuel
coal.sentence: He is holding a few pieces of coal.

coarse.sentence: Poor people used coarse cloth to make clothes in ancient China.
coarse.sentenceTrans: 在中国古代，穷人用粗糙的布料制作衣服。

coast.definition: 海岸，海滨；  v.沿海航行
coast.definitionEn: the land along or near a sea or ocean
coast.sentence: The view of the coast is amazing.
coast.sentenceTrans: 这片海岸的景色棒极了。

coastal.sentence: This coastal road has wonderful views of the mountains and the sea.
coastal.sentenceTrans: 在这条沿海公路上可以看到美丽的山海景色。
coastal.mnemonic: coast海岸 + al...的 → coastal海岸的

coat.definitionEn: a piece of outdoor clothing that is worn over other clothes to keep warm or dry. Coats have sleeves and may be long or short.
coat.sentence: The coat lining is detachable? That's perfect for our variable climate!
coat.sentenceTrans: 大衣内衬可拆卸？太适合多变天气了！

cock.sentence: The cock has a beautiful tail.
cock.sentenceTrans: 这只公鸡的尾巴很漂亮。

code.definition: 编码，代码；规范，准则；法典
code.definitionEn: a system of computer programming instructions
code.sentence: The programmer is writing code for the new software on his computer.
code.sentenceTrans: 这位程序员正在电脑上为一款新软件写代码。

coffee.definitionEn: the roasted seeds (called coffee beans) of a tropical bush; a powder made from them
coffee.sentence: Coffee is a drink made with water and ground coffee beans.
coffee.sentenceTrans: 咖啡是用水和磨碎的咖啡豆制成的饮料。

cognition.definitionEn: the psychological result of perception and learning and reasoning
cognition.sentence: Developing moral cognition is as important as acquiring knowledge.
cognition.sentenceTrans: 建立道德认知与获取知识一样重要。

cognitive.definitionEn: connected with mental processes of understanding
cognitive.sentence: This test will assess your cognitive skills and ability to think quickly.
cognitive.sentenceTrans: 这个测试可以评估你的认知能力和反应能力。
cognitive.mnemonic: cogn知道 + itive…的 → cognitive认识的

coherent.definition: 清楚易懂的；条理清楚的，有条理的
coherent.definitionEn: (of ideas, thoughts, arguments, etc.) logical and well organized; easy to understand and clear
coherent.sentence: The woman uses different graphs to make her presentation coherent.
coherent.sentenceTrans: 这个女人用不同的图表使她的演讲清楚易懂。
coherent.mnemonic: co共同 + her粘附 + ent……的 → 共同粘附的 → coherent连贯的；有条理的

coin.definition: 硬币；  v.铸造（硬币）；创造
coin.definitionEn: a small, flat, and usually round piece of metal issued by a government as money
coin.sentence: This coin is worth ten cents.

cold.definition: 寒冷；感冒，伤风；  adj.寒冷的
cold.definitionEn: having a lower than usual temperature; having a temperature lower than the human body
cold.sentence: His face turned red in the cold.
cold.sentenceTrans: 他的脸在寒冷中冻得发红。

collar.definition: 衣领；  v.抓住；为……戴上项圈，为……上领子
collar.definitionEn: the part around the neck of a shirt, jacket or coat that usually folds down
collar.sentence: The collar of this shirt is too tight.
collar.sentenceTrans: 这件衬衣的衣领太紧了。
collar.mnemonic: coll脖子 + ar名词后缀 → collar衣领

colleague.definitionEn: a person that you work with, especially in a profession or a business
colleague.sentence: I really learned a lot by discussing with my colleagues.
colleague.sentenceTrans: 通过和同事们讨论，我真的学到了很多。
colleague.mnemonic: col共同 + league捆绑 → 捆绑在一起的人 → colleague同事

collect.definitionEn: to buy or find things of a particular type and keep them as a hobby

collection.definitionEn: a group of objects, often of the same sort, that have been collected; a group of objects or people
collection.sentence: I own a very valuable collection of guitars.
collection.sentenceTrans: 我拥有一些很有价值的吉他珍藏。
collection.mnemonic: collect收集 + ion名词后缀 → collection采集，收藏

collective.definition: 集体的，共同的；【财】共同的；  n.集体
collective.definitionEn: done or shared by all members of a group of people; involving a whole group or society; used to refer to all members of a group
collective.sentence: Class fund is collective property. It needs everybody to contribute.
collective.sentenceTrans: 班费是集体财产，它需要每个人的贡献。
collective.mnemonic: col一起 + lect选择，收集 + ive……的 → 集中到一起 → 集体的

college.definitionEn: (often in names) (in Britain) a place where students go to study or to receive training after they have left school; (often in names) (in the US) a university where students can study for a degree after they have left school
college.sentence: Students are gathering in front of the college building.
college.sentenceTrans: 学生们聚集在学院大楼前。
college.mnemonic: col=com一起，与 + leg选择，收集 + e → 一起做研究工作的师生 → college大学

colony.definitionEn: a country or an area that is governed by people from another, more powerful, country
colony.sentence: A colony on another planet might look like this!
colony.sentenceTrans: 在另一个星球，殖民地可能是这样的！

color.definitionEn: the appearance that things have that results from the way in which they reflect light. Red, orange and green are colours.

colorful.definitionEn: full of bright colours or having a lot of different colours
colorful.mnemonic: color色彩 ＋ ful...的 → colorful多彩的，色彩的

colour.definitionEn: to put colour on something using paint, coloured pencils, etc.
colour.sentence: I like to paint with different colours.
colour.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢用不同的色彩画画。

colourful.sentence: Compared with her brother's painting, hers is more colourful.
colourful.sentenceTrans: 和她弟弟的画相比，她的画色彩更丰富。

column.definitionEn: a tall, solid, vertical  post made of steel, stone, etc., that is used as a support in a building
column.sentence: Only a few columns of the old building are still standing.
column.sentenceTrans: 这栋老建筑只有几根柱子还立在那儿。
column.mnemonic: col顶部 + u + mn名词后缀 → 突出顶部的物体 → column柱，栏

comb.definitionEn: to pull a comb through your hair in order to make it neat
comb.sentence: This monster became a red comb after being defeated.
comb.sentenceTrans: 女妖结罗被犬夜叉和戈薇击败后变成了一把红色的梳子。

combat.definition: 战斗，格斗；  v.与……战斗，与……斗争（读作/kəmˈbæt/）；防止，抑制
combat.definitionEn: to stop something unpleasant or harmful from happening or from getting worse
combat.sentence: The two servants were in combat all night for their master.
combat.sentenceTrans: 骑士王和枪哥为了他们的主人彻夜战斗。
combat.mnemonic: com共同，对抗之意 + bat打 → 一起对打 → combat战斗

combination.definitionEn: two or more things joined or mixed together to form a single unit; the act of joining or mixing together two or more things to form a single unit
combination.sentence: Fried chicken plus cold beer is a perfect combination on a snowy day.
combination.sentenceTrans: 下雪天，炸鸡和啤酒真是完美的搭配。
combination.mnemonic: com共同 + bin=bine藤蔓 + ation表名词 → combination结合，联合

combine.definitionEn: to come together in order to work or act together; to put two things or groups together so that they work or act together
combine.sentence: Combine yellow and blue, and you will get green.
combine.sentenceTrans: 把黄色和蓝色混合起来，你就会得到绿色。
combine.mnemonic: com与...一起 + bin成对地 + e → combine联合

come.definitionEn: to move to or towards a person or place; to arrive somewhere in order to do something or get something
come.sentence: Will he come to your home with Christmas gifts?
come.sentenceTrans: 他会带着圣诞礼物来你家么？

comedy.definitionEn: a play, movie, television program, novel, etc., that is meant to make people laugh
comedy.sentence: This TV comedy show makes people laugh a lot.
comedy.sentenceTrans: 这个电视喜剧节目引人发笑。
comedy.mnemonic: com宴会 + edy表名词 → 像宴会一样热闹 → comedy喜剧

comfort.definitionEn: to make somebody who is worried or unhappy feel better by being kind and sympathetic towards them
comfort.sentence: Ah! The level of comfort of this chair is amazing.
comfort.sentenceTrans: 啊！这张椅子的舒适度真是太棒了。
comfort.mnemonic: com共同 + fort加强 → 精神强大 → comfort安慰

comfortable.definitionEn: not having any physically unpleasant feelings; experiencing physical comfort
comfortable.sentence: The man looked so comfortable lying in the chair.
comfortable.sentenceTrans: 这个男人躺在椅子上，看起来非常舒适。
comfortable.mnemonic: com共同 + fort强大，力量 + able能…的 → comfortable愉快舒适的

command.definition: 值得，博得；命令；指挥，统率；掌管，控制；  n.命令；控制
command.definitionEn: an order given to a person or an animal
command.sentence: His good performance commands our praise.
command.mnemonic: com一起 + mand命令 → 命令大家一起做 → command指挥，命令

commander.definitionEn: a person who is in charge of something, especially an officer in charge of a particular group of soldiers or a military operation; an officer of fairly high rank in the British or American navy; (in Britain) a London police officer of high rank
commander.sentence: The commander was thinking about possible strategies.
commander.sentenceTrans: 指挥官在思考下一步可行的策略。
commander.mnemonic: com共同 + mand命令 + er表示做某事的人 → n.司令官，指挥员

comment.definition: 评论，意见；批评，指责；意见；批评；  v.评论
comment.definitionEn: to express an opinion about something
comment.sentence: Some of my friends left me comments.
comment.sentenceTrans: 我的一些朋友给我评论了。
comment.mnemonic: com共同 + ment思考，神智 → 共同思考 → 评论

commerce.definitionEn: trade, especially between countries; the buying and selling of goods and services
commerce.sentence: Online platforms have completely changed the mode of commerce.
commerce.sentenceTrans: 在线平台已经彻底改变了商业模式。
commerce.mnemonic: com共同 ＋ merce交易 → 共同交易 → commerce商业

commercial.definition: 商业广告；  adj.贸易的；商业的
commercial.definitionEn: connected with the buying and selling of goods and services
commercial.sentence: The kids are watching a TV commercial of fast food.
commercial.sentenceTrans: 孩子们正在看快餐的电视广告。
commercial.mnemonic: com共同 + merc交易 + ial...的 → 共同交易的 → 商业的

commercialise.sentence: The farmer decided to commercialise her homemade jam and sell it in the supermarket.
commercialise.sentenceTrans: 那位农民决定将她自制的果酱商业化，并在超市里销售。

commercialize.definitionEn: to use (something) as an opportunity to earn money
commercialize.sentence: Endorsing a product such as perfume can finally commercialize the model's personal image.
commercialize.sentenceTrans: 代言一种产品（如香水）最终可以商业化模特的个人形象。
commercialize.mnemonic: com 共同 + merci=merc交易 + al...的 + ize 使... → vt. 使商业化；使商品化

commission.definition: 委员会；佣金；  v.正式委托（谱写、制作等）；委任
commission.definitionEn: an official group of people who have been given responsibility to control something, or to find out about something, usually for the government
commission.sentence: The State Health Care Commission meets once every month to make policy.
commission.sentenceTrans: 州立卫生保健委员会每个月都会碰一次头来制定政策。
commission.mnemonic: com共同 + miss送 + ion名词后缀 → 共同选出的人 → commission委员会

commit.definitionEn: to do something wrong or illegal; to kill yourself deliberately
commit.sentence: The fox committed a crime and was sent to prison.
commit.sentenceTrans: 狐狸犯了罪，并被抓进了监狱。
commit.mnemonic: com一起 + mit释放，抛出 → 某种行为的宣泄 → commit承诺，自杀

commitment.definition: 承诺，许诺；信奉；奉献，献身
commitment.definitionEn: a promise to do something or to behave in a particular way; a promise to support somebody/something; the fact of committing yourself
commitment.sentence: They made a commitment to each other at their wedding ceremony.
commitment.sentenceTrans: 在婚礼上，他们相互做出承诺。
commitment.mnemonic: commit承诺 + ment名词后缀 → commitment承诺

committee.definitionEn: a group of people who are chosen, usually by a larger group, to make decisions or to deal with a particular subject
committee.sentence: The committee members come to the meeting to make decisions for the group they represent.
committee.sentenceTrans: 委员会成员们代表着他们各自的组织来开会做决议。
committee.mnemonic: com集合，团结 + mitt(mittere)解放 + ee名词后缀，受动者 → committee委员会

commodity.definitionEn: a product or a raw material that can be bought and sold; a thing that is useful or has a useful quality
commodity.sentence: You can find many commodities in supermarkets.
commodity.sentenceTrans: 你可以在超市看到各种各样的商品。
commodity.mnemonic: com共同 + mod方式，模式，风度 + ity名词后缀 → 有共同模式的东西 → 商品

common.definitionEn: happening often; existing in large numbers or in many places
common.sentence: It is common to see people take a bicycle to work.
common.sentenceTrans: 经常能看到人们骑自行车去上班。
common.mnemonic: com一起 + mon改变；去 → 所有人都共享的 → common普通的

communicate.definitionEn: to exchange information, news, ideas, etc. with somebody
communicate.sentence: The police communicate with each other by radio.
communicate.sentenceTrans: 警察通过无线电进行沟通。
communicate.mnemonic: com共同 + muni交流 + cate表动词 → 共同交流 → 传播

communication.definitionEn: the activity or process of expressing ideas and feelings or of giving people information
communication.sentence: They like to use cell phones for communication.
communication.sentenceTrans: 他们喜欢用手机来交流。
communication.mnemonic: communi通常，一般 + cation名词后缀 → 共同的事物 → communication通信，交流

community.definitionEn: all the people who live in a particular area or place
community.sentence: The largest Chinese community in this city lives in its Chinatown.
community.sentenceTrans: 这个城市最大的华人社区居住在其唐人街。
community.mnemonic: com共同 + mun公共的 + ity状态 → 公共状态 → community社区

commute.definition: 通勤；  n.通勤，在两地之间乘车往返
commute.definitionEn: to travel regularly by bus, train, car, etc. between your place of work and your home
commute.sentence: If I didn't have to commute two hours every day, I'd have so much more time for vlogging!
commute.sentenceTrans: 如果我每天不用通勤两个小时，我就会有更多时间来做 vlog 了！
commute.mnemonic: com和，一起 + mute改变 -> commute两地往返

compact.definition: 紧凑的，密集的；  n.合约，条约
compact.sentence: The room is compact but well-equipped.
compact.sentenceTrans: 这个房间虽然布局紧凑，但设施一应俱全。
compact.mnemonic: com共同 + pact压紧 → 全部压紧 → compact紧密的

companion.definitionEn: a person or an animal that travels with you or spends a lot of time with you
companion.mnemonic: com共同 + panion面包 → 吃一条面包的 → companion同伴

company.definitionEn: a business organization that makes money by producing or selling goods or services
company.sentence: The little girl smiled in her father's company.
company.sentenceTrans: 她在父亲的陪伴下笑了。
company.mnemonic: com一起 + pany面包 → 一起吃面包 → company陪伴

comparable.definition: 类似的，比得上的，可比较的
comparable.definitionEn: similar to somebody/something else and able to be compared
comparable.sentence: The two dogs are comparable in size and strength.
comparable.sentenceTrans: 这两条狗在大小和强壮程度方面都不相上下。
comparable.mnemonic: compar=compare比较，对照 + able形容词后缀，可……的 → (to)比得上的；(with)可比较的,类似的

comparative.definitionEn: connected with studying things to find out how similar or different they are
comparative.sentence:
The performance measures chosen by local authorities usually consist of comparative statistics and unit 
costs.
comparative.sentenceTrans: 地方当局选择的绩效衡量标准通常包括比较统计数据和单位成本。
comparative.mnemonic: com共同 + par看见 + ative...的 → 看见共同之处的 → comparative比较的

compare.definition: 与……相比较；将……比作； 比较；对比
compare.definitionEn: to examine people or things to see how they are similar and how they are different
compare.sentence: It's smart to compare products when you go shopping.
compare.sentenceTrans: 当你购物时，比较一下商品是很明智的。
compare.mnemonic: com共同 + pare=par平等 → 平等放在一起 → compare对照；比较

comparison.definitionEn: the process of comparing two or more people or things
comparison.sentence: I made a comparison between the two houses.
comparison.sentenceTrans: 我将这两栋房子做了比较。
comparison.mnemonic: compar=compare比较 + ison表名词 → comparison比较

compass.definitionEn: an instrument for finding direction, with a needle that always points to the north
compass.sentence: When you lose your way, you can use a compass.
compass.sentenceTrans: 当你迷路时，你可以使用指南针。
compass.mnemonic: com一起，共同 + pass传播，走 → compass指南针

compatible.definitionEn: able to exist together without trouble or conflict: going together well
compatible.sentence: He is compatible with his friend because of their similar interests and opinions.
compatible.sentenceTrans: 他和他的朋友很合得来，因为他们有相似的兴趣和观点。
compatible.mnemonic: com共同+pat感情+ible能...的→有共同感情的→相容的

compel.definitionEn: to force somebody to do something; to make something necessary
compel.sentence: He was compelled to stay in the circle.
compel.sentenceTrans: 他被迫待在一个圆圈里。
compel.mnemonic: com共同 + pel推 → 一起推 → 强迫

compensate.definitionEn: to provide something good to balance or reduce the bad effects of damage, loss, etc.; to pay somebody money because they have suffered some damage, loss, injury, etc.
compensate.sentence: He should be compensated for his work-related injury.
compensate.mnemonic: com全部 + pens花费 + ate动词后缀 → 花费的钱全部拿回来 → 赔偿

compensation.definition: 赔偿金；补偿；补偿，报酬，赔偿金
compensation.definitionEn: something, especially money, that somebody gives you because they have hurt you, or damaged something that you own
compensation.sentence: The injured man received his compensation from the insurance agent.
compensation.sentenceTrans: 那个受伤的人收到了保险代理人的赔偿金。

compete.definitionEn: to try to be more successful or better than somebody else who is trying to do the same as you
compete.sentence: We compete against each other to see who's the fastest rider.
compete.sentenceTrans: 我们相互竞争，想看看谁才是最快的骑手。
compete.mnemonic: com共同 + pete追求 → 一起追 → compete比赛

competent.definitionEn: having enough skill or knowledge to do something well or to the necessary standard; of a good standard but not very good; having the power to decide something
competent.sentence: She's a competent worker and is good at her job.
competent.sentenceTrans: 她是一个有能力的员工，并且擅长她的工作。
competent.mnemonic: com共同 + pet追寻，寻求 + ent……的 → competent有资格的

competition.definitionEn: an event in which people compete with each other to find out who is the best at something
competition.sentence: Who is going to win this competition?
competition.mnemonic: compet=compete竞争 + ition名词后缀 → competition比赛

competitive.definitionEn: used to describe a situation in which people or organizations compete against each other
competitive.sentence: In competitive inhibition, an inhibitor binds to the active site of the enzyme.
competitive.sentenceTrans: 在竞争性抑制中，抑制剂与酶的活性位点结合。
competitive.mnemonic: compet=compete竞争 + itive..的 → competitive有竞争力的；竞争的

competitor.definitionEn: a person or an organization that competes against others, especially in business; a person who takes part in a competition
competitor.sentenceTrans: 3000多名参赛者参加了跑步比赛。
competitor.mnemonic: com共同 + pet追求 + itor人 → competitor比赛者

complacent.definitionEn: satisfied with how things are and not wanting to change them
complacent.sentence: The complacent driver is too confident and hasn't noticed the danger on the icy road.
complacent.sentenceTrans: 这个自以为是的司机太自信了，并没意识到在结冰的路上驾驶的危险。
complacent.mnemonic: com加强语气 + plac使满意 + ent形容词后缀 → 被取悦 → complacent自满的

complain.definitionEn: to express complaints, discontent, displeasure, or unhappiness
complain.sentence: The man complained about his neighbors being too noisy.
complain.sentenceTrans: 这个男人抱怨他的邻居太吵。
complain.mnemonic: com共同 + plain抱怨 → 抱怨，诉苦；控告

complaint.definitionEn: a reason for not being satisfied; a statement that somebody makes saying that they are not satisfied
complaint.sentence: The customer made a complaint to the manager.
complaint.mnemonic: com全部 + plaint抱怨 → 对全部东西抱怨 → complaint抱怨

complete.definitionEn: including all the parts, etc. that are necessary; whole
complete.mnemonic: com全部 + plete满 → 全满 → complete完全的

completely.definitionEn: (used to emphasize the following word or phrase) in every way possible
completely.mnemonic: com共同 + plete=plet满，填满 + ly……地 → adv.完全地，彻底地；完整地

complex.definition: 复杂的，难解的；复合的（读作/kɑmˈplɛks/）；  n.情结；综合体，集合体（读作/ˈkɒmpleks/）
complex.definitionEn: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand
complex.sentence: He has no clue about how to solve this complex case.
complex.sentenceTrans: 他对如何解决这个复杂的案件毫无头绪。
complex.mnemonic: com共同 + plex重叠 → 全部重叠 → complex复杂的

complicate.definitionEn: to make something more difficult to do, understand or deal with
complicate.sentence: He always tended to complicate simple matters.
complicate.sentenceTrans: 他总喜欢把简单的问题复杂化。
complicate.mnemonic: com全部 + plic重叠，折叠 + ate使 → 全部重叠起来 → complicate弄复杂

complicated.definitionEn: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand
complicated.sentence: Math is a very complicated subject—it makes my head hurt.
complicated.sentenceTrans: 数学是一门非常复杂的学科，它让我很头疼。

comply.definitionEn: to obey a rule, an order, etc.
comply.sentence: We should comply with traffic regulations.
comply.sentenceTrans: 我们应该遵守交通规则。
comply.mnemonic: com共同 + ply重叠，折叠 → [观点]共同叠在一起 → 同意，答应

component.definition: 成分；零件，组成部分；  adj.组成的
component.definitionEn: one of several parts of which something is made
component.sentence: Each vaccine contains an active component that stimulates the immune response.
component.sentenceTrans: 每种疫苗都含有能激发免疫反应的活性成分。
component.mnemonic: com共同 + pon放 + ent名词后缀 → 放到一起的东西 → component成分

compose.definitionEn: to create and write (a piece of music or writing); to combine together to form a whole
compose.sentence: The man composes new songs on his keyboard.
compose.sentenceTrans: 这位男士在他的键盘上创作新歌。
compose.mnemonic: com一起 + pose放 → compose组成，构成；创作

composer.definitionEn: a person who writes music, especially classical music
composer.sentence: The composer has difficulty writing this piece.
composer.sentenceTrans: 作曲家在写这首曲子时遇到了困难。
composer.mnemonic: compos(e)创作 + er名词后缀：人 → composer作家，作曲家

composition.definitionEn: a piece of music or art, or a poem; the art of writing music
composition.sentenceTrans: 贝多芬的作曲是伟大的作品。
composition.mnemonic: com一起 + posit放 + ion名词后缀 → 放到一起 → 组合 → composition创作、作文

compound.definition: 【化学】化合物；复合物；  adj.合成的；复合的；多功能的（读作/ˈkɑːmpaʊnd/）
compound.definitionEn: a substance created when the atoms of two or more chemical elements join together
compound.sentence: The science teacher is teaching about chemical compounds.
compound.sentenceTrans: 理科老师正在课堂上讲化学化合物。
compound.mnemonic: com一起 + pound放 → compound 混合物

comprehend.sentence: I like my teacher because she makes difficult ideas easier to comprehend.
comprehend.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢我的老师，因为她把复杂的概念变得简单易懂。
comprehend.mnemonic: com全部 + prehend抓住 → 全部抓住 → comprehend理解

comprehension.sentence: The two guys must have a high level of comprehension to understand this picture.
comprehension.sentenceTrans: 这俩人肯定具有高水平的理解能力，所以才能看懂这幅画。
comprehension.mnemonic: com全部 + prehens抓住 + ion名词后缀 → 全部抓住 → comprehension理解

comprehensive.definition: 全面的，完整的；详尽的；广泛的，无所不包的；广义的；综合的
comprehensive.definitionEn: includes everything that is needed or relevant; including all, or almost all, the items, details, facts, information, etc., that may be concerned
comprehensive.sentence: She's making a comprehensive consideration of all her options.
comprehensive.sentenceTrans: 她正在全面考虑她所有的选择。
comprehensive.mnemonic: comprehens理解 + ive形容词后缀 → comprehensive有理解力的；综合的

compress.definition: 压缩；压紧，压缩，压榨（读作/kəmˈpres/）；  n.（止血、减痛等的）敷布，压布（读作/ˈkɑmˌpres/）
compress.definitionEn: to press or squeeze something together or into a smaller space; to be pressed or squeezed in this way; to reduce something and fit it into a smaller space or amount of time; to make computer files, etc. smaller so that they use less space on a disk, etc.
compress.sentence: The band decided to compress their tracks for a punchier sound.
compress.sentenceTrans: 这个乐队决定压缩他们的音轨以获得更有力的声音。
compress.mnemonic: com共同 + press压 → 一起压 → compress压缩

comprise.definitionEn: to have somebody/something as parts or members
comprise.sentence: These animals comprise most of the cat family.
comprise.sentenceTrans: 这些动物构成了猫科动物的大部分。
comprise.mnemonic: com全部 + prise拿住，抓住 → 全部抓住 → comprise包括，含有

compromise.definitionEn: an agreement made between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end
compromise.sentence: The seller made a compromise and sold the dress at 50 yuan.
compromise.sentenceTrans: 卖方做出了妥协，以50元的价格卖出了那条裙子。
compromise.mnemonic: com共同 + pro前面 + mise送，放出 → 共同承诺、遵守一项决定 → 妥协，和解

compute.definitionEn: make a mathematical calculation or computation
compute.sentence: I like using a calculator to compute.
compute.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢用计算器来计算。
compute.mnemonic: com一起 + pute计算，思考 → 算在一起 → compute计算，估算

computer.definitionEn: an electronic machine that can store and work with large amounts of information
computer.sentence: The computer's hostname and IP address are retrieved using the socket module in Python.
computer.sentenceTrans: 使用Python的socket模块获取计算机的主机名和IP地址。
computer.mnemonic: com一起 + pute估计，精简 + r → 通过计算确定 → computer计算机，电脑

conceal.sentence: I use this mask to conceal my face.
conceal.sentenceTrans: 我用面具来隐藏我的脸。
conceal.mnemonic: con加强 + ceal隐藏 → conceal隐埋，掩盖

concentrate.definition: 全神贯注于；浓缩；  n.浓缩物
concentrate.definitionEn: to give all your attention to something and not think about anything else
concentrate.sentence: He is concentrating on making his bread look perfect.
concentrate.sentenceTrans: 他正在专心地使面包看起来完美。
concentrate.mnemonic: con共同 + centr中心 + ate动词后缀 → 都在中心 → concentrate集中；浓缩

concentration.definitionEn: the ability to direct all your effort and attention on one thing, without thinking of other things
concentration.sentence: Repairing watches requires a great deal of concentration.
concentration.sentenceTrans: 修理手表需要注意力非常集中。
concentration.mnemonic: con共同 + centr中心 + ation后缀 → 都在中心 → concentration集中；浓缩

concept.definitionEn: an idea or a principle that is connected with something abstract
concept.sentence: Copernicus presented a new concept regarding the solar system.
concept.sentenceTrans: 哥白尼提出了一个有关太阳系的新概念。
concept.mnemonic: con共同 + cept掌握 → 能共同掌握的 → 概念，设计

concern.definitionEn: a feeling of worry, especially one that is shared by many people; a desire to protect and help somebody/something
concern.sentence: Hair loss is a real concern for her.
concern.sentenceTrans: 脱发的确是她所担忧的问题。
concern.mnemonic: con表强调 + cern区别 → 区分开，只关心自己的部分 → concern关系到

concerning.sentence: The book gives lots of useful information concerning Botany.
concerning.sentenceTrans: 这本书介绍了许多关于植物学的有用信息。
concerning.mnemonic: con共同 ＋ cern搞清 ＋ ing构成介词 → concerning关于

concert.sentence: I went to the concert. It was awesome.
concert.sentenceTrans: 我去了那场音乐会。真的棒极了。
concert.mnemonic: con一起 + cert歌唱 → 一起歌唱 → concert音乐会

conclude.definition: 推断出；得出结论；使结束，终止
conclude.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) to decide or believe something as a result of what you have heard or seen
conclude.sentence: The doctor concluded that she was not seriously ill, but just caught a cold.
conclude.sentenceTrans: 医生推断她没什么大病，只是感冒了而已。
conclude.mnemonic: con共同 + clude关闭 → 全部关闭 → conclude结束，总结

conclusion.definitionEn: something that you decide when you have thought about all the information connected with the situation
conclusion.sentence: She drew a conclusion from these facts.
conclusion.sentenceTrans: 她终于从这些事实中得出了一条结论。
conclusion.mnemonic: conclu表示结束 + sion为名词后缀 → conclusion结论；结束

conclusive.definition: 决定性的，无争论余地的
conclusive.definitionEn: proving something, and allowing no doubt or confusion
conclusive.sentence: The fingerprint is conclusive evidence that he is the criminal.
conclusive.sentenceTrans: 指纹是证明他是罪犯的决定性证据。
conclusive.mnemonic: con全部 + clus关闭 + ive……的 → conclusive结论性的

concrete.definition: 混凝土；  adj.具体的；  v.给 (道路等) 浇混凝土
concrete.definitionEn: building material that is made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones and water
concrete.sentence: The workers are mixing the concrete together.
concrete.sentenceTrans: 工人们正在把混凝土搅拌在一起。
concrete.mnemonic: con共同 + crete=cre制造 → 共同制造 → concrete混凝土

condemn.definitionEn: to express very strong disapproval of somebody/something, usually for moral reasons
condemn.sentence: People condemned the thief for stealing from the supermarket.
condemn.sentenceTrans: 人们谴责这个超市偷东西的小偷。
condemn.mnemonic: con表强调 + demn伤害，破坏 → condemn谴责

condition.definition: 环境，形势；状况，状态；条件；  v.使适应，使处于良好状态
condition.definitionEn: the circumstances or situation in which people live, work or do things
condition.sentence: The living conditions here are really poor.
condition.sentenceTrans: 这儿的生活条件真的很差。
condition.mnemonic: con和，一起 + dit说 +ion名词后缀 → condition状况，形势

conduct.definition: 指挥；传导；进行；  n.行为；引导（读作/ˈkɑnˌdʌkt/）
conduct.definitionEn: a person’s behaviour in a particular place or in a particular situation
conduct.sentenceTrans: 他正指挥着一支交响乐团。
conduct.mnemonic: con共同 + duct引导，带来 → 引导大家一起做→conduct指挥

conductor.definitionEn: a person who stands in front of an orchestra, a group of singers etc., and directs their performance, especially somebody who does this as a profession
conductor.sentence: The conductor is leading the band.
conductor.sentenceTrans: 乐队指挥正在指挥乐队。
conductor.mnemonic: con共同 + duct引导，带来 + or表名词，人 → 引导大家共同做事情的人 → conductor指挥家

conference.definitionEn: a large official meeting, usually lasting for a few days, at which people with the same work or interests come together to discuss their views; a meeting at which people have formal discussions
conference.sentence: He is delivering his speech at the pet owners' conference.
conference.sentenceTrans: 他正在宠物主人会议上发表演讲。
conference.mnemonic: con共同 + fer承担 + ence名词后缀 → 共同商议承担 → conference会议

confess.definition: （向神父或上帝）忏悔；承认，坦白
confess.definitionEn: to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven
confess.sentence: Father, I'm here to confess all my sins.
confess.sentenceTrans: 神父，我在此忏悔我所有的罪行。
confess.mnemonic: con全部 + fess说 → 全部说出 → confess承认，坦白

confidence.definitionEn: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of somebody/something
confidence.sentence: The student raised her hand with confidence to answer the question.
confidence.sentenceTrans: 这个学生自信地举起手回答问题。
confidence.mnemonic: con全部 + fid相信，信念 + ence名词后缀 → 全部相信 → confidence自信，信任

confident.definitionEn: feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful
confident.sentence: She is a confident woman who is certain of her views.
confident.sentenceTrans: 她是一位充满自信的女性，对自己的观点深信不疑。
confident.mnemonic: con全部 + fid相信，信念 + ent...的 → confident自信的

confidential.definitionEn: meant to be kept secret and not told to or shared with other people
confidential.sentence: He destroyed the confidential document as soon as he had finished reading it.
confidential.sentenceTrans: 他一读完机密文件就把它销毁了。
confidential.mnemonic: confident有信心的 + ial形容词后缀 → confidential表示信任的

confine.definitionEn: to keep somebody/something inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.
confine.sentence: I am confined to my jail cell.
confine.mnemonic: con加强意义 + fine界限 → confine边界；限制

confirm.definitionEn: to state or show that something is definitely true or correct, especially by providing evidence
confirm.sentence: The X-ray picture confirmed that he had broken his finger.
confirm.sentenceTrans: X光影像证实他的手指已经骨折。
confirm.mnemonic: con共同 + firm坚定 → confirm证实；坚定

conflict.definition: 冲突，矛盾；  v.冲突，抵触（读作/kənˈflɪkt/）
conflict.definitionEn: a situation in which people, groups or countries are involved in a serious disagreement or argument
conflict.sentence: Apparently there is a conflict between them.
conflict.mnemonic: con共同 + flict打 → 一起打斗 → conflict冲突

conform.definitionEn: to obey a rule, law, etc.
conform.sentence: Passport photos must conform to certain standards.
conform.sentenceTrans: 护照照片必须要符合一定的标准。
conform.mnemonic: con共同 + form形状 → conform符合，一致

confront.definitionEn: to face somebody so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation
confront.sentence: He has confronted a difficult situation.
confront.sentenceTrans: 他面临着一个困难的局面。
confront.mnemonic: con共同 + front前额 → 互相面对 → confront对抗，面临

confrontation.definitionEn: a situation in which there is an angry disagreement between people or groups who have different opinions
confrontation.sentence: They felt confrontation was the only way to solve their disagreement.
confrontation.sentenceTrans: 他们觉得对抗是解决他们之间的分歧的唯一办法。
confrontation.mnemonic: confront面对 + ation名词后缀 → confrontation面对，对峙

confuse.definitionEn: to think wrongly that somebody/something is somebody/something else; to make somebody unable to think clearly or understand something
confuse.sentence: I always confuse the girl with her twin sister.
confuse.sentenceTrans: 我一直把那个女孩和她的双胞胎姐姐搞混。
confuse.mnemonic: con一起 + fuse流 → confuse混淆，使困惑

confusion.definitionEn: a state of not being certain about what is happening, what you should do, what something means, etc.
confusion.sentence: He is in a state of confusion.
confusion.sentenceTrans: 他正处于一个混乱的状态。
confusion.mnemonic: confus使混乱 + ion名词后缀 → confusion混乱

congratulate.definitionEn: to tell somebody that you are pleased about their success or achievements; to feel pleased and proud because you have achieved something or been successful at something
congratulate.sentence: My colleagues congratulated me on the promotion.
congratulate.sentenceTrans: 我的同事们祝贺我升职了。
congratulate.mnemonic: con和，一起 + gratulate致谢 → congratulate祝贺

congratulation.definition: 祝贺（常用复数形式）；恭喜
congratulation.definitionEn: used when you want to congratulate somebody; the act of congratulating somebody
congratulation.sentence: He received many congratulations for his excellent work.
congratulation.sentenceTrans: 由于出色地完成了工作，他收到很多祝贺。
congratulation.mnemonic: con共同 + grat高兴 + u + lat拿出 + ion表示状态 → 喜事拿出来一起高兴 → congratulation祝贺，恭喜

congress.definitionEn: (in the US and some other countries) the name of the group of people who are elected to make laws, in the US consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives
congress.sentence: A congress is a legislative body that discusses national policies.
congress.sentenceTrans: 国会是讨论国家政策的立法机构。
congress.mnemonic: con共同 + gress行走 → 走到一起 → congress代表大会

connect.definitionEn: to join together two or more things; to be joined together
connect.sentence: My phone is connected to the computer.
connect.sentenceTrans: 我的手机正连接着电脑。
connect.mnemonic: con共同 + nect连结 → connect连结

connection.definitionEn: the act of connecting or the state of being connected
connection.sentence: Each one of these cables is an Internet connection.
connection.sentenceTrans: 这儿的每一条线缆都是互联网上的一次连接。
connection.mnemonic: connect连结 + ion名词后缀 → connection连结

conquer.definitionEn: to defeat somebody, especially in a competition, race, etc.;  to succeed in dealing with or controlling something
conquer.sentence: I managed to conquer the difficulties in my work.
conquer.sentenceTrans: 我成功地克服了工作上的困难。
conquer.mnemonic: con表加强 + quer寻求 → 寻求直到拥有 → conquer征服

conscious.definition: 神志清醒的；意识到的；有意的
conscious.definitionEn: aware of something (such as a fact or feeling); knowing that something exists or is happening
conscious.sentence: The patient was fully conscious hours after the operation.
conscious.sentenceTrans: 手术几小时后，这个病人完全清醒了。
conscious.mnemonic: con全部 + sci知道 + ous形容词后缀 → conscious有意识的

consciousness.definitionEn: the state of being able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening; the state of being aware of something
consciousness.sentence: His consciousness was clouded by the pain.
consciousness.sentenceTrans: 疼痛使他的意识变得模糊。
consciousness.mnemonic: conscious有意识的 + ness名词后缀 → consciousness意识，知觉

consequence.definitionEn: a result of something that has happened
consequence.sentence: The consequence of eating too much junk food is getting fat.
consequence.sentenceTrans: 吃太多垃圾食品的后果就是长胖。
consequence.mnemonic: con一起 + sequ跟随  + ence名词后缀 → 随之而来的事物 → consequence后果

consequently.sentence: She studied hard，and consequently got high marks.
consequently.sentenceTrans: 她努力学习，因此得到了高分。

conservative.definition: 保守的；保守估计的；保守党的；  n.保守者；保守党党员
conservative.definitionEn: opposed to great or sudden social change; showing that you prefer traditional styles and values
conservative.sentence: His conservative grandfather still wears traditional clothes every day.
conservative.sentenceTrans: 他那位保守的爷爷每天仍然穿着传统服装。
conservative.mnemonic: conserv保留 + a + tive形容词后缀 → conservative保守的

conserve.definition: 保护，保存；节约（读作/kənˈsɜrv/）；  n.蜜饯，果酱（读作/ˈkɑnˌsɜrv/）
conserve.definitionEn: to use as little of something as possible so that it lasts a long time
conserve.sentence: Our long-term goal is not just to protect, but to conserve the wildlife in this area for future generations.
conserve.sentenceTrans: 我们的长期目标不仅是保护，更是要为子孙后代保育这一地区的野生动物。
conserve.mnemonic: con全部 + serve服务，保持 → 全部保持下来 → 保存

consider.definitionEn: to think about (something or someone) carefully especially in order to make a choice or decision
consider.sentence: I will consider your offer, but I think I can find a better one.
consider.sentenceTrans: 我会考虑你给的职位，但我觉得我能找到一个更好的。
consider.mnemonic: con有关 + sider星座 → 对星座的观察 → consider考虑

considerable.definition: 相当大的，相当重要的；重要的；可观的
considerable.definitionEn: great in amount, size, importance, etc.
considerable.sentence: Students have considerable pressure in their final year of university.
considerable.sentenceTrans: 学生们在大学的最后一年有相当大的压力。
considerable.mnemonic: consider考虑 + able可……的 → 需要考虑的很多 → considerable相当大的

considerate.definitionEn: always thinking of other people’s wishes and feelings; careful not to hurt or upset others
considerate.sentence: As a considerate boyfriend, he took good care of her when she was ill.
considerate.sentenceTrans: 作为一个体贴的男朋友，他在她生病时无微不至地照顾她。
considerate.mnemonic: consider仔细思考，考虑 + ate...的 → 考虑周到的

consideration.definition: 考虑，思考；体贴，体谅，顾及
consideration.definitionEn: the quality of being sensitive towards others and thinking about their wishes and feelings
consideration.sentence: He has three cars as options for consideration.
consideration.sentenceTrans: 他有三辆车作为选择以供考虑。

consist.sentence: A bicycle consists of many parts.
consist.sentenceTrans: 自行车由许多部分组成。
consist.mnemonic: con共同 + sist站立 → 站到一起 → consist由…组成；与…一致

consistent.definition: 【计】一致的；始终如一的，一致的
consistent.definitionEn: always behaving in the same way, or having the same opinions, standards, etc.; happening in the same way and continuing for a period of time; in agreement with something; not contradicting something; (of an argument or a set of ideas) having different parts that all agree with each other
consistent.sentence: If the user inputs are the same, we can say that the inputs are consistent.
consistent.sentenceTrans: 如果用户的输入相同，我们可以说这些输入是一致的。
consistent.mnemonic: con共同 + sist站立 + ent形容词后缀……的 → consistent 一致的，一贯的

consistently.sentence: The company has consistently denied it had knowingly broken arms embargoes.
consistently.sentenceTrans: 这家公司一致否认自己是有意违反武器禁运规定。
consistently.mnemonic: con共同 + sist站立 + ent...的 + ly...地 → consistently一贯地；一致地

constant.definition: 持续不断的；不变的；  n.常数，恒量
constant.definitionEn: happening all the time or repeatedly
constant.sentence: The baby needs his mother's constant attention.
constant.sentenceTrans: 这个婴儿需要妈妈时刻的照料。
constant.mnemonic: con始终 + stant站立 → 始终站着 → constant不变的

constantly.sentence: He is constantly updating his blog.
constantly.sentenceTrans: 他不断地更新他的博客。
constantly.mnemonic: con始终 + stant=stand站 + ly ...地 → constant始终站着=不变的 + ly ...地 → constantly不变地

constitute.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) to be the parts that together form something; to form a group legally or officially; (not used in the progressive tenses) to be considered to be something
constitute.sentence: Bread, beef, cheese and salad constitute the perfect burger.
constitute.sentenceTrans: 面包、牛肉、芝士和沙拉组成了一个完美的汉堡。
constitute.mnemonic: con共同 + stitute=set up放 → 放到一起 → constitute构成，组成

constitution.definition: 宪法，章程；体质，体格；体质
constitution.definitionEn: the system of laws and basic principles that a state, a country or an organization is governed by
constitution.mnemonic: constitut组成 + ion名词后缀 → constitution构成；宪法

construct.definition: 建造；作（图）；  n.结构体；构想，构筑，构思；概念
construct.definitionEn: an idea or a belief that is based on various pieces of evidence which are not always true
construct.sentence: The workers are constructing a tall building.
construct.sentenceTrans: 工人们正在建造一座高楼。
construct.mnemonic: con共同 + struct建立 → 共同建立 → construct建造

construction.definitionEn: the process or method of building or making something, especially roads, buildings, bridges, etc.;  the way that something has been built or made
construction.sentence: They are doing construction at night around the Montmartre so as not to disturb daytime traffic.
construction.sentenceTrans: 为了不影响白天的交通，他们晚上在蒙马特酒店附近建造施工。

consult.definitionEn: to go to somebody for information or advice; to ask for the professional opinion of someone
consult.sentence: The couple are consulting the advisor for help.
consult.sentenceTrans: 这对夫妇正在咨询那位顾问以寻求帮助。
consult.mnemonic: con共同，一起 + sult跳跃 → 召集人们聚到一起 → consult咨询

consultant.definitionEn: a person who knows a lot about a particular subject and is employed to give advice about it to other people
consultant.sentence: The consultant will explain how we should run our business.
consultant.sentenceTrans: 顾问将会解释我们应该如何经营我们的事业。

consume.definitionEn: to use something, especially fuel, energy or time
consume.sentence: We've consumed all of the toilet paper that we bought from the supermarket.
consume.sentenceTrans: 我们把从超市买来的厕纸都用完了。

consumer.definitionEn: a person who buys goods or uses services

consumption.definitionEn: the act of using energy, food or materials; the amount used; the act of buying and using products;
consumption.sentence: We need to reduce energy consumption.
consumption.sentenceTrans: 我们需要减少能源消耗。

contact.definitionEn: to communicate with somebody, for example by telephone or letter

contact.sentenceTrans: 他们正通过视频电话来联系对方。

contain.definition: 包含，含有，容纳；自制，抑制，克制

container.definitionEn: a large metal or wooden box of a standard size in which goods are packed so that they can easily be lifted onto a ship, train, etc. to be transported

container.mnemonic: con全部 + tain握住 + er表示物 → container容器，集装箱

contemporary.definition: 同时代的；当代的，现代的；  n.同时代的人；同龄人，同辈

content.definition: 目录；  adj.满足的；  v.使满意（读作/kənˈtent/）

content.sentence: You can get a brief idea of a book from the table of contents.
content.sentenceTrans: 你可以从目录页了解一本书的大致内容。
content.mnemonic: con一起，全部 + tent拿  → 一起拿住  → content容量，引申为内容

contest.definition: 比赛，竞争（读作/ˈkɑːntest/）；  v.争夺，争论（读作/kənˈtest/）；争辩
contest.definitionEn: a competition in which people try to win something; a struggle to gain control or power

context.definitionEn: the situation in which something happens and that helps you to understand it
context.sentence: Context-oriented Programming enables the expression of behavioral variation dependent on context.
context.sentenceTrans: 以上下文为导向的程序设计能够根据上下文表达行为变化。

continent.definitionEn: one of the large land masses of the earth such as Europe, Asia or Africa
continent.sentence: The continents were closer to each other in the past.
continent.sentenceTrans: 在过去，各大洲之间的距离都比较近。
continent.mnemonic: con共同 + tin握，持 + ent名词后缀：物 → 保持连在一起的陆地 → continent大陆，陆地，大洲

continual.sentence: Learning English is a long-term continual process.
continual.sentenceTrans: 学习英语是一个长期的、连续不断的过程。
continual.mnemonic: continu(e)持续 + al形容词后缀 → continual持续的，不间断的

continue.definitionEn: to keep existing or happening without stopping; to keep doing something without stopping
continue.sentence: She continued running when the others stopped.
continue.sentenceTrans: 当其他人停下的时候，她还在继续奔跑。
continue.mnemonic: con全部 + tinu握住 + e → 全部拿住 → 做事做到尾 → continue继续

continuous.definitionEn: happening or existing for a period of time without interruption; spreading in a line or over an area without any spaces
continuous.sentence: There will be three days of continuous snow.
continuous.sentenceTrans: 接下来连续三天都会下雪。
continuous.mnemonic: continu(e)持续 + ous形容词后缀 → continuous持续不断的

contract.definition: 合同，契约（读作/ˈkɑːntrækt/）；  v.感染（疾病）；签合同；缩减
contract.sentence: I signed the contract and bought the house.
contract.sentenceTrans: 我签了合同，买下了这栋房子。
contract.mnemonic: con共同 + tract拉 → 拉到一起来 → contract合同

contradict.definitionEn: to say that something that somebody else has said is wrong, and that the opposite is true; (of statements or pieces of evidence) to be so different from each other that one of them must be wrong

contrary.definitionEn: different from something; against something; completely different in nature or direction
contrary.sentence: The lady and the man hold contrary views.
contrary.sentenceTrans: 这位女士和这位男士持有相反的意见。
contrary.mnemonic: contr反对，相反 + ary形容词后缀 → contrary相反的

contrast.definition: 差异；对照，对比；  v.对照，对比（读作/kənˈtræst/）
contrast.definitionEn: a difference between two or more people or things that you can see clearly when they are compared or put close together; the fact of comparing two or more things in order to show the differences between them; a person or thing that is clearly different from somebody/something else
contrast.sentence: There's a striking contrast between his portrayals of two different characters.
contrast.sentenceTrans: 他扮演的两个不同的角色很有反差感。
contrast.mnemonic: contra相反 + st站 → 站在对立面 → contrast对比

contribute.definitionEn: to give something, especially money or goods, to help somebody/something
contribute.sentence: Many people contribute money to help people in need.

contribution.definitionEn: something that is given to help a person, a cause, etc.
contribution.sentence: Thanks to all of you for making a contribution to our charity.

contribution.mnemonic: con 共同 + tribut 给予 + ion 抽象名词 → n. 贡献,促成作用;捐款,捐献物;(投给报刊等的)稿件

control.definition: 控制，管理；  n.控制，管理
control.definitionEn: to have power over a person, company, country, etc. so that you are able to decide what they must do or how it is run
control.sentence: The little boy can control the direction of his toy car.

convenience.definitionEn: the quality of being useful, easy or suitable for somebody

convenient.definitionEn: useful, easy or quick to do; not causing problems

convention.definition: 会议；习俗；惯例；（尤指国际性的）公约，协定

conversion.definition: 转变，转换；【化】转化，转换；（宗教或信仰的）改变

convey.definitionEn: to take, carry or transport somebody/something from one place to another

cook.definition: 厨师；  v.烹饪，烹调；煮，烧

cook.sentenceTrans: 她是个很棒的厨师。看看这些美食！

copy.definition: 副本，拷贝；复印件，复制品；  v.【计】拷贝；复制，复印

correspond.definition: 相似；相符，一致；通信；  v.类似于

correspond.sentence: The clothes of the mother and the daughter correspond closely.

correspondence.sentence: Nowadays, we can keep up correspondence with our families via our phones.

correspondent.definitionEn: a person who reports news from a particular country or on a particular subject for a newspaper or a television or radio station
correspondent.sentence: After the earthquake, the correspondent sent us the first news.
correspondent.sentenceTrans: 发生地震后，这记者发回了第一手新闻。

corresponding.definition: 相应的；符合的，一致的；通信的

cosmetic.definition: 化妆品；  adj.化妆用的，美容的；装门面的 [表不满]

cost.definition: 费用，价钱；代价，损失；  v.花费，价钱为

costly.definitionEn: costing a lot of money, especially more than you want to pay

cotton.definitionEn: a soft, white material that grows on the seeds of a tall plant and that is used to make cloth

couch.definitionEn: a long comfortable seat for two or more people to sit on

cough.definitionEn: to force out air suddenly and noisily through your throat, for example when you have a cold

could.definitionEn: used as the past tense of ‘can’

council.definitionEn: a group of people who are elected to govern an area such as a city or county

count.definition: 计算；认为；计数；  n.计数

counter.definition: 柜台；回击，反击；  v.抵制；  adv.相反地

counter.sentence: Customers pay money at the counter.

counterpart.definitionEn: a person or thing that has the same position or function as somebody/something else in a different place or situation

countless.definitionEn: too many to be counted :very many

country.definitionEn: an area of land that is controlled by its own government

countryside.definitionEn: land outside towns and cities, with fields, woods, etc.

countryside.mnemonic: country农村 + side边 → countryside乡下，农村

couple.definition: 一对；几个（人或事物）；夫妇；  v.配对，连接，结合

couple.sentence: There are a couple of rabbits sitting on the grass.

courage.definitionEn: the ability to do something dangerous, or to face pain or opposition, without showing fear

courageous.definition: 勇敢的，英勇的，有胆量的
courageous.sentence: The courageous prince is fighting against the fierce dragon.

dear.definitionEn: loved by or important to somebody
dear.sentence: "I love you so much," the father said to his dear son.
dear.sentenceTrans: “我非常爱你。”父亲对他亲爱的儿子说。

death.definitionEn: the fact of somebody dying or being killed; the state of being dead
death.sentence: Mr. Egg is crying over the death of his friend.
death.sentenceTrans: 蛋先生为他朋友的死而哭泣。

debate.definition: 辩论；争论，议论；  n.辩论；讨论，争论
debate.definitionEn: In a debate two or more speakers express opposing views and then there is often a vote on the issue; a formal discussion of an issue at a public meeting or in a parliament
debate.sentence: She was on the stage debating with the bearded man.
debate.sentenceTrans: 克莱尔和大胡子对手在台上激烈辩论。
debate.mnemonic: de否定，相反 + bat打，击 + e → 持对方相反的观点而与之进行口头上的攻击 → 反驳，辩论

debt.definitionEn: a sum of money that somebody owes; the situation of owing money, especially when you cannot pay
debt.sentence: The man is burdened with the housing debt.

decade.definitionEn: a period of ten years, especially a continuous period, such as 1910–1919 or 2000–2009
decade.sentence: People can change a lot after a decade.
decade.sentenceTrans: 十年会给人带来很大的变化。
decade.mnemonic: dec=deca十 + ade名词后缀，表状态 → 十年

decay.definitionEn: to be destroyed gradually by natural processes; to destroy something in this way
decay.sentence: These oranges have decayed on top.
decay.sentenceTrans: 这些橘子从顶部开始腐烂了。
decay.mnemonic: de向下 + cay落下 → 向下掉 → decay腐烂，衰退

deceive.definitionEn: to make (someone) believe something that is not true
deceive.sentence: The man deceives others by wearing a hilarious mask.
deceive.sentenceTrans: 这个男人用一张搞笑面具来欺骗别人。
deceive.mnemonic: de相反 + ceive拿，抓，握 → deceive欺骗

decelerate.sentence: These speed bumps force the driver to decelerate.
decelerate.sentenceTrans: 这些减速带迫使司机减速。
decelerate.mnemonic: de 降低，减少 + celer 快，速 + ate 表示使之成... → v.(使)减速

december.definitionEn: the 12th and last month of the year
december.sentenceTrans: 人们在十二月庆祝圣诞节。

decent.definition: 体面的，得体的；相当不错的；正派的
decent.definitionEn: of a good enough standard or quality
decent.sentence: The gentleman in the decent suit displayed great charm.
decent.sentenceTrans: 这位绅士衣着得体，魅力十足。
decent.mnemonic: dec合适的 + ent形容词后缀 → decent得体的

decide.definition: 对...做出抉择，决定，下决心
decide.definitionEn: to think carefully about the different possibilities that are available and choose one of them; to make an official or legal judgement; to affect the result of something; to be the reason why somebody does something
decide.sentence: It's time to decide which way to go.
decide.sentenceTrans: 是时候决定走哪条路了。
decide.mnemonic: de使…成为 + cide切 → 切下去 → 下决心 → 决定，决心

decision.definitionEn: a choice or judgement that you make after thinking and talking about what is the best thing to do
decision.sentence: Facing three paths in the forest, he made a decision to take the left one.
decision.sentenceTrans: 面对森林中的三条小道，他决定走左边那条。
decision.mnemonic: deci决定 + sion名词后缀 → decision决定

decisive.definitionEn: very important for the final result of a particular situation; able to decide something quickly and with confidence
decisive.sentence: The last judge has the decisive vote in deciding the winner.
decisive.sentenceTrans: 最后一个评委拥有选出胜利者的决定性一票。
decisive.mnemonic: deci决定 + sive形容词后缀 → decisive决定性的

declaration.definitionEn: an official or formal statement, especially about the plans of a government or an organization; the act of making an official statement about something
declaration.sentence: The leaders in the room drafted the Declaration of Independence.
declaration.sentenceTrans: 屋子里的几位领导人拟定了《独立宣言》。
declaration.mnemonic: declar宣称 + ation名词后缀 → declaration宣言

declare.definitionEn: to say something officially or publicly
declare.sentence: I now declare this meeting open.
declare.sentenceTrans: 我现在宣布本次会议开始。
declare.mnemonic: de加强 + clare（拉丁语）澄清 → declare表明，声明

decline.definition: 衰退，衰落；  v.拒绝，谢绝；婉言拒绝，谢绝；下降；衰退
decline.definitionEn: a continuous decrease in the number, value, quality, etc. of something
decline.sentence: The world economy is on a decline.

decorate.definitionEn: to make something more attractive by putting things on it
decorate.sentence: They are decorating the Christmas tree.
decorate.sentenceTrans: 佩妮和莱纳德正一起装饰圣诞树。
decorate.mnemonic: decor装饰 + ate动词后缀 → decorate装修，装潢

decoration.definitionEn: a thing that makes something look more attractive on special occasions
decoration.sentence: There are many pretty decorations on the Christmas tree.
decoration.sentenceTrans: 圣诞树上有许多漂亮的装饰品。
decoration.mnemonic: decor装饰 + ation表示行为、情况、状态、过程、结果 → 装饰，装潢；装饰品；奖章

decrease.definitionEn: to become or make something become smaller in size, number, etc.
decrease.sentence: Our sales have decreased for the last two years, and now we're out of money.
decrease.sentenceTrans: 过去两年我们的销售额都在减少，现在我们没钱了。
decrease.mnemonic: de向下 + crease增长 → 向下增加 → 减少

dedicate.definition: 致力于，献出（全部时间、精力等）
dedicate.definitionEn: to give a lot of your time and effort to a particular activity or purpose because you think it is important; to say at the beginning of a book, a piece of music or a performance that you are doing it for somebody, as a way of thanking them or showing respect; to hold an official ceremony to say that a building or an object has a special purpose or is special to the memory of a particular person
dedicate.sentence: The teacher has dedicated his life to education.
dedicate.sentenceTrans: 这位老师把他的一生献给了教育事业。
dedicate.mnemonic: de加强 + dic说 + ate使，造成 → 再说 → 努力献身

deed.definitionEn: (formal, literary) a thing that somebody does that is usually very good or very bad
deed.sentence: The kind man did many good deeds for people.
deed.sentenceTrans: 这个善良的男人为人们做了很多好事。

deem.definitionEn: (not usually used in the progressive tenses) to have a particular opinion about something

deep.definition: 深的；  adv.深深地；  n.深处
deep.definitionEn: having a large distance from the top or surface to the bottom
deep.sentence: No one has found the ship's treasure because it lies deep under the sea.
deep.sentenceTrans: 没有人能找到船里的宝藏，因为它处于大海中很深的地方。

deeply.definitionEn: in a way that is very complete, extreme, strongly felt, etc. :in a deep way
deeply.sentence: I care deeply for my new baby.
deeply.sentenceTrans: 我深深地牵挂着我刚出生的小宝宝。
deeply.mnemonic: deep深的 + ly副词后缀 → deeply深刻地，浓浓地

deer.definitionEn: an animal with long legs, that eats grass, leaves, etc. and can run fast. Most male deer have antlers
deer.sentence: The girl with food was immediately surrounded by deer.
deer.sentenceTrans: 拿着食物的小女孩被小鹿们迅速围住了。

defeat.definition: 打败，击败，战胜；  n.挫败；失败，战败
defeat.definitionEn: to win against somebody in a war, competition, sports game, etc.
defeat.sentence: Our team defeated them in the final game.
defeat.sentenceTrans: 我们的球队在决赛中击败了他们。
defeat.mnemonic: de向下 + feat做，制作 → 做下去 → 打下去 → defeat打败，摧毁

defence.definitionEn: the act of defending someone or something from attack
defence.sentence: The iron fence built by the shepherd is a great defence against the wolf.
defence.sentenceTrans: 牧羊人建造的铁栅栏可以很好地防御狼。
defence.mnemonic: de从...离开 + fen打，打击 + ce表名词 → defence防御

defend.definition: 保卫，防守；为……辩护，为……辩解
defend.sentence: The dog defends its friend with a knife and shield.
defend.sentenceTrans: 这只小狗用刀和盾保护它的朋友。
defend.mnemonic: de去掉 + fend打击 → 打退敌人 → defend保卫，防御

defendant.definitionEn: the person in a trial who is accused of committing a crime, or who is being sued by another person
defendant.sentence: The defendant pleaded not guilty to all charges.
defendant.sentenceTrans: 被告人对所有指控都表示无罪。
defendant.mnemonic: de使成… + fend打击 + ant表示人→ 成为被打击的人→ 被告

defender.definition: 防卫者，拥护者，辩护者，【运动】卫冕者
defender.definitionEn: a player who must stop the other team from scoring in games such as football (soccer ), hockey, etc.; a person who defends and believes in protecting something
defender.sentence: This knight is the defender of the King's treasure.
defender.sentenceTrans: 这个骑士是国王的宝藏的守护者。
defender.mnemonic: de否定，相反 + fend=strike，表示“打击” + er[名词后缀]，行为的主动者 → defender防卫者，拥护者

defense.definitionEn: the act of defending someone or something from attack
defense.sentence: The iron fence built by the shepherd is a great defense against the wolf.
defense.sentenceTrans: 牧羊人建造的铁栅栏可以有效地防狼。
defense.mnemonic: de去掉 + fens打击 + e → 去掉打击 → 打退敌人 → defense保卫

deficiency.definitionEn: the state of not having, or not having enough of, something that is essential
deficiency.sentence: Sleep deficiency may cause dark circles under the eyes.
deficiency.sentenceTrans: 睡眠不足可能会导致黑眼圈。
deficiency.mnemonic: de不 + fic做 + iency表名词 → 做得不够 → 缺陷

deficit.definitionEn: the amount by which money spent or owed is greater than money earned in a particular period of time
deficit.sentence: The company was in a financial deficit in 2018.
deficit.sentenceTrans: 该公司在2018年出现了亏损。
deficit.mnemonic: de不 ＋ fic做 ＋ it名词后缀，表抽象名词 → 做得不够 → deficit亏空

define.definition: 给（词、短语等）下定义；界定，解释
define.definitionEn: to say or explain what the meaning of a word or phrase is
define.sentence: Many believe achieving success defines the American Dream.
define.sentenceTrans: 许多人认为“取得成功”能定义美国梦。
define.mnemonic: de加强语意 + fine边界 → define下定义

definite.definitionEn: sure or certain; unlikely to change
definite.sentence: The police found definite proof that he committed the crime.
definite.sentenceTrans: 警方已经掌握明确证据，可以证明是他实施了犯罪。
definite.mnemonic: defin明确 + ite形容词后缀 → definite明确的

definition.definitionEn: an explanation of the meaning of a word or phrase, especially in a dictionary; the act of stating the meanings of words and phrases
definition.sentence: The dictionary contains the definition of thousands of words.
definition.sentenceTrans: 字典包含了成千上万个词的释义。
definition.mnemonic: de使…成为 + fin界限 + ition名词后缀 → 划出界限 → 定义

degree.definitionEn: the qualification obtained by students who successfully complete a university or college course; a unit for measuring temperature
degree.sentence: I finally got my degree after four years of studying.
degree.sentenceTrans: 经过四年的学习，我终于拿到了学位。
degree.mnemonic: de下面 + gree一步，一个台阶 → 一个位置和阶段 → degree学位

delay.definition: 延误，延迟；磨蹭，使迟到；耽误；  n.延期，耽搁；耽搁（的时间）
delay.definitionEn: to make somebody late or force them to do something more slowly
delay.sentence: His flight is delayed because of bad weather.
delay.sentenceTrans: 他的航班由于恶劣的天气晚点了。
delay.mnemonic: de从...离开 + lay留下，停留 → delay延迟

delegate.definition: 【财】委派；授权（读作/ˈdɛləˌgeɪt/）；  n.代表（读作/ˈdɛləgɪt/）
delegate.definitionEn: to give (control, responsibility, authority, etc.) to someone; to entrust duties, rights, etc. to sb
delegate.sentence: Tasks neither urgent nor important should be delegated or binned.
delegate.sentenceTrans: 即不紧急也不重要的任务可以委派他人处理或者直接舍弃。
delegate.mnemonic: de使…成为，加强 + leg法律 + ate动词后缀 → 加强法律 → delegate授权

delete.definitionEn: to remove something that has been written or printed, or that has been stored on a computer
delete.sentence: Remember to delete your search history.
delete.sentenceTrans: 记得及时删除你的搜索记录。

deliberate.definitionEn: done on purpose rather than by accident
deliberate.sentence: The boy made a deliberate attempt to annoy the girl.
deliberate.sentenceTrans: 男孩故意要惹女孩生气。
deliberate.mnemonic: de否定 + liber自由 + ate……的 → 不是任意而为 → deliberate故意的

deliberately.definition: 故意地；慢条斯理地，从容不迫地
deliberately.definitionEn: done in a way that was planned, not by chance
deliberately.sentence: Why does he deliberately try to make other people fall over?
deliberately.sentenceTrans: 他为什么故意绊倒别人？
deliberately.mnemonic: deliberate故意的 + ly……地 → deliberate不是任意而为=故意的

delicate.definition: 易碎的，脆弱的；精美的，精致的；（人）娇弱的，体弱多病的
delicate.sentence: The vase is delicate and should be packed with care.
delicate.mnemonic: de远离 + licate诱惑，吸引 → 易损坏但有吸引力的 → delicate精致的，易碎的

delicious.definitionEn: having a very pleasant taste or smell; extremely pleasant or enjoyable
delicious.sentence: The rice noodles my brother is cooking look so delicious!
delicious.sentenceTrans: 我哥哥煮的米粉看起来真美味！
delicious.mnemonic: de再 + lic诱惑 + ious表形容词 → 再引诱的 → delicious美味的，可口的

delight.definition: 快乐；高兴事；  v.使快乐
delight.sentence: To the delight of the children, the ice cream truck stopped right in front of the house.
delight.sentenceTrans: 令孩子们万分高兴的是，冰淇淋车正好停在房子前面。
delight.mnemonic: de完全地 + light诱惑 → 完全将其迷惑住 → delight使高兴

delighted.definitionEn: extremely pleased and excited about something
delighted.sentence: She is delighted that she finished her work.
delighted.sentenceTrans: 她很高兴她完成了工作。
delighted.mnemonic: de加强意义 + light光明 + ed…的 → 阳光的 → delighted欣喜的，快乐的

deliver.definition: 递送，交付；发表（演讲）；分娩；传达
deliver.definitionEn: to take goods, letters, etc. to the person or people they have been sent to; to do what you promised to do or what you are expected to do
deliver.sentence: The man delivers the packages to the woman.
deliver.sentenceTrans: 男人把包裹送到这位女士的手上。
deliver.mnemonic: de离开 + liver自由 → deliver投递，投送

delivery.definitionEn: the act of taking goods, letters, etc. to the people they have been sent to; the process of giving birth to a baby
delivery.sentence: The delivery service aims to deliver each package as quickly as possible.
delivery.sentenceTrans: 投递服务旨在尽快派送每个包裹。
delivery.mnemonic: de完全 + liver释放 + y形容词后缀 → 快递;投递;交付;分娩

demand.definition: 强烈要求，坚决要求；  n.需求，需要
demand.definitionEn: to ask for something very firmly; to need something in order to be done successfully
demand.sentence: He has always demanded some unreasonable things from his children.
demand.sentenceTrans: 他总是向子女们提出一些无理的要求。
demand.mnemonic: de加强 + mand命令 → demand要求

democracy.definition: 民主制度；民主国家；民主主义；民众
democracy.definitionEn: a system of government in which all the people of a country can vote to elect their representatives
democracy.sentence: Voting is an important part of democracy.
democracy.sentenceTrans: 投票是民主制度的一个重要部分。
democracy.mnemonic: demo人民 + cracy统治 → democracy民主政治

democratic.definition: 民主的，民主政体的，民主党的
democratic.definitionEn: (of a country, state, system, etc.) controlled by representatives who are elected by the people of a country; connected with this system; based on the principle that all members of society are equal rather than divided by money or social class; connected with the Democratic Party in the US
democratic.sentence: In a democratic society, everyone has the right to vote.
democratic.sentenceTrans: 在一个民主的国家，人民有权投票选举。
democratic.mnemonic: demo人民 + cr + atic…的 → 民主的，民主主义的；民主政体的

demonstrate.definition: 演示，展示；（用实例、实验）论证；示范；示威
demonstrate.definitionEn: to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence
demonstrate.sentence: The salesman demonstrates how the device works on a watermelon.
demonstrate.sentenceTrans: 推销员在演示怎么操作切瓜神器。
demonstrate.mnemonic: de加强 + monstr指出 + ate动词后缀 → 特别指出 → demonstrate证明

demonstration.definitionEn: a public meeting or march at which people show that they are protesting against or supporting somebody/something
demonstration.sentence: He gave a demonstration of how to use the new smartphone.
demonstration.sentenceTrans: 他对如何使用新的智能手机进行了演示。
demonstration.mnemonic: de加强 + monstr显示 + ation表名词 → 证明；示威游行

dense.definitionEn: containing a lot of people, things, plants, etc. with little space between them; difficult to see through
dense.sentence: This area is very dense with so many buildings everywhere.
dense.sentenceTrans: 这是一片密集的区域，到处都是建筑物。

density.definitionEn: the quality of being dense; the degree to which something is dense
density.sentence: The high density of buildings makes the city so crowded.
density.sentenceTrans: 这个城市的建筑密度很高，所以城市也非常拥挤。
density.mnemonic: dens稠密的 + ity名词后缀表性质 → 稠密 → density稠度，密度

dentist.definitionEn: a person whose job is to take care of people’s teeth
dentist.sentence: The dentist explained the procedure to the patient before starting the treatment.
dentist.sentenceTrans: 牙科医生在开始治疗前向病人解释了整个过程。
dentist.mnemonic: dent牙齿 + ist人 → dentist牙科医生

deny.definitionEn: to say that something is not true; to refuse to admit or accept something; to refuse to allow somebody to have something that they want or ask for
deny.sentence: The little boy denied breaking the window.
deny.sentenceTrans: 小男孩否认是他打破了窗户。
deny.mnemonic: de向下 + ny=neg否决 → deny否认

depart.definitionEn: to leave a place, especially to start a trip
depart.sentence: The steamship just departed from the dock.
depart.sentenceTrans: 这艘蒸汽轮船刚刚离开了港口。

department.definitionEn: a section of a large organization such as a government, business, university, etc.
department.sentence: Our company consists of three departments.
department.sentenceTrans: 我们公司由三个部门组成。
department.mnemonic: de加强意义 + part部分 + ment名词后缀 → 一部分 → department部门，系

departure.definitionEn: the act of leaving a place; an example of this; a plane, train, etc. leaving a place at a particular time
departure.sentence: His departure from home made his family sad.
departure.sentenceTrans: 他离开了家，这使其家人感到悲伤。
departure.mnemonic: depart出发 + ure名词后缀 → departure离开，出发

depend.definitionEn: to rely on somebody/something and be able to trust them; (not usually used in the progressive tenses) to need money, help, etc. from somebody/something else for a particular purpose; (not used in the progressive tenses) to be affected or decided by something
depend.sentence: Sometimes people have to depend on others for help.
depend.sentenceTrans: 有时候，人们不得不依靠他人的帮助。
depend.mnemonic: de加强 + pend挂  → 挂在...上面  → depend依靠；依赖

dependent.definition: 依赖的；  n.依赖他人者
dependent.definitionEn: needing somebody/something in order to survive or be successful
dependent.sentence: Ever since the accident, she's been dependent on her son to help her get around.
dependent.sentenceTrans: 那场车祸后，她的行动就一直依赖她儿子。
dependent.mnemonic: depend依靠 + ent形容词后缀 → dependent依靠的

deposit.definitionEn: to put money into a bank account; to put or lay somebody/something down in a particular place
deposit.sentence: I deposit money in my piggy bank when I get money.
deposit.sentenceTrans: 当我有钱时我会往我的存钱罐里存钱。

depress.definition: 使沮丧；压下，压低；使萧条；  v.降低(价格)
depress.definitionEn: to make somebody sad and without enthusiasm or hope
depress.sentence: Life depresses him so he drinks some liquor.
depress.sentenceTrans: 生活使他感到沮丧，于是他借酒消愁。
depress.mnemonic: de向下 + press压 → depress压下；使沮丧

depressed.sentence: He felt very depressed when he got fired.
depressed.sentenceTrans: 被解雇时，他感到非常沮丧。
depressed.mnemonic: de向下 + press挤压 + ed形容词后缀 → 向下挤压的 → depressed感到压抑的

depressing.definitionEn: causing someone to feel sad or without hope :causing depression
depressing.sentence: The lonely woman found tea time to be very depressing without anyone to talk to.
depressing.sentenceTrans: 没有人和她谈话，这位孤独老妇人觉得下午茶变得令人沮丧。
depressing.mnemonic: de使成… + press挤压 + ing...的 → depressing压抑的；使人沮丧的

depression.definition: 抑郁，沮丧；不景气，萧条（期）；洼地，凹陷
depression.definitionEn: a medical condition in which a person feels very sad and anxious and often has physical symptoms such as being unable to sleep, etc.; the state of feeling very sad and without hope
depression.sentence: My cat sank into a deep depression since I had a boyfriend.
depression.sentenceTrans: 自从我有了男朋友，我的猫就陷入了深深的抑郁之中。
depression.mnemonic: de向下 + press挤压 + ion名词后缀 → 向下挤压 → 沮丧；萧条

deprive.definitionEn: to prevent somebody from having or doing something, especially something important
deprive.sentence: The baby cried as his friend deprived him of the toy.
deprive.sentenceTrans: 这个婴儿哭了，因为他的朋友抢走了他的玩具。
deprive.mnemonic: de去掉 + prive单个 → 从个人身边拿走 → 剥夺，夺去

depth.definitionEn: the distance from the top or surface to the bottom of something
depth.sentence: These fish dived to a depth of 150 meters.
depth.sentenceTrans: 这些鱼潜至水下150米深处。
depth.mnemonic: dep深的 + th名词后缀 → depth深度

derive.definitionEn: to come or develop from something
derive.sentence: The English word "teacher" derives from the root word "teach".
derive.sentenceTrans: 英文单词“teacher”一词来源于词根“teach”。
derive.mnemonic: de离开 + riv河流 + e → 派生，得出

describe.definitionEn: if you describe a person, object, event, or situation, you say what they are like or what happened
describe.sentence: She described her missing child to a passer-by.
describe.sentenceTrans: 她向一位路人描述她走失的孩子的模样。
describe.mnemonic: de表加强 + scribe写 → describe描写

description.definitionEn: a piece of writing or speech that says what somebody/something is like; the act of writing or saying in words what somebody/something is like
description.sentence: The policeman asked the girl to give a description of the criminal.
description.sentenceTrans: 警察让女孩描述一下犯罪嫌疑人的样子。
description.mnemonic: de向下 + script写 + ion表名词 → 写下来 → description描写

desert.definition: 荒漠，沙漠（读作/ˈdezərt/）；  v.离弃（读作/dɪˈzɜːt/）
desert.definitionEn: a large area of land that has very little water and very few plants growing on it. Many deserts are covered by sand.
desert.sentence: I finally found water in the desert.
desert.sentenceTrans: 我终于在沙漠里找到水了。
desert.mnemonic: de分开 + sert加入，插入 → 不再加入 → desert离开

deserve.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) if somebody/something deserves something, it is right that they should have it, because of the way they have behaved or because of what they are
deserve.sentence: She deserves a pat on the back for all her hard work.
deserve.sentenceTrans: 她工作兢兢业业，值得嘉许。
deserve.mnemonic: de加强语气 + serve为…服务 → deserve值得，应得

design.definition: 设计（方案）；  v.设计，构思
design.definitionEn: the general arrangement of the different parts of something that is made, such as a building, book, machine, etc.
design.sentence: The design for the house looks great - now let's build it!
design.sentenceTrans: 这个房子的设计很棒，现在我们来建造它吧！
design.mnemonic: de使…成为，加强 ＋ sign写，做标志 → design设计，计划

designer.definitionEn: a person whose job is to decide how things such as clothes, furniture, tools, etc. will look or work by making drawings, plans or patterns
designer.sentence: I am a fashion designer; I design clothes for women.
designer.sentenceTrans: 我是一个服装设计师，专门设计女装。
designer.mnemonic: design设计 + er名词后缀：人 → designer设计师

desirable.definition: 令人向往的；理想的，值得拥有的；令人满意的
desirable.definitionEn: that you would like to have or do; worth having or doing
desirable.sentence: Doctors are seen as a high status and desirable profession.
desirable.sentenceTrans: 医生被视为社会地位高、令人向往的职业。
desirable.mnemonic: desir=desirede渴望 + able能……的 → 值得要的

desire.definition: 渴望；欲望；愿望；要求；  v.有希望，期望，愿望；  v.希望，渴望；请求，要求
desire.definitionEn: a strong wish to have or do something
desire.sentence: The cat is filled with the desire to eat the fish.
desire.sentenceTrans: 这只猫心里充满了想要吃掉这条鱼的渴望。

desk.definitionEn: a piece of furniture like a table, usually with drawers in it, that you sit at to read, write, work, etc.
desk.sentence: There is an empty desk right here.

despair.definition: 绝望；  v.绝望，感到无望
despair.definitionEn: the feeling of having lost all hope
despair.sentence: "All of my money is gone!" the man cried in despair.
despair.sentenceTrans: “我的钱全没了！”这个男人绝望地哭喊道。
despair.mnemonic: de去掉 + spair希望 → despair 绝望

desperate.definition: 绝望的；拼命的；极需要的，渴望的
desperate.definitionEn: very sad and upset because of having little or no hope; feeling or showing despair
desperate.sentence: She made a desperate cry for help in the fire.
desperate.sentenceTrans: 她在大火中发出绝望的呼喊。
desperate.mnemonic: de去掉 + sper希望 + ate动词后缀 → 去掉希望 → desperate绝望的

despite.definitionEn: used to show that something happened or is true although something else might have happened to prevent it
despite.sentence: Despite the windy day, the reporter was still working outdoors.
despite.sentenceTrans: 尽管风很大，这名记者仍然在户外工作。
despite.mnemonic: de向下 + spite看向，观察  → despite尽管

dessert.definitionEn: sweet food eaten at the end of a meal
dessert.sentence: I’d like to have some dessert with a cup of tea after dinner.
dessert.sentenceTrans: 吃完晚饭后，我还想吃些甜点、喝杯茶。
dessert.mnemonic: des去掉，取消 + sert服务 → 停止正餐服务，上甜点 → dessert甜点

destination.definitionEn: a place to which somebody/something is going or being sent
destination.sentence: The destination of their journey was the Western Heaven.
destination.sentenceTrans: 他们此行的目的地是西天。
destination.mnemonic: de向下 + stin站立 + ation名词后缀 → 下一个立足点 → destination目的地，目标

destroy.definitionEn: to damage something so badly that it no longer exists, works, etc.; to kill an animal deliberately, usually because it is sick or not wanted
destroy.sentence: My computer was completely destroyed in the fire.
destroy.sentenceTrans: 我的电脑被大火毁尽了。
destroy.mnemonic: de向下，表否定 + stroy建立 → destroy毁灭

destruction.definitionEn: the act of destroying something; the process of being destroyed
destruction.sentence: The war caused the destruction of the city.
destruction.sentenceTrans: 这场战争毁了整座城市。
destruction.mnemonic: destruct破坏 + ion名词后缀 → destruction破坏

detail.definition: 细节；  v.详细说明；派遣
detail.definitionEn: a small individual fact or item; a less important fact or item; the small facts or features of something, when you consider them all together
detail.sentence: When the leaf is seen up close, you can see a lot of fine details.
detail.sentenceTrans: 近距离看树叶时，你可以看到很多细节。
detail.mnemonic: de向下 + tail切割 → detail 细节

detailed.definitionEn: developed or executed with care and in minute detail
detailed.sentenceTrans: 这是一份详细的路线图。

detect.definitionEn: to discover or notice the presence of (something that is hidden or hard to see, hear, taste, etc.)
detect.sentence: The dog can detect drugs with its nose.
detect.sentenceTrans: 狗可以用它的鼻子探测毒品。
detect.mnemonic: de打开 + tect遮盖 → detect发觉，侦查

detection.definitionEn: the process of detecting something; the fact of being detected
detection.sentence: Good eyes are required for detection of tiny objects.
detection.sentenceTrans: 对微小物体的侦查需要好眼力。
detection.mnemonic: detect发觉 + ion表名词 → detection发觉

detective.definitionEn: a police officer whose job is to find information about crimes that have occurred and to catch criminals
detective.sentence: A detective must know how to see through people's lies.
detective.sentenceTrans: 侦探必须知道如何看穿人们的谎言。
detective.mnemonic: de相反 + tect掩盖 + ive...的 → 无法掩盖 → 发现 → detective侦探；侦探的

determination.definitionEn: a quality that makes you continue trying to do or achieve something even when it is difficult
determination.sentence: His determination helps him lose weight through exercise.
determination.sentenceTrans: 他的决心帮助他通过运动减肥。

determine.definition: 下决心；做决定；确定，测定
determine.definitionEn: to discover the facts about something
determine.sentence: The chubby dog is determined to lose weight.
determine.sentenceTrans: 这只胖狗下定决心要减肥。
determine.mnemonic: de加强动作 + termin界限 + e → 加强界限 → determine下决心

develop.definition: 发展，壮大；逐渐形成，逐渐养成
develop.definitionEn: to gradually grow or become bigger, more advanced, stronger, etc.; to make something do this; to think of or produce a new idea, product, etc. and make it successful; to begin to have something such as a disease or a problem; to start to affect somebody/something; to start to have a skill, ability, quality, etc. that becomes better and stronger; to become better and stronger
develop.sentence: The city's road system is developing very rapidly.
develop.sentenceTrans: 这座城市的道路系统发展地非常迅速。
develop.mnemonic: de不 + velop盖上 → 不阻止，不掩盖 → develop发展

development.definitionEn: the gradual growth of something so that it becomes more advanced, stronger, etc.
development.sentence: This picture shows the development of phones over time.
development.sentenceTrans: 这张图展示了电话发展变化的历程。
development.mnemonic: develop发展 + ment名词后缀 → development发展

device.definition: 【计】设备；装置，设备；手段，计谋；方法
device.definitionEn: an object or a piece of equipment that has been designed to do a particular job; a bomb or weapon that will explode
device.sentence: The AI algorithm runs on a powerful machine learning device.
device.sentenceTrans: AI算法在一个功能强大的机器学习设备上运行。

devise.definitionEn: to invent something new or a new way of doing something
devise.sentence: They devised a plan for their company's future.
devise.sentenceTrans: 他们制定了公司未来发展计划。
devise.mnemonic: de加强意义 + vis =separate分开 + e → 使分开的部件组装成新的发明 → devise设计，发明

devote.definition: 献身于，专心致力于，把……专用于
devote.definitionEn: to give entirely to a specific person, activity, or cause
devote.sentence: The chicken jumped into the pot and devoted his life to us.
devote.sentenceTrans: 这只鸡跳进锅里，为我们献出了生命。
devote.mnemonic: de加强 + vot发誓 + e → 拼命发誓，以命起誓 → devote将…奉献，致力于

devotion.definitionEn: the action of spending a lot of time or energy on something
devotion.sentence: Many people show great devotion to their professions, such as doctors, scientists, and soldiers.
devotion.sentenceTrans: 许多人展示了他们对职业的非凡投入，比如医生、科学家以及士兵。
devotion.mnemonic: devot献身 + ion名词后缀 → devotion献身，投入

diagnose.definitionEn: to say exactly what an illness or the cause of a problem is
diagnose.sentence: The doctor used several tests to diagnose the patient’s condition.
diagnose.sentenceTrans: 医生用了几项检查来诊断患者的病情。
diagnose.mnemonic: dia穿过，二者之间 + gnos知道 + e → diagnose诊断(疾病)，对（病人）下诊断结论

diagram.definitionEn: a simple drawing using lines to explain where something is, how something works, etc.
diagram.sentence: The diagram in this textbook shows how the water cycle works.
diagram.sentenceTrans: 这本教科书中的图解展示了水循环的过程。
diagram.mnemonic: dia穿过，二者之间 + gram写，图 → 交叉对着画 → 图表

dial.definition: 拨（电话号码）；  n.仪表盘
dial.definitionEn: to use a telephone by pushing buttons or turning the dial to call a number
dial.sentence: I am dialing a number on my phone.
dial.sentenceTrans: 我正在手机上拨电话号码。

dialect.definitionEn: a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations
dialect.sentence: They come from two different areas, so they speak different dialects.
dialect.sentenceTrans: 他们来自两个不同的地区，所以他们说不同的方言。
dialect.mnemonic: dia在…之间 + lect讲，读 → 在一部分人之间说 → dialect方言

dialog.definitionEn: conversations in a book, play, or film/movie; a formal discussion between two groups or countries, especially when they are trying to solve a problem, end a disagreement, etc.
dialog.sentence: The two sides entered into a peace dialog.
dialog.sentenceTrans: 双方进行了一次和平对话。
dialog.mnemonic: dia穿过，之间 + log说话 → dialog对话

dialogue.definitionEn: a conversation between two or more people
dialogue.sentence: These two women are having a dialogue about their babies.
dialogue.sentenceTrans: 这两个女人在谈论她们的小孩。
dialogue.mnemonic: dia穿过，二者之间 + logue话 → 对着说话 → dialogue对话

diameter.definitionEn: a straight line going from one side of a circle or any other round object to the other side, passing through the centre
diameter.sentence: The worker was measuring the lumber's diameter.
diameter.sentenceTrans: 工人正在测量木材的直径。
diameter.mnemonic: dia穿过，二者之间 + meter测量 → 穿过两者之间测量 → diameter直径

diamond.definitionEn: a clear precious stone of pure carbon, the hardest substance known. Diamonds are used in jewellery and also in industry, especially for cutting glass.
diamond.mnemonic: diam=adam强硬的，不屈服的 + ond → 坚硬的石头 → 钻石

diary.definitionEn: a book in which you can write down the experiences you have each day, your private thoughts, etc.
diary.sentence: The girl keeps a diary every day.
diary.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩每天都写日记。
diary.mnemonic: di日子 + ary表名词 → diary日记
