dictation.definitionEn: the act of speaking words that someone writes down or that a machine records
dictation.sentence: He asked her to write down his dictation.
dictation.sentenceTrans: 他请她把自己的口述写下来。
dictation.mnemonic: dictat口授 + ion名词后缀 → 用嘴说的 → dictation口授，命令

dictionary.definitionEn: a reference book that contains words listed in alphabetical order and that gives information about the words' meanings, forms, pronunciations, etc.
dictionary.sentence: Use this dictionary if there are any words you don't know.
dictionary.sentenceTrans: 如果有不认识的单词，用这本词典查查。
dictionary.mnemonic: dict说话，断言 + ion行为 + ary表名词 → 措词的书 → dictionary字典

die.sentence: The leader lying on the ground died during the fight.
die.sentenceTrans: 杰出的三代火影在保卫木叶村的斗争中死去了。

differ.sentence: The red paper guy differs from the others in color.
differ.sentenceTrans: 这个红纸人的颜色不同于其他人。
differ.mnemonic: di分开 + ffer运行 → differ不同

difference.sentence: Their height difference is easy to see.
difference.sentenceTrans: 他们的身高差显而易见。
difference.mnemonic: differ不同 + ence名词后缀 → difference差异

different.definitionEn: not the same as somebody/something; not like somebody/something else
different.sentence: The red tomato looks so different from others.
different.sentenceTrans: 红色的西红柿看起来与其他的如此不同。
different.mnemonic: differ相异 ＋ ent...的 → 相异的 → different不同的

difficult.definitionEn: not easy; needing effort or skill to do or to understand
difficult.sentence: It is difficult for her to carry such a huge stone.
difficult.sentenceTrans: 让她搬起这么大的一块石头实在太难了。
difficult.mnemonic: dif不 + fic做 + ult表名词 → 不好做 → difficult困难的

difficulty.definitionEn: a problem; a thing or situation that causes problems
difficulty.sentence: He is having difficulty holding up the board.
difficulty.sentenceTrans: 他很难一直举着这块木板。
difficulty.mnemonic: difficult困难的 + y表名词 → difficulty困难

dig.definition: 挖掘，掘出；看中；  n.挖苦
dig.definitionEn: to make a hole in the ground or to move soil from one place to another using your hands, a tool or a machine
dig.sentence: The dog is digging a hole.

digest.definition: 消化；领会，理解（读作/daɪˈdʒest/）；  n.摘要（读作/ˈdaɪˌdʒest/）
digest.definitionEn: a short report containing the most important facts of a longer report or piece of writing; a collection of short reports
digest.sentence: Many parts of your body are involved in digesting food.
digest.sentenceTrans: 你身体中有很多的部位共同参与了食物的消化过程。
digest.mnemonic: di分离 + gest执行 → digest消化

digital.definitionEn: using a system of receiving and sending information as a series of the numbers one and zero, showing that an electronic signal is there or is not there
digital.sentence: This is a black digital stopwatch.
digital.sentenceTrans: 这是一块黑色的数码秒表。

dilemma.definitionEn: a situation which makes problems, often one in which you have to make a very difficult choice between things of equal importance
dilemma.sentence: The man swinging on the rope found himself in a dilemma.
dilemma.sentenceTrans: 在绳子上摇摆的男人发现自己进退两难。
dilemma.mnemonic: di两个，双 + lemma争论 → 二种争论 → dilemma进退两难

dim.definitionEn: not bright or clear; where you cannot see well because there is not much light
dim.sentence: This lamp gives out a dim light.
dim.sentenceTrans: 这盏灯发出一束微弱的亮光。

dimension.definitionEn: a measurement in space, for example the height, width or length of something
dimension.sentence: These different shapes have three dimensions.
dimension.sentenceTrans: 这些不同的图形都是三维的。
dimension.mnemonic: di=dis不同的方向 + men测量 + ion名词后缀 → dimension维度

dine.sentence: After finally meeting again, they sat down to dine.
dine.sentenceTrans: 终于再次见面后，他们坐下来一起吃饭。

dinner.definition: 正餐，主餐，（现通例指）晚餐
dinner.definitionEn: the main meal of the day, eaten either in the middle of the day or in the evening
dinner.sentence: The family enjoyed a big dinner.
dinner.sentenceTrans: 全家人享受了丰盛的晚餐。
dinner.mnemonic: di打破，与...相反 + nner空腹，饥饿 → 打破饥饿的状态吃大餐 → dinner正餐，晚餐

diplomat.definitionEn: a person whose job is to represent his or her country in a foreign country, for example, in an embassy
diplomat.sentence: The diplomat represents his country to make agreements with other countries.
diplomat.sentenceTrans: 外交官代表他的国家与他国达成协议。
diplomat.mnemonic: diploma公文 + t=ate表名词 → diplomate的简化 → diplomat外交官，外交家

direct.definitionEn: happening or done without involving other people, actions, etc. in between; going in the straightest line between two places without stopping or changing direction
direct.sentence: He used his hands to direct the person the right way.
direct.sentenceTrans: 关谷伸出双手为迪诺哥引路。
direct.mnemonic: di使...变成 + rect直 → direct直接；直接的

direction.definition: 方向，方位；指导，管理；指引，指示
direction.definitionEn: the general position a person or thing moves or points towards
direction.sentence: There are two different directions, left and right.
direction.sentenceTrans: 这里有左和右两个不同的方向。
direction.mnemonic: di通过 + rect正，直 + ion名词后缀 → 通过正确的道路 → direction指示，指引，说明，指导

directly.definition: 直接地，径直地；立即；坦率地；  conj.一……就……
directly.definitionEn: in a direct line or manner
directly.sentence: Why take the long way while you can walk directly to the company?
directly.sentenceTrans: 既然你能径直走去公司，为什么还要绕远路？
directly.mnemonic: di使...变成 + rect直 + ly…地 → direct直接的 + ly...地 → 直接地

director.definition: （电影、戏剧等的）导演；经理，董事；主任
director.definitionEn: one of a group of senior managers who run a company; a person who is in charge of a particular activity or department in a company, a college, etc.; a person in charge of a film/movie or play who tells the actors and staff what to do
director.sentence: "Cut!" the director shouted while shooting a film.
director.sentenceTrans: “卡!”导演在拍摄电影的时候大叫道。
director.mnemonic: di使……变成 + rect表示直 + or表示人 → director指导者，导演

dirt.definitionEn: any substance that makes something dirty, for example dust, soil or mud
dirt.sentence: The vacuum cleaner helps me get rid of the dirt.
dirt.sentenceTrans: 真空吸尘器帮我除去灰尘。

dirty.mnemonic: dirt灰 + y表形容词 → dirty肮脏的，有灰尘的

disabled.definitionEn: having a physical or mental disability; unable to perform one or more natural activities (such as walking or seeing) because of illness, injury, etc.
disabled.sentence: The disabled old man wants to go upstairs.
disabled.sentenceTrans: 这位残疾老人想上台阶。
disabled.mnemonic: dis没有 + abl=able能力 + ed形容词后缀 → 伤残的，丧失能力

disadvantage.definition: 不利地位，不利条件，弱点；  v.使不利
disadvantage.definitionEn: something that causes problems and tends to stop somebody/something from succeeding or making progress; a bad or undesirable quality or feature
disadvantage.sentence: When the books fell, the tall boy was at a disadvantage, unlike the short one.
disadvantage.sentenceTrans: 当书掉落时，不像矮个男孩，高个男孩处于不利地位。
disadvantage.mnemonic: dis不，非 + advantage优点 → disadvantage缺点

disagree.definition: 不同意，有分歧，持不同意见；（陈述或报道）不一致，不相符
disagree.definitionEn: if two people disagree or one person disagrees with another about something, they have a different opinion about it
disagree.sentenceTrans: 她不赞同他提出的建议。
disagree.mnemonic: dis否定 + agree赞同 → disagree不同意

disappear.definitionEn: to become impossible to see; to be lost or impossible to find
disappear.sentence: How amazing it is that he can make a bird disappear!
disappear.sentenceTrans: 他能把一只鸟变没了，真是太神奇了！
disappear.mnemonic: dis否定 + appear出现 → disappear消失

disappoint.definition: 使失望，使受挫折；使失望，使落空
disappoint.definitionEn: to make somebody feel sad because something that they hope for or expect to happen does not happen or is not as good as they hoped; to prevent something that somebody hopes for from becoming a reality
disappoint.mnemonic: dis不 + appoint预约 → 失约 → 失望 → 使失望；受挫折

disappointed.definitionEn: upset because something you hoped for has not happened or been as good, successful, etc. as you expected
disappointed.sentence: He felt quite disappointed about his test score.
disappointed.sentenceTrans: 他对他这次的考试成绩失望透顶。
disappointed.mnemonic: dis非，不是 + appoint约定 + ed形容词后缀 → disappointed失望的

disappointing.definitionEn: not as good, successful, etc. as you had hoped; making you feel disappointed
disappointing.sentence: I found the contents of my gift to be very disappointing.
disappointing.sentenceTrans: 当我看到礼物是什么的时候，我感到非常失望。

disapprove.definitionEn: to think that somebody/something is not good or suitable; to not approve of somebody/something
disapprove.sentence: The girl disapproved of having pizza for dinner.
disapprove.sentenceTrans: 那个女孩不赞成晚餐吃比萨。
disapprove.mnemonic: dis不 + ap一再 + prove测试，证明 → 不一再证明 → disapprove不赞成

disaster.definitionEn: something (such as a flood, tornado, fire, plane crash, etc.) that happens suddenly and causes much suffering or loss to many people
disaster.sentence: The entire city is destroyed. What a disaster!
disaster.sentenceTrans: 整个城市都被毁了，真是场灾难！
disaster.mnemonic: dis不 ＋ aster星 → 星位不正，表示有灾难 → disaster灾难，灾祸

disc.definition: 唱片；圆盘，盘状物；[计] 磁盘，磁碟片
disc.definitionEn: a thin round piece of plastic on which music, etc. is recorded
disc.sentence: The music is stored in the disc.
disc.sentenceTrans: 音乐储存在这张唱片里。

discharge.sentence: How long will the discharge of the container cargo take?
discharge.sentenceTrans: 卸载货柜装货物要花多久？
discharge.mnemonic: dis取消 + charge充电 → discharge放电

discipline.definition: 纪律；学科；  v.训练；惩罚，管制
discipline.definitionEn: the practice of training people to obey rules and orders and punishing them if they do not; the controlled behaviour or situation that results from this training
discipline.sentence: These soldiers are showing great discipline.
discipline.sentenceTrans: 这些士兵展现出很强的纪律性。
discipline.mnemonic: dis分散 + cip拿 + line一条直线 → 使分散的成为一条直线 → discipline纪律

disciplined.definitionEn: able to control the way you behave and to make yourself do things that you believe you should do
disciplined.sentence: Mr. Bear, who is disciplined, has never broken the rules.
disciplined.sentenceTrans: 遵守纪律的熊先生从未违反过规则。

disconnect.definition: 断开，拆开，使分离；【航】断开
disconnect.definitionEn: to remove a piece of equipment from a supply of gas, water or electricity; to officially stop the supply of telephone lines, water, electricity or gas to a building; to separate something from something; to break the contact between two people who are talking on the telephone
disconnect.sentence: The phone company disconnected my phone service because I didn't pay my bill.
disconnect.sentenceTrans: 电话公司切断了对我的服务，因为我没有付我的账单。
disconnect.mnemonic: dis分开 + con共同 + nect连结 → 拆开，分离

discount.definition: 折扣（读作/ˈdɪskaʊnt/）；  v.打折（读作/dɪsˈkaʊnt/）
discount.definitionEn: an amount of money that is taken off the usual cost of something
discount.sentence: We can buy many goods with great discounts during sales.
discount.sentenceTrans: 我们可以在打折季买到很多打折商品。
discount.mnemonic: dis取消 + count数量 → 取消一些金钱的花费 → discount折扣

discourage.definitionEn: to make somebody feel less confident or enthusiastic about doing something
discourage.sentence: The bad weather discouraged her from having a picnic.
discourage.sentenceTrans: 这糟糕的天气使她不能外出野餐。
discourage.mnemonic: dis除去，取消 + courage勇气 → discourage使失去勇气

discover.definitionEn: to be the first person to become aware that a particular place or thing exists; to find somebody/something that was hidden or that you did not expect to find
discover.sentence: The expert discovered a vase from the Tang dynasty.
discover.sentenceTrans: 这名专家发现了一个唐朝的花瓶。
discover.mnemonic: dis相反 + cover盖 → 把盖揭开 → discover发现

discovery.definitionEn: a thing, fact or person that is found or learned about for the first time
discovery.sentence: The discovery of liquid water on Mars is exciting to us.
discovery.sentenceTrans: 在火星上发现液态水是一件激动人心的事。
discovery.mnemonic: discover发现 + y名词后缀 → discovery发现

discriminate.definitionEn: to treat one person or group worse/better than another in an unfair way
discriminate.sentence: Discriminating against others is a bad behavior.
discriminate.sentenceTrans: 歧视他人是不好的行为。
discriminate.mnemonic: dis分开，分离 + crimin分辨 + ate动词后缀 → discriminate分辩开

discrimination.definition: 区别对待；辨别力，识别力；歧视
discrimination.definitionEn: the practice of treating somebody or a particular group in society less fairly than others; the ability to judge what is good, true, etc.; the ability to recognize a difference between one thing and another; a difference that is recognized
discrimination.sentence: This little duck suffers discrimination for its different look from others.
discrimination.sentenceTrans: 这只小鸭子因为长相不同而受到区别对待。
discrimination.mnemonic: discriminat(e)歧视 + ion名词后缀 → discrimination歧视

discuss.definitionEn: to talk about something with somebody, especially in order to decide something
discuss.sentence: The students discussed the topic on the blackboard.
discuss.sentenceTrans: 学生们讨论了黑板上的话题。
discuss.mnemonic: dis分开，分离 + cuss敲打 → 把问题分开敲 → discuss讨论

discussion.definitionEn: the process of discussing somebody/something; a conversation about somebody/something
discussion.sentence: The teacher and kids are in a discussion about the Earth.
discussion.sentenceTrans: 老师和孩子们在进行一场关于地球的讨论。
discussion.mnemonic: discuss讨论 + ion名词后缀 → discussion讨论

disease.definitionEn: an illness affecting humans, animals or plants, often caused by infection
disease.sentence: There is a disease spreading around the family.
disease.sentenceTrans: 有一种疾病在这家人之间传播。
disease.mnemonic: dis没有 + ease安逸 → 不舒服 → disease疾病

disguise.definition: 伪装；掩饰，掩盖；  n.伪装；伪装物
disguise.definitionEn: to change your appearance so that people cannot recognize you
disguise.sentence: Miss Bear disguised herself as a panda by wearing black stockings.
disguise.sentenceTrans: 熊小姐穿上黑色长袜把自己伪装成了一只熊猫。
disguise.mnemonic: dis相反 + guise外貌，外在的样子 → 掩盖外表 → disguise伪装

disgust.definition: 使作呕，使厌恶；  n.恶心
disgust.definitionEn: if something disgusts you, it makes you feel shocked and almost ill/sick because it is so unpleasant
disgust.sentence: The smell in the car disgusted him.
disgust.sentenceTrans: 车里的气味让他感到恶心。
disgust.mnemonic: dis与...相反 + gust尝 → disgust使作呕

disgusting.definition: 令人厌恶的；令人恶心的；令人无法接受的
disgusting.definitionEn: so unpleasant to see, smell, taste, consider, etc., that you feel slightly sick
disgusting.sentence: He finds the smell of the sock disgusting.
disgusting.sentenceTrans: 这只袜子的味道实在让他恶心。
disgusting.mnemonic: disgust使厌恶 + ing形容词后缀 → disgusting令人厌恶的

dish.definitionEn: food that is prepared in a particular way
dish.sentence: Add a slice of lemon to flavor the dish.
dish.sentenceTrans: 加上一片柠檬为这道菜肴调味。

disk.definitionEn: a thin round piece of plastic on which music, etc. is recorded; a piece or collection of music released as a record, or on CD, the Internet, etc.
disk.sentence: Music was recorded on this compact disk(CD).
disk.sentenceTrans: 音乐被刻录在这张光盘上。

dislike.sentence: As a lady of fine taste, she really dislikes this cheap watch.
dislike.sentenceTrans: 作为一位很有品味的贵妇，她实在不喜欢这块廉价手表。
dislike.mnemonic: dis否定 + like喜欢 → dislike不喜欢

dismiss.definitionEn: to officially remove somebody from their job; to send somebody away or allow them to leave; to put thoughts or feelings out of your mind
dismiss.sentence: The boss was angry and dismissed the staff.
dismiss.sentenceTrans: 老板很生气，并且开除了那个职员。
dismiss.mnemonic: dis离开 + miss送 → 我送你离开，千里之外 → dismiss解雇

dismissal.definitionEn: the act of dismissing somebody from their job; an example of this
dismissal.sentence: Do not come back. This is your final dismissal.
dismissal.sentenceTrans: 不要回来了。你已经被解雇了。
dismissal.mnemonic: dis分开 + miss送出 + al表名词 → dismissal解雇

disorder.definitionEn: an untidy state; a lack of order or organization
disorder.sentence: The room was in a state of disorder.
disorder.mnemonic: dis无 + order顺序 → 没有顺序 → 混乱

display.definition: 展示；显示；陈列；  n.显示；陈列
display.definitionEn: to put something in a place where people can see it easily; to show something to people
display.sentence: He proudly displayed the big fish he had caught.
display.sentenceTrans: 他自豪地展示着他钓到的大鱼。
display.mnemonic: dis分开，否定 + play折叠 → 打开，分散 → display展示

dispose.definitionEn: to arrange things or people in a particular way or position
dispose.sentence: She is disposing of the unwanted vegetables into the bin.
dispose.sentenceTrans: 她正在处理不需要的蔬菜，把它们全扔进垃圾箱里。
dispose.mnemonic: dis分开 + pos放 + e  → 分开排好 → dispose处理，处置

dispute.definition: 争论，争端；  v.争执，驳斥
dispute.definitionEn: an argument or a disagreement between two people, groups or countries; discussion about a subject where there is disagreement
dispute.sentence: They're having a dispute about the car accident.
dispute.sentenceTrans: 他们正在争论车祸的事情。
dispute.mnemonic: dis分开 + put思考 → 不同的思考 → 引申为dispute争论

dissolve.definitionEn: (of a solid) to mix with a liquid and become part of it; to make a solid become part of a liquid
dissolve.mnemonic: dis分开，分离 + solve解决，溶解 → 完全分散 → dissolve溶解

distance.definition: 距离；间距；  v.使与……保持距离，撇清和……的关系
distance.definitionEn: the amount of space between two places or things
distance.sentence: The distance between the two buildings is 2 km.
distance.sentenceTrans: 这两栋建筑之间的距离是2千米。
distance.mnemonic: dist距离 + ance表状态 → distance距离，远处

distant.definition: 遥远的；不亲近的；疏远的
distant.definitionEn: far away in space or time
distant.mnemonic: di分开 + stant站立 → 分开站 → distant有距离的

distinct.definition: 截然不同的；独特的；明显的；清晰的
distinct.definitionEn: clearly different or of a different kind
distinct.sentence: The red umbrella is distinct among the black ones.
distinct.sentenceTrans: 这把红伞在这些黑伞中显得与众不同。
distinct.mnemonic: dis分开 + stinct（sting）刺，做标记 → 分开标记的，区分清楚的 → distinct独特的，清楚的

distinction.definition: 差别，区分；优等评分，荣誉分数
distinction.definitionEn: a clear difference or contrast especially between people or things that are similar or related
distinction.sentence: The main distinction between the red and the black pencils is their color.
distinction.sentenceTrans: 红铅笔和黑铅笔的主要区别是它们的颜色。
distinction.mnemonic: distinct独特的 + ion名词后缀 → distinction卓越；区别

distinctly.definitionEn: in a way that is easily or clearly heard, seen, felt, etc.
distinctly.sentence: The colors of these two pictures are distinctly different.
distinctly.sentenceTrans: 这两张图片的颜色明显不一样。
distinctly.mnemonic: di分开 + stinct刺激 + ly……地 → 把刺分开 → 明显地；确实地

distinguish.definitionEn: to recognize the difference between two people or things; to be a characteristic that makes two people, animals or things different; to be able to see or hear something
distinguish.sentence: It's easy to distinguish the blue man from the gray men.
distinguish.sentenceTrans: 我们很容易就能把这个蓝色的人从一群灰色的人中辨别出来。
distinguish.mnemonic: dis分散，分开 + tingu=ting做标记 + ish动词后缀 → 分开做标记 → distinguish区别

distinguished.definitionEn: very successful and admired by other people
distinguished.sentence: Einstein is a distinguished physicist and scientist.
distinguished.sentenceTrans: 爱因斯坦是一位杰出的物理学家和科学家。
distinguished.mnemonic: distinguish区别 + ed表形容词 → 与众不同 → distinguished著名的

distort.definitionEn: to change the shape, appearance or sound of something so that it is strange or not clear
distort.sentence: Pressing the soft clay too hard will distort its smooth surface.
distort.sentenceTrans: 过度用力按压软陶会使其光滑表面变形。
distort.mnemonic: dis分离 + tort变形，扭曲 → distort扭曲

distract.definition: 转移（注意力），使分心；  v.转移(注意力)
distract.definitionEn: to cause (someone) to stop thinking about or paying attention to someone or something and to think about or pay attention to someone or something else instead
distract.sentence: The cat tried to distract his friend's attention and took his fish.
distract.sentenceTrans: 小猫试图转移他朋友的注意力，伺机拿走他的小鱼干。
distract.mnemonic: dis分开，分离 + tract拉 → 把心拉开 → 分心

distribute.definitionEn: to give things to a large number of people; to share something between a number of people; to send goods to shops/stores and businesses so that they can be sold
distribute.sentence: They distribute food to the people in need.
distribute.sentenceTrans: 他们把食物分发给有需要的人。
distribute.mnemonic: dis分开 + tribute赠品 → 分开给 → distribute分配；区分

district.definitionEn: one of the areas which a country, town or state is divided into for purposes of organization, with official boundaries (= borders)
district.sentence: The city is made up of four districts.
district.sentenceTrans: 这座城市由四个区域组成。
district.mnemonic: di分开 + str拉紧 + ict  → 把一块区域分开  → district地区，区域

disturb.definitionEn: to interrupt somebody when they are trying to work, sleep, etc.
disturb.sentence: My cute puppy often disturbs me while I'm working.
disturb.sentenceTrans: 我可爱的小狗经常在我工作的时候打扰我。
disturb.mnemonic: dis分开 + turb骚乱 → 分开了 → disturb扰乱，打扰

ditch.definition: 沟，沟渠；  v.丢弃；摆脱；迫降海上；  v.丢弃
ditch.definitionEn: a long channel dug at the side of a field or road, to hold or take away water
ditch.sentence: There is a ditch between the two fields.
ditch.sentenceTrans: 两块田之间有一条沟渠。

dive.definition: 跳水；急剧下降；  n.跳水；潜水；骤降
dive.definitionEn: to jump into water with your arms and head going in first
dive.sentence: Is the water in this swimming pool deep enough to dive into?
dive.sentenceTrans: 这个游泳池的水深到能跳水吗？

diverse.definitionEn: very different from each other and of various kinds
diverse.sentence: The park is home to diverse flowers, such as roses, tulips and sunflowers.
diverse.sentenceTrans: 这个公园里生长着多样的花朵，例如玫瑰、郁金香和向日葵。
diverse.mnemonic: di分开 + vers转变 + e → 转开了 → diverse不同的

divide.definitionEn: to separate or make something separate into parts; to separate something into parts and give a share to each of a number of different people, etc.; to use different parts of your time, energy, etc. for different activities, etc.; to separate two people or things
divide.sentence: The cabin crew closed the curtain to divide the business class from the economy section.
divide.sentenceTrans: 乘务员拉上了隔帘，将商务舱与经济舱隔开。
divide.mnemonic: di分开 + vide分开 → 分开 → divide分开

division.definitionEn: the process or result of dividing into separate parts; the process or result of dividing something or sharing it out
division.sentence: He finished the division of the cake.
division.mnemonic: di分开 + vis分开 + ion表名词 → division分，分配

divorce.definitionEn: the legal ending of a marriage; a separation; the ending of a relationship between two things
divorce.sentence: The couple have agreed to get a divorce.
divorce.sentenceTrans: 这对夫妻已经同意离婚了。
divorce.mnemonic: di使…变成、分开 + vorce=vert转 → 从伴侣身边转开 → 离婚

do.definitionEn: used to refer to actions that you do not mention by name or do not know about
do.sentence: The little boy is doing his homework.
do.sentenceTrans: 小男孩正在做家庭作业。

doctor.definition: 医生；博士；  v.篡改（文件，照片），伪造
doctor.definitionEn: a person who is skilled in the science of medicine :a person who is trained and licensed to treat sick and injured people
doctor.sentence: The doctor will see you in 10 minutes.
doctor.sentenceTrans: 医生会在10分钟内接诊您。
doctor.mnemonic: doct教 ＋ or表名词，人 → 教的人 → doctor博士，医生

document.definition: 文件，公文；  v.记录；证明（读作/ˈdɑkjuˌmɛnt/）
document.definitionEn: an official paper or book that gives information about something, or that can be used as evidence or proof of something
document.sentence: He checks out the document before signing it.
document.sentenceTrans: 在签署文件之前，他仔细检查了一遍。
document.mnemonic: docu=doc教 + ment名词后缀 → 用来告诉别人的东西 → document文件，公文

dog.definition: 狗，犬，犬科动物；  v.跟踪；尾随
dog.definitionEn: an animal with four legs and a tail, often kept as a pet or trained for work, for example hunting or guarding buildings. There are many types of dog, some of which are wild.; a male dog, fox or wolf

dollar.definitionEn: a basic unit of money in the U.S., Canada, Australia, and other countries that is equal to 100 cents
dollar.sentence: My mother gives me one dollar a week. She loves me so much!
dollar.sentenceTrans: 我妈一个礼拜给我一块钱。她太爱我啦！

domestic.definition: 国内的；家庭的；驯养的；  n.家仆
domestic.definitionEn: of, relating to, or made in your own country
domestic.sentence: More and more domestic products are sold abroad.
domestic.sentenceTrans: 越来越多国货销往海外。
domestic.mnemonic: domes屋，家 + tic形容词后缀 → 家里的 → domestic家里的；国内的

domestically.definitionEn: with respect to the internal affairs of a government
domestically.sentence: Giant pandas are very famous domestically.
domestically.sentenceTrans: 大熊猫在国内非常出名。

dominant.definition: 占优势的，占支配地位的；主要的；显著的
dominant.definitionEn: more important, powerful or noticeable than other things
dominant.sentence: He achieved a dominant position by occupying the majority of the market share.
dominant.sentenceTrans: 他占据了大部分市场份额，取得了市场主导地位。
dominant.mnemonic: domin=lord（主人）+ ant表示属于…的 → 属于主人的叫统治 → dominant统治的

dominate.definitionEn: to control or have a lot of influence over somebody/something, especially in an unpleasant way
dominate.sentence: Lions are the ultimate predators which dominate the great grassland.
dominate.sentenceTrans: 狮子是支配着大草原的顶级掠食者。
dominate.mnemonic: domin=dom屋，家 + ate做… → 像家长一样 → dominate支配，统治

donate.definitionEn: to give money, food, clothes, etc. to somebody/something, especially a charity
donate.sentence: We donated a sum of money to the charity.
donate.sentenceTrans: 我们向慈善机构捐了一笔钱。
donate.mnemonic: don给予 + ate使 → 给出去 → donate捐赠

donkey.definitionEn: an animal of the horse family, with short legs and long ears. People ride donkeys or use them to carry heavy loads.
donkey.sentence: The donkey is trying to eat a carrot.
donkey.sentenceTrans: 这头驴子正在努力吃一根胡萝卜。

door.definitionEn: a piece of wood, glass, etc. that is opened and closed so that people can get in and out of a room, building, car, etc.; a similar thing in a cupboard/closet
door.sentence: Where does the door lead to?

dormitory.definitionEn: a building on a school campus that has rooms where students can live
dormitory.sentence: My dormitory is clean and tidy.
dormitory.mnemonic: dorm睡眠 + itory表示场所 → 睡觉的地方 → dormitory寝室，宿舍

dose.definitionEn: the amount of a medicine, drug, or vitamin that is taken at one time
dose.sentence: In biochemistry, it's crucial to control the dose of the chemicals accurately for the experiment.
dose.sentenceTrans: 在生物化学中，精确剂量化学物质对于实验至关重要。
dose.mnemonic: do给，被“给”的+se名词后缀，物品→饮用药量 → 一剂药，一剂

dot.definition: 点（在域名里起分隔作用）
dot.definitionEn: a small round mark, especially one that is printed
dot.sentence: You need to type the correct dot com at the end of the website address.
dot.sentenceTrans: 你需要在网址末尾输入正确的.com。

double.definition: 两倍的，成双的，成对的；  v.使……翻倍
double.definitionEn: twice as much or as many as usual; having or made of two things or parts that are equal or similar
double.sentence: The hamburger in the middle is a double cheeseburger.
double.sentenceTrans: 中间的汉堡包是一个双层芝士堡。
double.mnemonic: doub二，双 + le反复 → 反复两倍 → double 翻倍

doubt.definition: 怀疑；  n.怀疑；疑惑，疑问
doubt.definitionEn: a feeling of being uncertain about something or not believing something
doubt.sentence: I really doubt whether aliens exist.
doubt.sentenceTrans: 我很怀疑外星人是否真的存在。

doubtful.definitionEn: (of a person) not sure; uncertain and feeling doubt; unlikely; not probable
doubtful.sentence: I'm doubtful about the true value of the painting.
doubtful.sentenceTrans: 我对这幅画的真实价值表示怀疑。
doubtful.mnemonic: doubt怀疑 + ful形容词后缀 → doubtful怀疑的

down.definition: 向下；  adj.向下的；沮丧的，情绪低落的
down.definitionEn: to or at a lower place or position
down.sentence: She keeps walking down the road.
down.sentenceTrans: 她沿着马路一直往下走。

download.definitionEn: to move or copy (a file, program, etc.) from a usually larger computer system to another computer or device
download.sentence: I use my computer to download apps for my phone.
download.sentenceTrans: 我用电脑给我的手机下载应用程序。

downstairs.definition: 在楼下，往楼下；  adj.楼下的
downstairs.definitionEn: down the stairs; on or to a floor of a house or building lower than the one you are on, especially the one at ground level
downstairs.mnemonic: down向下 + stairs楼梯 → downstairs楼下的

downtown.definition: 在市中心；  adj.市中心的，商业区的，闹市区的
downtown.definitionEn: to, toward, or in the main or central part of a city or town
downtown.sentence: She lives downtown and goes to work by bicycle.
downtown.sentenceTrans: 她住在市中心而且骑自行车去上班。

downward.definition: 向下；  adj.向下的，下降的
downward.definitionEn: from a higher place or level to a lower place or level
downward.sentence: I fell downward through the air, hoping my parachute would open.
downward.sentenceTrans: 我从空中降落，期望着我的降落伞会打开。
downward.mnemonic: down向下 ＋ ward向... → downward向下地

downwards.definitionEn: toward a direction that is the opposite of up
downwards.sentence: Gravity pulls objects downwards towards the center of the Earth.
downwards.sentenceTrans: 重力将物体向地球中心拉动，方向是向下的。
downwards.mnemonic: down下去 + wards表副词，向... → 向下，朝下

dozen.definitionEn: a group of twelve of the same thing
dozen.sentence:
A dozen eggs now cost twenty 
dollars—how expensive!
dozen.sentenceTrans: 一打鸡蛋现在要20美元——好贵啊！

draft.definitionEn: to draw the preliminary sketch, version, or plan of
draft.sentence: This is just the draft of a building.
draft.sentenceTrans: 这只是建筑的设计草图。

drag.definition: 拖，拉，拽，扯；（时间或事件）拖沓；  n.拖累物；空气阻力
drag.definitionEn: to pull somebody/something along with effort and difficulty
drag.sentence: You can drag this picture from this folder to the other.
drag.sentenceTrans: 你可以把图片从这个文件夹拖进另一个文件夹里。

drama.definitionEn: a play for the theatre, television or radio; plays considered as a form of literature
drama.sentence: The two actors are performing a great love drama.
drama.sentenceTrans: 这两名演员正在表演一部伟大的爱情剧。
drama.mnemonic: dra表演 + ma → 在舞台上表演的故事 → drama戏剧，剧本

dramatic.definition: 激动人心的；引人注意的；戏剧性化的
dramatic.definitionEn: (of a change, an event, etc.) sudden, very great and often surprising; exciting and impressive
dramatic.sentence: I see two rainbows over the road; it's so dramatic!
dramatic.sentenceTrans: 我在路上看到了两道彩虹,太激动人心了。
dramatic.mnemonic: drama戏剧 + tic形容词后缀 → dramatic戏剧的，戏剧性的

dramatically.definition: 显著地，剧烈地，引人注目地
dramatically.definitionEn: very suddenly and to a very great and often surprising degree; in a way that is exciting and impressive; in a way that is exaggerated in order to create a special effect and attract people's attention; in a way that is connected with the theatre or plays
dramatically.sentence: This selfie app can dramatically change a person's face.
dramatically.sentenceTrans: 自拍软件可以显著地改变一个人的面貌。
dramatically.mnemonic: drama戏剧 + tic……的 + ally……地 → dramatically戏剧性地

drastic.definitionEn: extreme in a way that has a sudden, serious or violent effect on something
drastic.sentence: They have experienced drastic weather changes in one day.
drastic.sentenceTrans: 他们在一天之内经历了极端的天气变化。
drastic.mnemonic: dra表演 + stic=istic有……性质的 → 表演十分投入的 → 充满激情的 → drastic激烈的

draw.definitionEn: to make (a picture, image, etc.) by making lines on a surface especially with a pencil, pen, marker, chalk, etc., but not usually with paint
draw.sentence: The girls are sitting on the ground drawing pictures.
draw.sentenceTrans: 女孩们正坐在地上画画。

drawer.definition: 抽屉；开票人，出票人（读作/ˈdrɔːər/）
drawer.definitionEn: a box that slides into and out of a piece of furniture (such as a desk) and that is used to store things
drawer.sentence: Remember to keep all your files in the drawer.
drawer.sentenceTrans: 记得把你的所有文件都放在抽屉里。
drawer.mnemonic: draw拉，拖 + er施动者名词后缀，表人或物 → 被人拉开 → drawer抽屉

drawing.definitionEn: a picture made using a pencil or pen rather than paint; the art or skill of making pictures, plans, etc. using a pen or pencil
drawing.sentence: That's a simple drawing of a big head man.
drawing.sentenceTrans: 那是一张简笔画，画的是一个大头男人。
drawing.mnemonic: draw画 + ing名词后缀 → 画画 → drawing图画,素描;绘图

dream.definition: 梦；梦想；愿望；理想；  v.做梦；梦想
dream.definitionEn: to experience a series of images, events and feelings in your mind while you are asleep; to imagine and think about something that you would like to happen
dream.sentence: In my dream, I was on a beach in Hawaii.
dream.sentenceTrans: 我在梦里去了夏威夷海滩。

dress.definitionEn: a piece of women’s clothing that is made in one piece and covers the body down to the legs, sometimes reaching to below the knees, or to the ankles
dress.sentence: I wear a long white dress.
dress.sentenceTrans: 我穿着一条白色的长裙。

drift.definition: 漂流；使漂流；  n.漂流物
drift.definitionEn: to move along smoothly and slowly in water or air
drift.sentence: The poet is drifting on a boat.
drift.sentenceTrans: 诗人正乘着小舟随波飘荡。

drill.definition: 钻孔；  n.训练；反复操练；钻头
drill.definitionEn: to make a hole in something, using a drill
drill.sentence: The worker drills into the wall.

drink.definitionEn: to take a liquid into your mouth and swallow it

drive.definition: 驾驶；驱使，迫使；  n.驱动力
drive.definitionEn: to operate a vehicle so that it goes in a particular direction
drive.sentence: The man is driving along the coast.
drive.sentenceTrans: 这个男人沿着海边开着车。

driver.definitionEn: a person who drives a vehicle
driver.sentence: The driver with a beard is very handsome.
driver.sentenceTrans: 这位留着胡子的司机非常帅气。
driver.mnemonic: driv驾驶 + er表示人 → driver驾驶员，司机

drop.definitionEn: a fall or reduction in the amount, level or number of something
drop.sentence: I accidentally dropped my phone. So upset!
drop.sentenceTrans: 我不小心把手机弄掉了。真难过！

drought.definitionEn: a long period of time when there is little or no rain
drought.sentence: Drought caused the river to dry up.

drown.definitionEn: to die because you have been underwater too long and you cannot breathe; to kill somebody in this way
drown.sentence: The apple drowned in the water because it couldn't swim.
drown.sentenceTrans: 苹果因为不会游泳而淹死在了水里。

drug.definition: 药物；毒品；  v.下麻药；  v.使服麻醉药
drug.definitionEn: an illegal substance that some people smoke, inject, etc. for the physical and mental effects it has; a substance used as a medicine or used in a medicine
drug.sentence: The doctor gave me some drugs.

drum.definitionEn: a musical instrument that is made with a thin layer of skin or plastic stretched over the end of a round frame and that is played by hitting the skin or plastic with sticks or with your hands
drum.sentence: She is playing the drums for the musical show.
drum.sentenceTrans: 她正在为音乐表演打鼓。

drunk.definitionEn: having drunk so much alcohol that it is impossible to think or speak clearly
drunk.sentence: They had drunk all night long and made a mess.
drunk.sentenceTrans: 他们喝了一整夜，搞得一团糟。

drunken.definitionEn: showing the effects of too much alcohol; involving people who are drunk
drunken.sentence: The drunken woman is sleeping on the bench.
drunken.sentenceTrans: 这个喝醉的女人正在长椅上睡觉。
drunken.mnemonic: drunk醉酒 + en过去分词时态 → 喝醉酒的 → drunken酒醉的

dry.definitionEn: not wet, damp or sticky; without water or moisture
dry.sentence: These flowers are dry but still beautiful.

duck.definitionEn: a common bird that lives on or near water and has short legs, webbed feet
duck.sentence: Ducks are swimming happily in the water.
duck.sentenceTrans: 鸭子们在水中欢快地游着。

due.definition: 预期的；欠债的，应给的；到期的
due.definitionEn: arranged or expected; when a sum of money is due, it must be paid immediately
due.sentence: Her baby is due on February 28th.
due.sentenceTrans: 她的宝宝预计于2月28日出生。

dull.definition: 枯燥的，沉闷的；愚笨的，迟钝的；无趣的
dull.sentence: The TV show is so dull that it makes him feel sleepy.
dull.sentenceTrans: 这档电视节目很无趣，让他想睡觉。

dumb.definition: 愚笨的；哑的，不能说话的；  v.使沉默
dumb.definitionEn: unable to speak; temporarily not speaking or refusing to speak; stupid
dumb.sentence: It's dumb to row on the cracked soil.
dumb.sentenceTrans: 在龟裂的土地上划船是件很蠢的事情。

dump.definition: 倾倒，丢弃；  n.垃圾场，废物堆
dump.definitionEn: to get rid of something you do not want, especially in a place which is not suitable
dump.sentence: The big truck is dumping waste materials.
dump.sentenceTrans: 这辆大卡车正在倾倒废料。

dumpling.definitionEn: a small ball of dough (= a mixture of flour, fat and water) that is cooked and served with meat dishes
dumpling.sentence: I enjoy eating Chinese dumplings for lunch.
dumpling.mnemonic: dump无秩序的累积 + ling名词后缀，表示小 → 无秩序地累积的小东西 → dumpling饺子；团子

duplicate.definition: 复制；  n.【计】副本；复制品；  adj.完全一样的
duplicate.definitionEn: to make an exact copy of something
duplicate.sentence: His right hand can duplicate the thing that his left hand touches.
duplicate.sentenceTrans: 库哔左手触摸死或不动物体，右手复制。
duplicate.mnemonic: du二，双 + plic折 + ate使，造成 → 折成相同的两份 → duplicate加倍，复制

durable.definitionEn: likely to last for a long time without breaking or getting weaker
durable.sentence: These shoes are quite durable and perfect for hiking.
durable.sentenceTrans: 这些鞋子非常耐用，非常适合徒步旅行。
durable.mnemonic: dur持久，坚硬 + able能……的 → 持久的

duration.definitionEn: the length of time that something exists or lasts
duration.sentence: The duration of this exam is two hours.
duration.sentenceTrans: 这场考试的时长是两个小时。
duration.mnemonic: dur持久 + ation名词后缀，表状态 → 持久的状态 → duration持续时间

during.definitionEn: throughout the entire time of (an event, period, occurrence, etc.)
during.sentence: It's rude to talk on the phone during dinner.
during.sentenceTrans: 在吃晚餐时打电话很没礼貌。
during.mnemonic: dur持久 ＋ ing构成介词 → during在…期间

dusk.definitionEn: the time of day when the light has almost gone, but it is not yet dark
dusk.sentence: I enjoy watching the sunset at dusk.
dusk.sentenceTrans: 我很享受在黄昏时看日落。

dust.definition: 尘土，沙土；  v.撒上粉末
dust.definitionEn: a fine powder that consists of very small pieces of sand, earth, etc.
dust.sentence: Driving down the dirt road so fast raised a lot of dust.
dust.sentenceTrans: 车从土路上全速驶过，激起漫天的尘土。

dustbin.definitionEn: a can for trash or garbage :a garbage can or trash can
dustbin.sentence: I put the trash into the dustbin.
dustbin.mnemonic: dust尘土 ＋ bin箱子 → dustbin垃圾桶，灰箱

duty.definitionEn: something that you feel you have to do because it is your moral or legal responsibility
duty.sentence: Everyone should carry out his duty conscientiously when at work.
duty.sentenceTrans: 每个人在工作时都应该认真履行自己的职责。
duty.mnemonic: du=de离开 + ty有 → 有责任所以不能离开 → duty责任，义务

dwarf.definition: 侏儒；[天]矮星；  v.使……相形见绌
dwarf.definitionEn: an extremely small person, who will never grow to a normal size because of a physical problem; a person suffering from dwarfism
dwarf.sentence: The Seven Dwarfs were happy when staying with Snow White.
dwarf.sentenceTrans: 七个小矮人和白雪公主在一起时非常开心。

dynamic.definition: 动态的；有活力的，有生机的；不断变化的；  n.动力
dynamic.definitionEn: (of a person) having a lot of energy and a strong personality
dynamic.mnemonic: dynam=power，表示“力量” + ic…的 → dynamic有活力的

each.definitionEn: used to refer to every one of two or more people or things, when you are thinking about them separately
each.sentence: Try to support each other when one of you is feeling down.
each.sentenceTrans: 当有人觉得情绪低落时，要努力相互打气。
each.mnemonic: ea曾经，总是 + ch相似 → 不同事物的对照 → each每个

eager.definition: 热切的，渴望的，急不可耐的
eager.definitionEn: very interested and excited by something that is going to happen or about something that you want to do
eager.sentence: The kids are eager to eat the cake on the table.
eager.sentenceTrans: 孩子们急不可耐地想要吃掉桌上的蛋糕。

eagle.definitionEn: a large bird of prey (= a bird that kills other creatures for food) with a sharp curved beak and very good sight
eagle.sentence: A huge eagle is flying high in the sky.

ear.definitionEn: either of the organs on the sides of the head that you hear with

early.definitionEn: near the beginning of a period of time, an event etc.
early.sentence: It is far too early in the morning to get up!
early.mnemonic: ear早 + ly副词后缀 → early早的，早期的

earn.definitionEn: to get money for work that you do
earn.sentence: She earns some extra money by doing a part-time job.
earn.sentenceTrans: 她通过做兼职赚了一些外快。

earnest.sentence: "Thank you very much!" said the granny with an earnest expression on her face.
earnest.sentenceTrans: “非常感谢你！”这位老奶奶满脸真诚地说道。

earnings.definitionEn: the money that you earn for the work that you do
earnings.sentence: A rise in his online business earnings made him excited.
earnings.sentenceTrans: 网络业务收入的增长让他兴奋不已。

earth.definitionEn: the world; the planet that we live on
earth.sentence: This is what the Earth looks like from the outer space.
earth.sentenceTrans: 这就是地球从外太空看到的样子。

earthquake.definitionEn: a sudden, violent shaking of the earth’s surface
earthquake.sentence: The rescue team went to rescue the victims of the earthquake.
earthquake.sentenceTrans: 营救小组去营救地震的受害者。
earthquake.mnemonic: earth地球 + quake震动 → earthquake地震

ease.definition: 轻松；安逸；  v.缓解；解除痛苦
ease.sentence: The strong man can lift the rock with ease.
ease.sentenceTrans: 这个强壮的男人可以轻松地举起石头。

east.definition: 东方；  adj.东方的；  adv.在东方
east.definitionEn: the countries of Asia (such as Japan, China, and Korea)
east.sentence: You can see this Buddha in the east.
east.sentenceTrans: 你可以在东方看到这尊佛像。

eastern.definitionEn: located in the east or facing east; connected with the part of the world that is to the east of Europe
eastern.sentence: I saw the sunrise in the eastern sky.
eastern.sentenceTrans: 我看到太阳从东方升起。
eastern.mnemonic: east东方 + ern形容词后缀 → eastern东方的

easy.definitionEn: not difficult; done or obtained without a lot of effort or problems
easy.sentence: It is easy for the tall boy to touch the ceiling.
easy.sentenceTrans: 这个高个子男孩很容易摸到天花板。
easy.mnemonic: ease安乐 + y表形容词 → easy容易的

eat.definitionEn: to put food in your mouth, chew it and swallow it; to have a meal
eat.sentence: I got so fat that doctor told me from now on I can only eat fruit.
eat.sentenceTrans: 我太胖了，医生告诉我从现在起我只能吃水果。

echo.definition: 回声；  v.发出回声，产生回响
echo.definitionEn: if a sound echoes, it is reflected off a wall, the side of a mountain, etc. so that you can hear it again
echo.sentence: If you shout in this valley, you'll hear an echo.
echo.sentenceTrans: 如果你在这个山谷里大喊，你就会听见回声。

ecology.definitionEn: the relation of plants and living creatures to each other and to their environment; the study of this
ecology.sentence: Animals, plants and humans form the Earth's ecology.
ecology.sentenceTrans: 动物、植物和人类构成了地球的生态。
ecology.mnemonic: eco生态 + logy…学 → ecology生态；生态学

economic.definition: 经济上的，经济学的；有利可图的
economic.definitionEn: connected with the trade, industry and development of wealth of a country, an area or a society
economic.sentence: It is important to keep a balance between economic development and environmental protection.
economic.sentenceTrans: 在经济的发展和环境的保护之间保持平衡是非常重要的。
economic.mnemonic: eco经济 + nom学术领域 + ic……的 → 经济的，经济学的

economical.definitionEn: providing good service or value in relation to the amount of time or money spent
economical.sentence: To save money, he always makes the most economical decisions.
economical.sentenceTrans: 为了省钱，他总是做出精打细算的决定。
economical.mnemonic: eco经济 + nom学术领域 + ical…的 → economical节约的；经济学的

economics.definitionEn: the study of how a society organizes its money, trade and industry
economics.sentence: This is a book about economics.
economics.sentenceTrans: 这是一本关于经济学的书。
economics.mnemonic: eco经济 + nom学术领域 + ics……学 → economics经济学

economy.definitionEn: the relationship between production, trade and the supply of money in a particular country or region; a country, when you are thinking about its economic system
economy.sentence: The economy is improving and people have more money.
economy.sentenceTrans: 经济正在改善，人们也有了更多的钱。
economy.mnemonic: eco环境，经济 + nomy学术领域 → economy经济（学）

edge.definition: （悬崖、峭壁的）边缘；  v.（使）徐徐移动；给……开刃，使锐利
edge.definitionEn: the outside limit of an object, a surface or an area; the part furthest from the centre
edge.sentence: The chicken is so afraid when standing on the edge.
edge.sentenceTrans: 站在悬崖边上时，小鸡感到非常害怕。

edit.definitionEn: when somebody edits a film/movie, television programme, etc. they take what has been filmed or recorded and decide which parts to include and in which order
edit.sentence: I edit the story using a pencil.
edit.mnemonic: e出 + dit给予 → 给出好文章 → 编辑

edition.definitionEn: the form in which a book is published; the total number of copies of a book, newspaper or magazine, etc. published at one time; a particular newspaper or magazine, or radio or television programme, especially one in a regular series
edition.sentence: The dictionary is now in its third edition, which was published in 2017.
edition.sentenceTrans: 这本字典现在是第三版，于2017年出版。
edition.mnemonic: edit编辑 + ion名词后缀 → 编成的样本 → edition版，版本

editor.definitionEn: a person who prepares a book to be published, for example by checking and correcting the text, making improvements, etc.
editor.sentence: The video editor is using special computer software to do his work.
editor.sentenceTrans: 这位视频编辑正在用特殊的电脑软件工作。
editor.mnemonic: edit编辑 + or表示人 → editor编者，编辑

editorial.definition: 编辑的，主笔的；  n.（报刊的）社论
editorial.definitionEn: an important article in a newspaper, that expresses the editor’s opinion about an item of news or an issue; in the US also a comment on radio or television that expresses the opinion of the station or network
editorial.sentence: The editorial team is responsible for the magazine's content and layout.
editorial.sentenceTrans: 编辑团队负责杂志的内容和版面设计。
editorial.mnemonic: editor编辑，编者 + ial形容词后缀 → 给出好文章的人的 → editorial编辑的

educate.definitionEn: to teach somebody over a period of time at a school, university, etc.; to teach somebody about something or how to do something
educate.sentence: He was educated at the Baicizhan University.
educate.sentenceTrans: 他在百词斩大学接受了教育。
educate.mnemonic: e出 + duc引导 + ate动词后缀 → educate教育

education.definitionEn: a particular kind of teaching or training
education.sentence: She received a high standard of education at a famous university.
education.sentenceTrans: 安迪在名校（斯坦福大学）接受了高等教育。
education.mnemonic: e出 + duc引导，带来 + ation行为 → 引出知识的行为 → education教育

educational.mnemonic: educat=educate教育 ＋ ion名词后缀 ＋ al...的 → educational教育的

educator.definitionEn: a person (such as a teacher or a school administrator) who has a job in the field of education
educator.sentence: Confucius is a famous educator in ancient China.
educator.sentenceTrans: 孔子是中国古代著名的教育家。
educator.mnemonic: educat = educate教育 + or名词后缀，表示人 → 教育者

effect.definition: 效果；影响；结果；  v.使发生；引起
effect.definitionEn: a particular look, sound or impression that somebody, such as an artist or a writer, wants to create
effect.sentence: That lighting effect makes the stage look very mysterious.
effect.sentenceTrans: 那种灯光效果使舞台看起来很神秘。
effect.mnemonic: ef出 + fect做，制作 → 做出来 → effect实施，生效；效果

effective.definitionEn: producing the result that is wanted or intended; producing a successful result
effective.sentence: The medicine she took was effective for treating colds.
effective.sentenceTrans: 她吃的药对治疗感冒很有效。
effective.mnemonic: ef出 ＋ fect做，制作 ＋ ive形容词后缀 → 做出来的 → effective有效的

efficiency.definitionEn: the quality of doing something well with no waste of time or money; ways of wasting less time and money or of saving time or money
efficiency.sentence: The robot greatly increases the efficiency of work.
efficiency.sentenceTrans: 机器人极大提高了工作的效率。
efficiency.mnemonic: ef出 + fic做 + iency表名词 → 做出事情 → efficiency有效率

efficient.definitionEn: doing something well and thoroughly with no waste of time, money or energy
efficient.sentence: He's very efficient at work, and can do many things at the same time.
efficient.sentenceTrans: 他工作很高效，能同时处理很多事情。
efficient.mnemonic: ef出 + fici做 + ent……的 → 能做出事来 → efficient做事有效的

effort.definitionEn: an attempt to do something especially when it is difficult to do
effort.sentence: She makes efforts to do exercise so that she can keep fit.
effort.sentenceTrans: 她努力健身以保持健康。
effort.mnemonic: ef出 + fort力量 → 付出力量 → effort努力

egg.definitionEn: a small oval object with a thin hard shell produced by a female bird and containing a young bird
egg.sentence: The eggs were put in the basket.

eighteen.sentence: Eighteen is the age when you become an adult.
eighteen.sentenceTrans: 十八岁是你成为成年人的年龄。

eighth.definitionEn: each of eight equal parts of something
eighth.sentence: We lit eight candles on his eighth birthday.
eighth.sentenceTrans: 在他的八岁生日上，我们点了八根蜡烛。

eighty.sentence: My grandfather is eighty years old.
eighty.mnemonic: eigh表示数字八 + ty表示数字十 → eighty八十

either.definition: 也（用于否定句或短语后）；  pron.（两者中的）任何一个

elaborate.definition: 精心设计的，精巧的；复杂的（读作/iˈlæbərɪt/）
elaborate.definitionEn: very complicated and detailed; carefully prepared and organized
elaborate.sentence: This elaborate wood carving features delicate flowers.
elaborate.sentenceTrans: 这件精巧的木雕上有精致的花朵。
elaborate.mnemonic: e=ex向外 + labor努力劳动 + ate表动词 → elaborate精心制作

elder.definition: 长辈；  adj.年长的，年龄较大的
elder.definitionEn: a person who has authority because of age and experience
elder.sentence: The elders sat together and lovingly watched the child play.
elder.sentenceTrans: 长辈们坐在一起，慈爱地看着孩子玩耍。

elderly.definitionEn: (of people) used as a polite word for ‘old’
elderly.sentence: No one offered a seat to the elderly man.
elderly.mnemonic: elder年长的 + ly……的 → elderly过了中年的，稍老的

elect.definitionEn: to select (someone) for a position, job, etc., by voting; to choose to do something
elect.sentence: We elect our next leader by voting.
elect.sentenceTrans: 我们通过投票来选举下一任领导。
elect.mnemonic: e出 + lect选择，收集 → 选出，选举

election.definitionEn: the process of choosing a person or a group of people for a position, especially a political position, by voting
election.sentence: In an election, we decide who our leaders will be.
election.sentenceTrans: 在选举中，我们决定谁来当我们的领导人。
election.mnemonic: e出 + lect选择，收集 + ion名词后缀 → election选举

electric.definitionEn: connected with electricity; using, produced by or producing electricity
electric.sentence: Don't touch these electric wires. It's dangerous.
electric.sentenceTrans: 不要碰这些电线，这很危险。

electrical.definitionEn: connected with electricity; using or producing electricity
electrical.sentence: The kettle is heated by electrical power.
electrical.sentenceTrans: 这个水壶是用电力加热的。
electrical.mnemonic: electric电 + al……的 → 电的，电气科学的

electricity.definitionEn: a form of energy from charged elementary particles, usually supplied as electric current through cables, wires, etc. for lighting, heating, driving machines, etc.
electricity.sentence: He touched the socket with a wet finger and the electricity gave him a shock.
electricity.sentenceTrans: 他用湿的手指碰到了插座，被电到了。
electricity.mnemonic: electric电的 + ity名词后缀 → electricity电力

electron.definitionEn: a very small piece of matter (= a substance) with a negative electric charge, found in all atoms
electron.sentence: An electron moves around an atom's nucleus.
electron.sentenceTrans: 电子绕着原子的原子核运动。
electron.mnemonic: electr电的 + on表名词 → electron电子

electronic.definitionEn: (of a device) having or using many small parts, such as microchips, that control and direct a small electric current
electronic.sentence: Laptops, mobile phones and tablet computers are all electronic devices.
electronic.sentenceTrans: 笔记本电脑、手机和平板电脑都属于电子设备。
electronic.mnemonic: electron电子 + ic形容词，……的 → 电子的

elegant.definitionEn: (of people or their behaviour) attractive and showing a good sense of style; (of clothes, places and things) attractive and designed well; (of a plan or an idea) clever but simple
elegant.sentence: The ballet dancer is incredibly elegant.
elegant.sentenceTrans: 这位芭蕾舞演员非常优雅。
elegant.mnemonic: e出 + leg选择，收集 + ant形容词后缀 → 选出的 → elegant好的，高雅的

element.definitionEn: a simple chemical substance that consists of atoms of only one type and cannot be split by chemical means into a simpler substance. Gold, oxygen and carbon are all elements.
element.sentence: Water contains the elements of hydrogen and oxygen.

elementary.definitionEn: in or connected with the first stages of a course of study
elementary.sentence: The elementary students are starting school for the first time.
elementary.sentenceTrans: 小学生们正准备第一次上学。
elementary.mnemonic: element要素 + ary形容词后缀 → 最简单的要素 → elementary元素的，基本的

elephant.definitionEn: a very large animal with thick grey skin, large ears, two curved outer teeth called tusks and a long nose called a trunk. There are two types of elephant, the African and the Asian.

elevate.definition: 举起；提高；  v.提升；使情绪高昂；鼓舞
elevate.definitionEn: to lift something up or put something in a higher position
elevate.sentence: The father elevates his lovely daughter high in the air.
elevate.sentenceTrans: 这位父亲将他可爱的女儿高高举起。
elevate.mnemonic: e出 + lev提高，举起，变轻 + ate动词后缀 → 举出 → elevate升高

elevator.definitionEn: a machine that carries people or goods up and down to different levels in a building or a mine
elevator.sentence: The three people are waiting for the elevator.
elevator.mnemonic: elevat升高 + or名词后缀 → elevator电梯

eleven.mnemonic: e一 + lev留下 + en后缀 → 多出一个 → eleven十一

eleventh.definitionEn: position 11 in a countable series of things

eliminate.definition: 消除，排除；（在比赛中）淘汰；  v.消除，排除
eliminate.definitionEn: to remove or get rid of something/somebody
eliminate.sentence: This device helps me eliminate the weeds in my garden.
eliminate.sentenceTrans: 这个装置帮助我除掉我花园里的杂草。
eliminate.mnemonic: e出 + limin门槛 + ate动词后缀 → eliminate消灭，删除

else.definition: 另外，其他；  adj.别的，其他的
else.definitionEn: different; in addition to something already mentioned
else.sentence: I'm happy, but everybody else is sad.
else.sentenceTrans: 我很高兴，但是别的家伙都苦着一张脸。

elsewhere.definitionEn: in, at or to another place
elsewhere.sentence: I want to move elsewhere because it's too noisy here.
elsewhere.sentenceTrans: 我想搬到别处去，因为这儿太吵了。
elsewhere.mnemonic: else别的 + where地方 → elsewhere在别处

email.definitionEn: (computer science) a system of world-wide electronic communication in which a computer user can compose a message at one terminal that is generated at the recipient's terminal when he logs in
email.sentence: She received several emails and read one of them.
email.sentenceTrans: 她收到了几封邮件，并阅读了其中一封。

embarrass.definitionEn: to make somebody feel shy, awkward or ashamed, especially in a social situation
embarrass.sentence: He embarrassed himself when he didn't have enough funds to cover the payment.
embarrass.sentenceTrans: 买单时显示余额不足，他非常尴尬。
embarrass.mnemonic: em进入…之中，包围 + barrass套子 → 进入套子 → embarrass使难堪

embarrassing.definitionEn: makes you feel shy or ashamed.
embarrassing.sentence: It's too embarrassing to poop with all these kittens watching.
embarrassing.sentenceTrans: 这么多猫看着我蹲坑，实在是太尴尬了……
embarrassing.mnemonic: em进入…之中 ＋ barrass套子 ＋ ing形容词后缀…的 → 进入套中 → embarrassing使人尴尬的；令人为难的

embarrassment.definition: 尴尬；令人难堪的人或事；窘迫
embarrassment.definitionEn: A feeling of self-consciousness, shame, or awkwardness.
embarrassment.sentence: She felt a deep embarrassment when she forgot her speech in the meeting.
embarrassment.sentenceTrans: 她在会议上忘记发言稿时感到非常尴尬。

embassy.definitionEn: the building in which an embassy works
embassy.sentence: The US embassy in the UK is located in London.
embassy.sentenceTrans: 美国驻英大使馆位于伦敦。
embassy.mnemonic: ambi两边，周围 + ass做，代理 + y表名词 → 代理围在一起做事 → embassy大使馆

embrace.definition: 拥抱；欣然接受，乐意采纳；  n.拥抱
embrace.definitionEn: to put your arms around somebody as a sign of love or friendship
embrace.sentence: The Chinese women's football team embraced to celebrate qualifying.
embrace.sentenceTrans: 中国女足运动员们拥抱庆祝晋级。
embrace.mnemonic: em进入 + brace手臂 → embrace拥抱

emerge.definitionEn: to come out of a dark, confined or hidden place
emerge.sentence: A little rabbit emerged from the hole to look for food.
emerge.sentenceTrans: 一只小兔子从洞口钻出来找吃的。
emerge.mnemonic: e出 + merge沉没 → 沉没的东西出现 → emerge浮现

emergency.definitionEn: a sudden serious and dangerous event or situation which needs immediate action to deal with it
emergency.sentence: It's an emergency; get her to the hospital as soon as possible.
emergency.sentenceTrans: 情况紧急，尽快送她去医院。
emergency.mnemonic: e出 + merg沉，没 + ency名词后缀 → emergency突然出现的事情

emission.definitionEn: the production or sending out of light, heat, gas, etc.
emission.sentence: The emissions from the coal power station will pollute the air.
emission.sentenceTrans: 燃煤发电站排放的废气会污染空气。
emission.mnemonic: e向外+miss送、放、发射+ion名词后缀→ emission排放物

emotion.definition: 情绪，情感；感情；强烈的感情；感性
emotion.definitionEn: a strong feeling (such as love, anger, joy, hate, or fear)
emotion.sentence: She expressed different emotions when watching this TV series.
emotion.sentenceTrans: 她看这部电视剧的时候表现出了不同的情绪。
emotion.mnemonic: e出 + mot移动 + ion名词后缀 → 动出[感情] → emotion感情

emotional.definitionEn: connected with people’s feelings (= with the emotions); showing strong emotions, sometimes in a way that other people think is unnecessary
emotional.sentence: She gave an emotional speech at her best friend's wedding.
emotional.sentenceTrans: 她在好朋友的婚礼上发表了一段感人至深的演讲。
emotional.mnemonic: emotion情感 + al形容词后缀 → emotional情感上的

emperor.sentence: In ancient China, the emperor had supreme power.
emperor.sentenceTrans: 在中国古代，皇上有着至高无上的权力。
emperor.mnemonic: emper命令，统治 ＋ or表示人 → 统治者 → emperor皇帝

emphasis.definitionEn: special importance that is given to something
emphasis.sentence: The word has been highlighted to provide emphasis.
emphasis.mnemonic: em进入 + phasis显示 → 进入显示 → emphasis强调

emphasise.definitionEn: to give special importance to something
emphasise.sentence: The teacher emphasised the correct pronunciation of this Chinese character.
emphasise.sentenceTrans: 老师强调了这个汉字的正确发音。

emphasize.definitionEn: to give special importance to (something); to place emphasis on (something)
emphasize.sentence: I want to emphasize the importance of teamwork.
emphasize.sentenceTrans: 我想强调团队合作的重要性。
emphasize.mnemonic: emphasi=emphasis强调 + ize动词后缀 → emphasize强调

employ.definitionEn: to give somebody a job to do for payment
employ.sentence: She employed a babysitter to look after her children.
employ.sentenceTrans: 她雇了个保姆来照顾她的孩子。
employ.mnemonic: em在……里 + ploy折叠 → employ投入，雇佣

employee.definitionEn: a person who is paid to work for somebody
employee.sentence: The employee felt very happy when his boss praised him.
employee.sentenceTrans: 听到老板表扬他，这位员工感到很高兴。

employer.definitionEn: a person or company that pays people to work for them
employer.sentence: The girl is hired by the employer.
employer.mnemonic: employ雇用 + er施动者 → employer雇主

employment.definitionEn: work, especially when it is done to earn money; the state of being employed
employment.sentence: She found employment as an English teacher.
employment.sentenceTrans: 她找到了一份英语老师的工作。
employment.mnemonic: employ雇佣 + ment名词后缀 → employment雇佣

empty.definition: 空的；无意义的，缺乏力量(或效果)的；  v.倒空；腾空
empty.definitionEn: with no people or things inside; (of something that somebody says or does) with no meaning; not meaning what is said
empty.sentence: There are many seats in the meeting room, but they are all empty.
empty.sentenceTrans: 会议室有很多座位，但是都是空的。

enable.definitionEn: to make it possible for somebody to do something; to make it possible for something to happen or exist by creating the necessary conditions
enable.sentence: Vegetables enable me to keep healthy.
enable.mnemonic: en使…进入状态 + able能够 → enable使能够

enclose.definitionEn: (especially of a wall, fence, etc.) to surround something
enclose.sentence: I enclose two tickets along with a letter.

encounter.definitionEn: to meet somebody, or discover or experience something, especially somebody/something new, unusual or unexpected; to experience something, especially something unpleasant or difficult, while you are trying to do something else
encounter.sentence: We encountered a deer in the forest.
encounter.sentenceTrans: 我们在森林里偶遇了一只鹿。
encounter.mnemonic: en在...中 + counter与...相反 → 在某地与反方向的人遇到 → encounter邂逅，偶遇

encourage.definitionEn: to give somebody support, courage or hope
encourage.sentence: My teacher always encouraged me to pursue my passion for music.
encourage.sentenceTrans: 我的老师总是鼓励我追求对音乐的热爱。
encourage.mnemonic: en加强 + courage内心的力量=勇气 → encourage鼓励

encouragement.definitionEn: the act of encouraging somebody to do something; something that encourages somebody
encouragement.sentence: The trainer offered words of encouragement to the girl as she was running.
encouragement.sentenceTrans: 女孩跑步的时候，教练用言语鼓励她。
encouragement.mnemonic: encourage鼓励 + ment表名词 → encouragement鼓励

end.definition: 末端，终点；终止，结束；末端；尽头；末尾；目的，目标；  v.结束；终止，结束
end.definitionEn: to finish; to make something finish
end.sentence: She is at the end of the queue.

endanger.definitionEn: to put somebody/something in a situation in which they could be harmed or damaged
endanger.sentence: Cutting down trees will endanger the habitats of many animals.
endanger.sentenceTrans: 砍伐树木会危及许多动物的家园。
endanger.mnemonic: en使…进入状态 + danger危险 → 使危险

endless.definitionEn: continuing for a long time and seeming to have no end
endless.sentence: There is an endless supply of pickles in the kitchen.
endless.sentenceTrans: 厨房里的咸菜无限量供应。
endless.mnemonic: end结束 + less无…的 → endless无止境的

endurance.definitionEn: the ability to deal with pain or suffering that continues for a long time
endurance.sentence: It takes great endurance to do this exercise.
endurance.sentenceTrans: 做这项锻炼需要很强的耐力。
endurance.mnemonic: endur忍耐 + ance表性质 → endurance忍耐力

endure.definitionEn: to experience and deal with something that is painful or unpleasant, especially without complaining
endure.sentence: It is very hard to endure the toothache.
endure.mnemonic: en艰难 + dure使……艰难 → endure度过，忍受

enemy.definitionEn: a person who hates somebody or who acts or speaks against somebody/something
enemy.sentence: The man who holds the pan is her enemy.
enemy.sentenceTrans: 拿着平底锅的男人是她的敌人。
enemy.mnemonic: en不是 + emy朋友 → enemy敌人

energetic.definition: 精力充沛的，充满活力的
energetic.definitionEn: having or showing a lot of energy
energetic.sentence: Her energetic dance makes her hair go back.
energetic.sentenceTrans: 她充满活力的舞蹈让她的头发向后甩动。
energetic.mnemonic: energ活力 + etic形容词后缀 → energetic充满活力的

energy.definitionEn: the capacity of acting or being active
energy.sentence: The panels use solar energy to make electricity.
energy.sentenceTrans: 这些板子能够用太阳能发电。
energy.mnemonic: en在...上 + ergy功 → energy 能量

enforce.definitionEn: to make sure that people obey a particular law or rule
enforce.sentence: The new parking restrictions will be strictly enforced.
enforce.sentenceTrans: 新的停车规定将被严格执行。
enforce.mnemonic: en进入 + force强大，力量 → 进入力量 → 强行

enforcement.definitionEn: the act of enforcing; insuring observance of or obedience to
enforcement.sentence: The police are responsible for the enforcement of the law.

engage.definition: 参加；（军队）交战；使从事；吸引住（注意力、兴趣）；与......建立密切关系
engage.definitionEn: to become involved with and try to understand something/somebody
engage.sentence: She used to exercise alone, but now she engages in the group running.
engage.sentenceTrans: 她过去常常独自锻炼，但现在她加入了集体跑步的行列。
engage.mnemonic: en进入，使 + gage承诺 → 使人承诺（以加入）→ engage加入，参加

engagement.definitionEn: an agreement to marry somebody; the period during which two people are engaged
engagement.sentence: We announced our engagement last week, so now everybody knows we're getting married.
engagement.sentenceTrans: 我们上周宣布了订婚的消息，所以现在大家都知道我们要结婚了。
engagement.mnemonic: en在…中 + gage承诺 + ment名词后缀 → engagement订婚

engine.definitionEn: the part of a vehicle that produces power to make the vehicle move
engine.sentence: The engine at the front of the car makes the car move.
engine.sentenceTrans: 汽车前部的引擎使汽车移动。
engine.mnemonic: en=in内部 + gine生育 → engine引擎

engineer.definition: 工程师；技师；火车司机；  v.设计；建造
engineer.definitionEn: a person whose job involves designing and building engines, machines, roads, bridges, etc.; a person who is trained to repair machines and electrical equipment
engineer.sentence: The two engineers are discussing their new building plans.
engineer.sentenceTrans: 这两个工程师正在讨论新的建筑计划。
engineer.mnemonic: engine发动机 + er人 → engineer工程师

engineering.definitionEn: the activity of applying scientific knowledge to the design, building and control of machines, roads, bridges, electrical equipment, etc.
engineering.sentence: All the workers are trying to solve the engineering problem.
engineering.sentenceTrans: 所有工人都尝试着解决这个工程问题。
engineering.mnemonic: engineer工程师 + ing表名词 → engineering工程、工程师行业

enhance.definition: 提高（强度、力量、数量等）；增强
enhance.definitionEn: to increase or further improve the good quality, value or status of somebody/something
enhance.sentence: My colleague helps me to enhance my working skills.
enhance.sentenceTrans: 我的同事帮助我提升工作技能。

enjoy.definitionEn: to get pleasure from something; to be happy and get pleasure from what you are doing; to have something good that is an advantage to you
enjoy.sentence: A birthday party should be an event everyone can enjoy.
enjoy.sentenceTrans: 生日派对应该是每个人都能享受的事情。
enjoy.mnemonic: en进入 + joy高兴 → 做高兴的事 → enjoy享受

enjoyment.definitionEn: a feeling of pleasure caused by doing or experiencing something you like
enjoyment.sentence: He's eating the hamburgers with great enjoyment.
enjoyment.sentenceTrans: 他十分愉快地吃着汉堡。
enjoyment.mnemonic: enjoy享受 + ment名词后缀 → enjoyment 享受

enlarge.definitionEn: to make something bigger; to become bigger; to make a bigger copy of a photograph or document
enlarge.sentence: The doctor advised surgery if the tumor continued to enlarge.
enlarge.sentenceTrans: 医生建议如果肿瘤继续增大就进行手术。

enlighten.definitionEn: to give somebody information so that they understand something better
enlighten.sentence: The teacher really enlightens her students.
enlighten.sentenceTrans: 这个老师的确启发了她的学生。
enlighten.mnemonic: en使…进入状态 + light光 + en表动词，使变成 → 给人光明 → 启发

enlightened.definition: 开明的；  v.动词enlighten的过去式和过去分词.
enlightened.definitionEn: people who have been introduced to the mysteries of some field or activity
enlightened.sentence: The teacher's words made me at once become enlightened.
enlightened.sentenceTrans: 老师的一席话使我顿开茅塞。

enormous.definition: 庞大的，巨大的；（范围、程度）极大的；庞大的
enormous.definitionEn: very great in size or amount
enormous.sentence: The little girl was shocked by the enormous dog.
enormous.sentenceTrans: 小女孩被这只巨大的狗震惊了。
enormous.mnemonic: e出 + norm规则，规范 + ous形容词后缀 → 超出了正常状态 → enormous巨大的

enough.definition: 足够的；  adv.足够地；  pron.很多
enough.definitionEn: used before plural or uncountable nouns to mean ‘as many or as much as somebody needs or wants’
enough.sentence: No, no, no, I already have enough food.
enough.sentenceTrans: 别给我夹菜了，已经够多了。

enquire.definitionEn: to ask somebody for some information
enquire.sentence: Please enquire at the reception desk.
enquire.mnemonic: en=in进入 + quire询问 → enquire询问

enquiry.definitionEn: a request for information about somebody/something; a question about somebody/something; an official process to find out the cause of something or to find out information about something
enquiry.sentence: The police made several enquiries about the theft with the passers-by.
enquiry.sentenceTrans: 警察向路人询问了很多关于这起盗窃案的问题。
enquiry.mnemonic: en=in在里面 + quir询问 +y表名词 → enquiry询问

enrich.definitionEn: to improve the quality of something, often by adding something to it
enrich.sentence: He used his position to enrich himself.
enrich.mnemonic: en使成某种状态 + rich富裕 → enrich使富裕

ensure.definitionEn: to make sure that something happens or is definite
ensure.sentence: The swimming rings could ensure the safety of the pigs.
ensure.sentenceTrans: 这些游泳圈可以保证小猪们的安全。
ensure.mnemonic: en使 + sure确定 → ensure 保证

enter.sentence: Two men and a woman are entering the building.
enter.sentenceTrans: 两男一女正在走进大楼。

enterprise.sentence: This small enterprise specializes in milk.
enterprise.mnemonic: enter进入 + prise拿住，抓住 → 进入抓住 → enterprise事业，进取心

enterprising.definition: 有事业心的，有进取心的，有魅力的，有胆量的
enterprising.definitionEn: having or showing the ability or desire to do new and difficult things
enterprising.sentence: The enterprising boss has mentioned many financial targets and ambitious ideas.
enterprising.sentenceTrans: 极具事业心的老板提到了许多财务目标和自己的雄心壮志。
enterprising.mnemonic: enter进入+pris拿住，抓住+ing名词后缀 → 进入抓住目标的 → 有事业心的

entertain.definition: 使欢乐；招待，款待；心存，怀有
entertain.definitionEn: to interest and amuse somebody in order to please them
entertain.sentence: The woman plays the clown to entertain children at the party.
entertain.sentenceTrans: 这个女人扮成小丑在派对上逗孩子们开心。
entertain.mnemonic: enter在……中间 + tain拥有 → entertain娱乐

entertainment.definitionEn: films/movies, music, etc. used to entertain people; an example of this
entertainment.sentence: Which kind of entertainment do you enjoy? Games, movies, or TV?
entertainment.sentenceTrans: 你喜欢哪种娱乐方式，玩游戏、看电影，还是看电视？
entertainment.mnemonic: entertain娱乐，款待 + ment表名词 → entertainment娱乐；款待

enthusiasm.definitionEn: a strong feeling of excitement and interest in something and a desire to become involved in it
enthusiasm.sentence: Those kids always have so much enthusiasm about studying.
enthusiasm.sentenceTrans: 这些孩子总是对学习充满热情。
enthusiasm.mnemonic: en进入 + thus = theo神 + iasm状态 → 进入神的状态 → 热情

enthusiastic.definition: 狂热的，极感兴趣的；热情的
enthusiastic.definitionEn: feeling or showing a lot of excitement and interest about somebody/something
enthusiastic.mnemonic: en在...中 + thusi上天，天神 + astic形容词后缀 → 对宗教的虔诚信仰 → enthusiastic热情的，狂热的

entire.definitionEn: (used when you are emphasizing that the whole of something is involved) including everything, everyone or every part
entire.sentence: There's half a chocolate pie and an entire lemon cake on the shelf.
entire.sentenceTrans: 架子上有半个巧克力派和一整块柠檬蛋糕。
entire.mnemonic: en进 + tire紧 → 全部靠紧，挤进去 → entire全部的，完整的，整个的

entirely.definitionEn: to a complete degree or to the full or entire extent ('whole' is often used informally for 'wholly')
entirely.sentence: He agreed entirely with what his colleague said.
entirely.sentenceTrans: 他完全同意他的同事所说的话。

entitle.definitionEn: to give a title to a book, play, etc.
entitle.sentence: The book is entitled The Journey to the West.
entitle.sentenceTrans: 这本书被命名为《西游记》。
entitle.mnemonic: en=in在里面 + title名称 → entitle给...命名；赋予权利

entrance.definition: 入口，通道；出场，登场；  v.使出神，使入迷
entrance.definitionEn: a door, gate, passage, etc. used for entering a room, building or place
entrance.sentence: Children are gathering at the entrance of the park.
entrance.sentenceTrans: 孩子们在公园的入口处集合。
entrance.mnemonic: entr=enter进入 + ance表名词，状态、行为 → entrance入口；进入，入学

entry.definition: 进入；参与；条目，（日记的）一则；参赛；入口处
entry.definitionEn: the act of recording information in a computer, book, etc.
entry.sentence: He made his entry into the meeting room.

envelope.definitionEn: a flat paper container used for sending letters in; any wrapper or covering; the bag containing the gas in a balloon
envelope.sentence: The letter is put into the red envelope.
envelope.sentenceTrans: 信被放在了红色信封里。
envelope.mnemonic: en表示"进入…之中，包围" + velop=cover（盖上） + e → envelope信封，封套

envious.definitionEn: wanting to be in the same situation as somebody else; wanting something that somebody else has
envious.sentence: My dog is always envious of our dinner.
envious.sentenceTrans: 我的狗总是羡慕我们能吃到那样的晚餐。
envious.mnemonic: env羡慕 + ious形容词后缀 → envious羡慕的

environment.definitionEn: the natural world in which people, animals and plants live
environment.sentence: They are picking up trash to keep the environment clean.
environment.sentenceTrans: 为了保持环境整洁，他们正在捡垃圾。
environment.mnemonic: environ包围，环绕 + ment表名词 → environment环境

environmental.definitionEn: connected with the natural conditions in which people, animals and plants live; connected with the environment
environmental.sentence: This meeting is about environmental protection.
environmental.sentenceTrans: 本次会议是关于环境保护的。
environmental.mnemonic: environment环境 + al形容词后缀 → environmental环境的

envy.definitionEn: the feeling of wanting to be in the same situation as somebody else; the feeling of wanting something that somebody else has
envy.sentence: The baby girl envies her sister for having toys.
envy.sentenceTrans: 小女孩羡慕姐姐有玩具。
envy.mnemonic: en使 + vy=vid看到别人 → 妒忌

equal.definition: 平等的；相等的；  v.比得上；  n.同等的人
equal.definitionEn: having the same rights or being treated the same as other people, without differences such as race, religion or sex being considered
equal.sentence: Today, men and women are equal before the law.
equal.sentenceTrans: 如今，男女在法律面前是平等的。
equal.mnemonic: equ相等，平均 + al形容词后缀 → 相等的，平等的

equality.definitionEn: the fact of being equal in rights, status, advantages, etc.
equality.sentence: This picture shows the equality between men and women.
equality.sentenceTrans: 这张照片显示了男性与女性的平等。
equality.mnemonic: equal相等的 + ity名词后缀 → equality平等

equally.definitionEn: to the same degree; in the same or in a similar way
equally.sentence: Men and women should be treated equally.
equally.mnemonic: equ相等 ＋ ally...地 → equally同样地；相等地

equip.sentence: The worker equips himself with several items.
equip.sentenceTrans: 这名工人身上装备了好几样东西。

equipment.definitionEn: the things that are needed for a particular purpose or activity
equipment.sentence: Students now enjoy using the exercise equipment for working out.
equipment.sentenceTrans: 现在的学生喜欢使用健身器材运动。
equipment.mnemonic: equip配备，装备 + ment表名词 → equipment设备

equivalent.definition: 相等的；等值的；  n.等价物
equivalent.definitionEn: equal in value, amount, meaning, importance, etc.
equivalent.sentence: The weight of three small balls is equivalent to that of this large one.
equivalent.sentenceTrans: 三个小球的重量与这个大球的重量相等。
equivalent.mnemonic: equi相等，平均 + val力量 + ent形容词后缀→ 力量平等 → 相等的，等价的

era.definitionEn: a period of time that is associated with a particular quality, event, person, etc.
era.sentence: These kinds of costumes were quite popular in the Victorian era.
era.sentenceTrans: 这些装束在维多利亚时代非常流行。

erect.definition: 建造，建立；  adj.直立的，垂直的
erect.definitionEn: to build something; to put something in position and make it stand vertical
erect.sentence: The workers are busy erecting the building.
erect.mnemonic: e向外，向上 + rect指领 → erect建立

erode.definitionEn: to gradually destroy the surface of something through the action of wind, rain, etc.; to be gradually destroyed in this way
erode.sentence: The statue has been steadily eroded by acid rain and lost its face.
erode.sentenceTrans: 这座雕像已被酸雨逐渐侵蚀，失去了它的脸。
erode.mnemonic: e出 + rode咬 → 咬出去 → 侵蚀

error.definitionEn: a mistake, especially one that causes problems or affects the result of something
error.sentence: If you make an error, you can just erase it and write again.
error.sentenceTrans: 如果你写错了，擦掉重写就好了。
error.mnemonic: err错误 + or行为，状况 → error错误

escape.definition: 逃跑，逃脱；  n.逃跑，逃脱
escape.definitionEn: to get away from a place where you have been kept as a prisoner or not allowed to leave; to get away from an unpleasant or dangerous situation; to avoid something unpleasant or dangerous;
escape.sentence: The bird escapes from the cage.
escape.mnemonic: es向外 + cape帽子，斗篷 → 从斗篷里钻出来 → escape逃跑，逃脱

especially.sentence: The little girl loves drinking juice, especially orange juice.
especially.sentenceTrans: 小女孩很爱喝果汁，尤其是橙汁。
especially.mnemonic: especial特别的 + ly副词后缀 → especially特别地

essay.definitionEn: a short piece of writing by a student as part of a course of study
essay.sentence: The girl is busy writing her essay right now.
essay.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩正忙着写她的论文。
essay.mnemonic: ess=ex向外 + ay启动，开动 → essay企图

essential.definition: 必不可少的，极其重要的；本质的；基本的；  n.必需品
essential.definitionEn: completely necessary; extremely important in a particular situation or for a particular activity
essential.sentence: Hot pot and mahjong are essential components of Sichuan culture.
essential.sentenceTrans: 火锅和麻将是四川文化必不可少的一部分。
essential.mnemonic: essent存在，本质 + ial ...的 → essential必要的，本质的

establish.definition: 建立；确立；创立，成立；使确认
establish.definitionEn: to start having a relationship, especially a formal one, with another person, group or country
establish.sentence: The two businessmen are trying to establish links.
establish.sentenceTrans: 这两个商人在试图建立联系。
establish.mnemonic: e缓音字母，无含义 + stablish使稳固 → establish建立

establishment.definitionEn: the act of forming or establishing something
establishment.sentence: He cut the ribbon at the grand opening of the establishment.
establishment.sentenceTrans: 在这场盛大的开幕仪式上，他负责剪彩。
establishment.mnemonic: establish建立 + ment名词后缀 → establishment 建立

estate.definitionEn: a large area of land, usually in the country, that is owned by one person or family; an area of land with a lot of houses or factories of the same type on it; all the money and property that a person owns, especially everything that is left when they die
estate.sentence: She lives in a castle on an estate in London.
estate.sentenceTrans: 她住在伦敦一处庄园的城堡里。
estate.mnemonic: e出 + stat站着 + e强调 → 站出来的东西 → estate房子等不动产

esteem.definitionEn: great respect and admiration; a good opinion of somebody
esteem.sentence: Investors esteem a strong financial performance in a company.
esteem.sentenceTrans: 投资者看重公司的强大财务表现。
esteem.mnemonic: esteem=estim价值 → 有价值 → 仰慕 → esteem尊敬

estimate.definition: 估价，估计；  n.估价，估计
estimate.definitionEn: to form an idea of the cost, size, value etc. of something, but without calculating it exactly
estimate.sentence: The man is estimating the value of the watch.
estimate.sentenceTrans: 这个男人在给这块手表估价。
estimate.mnemonic: estim估计 + ate动词后缀 → estimate估计

ethic.definitionEn: the principles of right and wrong that are accepted by an individual or a social group
ethic.sentence: Anti-doping is an important code of ethics in sports.
ethic.sentenceTrans: 反兴奋剂是体育界的一条重要道德准则。

evade.definitionEn: to escape from somebody/something or avoid meeting somebody
evade.sentence: She tried to evade the embarrassing questions that the journalists asked.
evade.sentenceTrans: 她尽力回避记者提出的令人尴尬的问题。
evade.mnemonic: e出，出来 + vade走 → 走出去 → 逃避

evaluate.definitionEn: to form an opinion of the amount, value or quality of something after thinking about it carefully
evaluate.sentence: They evaluated our performance and thought it was good.
evaluate.sentenceTrans: 他们评价了我们的表演，认为很不错。
evaluate.mnemonic: e使 + valu价值 + ate动词后缀 → 使……定价 → evaluate估价

evaluation.definition: 评价；口头（或书面）评估；估价
evaluation.definitionEn: the act of forming an opinion of the amount, value or quality of something after thinking about it carefully
evaluation.sentence: Customers can make an online evaluation of the service they received.
evaluation.sentenceTrans: 客户可以在线评估他们接受的服务。
evaluation.mnemonic: e使 + valu价值 + ation名词后缀 → evaluation评估，估价

eve.definitionEn: the day or evening before an event, especially a religious festival or holiday; evening
eve.sentence: We set off some fireworks on New Year's Eve.
eve.sentenceTrans: 我们在新年前夜放了一些烟花。

even.definition: 甚至更加；  adj.偶数的；平坦的；  v.使打平，使相等
even.definitionEn: (of an amount of something) equal or the same for each person, team, place, etc.
even.sentence: She was even more tired after reading the e-mail.
even.sentenceTrans: 读完这封邮件之后她甚至更疲惫了。

evening.definitionEn: the part of the day between the afternoon and the time you go to bed
evening.sentence: In the evening, we watched the sunset by the beach.
evening.sentenceTrans: 傍晚，我们在沙滩边看日落。

event.definitionEn: one of the races or competitions in a sports programme
event.sentence: The "911 incident" was an event that shocked the world.
event.mnemonic: e向外 + vent到来 → event事件

eventually.definitionEn: at some later time; in the end
eventually.sentence: After weeks of hard study, he eventually got a satisfying result.
eventually.sentenceTrans: 经过几周的刻苦学习，他终于得到了令人满意的结果。
eventually.mnemonic: eventual最后的 + ly 表示方式、程度、状态、“...地” → adv.终于；最后

ever.definitionEn: used in negative sentences and questions, or sentences with if to mean ‘at any time’
ever.sentence: Have you ever been on a hot air balloon?

every.definitionEn: used with singular nouns to refer to all the members of a group of things or people
every.sentenceTrans: 不是每一个商人都值得相信。

everybody.sentenceTrans: 每个人都很享受瑜伽课。
everybody.mnemonic: every每个 + body人 → everybody每人，人人

everyday.definitionEn: used or happening every day or regularly; ordinary
everyday.sentence: Doing exercise and keeping a healthy diet have become my everyday life.
everyday.sentenceTrans: 做运动和坚持健康的饮食已经成了我的日常生活。
everyday.mnemonic: every每个的 + day天 → everyday每天的，日常的

everyone.sentence: Everyone in the world should care about the planet.
everyone.sentenceTrans: 世界上的每个人都应该关爱地球。
everyone.mnemonic: every每 + one一个人 → everyone每个人

everything.definitionEn: to refer to all the objects, actions, activities, or facts in a particular situation
everything.sentence: The man had eaten everything in the fridge.
everything.sentenceTrans: 那个男人把冰箱里的所有东西都吃光了。

everywhere.definitionEn: in, to or at every place; all places
everywhere.sentence: I want to travel everywhere in the world.
everywhere.sentenceTrans: 我想走遍世界的每个角落。

evidence.definition: 证物；证据，证明；  v.证明
evidence.definitionEn: the facts, signs or objects that make you believe that something is true
evidence.sentence: Keep every piece of evidence to help us solve the crime.
evidence.sentenceTrans: 保留所有的证据来帮助我们破案。
evidence.mnemonic: e出 + vid看 + ence表名词 → 明显的证据 → evidence证据，证人

evident.definitionEn: clear to the sight or mind
evident.sentence: It's evident that the salesman is lying.
evident.sentenceTrans: 很明显这个推销员在说谎。
evident.mnemonic: e易于的 + vident看 → evident明显的

evidently.definitionEn: clearly; that can be seen or understood easily
evidently.sentence: Evidently, it was my cat who ate my dinner!
evidently.sentenceTrans: 很显然，我的猫偷吃了我的晚餐！
evidently.mnemonic: evident明显的 + ly副词后缀 → evidently显然地，显然

evil.definition: 邪恶的；  n.邪恶，罪恶，恶行
evil.definitionEn: (of people) enjoying harming others; morally bad and cruel
evil.sentence: This evil monster has a devilish stare.
evil.sentenceTrans: 这个邪恶的怪物眼中闪过一丝魔鬼般的光芒。
