evil.mnemonic: e加强或引申意义、使… + vil=base（卑劣的）→ evil邪恶；罪恶的

evoke.definitionEn: to bring a feeling, a memory or an image into your mind
evoke.sentence: This picture evokes feelings of summer.
evoke.sentenceTrans: 这张照片唤起了夏天的感觉。
evoke.mnemonic: e出 + voke=vok呼喊，声，召集 → 喊出思想 → evoke唤醒

evolution.definitionEn: (biology) the gradual development of plants, animals, etc. over many years as they adapt to changes in their environment
evolution.sentence: The theory of evolution is a wonderful explanation of how life arose.
evolution.sentenceTrans: 进化论是关于生命如何产生的精彩阐释。
evolution.mnemonic: e出 + volu转 + tion表名词 → evolution进化

evolutionary.definitionEn: of or pertaining to evolution or development
evolutionary.sentence: The chart shows the evolutionary process of phones.
evolutionary.sentenceTrans: 这张图表显示了手机的进化过程。
evolutionary.mnemonic: e出+volu=vol转+tion表名词 + ary ...的 →evolution进化 + ary ...的 → 进化的，演进的

evolve.definitionEn: to develop gradually, especially from a simple to a more complicated form
evolve.sentence: Even today, the human race continues to evolve.
evolve.sentenceTrans: 直到今天，人类都还在持续进化中。
evolve.mnemonic: e出 + volve旋转，卷 → 转出来 → evolve使发展，使进化

exact.definitionEn: correct in every detail; (of people) very accurate and careful about details; (of a science) using accurate measurements and following set rules
exact.sentence: The exact height of the tree is 5.386 meters.
exact.sentenceTrans: 这棵树的确切高度是5.386米。
exact.mnemonic: ex出，向外 + act启动，驱动 → 明确执行某事 → exact确切的

exactly.definitionEn: used to emphasize that something is correct in every way or in every detail
exactly.sentence: I want all my grass to be exactly the same height.
exactly.sentenceTrans: 我要我的草都完全一样高。
exactly.mnemonic: exact精确的 + ly副词后缀 → exactly精确地

exaggerate.definitionEn: to make something seem larger, better, worse or more important than it really is
exaggerate.sentence: The sheep exaggerated the size of the wolf when retelling the story to his friends.
exaggerate.sentenceTrans: 这只羊在向朋友们复述这个故事时夸大了狼的体型。
exaggerate.mnemonic: ex使…，加强意义 + agger堆积 + ate动词后缀 → exaggerate夸大

examination.definitionEn: inquiry; a close and careful study of someone or something to find signs of illness or injury
examination.sentence: The students are taking an examination.
examination.mnemonic: examin检查 + ation名词后缀 → examination检查

examine.definitionEn: to look at somebody/something closely, to see if there is anything wrong or to find the cause of a problem
examine.sentence: I took my dog to the vet to be examined.
examine.sentenceTrans: 我带我的狗去兽医那里检查。
examine.mnemonic: ex向外 + act做，驱使，称量 → (拼写受example影响) → examine检查，测验

example.definitionEn: a person or way of behaving that is seen as a model that should be followed
example.sentence: The math example was completed by Mr. Li.
example.sentenceTrans: 这道数学例题是李老师完成的。
example.mnemonic: ex出 + ample拿，获得 → 拿出来作为榜样 → example 样本,榜样

exceed.definitionEn: to do more than the law or an order, etc. allows you to do
exceed.sentence: The temperature is expected to exceed 90 degrees Fahrenheit today.
exceed.sentenceTrans: 今天的气温预计会超过90华氏度。
exceed.mnemonic: ex向外 + ceed去；让步 → exceed超出

excellent.sentence: He's an excellent student who always gets excellent scores.
excellent.sentenceTrans: 他是一名优秀的学生，总是得高分。
excellent.mnemonic: ex离开 + cell监狱 + ent…的 → 品德优秀的人离监狱很远 → excellent杰出的

except.definition: 除了，只是；  v.把……除外；  prep.除……之外
except.definitionEn: used before you mention the only thing or person about which a statement is not true
except.sentence: Except for the color, these two cars are identical.
except.sentenceTrans: 除了颜色，这两辆车完全一样。
except.mnemonic: ex向外 + cept拿走 → 把东西拿走 → except除了

exception.definitionEn: a person or thing that is not included in a general statement; a thing that does not follow a rule
exception.sentence: Most of the buildings are modern, but the quadrangle is the only exception.
exception.sentenceTrans: 这些大多是现代建筑，不过这座四合院是唯一的例外。
exception.mnemonic: ex出 + cept拿，抓，握住 + ion名词后缀 → exception除外

excess.definitionEn: in addition to an amount that is necessary, usual or legal
excess.sentence: There is an excess of food for only one person.
excess.sentenceTrans: 这些食物对于一个人而言过多了。
excess.mnemonic: ex出 + cess行走 → excess过度，过剩

excessive.definitionEn: greater than what seems reasonable or appropriate
excessive.sentence: Excessive food intake made the cat overweight.
excessive.sentenceTrans: 贪食使得这只猫超重了。
excessive.mnemonic: ex出，出去 + cess行走 + ive形容词后缀 → excessive过度的

exchange.definition: 交流；交换；交易；  n.交易所
exchange.definitionEn: to give something to somebody and at the same time receive the same type of thing from them
exchange.sentence: People can exchange their thoughts and ideas.
exchange.sentenceTrans: 人们可以交换他们的思想和想法。
exchange.mnemonic: ex出 + change交换 → exchange交换，交流

excite.definitionEn: to make somebody feel very pleased, interested or enthusiastic, especially about something that is going to happen
excite.sentence: The message she received excited her.
excite.sentenceTrans: 她收到的信息让她很激动。
excite.mnemonic: ex使…出自 + cite使开始工作 → excite激发

excited.definitionEn: feeling or showing happiness and enthusiasm
excited.sentence: Joey was excited when he saw himself on TV.
excited.sentenceTrans: 乔伊看到自己出现在电视上，兴奋极了。
excited.mnemonic: excit使兴奋 + ed形容词后缀 → excited 兴奋的

excitement.definitionEn: the state of feeling excited; something that you find exciting
excitement.sentence: She couldn't control her excitement at receiving the message.
excitement.sentenceTrans: 她无法控制她收到信息时的兴奋。
excitement.mnemonic: excite使兴奋 + ment名词后缀 → excitement兴奋

exciting.definitionEn: causing feelings of interest and enthusiasm; causing excitement
exciting.sentence: It was really exciting when she got into the cat's house.
exciting.sentenceTrans: 对小春来说，进入这个小版的猫事务所十分令人兴奋。
exciting.mnemonic: excit使兴奋 + ing形容词后缀 → exciting使人兴奋的

exclaim.definitionEn: to say something suddenly and loudly, especially because of strong emotion or pain
exclaim.sentence: "Help!" the woman exclaimed as the man stole her bag.
exclaim.sentenceTrans: 这个男人偷了她的包，她大喊：“帮帮我！”
exclaim.mnemonic: ex出 + claim叫喊 → exclaim叫喊，大声说

exclude.definitionEn: to prevent (someone) from doing something or being a part of a group; to decide or prove that it is wrong and not worth considering.
exclude.sentence: He was excluded by other teenagers.
exclude.mnemonic: ex向外 + clude关 → 关在外面 → exclude不包括

exclusive.definitionEn: (of a group, society, etc.) not very willing to allow new people to become members, especially if they are from a lower social class
exclusive.sentence: Sorry, this club is very exclusive: VIPs only.
exclusive.sentenceTrans: 对不起，这家俱乐部只接受VIP会员。
exclusive.mnemonic: exclu(de)排除 + sive形容词后缀 → exclusive专有的，排外的

excursion.definition: 远足；（尤指集体度假时的）短途旅行
excursion.definitionEn: a short journey made for pleasure, especially one that has been organized for a group of people
excursion.sentence: We took an excursion into the forest.
excursion.mnemonic: ex出+curs跑，发生+ion行为 → 远足；游览

excuse.definition: 借口；  v.表示宽恕（读作/ɪkˈskjuːz/）；原谅；辩解
excuse.definitionEn: a reason, either true or invented, that you give to explain or defend your behaviour
excuse.sentence: He made up a stupid excuse for not doing homework.
excuse.sentenceTrans: 他为没做作业编了个愚蠢的借口。
excuse.mnemonic: ex远离 + cuse指控 → 逃脱指控 → excuse借口

execute.definition: 处决，处死；完成（动作）；实行；执行（计划）
execute.definitionEn: to kill somebody or something, especially as a legal punishment
execute.sentence: This pathetic bird is going to be executed by the cruel hunter.
execute.sentenceTrans: 这只可怜的小鸟将要被残酷的猎人处决了。
execute.mnemonic: ex向外 + (s)ec跟随，相接 + ute → 一步接一步的执行 → 实施，将……处死

executive.definition: 经理；执行者；行政人员；  adj.执行的
executive.definitionEn: a person who has an important job as a manager of a company or an organization
executive.sentence: The executives of both companies discussed the issue in depth.
executive.sentenceTrans: 双方公司的经理深入地讨论了这个问题。
executive.mnemonic: execut执行 + ive名词后缀 → executive执行者

exercise.definition: 操练，运动；活动；锻炼；  v.行使，运用；锻炼
exercise.definitionEn: physical activity that is done in order to become stronger and healthier
exercise.sentence: Exercise is the key to keeping healthy.
exercise.sentenceTrans: 锻炼是保持健康的关键。
exercise.mnemonic: ex出 + erc力量 + ise表名词，物品，状态 → exercise练习，锻炼

exert.definitionEn: to use power or influence to affect somebody/something; to make a big physical or mental effort
exert.sentence: I exerted all my strength to lift all the boxes.
exert.sentenceTrans: 我用尽全力抬起所有箱子。
exert.mnemonic: ex向外 + ert连接 → exert尽力

exhaust.definition: 使筋疲力尽；耗尽；详尽论述；  n.排气装置；废气
exhaust.definitionEn: to use all of someone's mental or physical energy; to tire out or wear out (someone) completely
exhaust.mnemonic: ex完全 + haust抽出 → exhaust用尽，耗尽

exhausted.definitionEn: completely used or finished; very tired
exhausted.sentence: I am exhausted after a long day of work.
exhausted.sentenceTrans: 一天的工作后，我感到精疲力竭。
exhausted.mnemonic: exhaust使精疲力竭 + ed形容词后缀 → exhausted 精疲力竭的

exhibit.definition: 展览会，陈列品；  v.展览，陈列
exhibit.definitionEn: a collection of things, for example works of art, that are shown to the public
exhibit.sentence: Let's go to see the Picasso exhibit tomorrow.
exhibit.sentenceTrans: 我们明天去看毕加索的展览吧。
exhibit.mnemonic: ex出 + hibit拿住 → 拿来 → exhibit展览，显示

exhibition.definitionEn: an event at which objects (such as works of art) are put out in a public space for people to look at; a public show of something
exhibition.sentence: They are visiting a new oil painting exhibition.
exhibition.sentenceTrans: 他们正在参观一场新的油画展览。
exhibition.mnemonic: ex出 + hibit拿住 + ion名词后缀 → 拿出去给人看 → 展览；陈列

exist.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) to be real; to be present in a place or situation
exist.sentence: Do aliens exist on other planets?
exist.sentenceTrans: 其他星球上会有外星人存在吗？
exist.mnemonic: ex出 + ist站立 → 站出来 → 活下来 → exist存在，生存

existence.definitionEn: the state or fact of being real or living or of being present
existence.sentence: These fossils prove the existence of dinosaurs.
existence.sentenceTrans: 这些化石证明了恐龙的存在。
existence.mnemonic: exist存在 + ence名词后缀 → existence存在

exit.definitionEn: a way out of a public building or vehicle
exit.sentence: You can find the exit by following the green light.
exit.sentenceTrans: 跟着绿灯走，你就能找到出口。

expand.definitionEn: to become greater in size, number or importance; if a business expands or is expanded, new branches are opened, it makes more money, etc.
expand.sentence: Our business is expanding across the whole country.
expand.sentenceTrans: 我们的业务正在全国范围内扩大。
expand.mnemonic: ex出 + pand展开，膨胀 → expand伸展

expansion.definitionEn: an act of increasing or making something increase in size, amount or importance
expansion.sentence: The abnormal expansion of the left ventricle was observed on the echocardiogram.
expansion.sentenceTrans: 超声心动图上发现左心室异常扩张。
expansion.mnemonic: ex出 + pans扩展 + ion表示名词，构成抽象名词 → 扩张，expanse扩大

expansive.definitionEn: growing quickly or steadily :marked by expansion
expansive.sentence: The horses are grazing on the expansive grassy land.
expansive.sentenceTrans: 马儿在广阔的草地上撒欢。

expect.definitionEn: to think or believe that something will happen or that somebody will do something
expect.sentence: The little rabbit is expecting the girl to feed it carrots.
expect.sentenceTrans: 小兔子正期待着女孩喂它吃胡萝卜。
expect.mnemonic: ex出 + pect=spect看 → 看出去 → expect期待

expectation.definitionEn: a belief that something will happen because it is likely
expectation.sentence: My parents have high expectations of me.
expectation.sentenceTrans: 我的父母对我有很高的期待。
expectation.mnemonic: expect期待 + ation表名词 → 期待，希望

expend.definitionEn: to use or spend a lot of time, money, energy, etc.
expend.sentence: I would expend my savings on a car.
expend.sentenceTrans: 我会花光存款来买一辆车。
expend.mnemonic: ex出 + pend花费 → 花钱出去 → expend花费

expenditure.definitionEn: the act of spending or using money; an amount of money spent; the use of energy, time, materials, etc.
expenditure.sentence: Our company needs to cut down on unnecessary expenditure.
expenditure.sentenceTrans: 我们公司需要削减不必要的支出。
expenditure.mnemonic: ex出 + pendi=pend花费 + ture表名词 → expenditure支出，开销

expense.definitionEn: the money that you spend on something
expense.sentence: Buying a car can be a great expense.
expense.mnemonic: ex出 + pense付钱 → expense支出，花费，消费

expensive.definition: 昂贵的，价格高的，花钱多的
expensive.sentence: These are so expensive! You shouldn't have bought them for me.
expensive.sentenceTrans: 这些太贵重了！你不该买给我的。
expensive.mnemonic: ex出 + pens花费 + ive形容词后缀 → 要花钱的 → expensive昂贵的

experience.definition: （一次）经历，感受，体验；  v.体验，感受
experience.definitionEn: the knowledge and skill that you have gained through doing something for a period of time; the process of gaining this; the things that have happened to you that influence the way you think and behave; an event or activity that affects you in some way; events or knowledge shared by all the members of a particular group in society, that influences the way they think and behave
experience.sentence: That roller coaster ride was really a frightening experience.
experience.sentenceTrans: 这趟过山车真是一次可怕的经历。
experience.mnemonic: ex出 + per尝试 + ience名词后缀 → 尝试出来的东西 → experience经验

experiment.definition: 实验；试验；  v.进行实验
experiment.definitionEn: a scientific test that is done in order to study what happens and to gain new knowledge
experiment.sentence: There are many scientists doing experiments to find a cure.
experiment.sentenceTrans: 为了找到治疗方法，许多科学家在进行实验。
experiment.mnemonic: ex出 + peri尝试 + ment名词后缀 → experiment实验

expert.definition: 专家；  adj.专业的；熟练的；内行的
expert.definitionEn: a person with special knowledge, skill or training in something
expert.sentence: The expert is sharing his knowledge of traditional Chinese medicine on the TV show.
expert.sentenceTrans: 这个电视节目里的专家正在给观众讲授传统中医知识。
expert.mnemonic: ex向外 + per尝试，试验 + t后缀 → 经历多次的人 → expert专家，行家

expertise.definitionEn: expert knowledge or skill in a particular subject, activity or job
expertise.sentence: He has considerable expertise in bridge design.
expertise.sentenceTrans: 他在桥梁设计方面有很在行的专门知识。
expertise.mnemonic: expert专家 + ise名词后缀 → 专门知识

expire.definitionEn: (of a document, an agreement, etc.) to be no longer valid because the period of time for which it could be used has ended; (of a period of time, especially one during which somebody holds a position of authority) to end
expire.sentence: As it has expired, the contract is no longer valid.
expire.sentenceTrans: 合同已经到期，所以不再有效。
expire.mnemonic: ex出 + pir=spir呼吸 + e强调 → 只出气不进气 → expire断气；期满

explain.definitionEn: to tell somebody about something in a way that makes it easy to understand
explain.sentence: The doctor is explaining the patient's illness to her.
explain.sentenceTrans: 医生正在向她解释病人的病情。
explain.mnemonic: ex出 + plain清楚的 → 说清楚的 → explain解释

explanation.definitionEn: a statement, fact, or situation that tells you why something happened; a reason given for something; a statement or piece of writing that tells you how something works or makes something easier to understand
explanation.sentence: The boy is giving his explanation for why he arrived late for school.
explanation.sentenceTrans: 男孩正在解释他上学迟到的原因。
explanation.mnemonic: explan=explain解释 + ation名词后缀，表行为 → explanation说明，解释

explicit.definitionEn: (of a statement or piece of writing) clear and easy to understand
explicit.sentence: The map shows an explicit route to me.
explicit.sentenceTrans: 这张地图给我指出了明确的路线。
explicit.mnemonic: ex出 + plic折叠 + it → 说话不重叠的 → explicit明确的

explode.definitionEn: to burst or make something burst loudly and violently, causing damage; to increase suddenly and very quickly in number; to suddenly express an emotion
explode.sentence: If a light bulb explodes, it is very dangerous to be nearby.
explode.sentenceTrans: 如果灯泡爆炸了，在那附近是非常危险的。
explode.mnemonic: ex出 + plode爆炸声 → 发出爆炸声 → explode爆炸

exploit.definition: 剥削，压榨；开发；  n.辉煌的功绩（读作/ˈeksplɔɪt）
exploit.definitionEn: (disapproving) to treat somebody unfairly by making them work and not giving them much in return; to treat a person or situation as an opportunity to gain an advantage for yourself
exploit.sentence: The greedy employer exploits his workers for his own profits.
exploit.sentenceTrans: 这个贪婪的老板为了自己的利益剥削工人。

exploration.definitionEn: the act of travelling through a place in order to find out about it or look for something in it
exploration.sentence: She used her flashlight during her exploration of the cave.
exploration.sentenceTrans: 她拿着手电筒在洞穴里探索。
exploration.mnemonic: ex出 + plor喊，哭 + ation名词后缀 → 喊出来 → 探索

explore.definitionEn: to examine something completely or carefully in order to find out more about it
explore.sentence: They will explore the dark cave.
explore.sentenceTrans: 他们即将探索这个漆黑的洞穴。
explore.mnemonic: ex出，向外 + plore哭泣，叫喊 → explore探险

explorer.definitionEn: someone who travels into little known regions (especially for some scientific purpose)
explorer.sentence: The explorer is reading the map.
explorer.sentenceTrans: 这位探险家正在看地图。
explorer.mnemonic: explor=explore探索 + er表示人 → 探险家

explosion.definitionEn: the sudden violent bursting and loud noise of something such as a bomb exploding; the act of deliberately causing something to explode
explosion.sentenceTrans: 烟花爆炸的场景真是一场视觉盛宴。
explosion.mnemonic: explo(de)爆炸 + sion名词后缀 → explosion爆炸

explosive.definition: 爆炸的，引起爆炸的；  n.炸药
explosive.definitionEn: easily able or likely to explode
explosive.sentence: The scientist was hurt by explosive liquid!
explosive.sentenceTrans: 这个科学家被易爆的液体伤到了！
explosive.mnemonic: explos=explode爆炸 + ive表名词 → explosive炸药

export.definition: 出口，输出；  n.出口，输出
export.definitionEn: to sell and send goods to another country
export.sentence: Our company exports products to many different countries.
export.sentenceTrans: 我们公司向许多国家出口货物。
export.mnemonic: ex出 + port拿，引申为港口 → 拿出港口 → 出口

exportation.definitionEn: commodities (goods or services) sold to a foreign country
exportation.sentence: Modern transportation makes exportation much easier.
exportation.sentenceTrans: 现代运输工具使出口变得更加简单。

expose.definitionEn: to show something that is usually hidden; to tell the true facts about a person or a situation, and show them/it to be immoral, illegal, etc.
expose.sentence: Some cement fell from the wall, leaving the bricks exposed.
expose.sentenceTrans: 墙上的水泥掉下来后，砖块露了出来。
expose.mnemonic: ex出，出去 + pose放 → 放出去 → expose暴露

exposure.definitionEn: the state of being in a place or situation where there is no protection from something harmful or unpleasant
exposure.sentence: Because of exposure to the sun, the corn is scorched.
exposure.sentenceTrans: 因为暴露在太阳底下，这根玉米被晒伤了。
exposure.mnemonic: ex出 ＋ pos放 ＋ ure名词后缀，表行为、状态 → exposure暴露，揭露

express.definition: 表达，表示；  adj.明确的；  n.快递；快车
express.definitionEn: travelling very fast; operating very quickly
express.sentence: I would like to express my love for you.
express.mnemonic: ex出来 + press挤压 → 挤出来 → express表达

expression.definitionEn: a look on a person’s face that shows their thoughts or feelings
expression.sentence: She had a puzzled expression on her face when she saw the math problem.
expression.sentenceTrans: 当她看到那道数学题时，脸上露出了困惑的表情。
expression.mnemonic: ex出来 + press挤压 + ion名词后缀 → expression表达；表情

extend.definition: 延伸；给予，表示；延长；提供
extend.definitionEn: to make something longer or larger
extend.sentence: The highway extends all the way to the horizon.
extend.sentenceTrans: 这条公路向着地平线无限延伸。
extend.mnemonic: ex出 + tend延伸 → 伸出去 → extend扩张

extended.definitionEn: relatively long in duration; tediously protracted
extended.sentence: The shop now has extended hours until midnight.
extended.sentenceTrans: 这家商店现在的营业时间延长到了半夜12点。

extension.definitionEn: the act of increasing the area of activity, group of people, etc. that is affected by something
extension.sentence: The extension of the tumor into surrounding tissues complicates surgical removal.
extension.sentenceTrans: 肿瘤向周围组织的延伸使手术切除变得复杂。
extension.mnemonic: ex出 + tend伸展 + sion表名词 → 延展，扩张；延期

extensive.definitionEn: large in amount, area, or range
extensive.sentence: The rain led to extensive damage to the area.
extensive.sentenceTrans: 雨水导致该地区遭受大面积洪水破坏。
extensive.mnemonic: ex向外 + tens延伸 + ive形容词后缀 → 向外伸展的 → extensive大面积的

extent.definitionEn: how large, important, serious, etc. something is
extent.sentence: The extent of the damage from the earthquake is massive.
extent.sentenceTrans: 这场地震的破坏程度太大了。
extent.mnemonic: ex出 + tent伸展 → 伸出去的范围 → extent范围

external.definitionEn: connected with or located on the outside of something/somebody
external.sentence: This medicine is just for external use, so we can't spray it into our mouth.
external.sentenceTrans: 这种药只能外用，因此我们不能往嘴里喷。
external.mnemonic: exter出去 + nal=al……的 → 出去的 → 在外面的  → external外部的

externally.sentence: The aircraft is externally inspected before each flight.
externally.sentenceTrans: 每次飞行前，都会对飞机进行外部检查。

extra.definition: 额外的，附加的；  adv.额外地；  n.额外的事务
extra.definitionEn: more than is usual, expected, or than exists already
extra.sentence: Could you give me some extra ice cream?
extra.sentenceTrans: 你能再多给我一点儿冰激凌吗？
extra.mnemonic: extra=out出去 → 出去的 → 余出的 → extra额外的

extraordinary.definitionEn: not normal or ordinary; greater or better than usual
extraordinary.sentence: Her little daughter has extraordinary musical talent.
extraordinary.sentenceTrans: 她的小女儿在音乐方面天赋异禀。
extraordinary.mnemonic: extra超过 + ordinary普通的 → extraordinary特别的

extreme.definition: 极端的；极限的；  n.极端
extreme.definitionEn: not ordinary or usual; serious or severe
extreme.sentence: Extreme weather conditions destroyed the city.
extreme.sentenceTrans: 极端天气状况摧毁了这座城市。
extreme.mnemonic: extr出去 + eme表最高级 → extreme极端的

extremely.sentence: Compared with the Earth, the Sun is extremely large.
extremely.sentenceTrans: 和地球相比，太阳非常大。
extremely.mnemonic: extreme极端的 + ly表副词 → 过分地，极端地

eye.definitionEn: either of the two organs on the face that you see with

eyesight.sentence: Your eyesight is terrible! You need glasses.
eyesight.sentenceTrans: 你视力太差了！你需要配眼镜。
eyesight.mnemonic: eye眼睛 + sight眼光 → eyesight视力

face.definition: 脸部；  v.面对，面临；面对（困境）
face.definitionEn: the front part of the head between the forehead and the chin
face.sentence: The patient has a cut on her face which needs stitches.
face.sentenceTrans: 病人的脸部有一处需要缝合的切口。
face.mnemonic: face=fac表示脸、面 → face脸，表面，外表

facility.definition: 设施，设备；才能，资质；（供特定用途的）场所
facility.definitionEn: buildings, services, equipment, etc. that are provided for a particular purpose; a special feature of a machine, service, etc. that makes it possible to do something extra
facility.sentence: The new sports facility includes a swimming pool, a gymnasium, and several tennis courts.
facility.sentenceTrans: 新的体育设施包括一个游泳池、一个体育馆和几个网球场。
facility.mnemonic: facile简单的 + ity表名词 → 促进事务简化的设施或工具  → facility设施，设备

fact.definitionEn: something that truly exists or happens: something that has actual existence
fact.sentence: My photo proved the fact that the ghosts weren't real.
fact.sentenceTrans: 我的照片证明了一个事实：这些鬼都是假的。

factor.definition: 因素；系数；  v.把…因素包括进去
factor.definitionEn: one of several things that cause or influence something
factor.sentence: An important factor for him when buying a car is its appearance.
factor.sentenceTrans: 车的外观是他买车时考虑的一个重要因素。
factor.mnemonic: fact做，制作 + or表名词，人或物 → 促使人做的东西 → factor要素；动力

factory.definitionEn: a building or group of buildings where goods are made
factory.mnemonic: fact做 + ory场所，地点后缀 → 做东西的场所 → factory工厂

faculty.definition: 能力，才能；全体教员；院系
faculty.definitionEn: all the teachers of a particular university or college
faculty.sentence: The boy has the faculty to play the piano.
faculty.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩有弹钢琴的能力。
faculty.mnemonic: facul做 + ty表名词 → 会做东西 → faculty能力

fade.sentence: The trees were fading away into the mist.

fail.definition: 失败； 不及格；衰退；  n.失败；不及格
fail.definitionEn: to not be successful in achieving something; to not pass a test or an exam; to decide that somebody/something has not passed a test or an exam

failure.definitionEn: a person or thing that is not successful
failure.sentence: He doesn't believe his failure in the EQ test.
failure.sentenceTrans: 他无法相信自己在情商测试中的失败。
failure.mnemonic: fail犯错误，欺骗 + ure名词后缀 → 错误状态 → failure失败

faint.definition: 晕倒；昏厥；  adj.（光、声、味）微弱的
faint.definitionEn: to become unconscious when not enough blood is going to your brain, usually because of the heat, a shock, etc.
faint.sentence: The hot weather made him faint.
faint.sentenceTrans: 炎热的天气使他晕倒了。

fair.definition: 合理的，公平的；相当的，尚好的；  n.集市，市场，交易会
fair.definitionEn: agreeing with what is thought to be right or acceptable
fair.sentence: Compared to that on the left, the drink on the right is being sold at a fair price.
fair.sentenceTrans: 相比左边的饮料，右边的饮料售价更合理。

fairly.definitionEn: in a fair and reasonable way; honestly
fairly.sentence: The bag on the right looks fairly heavy.
fairly.sentenceTrans: 右边那个书包看上去相当沉。
fairly.mnemonic: fair公平 + ly……地 → fairly公平地

faith.sentence: Many people go on an annual pilgrimage to this sacred place to express their faith.
faith.sentenceTrans: 很多人每年会到这个神圣的地方来参拜，以表达他们的信仰。

faithful.definitionEn: having or showing true and constant support or loyalty
faithful.sentence: Dogs are the most faithful pets you can have.
faithful.sentenceTrans: 狗是你可以拥有的最忠诚的宠物。
faithful.mnemonic: faith忠诚 + ful表形容词 → faithful忠诚的

faithfully.sentence: This dog faithfully waits for its master to come home every day.
faithfully.sentenceTrans: 这只狗每天忠诚地等待他的主人回家。
faithfully.mnemonic: faith忠实 ＋ ful...的 ＋ ly...地 → faithfully忠实地

fake.definitionEn: not genuine; appearing to be something it is not
fake.sentence: Do you know which rabbit is the fake one?
fake.sentenceTrans: 你知道哪一只小兔子是假的吗？

fall.definition: 落下；坠落；下降，减弱；  v.跌落；  n.落下；秋天
fall.definitionEn: to drop down from a higher level to a lower level
fall.sentence: An apple fell from the tree and hit Newton.
fall.sentenceTrans: 苹果从树上落下并砸中了牛顿。

false.definitionEn: wrong; not correct or true; not genuine, but made to look real to cheat people; wrong or mistaken, because it is based on something that is not true or correct
false.sentence: Is this question true or false?

fame.definitionEn: the condition of being known or recognized by many people
fame.sentence: The actor enjoys fame and loves the attention that it brings him.
fame.sentenceTrans: 这位男演员沉浸在名望中，并享受着由此带来的关注度。

familiar.definition: 熟悉的，通晓的；不拘礼节的；亲密的；随便的；  n.密友；常客；高级官吏的家属
familiar.definitionEn: well known to you; often seen or heard and therefore easy to recognize
familiar.sentence: Its owner's voice is very familiar to the dog.
familiar.sentenceTrans: 狗对它主人的声音很熟悉。
familiar.mnemonic: famili家庭 + ar……的 → familiar熟悉的

family.definition: 家庭；家族；  adj.家庭的，家族的
family.definitionEn: a group of people who are related to each other
family.sentence: There are five people in my family.

famine.definitionEn: a situation in which many people do not have enough food to eat
famine.sentence: These poor African kids suffer a lot from famine.
famine.sentenceTrans: 这些可怜的非洲儿童饱受饥荒之苦。
famine.mnemonic: fam饿 + ine表名词 → famine饥荒

famous.sentence: When I go to America, I want to go and see the famous Statue of Liberty.
famous.sentenceTrans: 当我去美国的时候，我想去看著名的自由女神像。
famous.mnemonic: fam=fame荣誉 + ous形容词后缀 → famous著名的

fan.definition: 风扇，扇子；（影，球等）迷；  v.煽动，激起
fan.definitionEn: a machine with blades that go round to create a current of air; a thing that you hold in your hand and wave to create a current of cool air; a person who admires somebody/something or enjoys watching or listening to somebody/something very much
fan.sentence: In summer, she cools herself in front of an electric fan.
fan.sentenceTrans: 夏日里，她坐在电扇前让自己凉快些。

fancy.definition: 幻想，想象力；喜爱；  adj.奢华的；昂贵的；  v.想要；想象，幻想；喜欢
fancy.definitionEn: unusually complicated, often in an unnecessary way; intended to impress other people; (especially of small things) with a lot of decorations or bright colours
fancy.sentence: Her childhood fancy was to become a famous singer.
fancy.sentenceTrans: 她童年的幻想是成为一名著名歌手。

fantastic.definitionEn: extremely good; excellent; very large; larger than you expected; strange and showing a lot of imagination
fantastic.sentence: Welcome to this fantastic world where everything is made of tasty treats.
fantastic.sentenceTrans: 欢迎来到奇异世界，这里所有的东西都是甜食做的。

fantasy.definitionEn: a pleasant situation that you imagine but that is unlikely to happen; the act of imagining things; a person’s imagination
fantasy.sentence: She lives in a fantasy world where she imagines herself as a queen.
fantasy.sentenceTrans: 她生活在一个幻想世界里，把自己想象成女王。
fantasy.mnemonic: fan=fancy幻想 + tasy名词后缀 → fantasy想象，幻想

far.definition: （空间或时间）远，久远；  adj.远的，遥远的
far.sentence: Though we're far apart, you're always in my heart.
far.sentenceTrans: 虽然我们相隔遥远，但你永远在我心中。

fare.definition: 交通费；票价；  v.（事情）进行得（好或坏）
fare.sentence: She paid three dollars for the bus fare.
fare.sentenceTrans: 她付了三美元的公交车费。

farewell.definitionEn: the act of saying goodbye to somebody
farewell.sentence: She said her farewell and drove off.
farewell.sentenceTrans: 她说了句再见，就开车走了。
farewell.mnemonic: fare旅途 + well好的 → 祝路途愉快 → farewell再会；告别

farm.definitionEn: an area of land, and the buildings on it, used for growing crops and/or keeping animals
farm.sentence: My family has just bought an organic farm—they believe in natural food.
farm.sentenceTrans: 我的家人刚刚买了块有机农场——他们相信自然生长的食物。

farmer.definitionEn: a person who owns or manages a farm
farmer.sentence: Every day, the farmer checked the development of his crop fields.
farmer.sentenceTrans: 这位农场主每天都会查看农田的生长情况。
farmer.mnemonic: farm务农 + er表人 → 务农的人 → farmer农民

farther.definitionEn: (comparative of far) at or to a greater distance in space or time
farther.sentence: We need to move farther to reach the destination.
farther.sentenceTrans: 我们需要再往前走才会到达目的地。

fascinate.definitionEn: to attract or interest somebody very much
fascinate.sentence: That girl is fascinated by the delicious food.
fascinate.sentenceTrans: 那个姑娘被美食迷得神魂颠倒。
fascinate.mnemonic: fascin迷住 + ate动词后缀，使之成…… → fascinate使……入迷

fashion.definition: 时髦，风尚；  v.制作，塑造
fashion.definitionEn: a popular style of clothes, hair, etc. at a particular time or place; the state of being popular; a popular way of behaving, doing an activity, etc.; the business of making or selling clothes in new and different styles
fashion.sentence: He is trying to keep up with the latest fashion trend.
fashion.sentenceTrans: 他在努力追随最新的时尚潮流。
fashion.mnemonic: fash放置，设置 + ion名词后缀 → fashion制作，塑造，时尚

fashionable.definitionEn: following a style that is popular at a particular time; used or visited by people following a current fashion, especially by rich people
fashionable.sentence: Her dress in the Cannes Film Festival is so fashionable!
fashionable.sentenceTrans: 她在戛纳电影节上的着装太时髦了！
fashionable.mnemonic: fashion时髦 + able……的 → fashionable时髦的

fast.definition: 快速的，迅速的，动作敏捷的
fast.definitionEn: moving or able to move quickly
fast.sentence: The car was going so fast! I could hardly see it!
fast.sentenceTrans: 那辆车开得太快了！我几乎看不见它了。

fasten.definitionEn: to close something firmly so that it will not open; to be closed in this way
fasten.sentence: My mother is helping me fasten my seat belt.
fasten.sentenceTrans: 我的妈妈正在帮我系安全带。
fasten.mnemonic: fast紧紧地 + en动词后缀 → fasten扎牢

fat.definition: 肥的，肥胖的；  n.【生】脂肪
fat.definitionEn: (of a person’s or an animal’s body) having too much flesh on it and weighing too much
fat.sentence: You'll become fat if you drink too much soda.
fat.sentenceTrans: 如果喝太多汽水的话，你会长胖的。

fatal.definition: 致命的；灾难性的，毁灭性的
fatal.sentence: Some food like chocolate may be fatal to dogs.
fatal.sentenceTrans: 有些食物，比如巧克力，对狗来说是致命的。

fate.definitionEn: the things, especially bad things, that will happen or have happened to somebody/something; the power that is believed to control everything that happens and that cannot be stopped or changed
fate.sentence: It was my fate to marry him.
fate.sentenceTrans: 我嫁给他是命中注定的。

father.definitionEn: a male parent of a child or an animal; a person who is acting as the father to a child
father.sentence: A good father spends time with his kids.
father.sentenceTrans: 好爸爸会花时间陪他的孩子。

fatigue.definitionEn: a feeling of being extremely tired, usually because of hard work or exercise; (usually after another noun) a feeling of not wanting to do a particular activity any longer because you have done too much of it
fatigue.sentence: Due to heavy fatigue, I keep falling asleep at the desk.
fatigue.sentenceTrans: 我很疲劳，所以直接趴桌上睡着了。
fatigue.mnemonic: fat断裂 + ig做，驱动 + ue动词后缀 → fatigue快断裂的，接近极限点的 → fatigue疲乏，劳累

fool.definitionEn: a person who you think behaves or speaks in a way that lacks intelligence or good judgement
fool.sentence: He is such a fool that he can't answer this question.
fool.sentenceTrans: 他连这个问题都答不出，真是个傻瓜。

foolish.definitionEn: (of actions or behaviour) not showing good sense or judgement
foolish.sentence: It was foolish of the little dog to challenge the strong wolf.
foolish.sentenceTrans: 小狗去挑战这只强壮的狼是很愚蠢的。
foolish.mnemonic: fool笨蛋 + ish像…一样 → foolish愚蠢的

foot.definitionEn: the lowest part of the leg, below the ankle, on which a person or an animal stands
foot.sentence: She is lying in the sun with bare feet.

football.definitionEn: a game played by two teams of 11 players, using a round ball which players kick up and down the playing field. Teams try to kick the ball into the other team’s goal.
football.sentence: Football is a popular sport around the world.
football.sentenceTrans: 足球运动是一项在全球广受欢迎的体育项目。
football.mnemonic: foot脚 + ball球 → football足球比赛；足球

footprint.definitionEn: a mark left on a surface by a person’s foot or shoe or by an animal’s foot
footprint.sentence: Footprints on the sand can help in tracing the location of the enemy.
footprint.sentenceTrans: 沙滩上的脚印可以帮助追踪敌人的位置。

for.definitionEn: used to show who is intended to have or use something or where something is intended to be put
for.sentence: I make a card for my mom.

forbid.definitionEn: to order somebody not to do something; to order that something must not be done
forbid.sentence: We forbid smoking in the restaurant.
forbid.mnemonic: for反对；相反 + bid要求 → forbid禁止

force.definition: 强迫；推动；促使，迫使；  n.力量；武力；势力
force.definitionEn: to make somebody do something that they do not want to do
force.sentence: The child is being forced to have breakfast.
force.sentenceTrans: 这个孩子正被迫吃早饭。

forceful.definition: 有说服力的；强烈的，有效的
forceful.definitionEn: characterized by or full of force or strength (often but not necessarily physical)
forceful.sentence: She elaborated on several forceful proposals at the meeting.
forceful.sentenceTrans: 她在会议上阐释了一些具有说服力的方案。

forecast.definitionEn: a statement about what will happen in the future, based on information that is available now
forecast.sentence: The weather forecast says the weather next week will be terrible.
forecast.sentenceTrans: 天气预报说下周的天气会很糟糕。
forecast.mnemonic: fore前面，预先 + cast投射 → 预先投射 → forecast预料，预测

forehead.definitionEn: the part of the face above the eyes and below the hair
forehead.sentence: The boy smiled and pointed to his forehead.
forehead.sentenceTrans: 男孩笑着指了指自己的前额。
forehead.mnemonic: fore前面，预先 + head头 → forehead前额

foreign.definitionEn: in or from a country that is not your own

foreigner.definitionEn: a person who is from a country that is not your own
foreigner.sentence: We have two new classmates, and they are foreigners!
foreigner.sentenceTrans: 我们班来了两个新同学，他们是外国人！
foreigner.mnemonic: foreign外国的 + er名词后缀，人 → 外国人

foresee.definitionEn: to think something is going to happen in the future; to know about something before it happens
foresee.sentence: He foresaw that his journey would be delayed by bad weather.
foresee.sentenceTrans: 他预料到自己的旅程会被恶劣天气耽搁。
foresee.mnemonic: fore前面，预先 + see看见 → foresee预见，先见

forest.definitionEn: a large area of land that is thickly covered with trees
forest.sentence: The forest looks beautiful when the sun shines through the trees.
forest.sentenceTrans: 当阳光穿过树木时，整个森林看起来美极了。

forever.definitionEn: used to say that a particular situation or state will always exist; a very long time
forever.sentence: They turned into butterflies and stayed together forever.
forever.sentenceTrans: 他们变成了蝴蝶，会永远在一起。
forever.mnemonic: for适合于 + ever永远 → forever永远，总是，老是

forget.definitionEn: to be unable to remember sth that has happened in the past or information that you knew in the past
forget.sentence: He forgot to remove his key from the lock when he left his apartment.
forget.sentenceTrans: 他离开公寓时忘了把钥匙从门锁上拔下来。
forget.mnemonic: for否定，相反 + get得到，想起 → 想不起来的 → forget忘记

forgettable.sentence: Don’t make forgettable mistakes with your password.
forgettable.sentenceTrans: 不要在密码上犯容易被遗忘的错误。

forgive.definitionEn: to stop feeling angry with somebody who has done something to harm, annoy or upset you; to stop feeling angry with yourself; used to say in a polite way that you are sorry if what you are doing or saying seems rude or silly
forgive.sentence: The kitty has forgiven its master for hugging other cats.
forgive.sentenceTrans: 小猫原谅主人抱了别的猫。
forgive.mnemonic: for完全地 + give给予 → forgive饶恕

fork.definition: 叉，餐叉；分叉，分岔处，岔路；  v.叉起，耙成叉状；道路分叉
fork.definitionEn: a small tool with two or more pointed parts (called prongs or tines) used for picking up and eating food
fork.sentence: The fork is usually placed on the left side of the plate.
fork.sentenceTrans: 餐叉通常被放在餐盘的左侧。

form.definition: 形状；【计】表单，表格；  v.组织，建立
form.definitionEn: the particular way something is, seems, looks or is presented
form.sentence: These pieces can make many different forms.
form.sentenceTrans: 这些七巧板可以组成许多不同的形状。

formal.definitionEn: (of a style of dress, speech, writing, behaviour, etc.) very correct and suitable for official or important occasions
formal.sentence: His job requires formal dress, such as smart shoes, a shirt and a tie.
formal.sentenceTrans: 他的工作需要正式的着装，比如讲究的鞋子、衬衫和领带。
formal.mnemonic: form形式 + al…的 → formal正式的，正规的

format.definition: 版式；格式；总体安排；  v.使格式化
format.definitionEn: the general arrangement, plan, design, etc. of something
format.sentence: The format of the newspaper is well arranged.
format.sentenceTrans: 这份报纸排版十分整齐。
format.mnemonic: form形式 + at=ate表动词 → format使格式化

formation.sentence: There are many different formations that soccer teams can play.
formation.sentenceTrans: 足球队可以采取很多不同的队形来比赛。
formation.mnemonic: form形状 + ation表名词 → formation形成；形式

former.definitionEn: that existed in earlier times; that used to have a particular position or status in the past;  used to refer to the first of two things or people mentioned
former.sentence: The first photograph is our former headmaster.
former.sentenceTrans: 第一张照片是我们的从前的校长。
former.mnemonic: form=fore先前 + er表人/物 → former前者

formula.definitionEn: a series of letters, numbers or symbols that represent a rule or law; letters and symbols that show the parts of a chemical compound, etc.
formula.sentence: The formula for calculating the area of a rectangle is length times width.
formula.sentenceTrans: 计算矩形面积的公式是长度乘以宽度。
formula.mnemonic: form形式 + ula表名词 → 形成模式的 → formula公式

fortunate.definitionEn: having or bringing an advantage, an opportunity, a piece of good luck, etc.
fortunate.sentence: People believe that four-leaf clover is a fortunate symbol.
fortunate.sentenceTrans: 人们认为四叶草是幸运的象征。
fortunate.mnemonic: fortun=fort运气 + ate…的 → fortunate幸运的

fortunately.sentence: Fortunately, he actually won the lottery! One million dollars!
fortunately.sentenceTrans: 太幸运了，他中了彩票，那可是100万啊！
fortunately.mnemonic: fortun=fortune力量，运气一个 + ate表示有……性质的 + ly表示如……的、有……特征的 → fortunately幸运地，幸亏

fortune.definitionEn: chance or luck, especially in the way it affects people’s lives
fortune.sentence: What a good fortune! I won the first prize.
fortune.sentenceTrans: 运气真好！我中了一等奖。

forty.sentence: Congratulations on turning forty years old!

forward.definition: 【数】向前，前向；向前，向将来；前进；向前地；  v.发送，寄；促进
forward.definitionEn: towards a place or position that is in front;  towards a good result; towards the future; ahead in time
forward.sentence: This is the sign of forward and backward.
forward.sentenceTrans: 这是向前和向后的标志。
forward.mnemonic: for前 ＋ ward向…... → forward向前；今后

fossil.definitionEn: the remains of an animal or a plant which have become hard and turned into rock
fossil.sentence: There is a fossil of an ancient fish in the ground.
fossil.sentenceTrans: 地里有一块古代鱼类的化石。

foster.definitionEn: used with some nouns in connection with the fostering of a child
foster.sentence: Her parents play songs to foster her interest in music.
foster.sentenceTrans: 父母给她播放音乐，以培养她对音乐的兴趣。

found.definition: 成立，建立，创办；发现，感到（find的过去式）
found.sentence: These two businessmen founded a new company together.
found.sentenceTrans: 这两个商人一起创办了一家新公司。

foundation.definitionEn: a layer of bricks, concrete, etc. that forms the solid underground base of a building
foundation.sentence: A strong building needs a solid foundation.
foundation.sentenceTrans: 一座坚固的建筑需要有稳固的地基。
foundation.mnemonic: found基础 + ation表名词 → foundation基础，地基

fountain.definitionEn: a structure from which water is sent up into the air by a pump, used to decorate parks and gardens/yards
fountain.sentence: The fountain becomes so colorful at night.
fountain.sentenceTrans: 在晚上，喷泉变得五彩缤纷。

four.sentence: Even a child knows the number four. Do you?
four.sentenceTrans: 连小孩子都知道数字四的意思。你知道吗？

fox.definitionEn: a wild animal of the dog family, with reddish-brown fur, a pointed face and a thick heavy tail
fox.sentence: The fox gave the boy flowers and sat beside him.
fox.sentenceTrans: 狐狸给了男孩花，并坐在他身边。

fraction.definitionEn: a small part or amount of something
fraction.sentence: The fraction in the chart is shown in red.
fraction.sentenceTrans: 图表中那部分是用红色表示。
fraction.mnemonic: fract打碎 + ion名词后缀 → fraction部分；小片

frame.definitionEn: a strong border or structure of wood, metal, etc. that holds a picture, door, piece of glass, etc. in position; the supporting structure of a piece of furniture, a building, a vehicle, etc. that gives it its shape; a structure of plastic or metal that holds the lenses in a pair of glasses; the form or structure of a person or animal’s body
frame.sentence: The picture looks nice in this wooden frame.
frame.sentenceTrans: 这幅画在这个木质的画框里看起来很漂亮。

framework.definitionEn: the parts of a building or an object that support its weight and give it shape
framework.sentence: You can see the framework of the building so well at the moment.
framework.sentenceTrans: 你现在可以清楚地看见房子的框架。

frank.definitionEn: honest and direct in what you say, sometimes in a way that other people might not like
frank.sentence: She was frank about the food in my teeth.
frank.sentenceTrans: 她很直率地告诉我我牙上有东西。

free.definition: 自由的；免费的；  adv.自由地；免费地
free.definitionEn: able to do what you want to do/able to move, go, or act without being stopped
free.sentence: After quitting my job, I feel free as a bird escaping its cage.
free.sentenceTrans: 辞职以后，我感觉自己像一只逃出鸟笼的鸟。

freedom.definitionEn: the right to do or say what you want without anyone stopping you; the state of being able to do what you want, without anything stopping you; the state of not being a prisoner or slave; the state of not being affected by the thing mentioned
freedom.sentence: The birds finally get their freedom. They are flying out of the cage.
freedom.sentenceTrans: 鸟儿们终于自由了。它们正从笼子里飞出来。
freedom.mnemonic: free自由的 + dom状态或领域 → freedom自由

freeze.definition: 冰冻，冻结；（使）冻住；  n.严寒，冻结
freeze.definitionEn: to become hard, and often turn to ice, as a result of extreme cold; to make something do this
freeze.sentenceTrans: 水在零摄氏度时会结冰。

frequency.definition: （声波或电磁波振动的）频率；频繁
frequency.definitionEn: the rate at which a sound or electromagnetic wave vibrates (= moves up and down)
frequency.sentence: The sounds had a high frequency.

frequent.sentence: My daddy bothers me on a frequent basis.
frequent.mnemonic: frequ挤在一起 + ent形容词后缀 -> frequent时常的，频繁的

frequently.sentence: He went to the bathroom frequently after drinking too much water.
frequently.sentenceTrans: 喝了太多水后，他频繁地去上厕所。
frequently.mnemonic: frequent经常的 ＋ ly...地 → frequently经常地，频繁地

fresh.definition: 新鲜的；没经验的；  adv.刚刚，才
fresh.definitionEn: newly produced, made, gathered, etc. :not preserved by being frozen, canned, etc.
fresh.sentence: Eating fresh fruit is great for your health.
fresh.sentenceTrans: 吃新鲜的水果对你的健康有益。

freshman.definitionEn: a first-year student at a university or college; a first-year student at high school or junior high school
freshman.sentence: Freshmen always have lots of things to do in their first few days at college.
freshman.sentenceTrans: 在入学的头几天，新生们通常有很多事要做。
freshman.mnemonic: fresh新鲜 + man人 → freshman新手，生手

friday.definitionEn: the day of the week after Thursday and before Saturday

friend.definitionEn: a person you know well and like, and who is not usually a member of your family

friendly.definitionEn: having or showing the feelings that friends have for each other
friendly.sentence: Tom and his buddy are very friendly with each other.
friendly.sentenceTrans: 汤姆和他的伙计互相很友好。

friendship.sentence: I hope my college friendships will survive my college years.
friendship.sentenceTrans: 我希望大学时代的友谊能够超越大学生活，延续下去。
friendship.mnemonic: friend朋友 ＋ ship名词后缀 → friendship友谊

frighten.definitionEn: to make somebody suddenly feel afraid
frighten.sentence: My brother jumped out of the closet and frightened me.
frighten.sentenceTrans: 我的弟弟从衣柜里跳出来，吓到我了。
frighten.mnemonic: fright惊恐 + en使… → frighten使惊恐

frightened.definition: 受惊的，受恐吓的；害怕的
frightened.sentence: The boy was frightened by the sudden noise outside the window.
frightened.sentenceTrans: 男孩被窗外的突然声响吓到了。
frightened.mnemonic: fright惊恐 + en表动词 + ed…的 → frightened受惊的，受恐吓的

frightening.definitionEn: causing fear or dread or terror
frightening.sentence: OMG! Look at the frightening look of that wolf!
frightening.sentenceTrans: 我的天！快看那狼多骇人！
frightening.mnemonic: fright惊恐+en表动词 + ing...的→frightening令人恐惧的

frog.definitionEn: a small animal with smooth skin, that lives both on land and in water (= is an amphibian). Frogs have very long back legs for jumping, and no tail.
frog.sentence: The frog is jumping out of the water.

from.definitionEn: used to show where somebody/something starts; to show when something starts; to show who sent or gave something/somebody
from.sentence: The black pepper came from the Western Regions.

front.definition: 前面，正面；  adj.前面的，正面的
front.definitionEn: the part or side of something that faces forward; the side of something that you look at first
front.sentence: I like to sit in the front so no one can block my view.
front.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢坐在前排，这样一来就没有人能够挡住我的视线。

frost.definitionEn: the thin white layer of ice that forms when the temperature drops below 0°C; a weather condition in which the temperature drops below 0°C
frost.sentence: The leaves were covered with frost.

fruit.definition: 水果；成果，产物；  v.结果实
fruit.definitionEn: (of a tree or plant) to produce fruit
fruit.sentence: A basket of fruits is on the wooden table.

frustrate.definitionEn: to make somebody feel annoyed or impatient because they cannot do or achieve what they want
frustrate.sentence: The five of them are frustrated by the loss of the game.
frustrate.sentenceTrans: 他们五个人因输掉比赛而感到挫败。
frustrate.mnemonic: frustr犯错误 + ate做，造成 → frustrate挫败

fry.definitionEn: to cook something in hot fat or oil; to be cooked in hot fat or oil
fry.sentence: It's easy to fry eggs; I can make two for you.
fry.sentenceTrans: 煎鸡蛋很容易，我可以给你做两个。

fuel.definitionEn: any material that produces heat or power, usually when it is burnt
fuel.sentence: I need to add fuel to my car.
fuel.sentenceTrans: 我需要给我的车加燃料。

fulfil.definition: 实现，履行，实践（=fulfill）；满足…的要求
fulfil.definitionEn: to do or achieve what was hoped for or expected
fulfil.sentence: He has fulfilled his childhood dream of becoming an astronaut.
fulfil.sentenceTrans: 他实现了成为一名宇航员的童年梦想。

fulfill.definition: 履行，实现，完成；满足，实现
fulfill.definitionEn: to do or achieve what was hoped for or expected; to do or have what is required or necessary; to have a particular role or purpose
fulfill.sentence: She fulfilled her goals on the list.
fulfill.sentenceTrans: 她完成了清单上的目标。
fulfill.mnemonic: ful完全，完整 + fill填满 → 完全填满 → fulfill实现，完成

fulfillment.sentence: The joy of victory is the ultimate fulfillment in life.
fulfillment.sentenceTrans: 胜利的喜悦是生命的终极目标。
fulfillment.mnemonic: ful 完全的 + fill 装满，使充满 + ment 表示行为、行为的过程或结果 → fulfillment履行；实行

fulfilment.definitionEn: a feeling of satisfaction at having achieved your desires
fulfilment.sentence: She got a sense of fulfilment from the good comments of her work.
fulfilment.sentenceTrans: 她从对她工作的好评中获得了一种满足感。

full.definition: 满的，充满的；  n.完全，全部；  adv.完全地，充分地，到最大程度
full.definitionEn: containing or holding as much or as many as possible; having no empty space
full.sentence: The cup on the left is full of water.
full.sentenceTrans: 左侧的杯子中装满了水。

fun.sentence: They're all having fun at the party.
fun.sentenceTrans: 他们在派对上玩得很开心。

function.definition: 功能，作用，用途，机能；  v.工作，运转
function.definitionEn: the special purpose or activity for which a thing exists or is used
function.sentence: This kind of bottle with holes has many useful functions.
function.sentenceTrans: 这种带孔的瓶子有许多实用的功能。
function.mnemonic: funct活动 + ion表名词 → function功能

fund.definition: 资金，基金；  v.拨款，提供资金
fund.definitionEn: an amount of money that is used for a special purpose; money on deposit on which checks or drafts can be drawn
fund.sentence: The fund was established to protect our environment.
fund.sentenceTrans: 这笔基金是为保护环境而设立的。
fund.mnemonic: fund基础，创办事业的基础 → 底子，本钱 → fund基金

fundamental.definition: 基本的；至关重要的；基础的；  n.基本原理；基本规律
fundamental.definitionEn: of or relating to the basic structure or function of something
fundamental.sentence: Among Maslow's needs, physiologic needs are people's most fundamental needs.
fundamental.sentenceTrans: 在马斯洛的需求中，生理需求是人最基本的需求。
fundamental.mnemonic: fundament基础 + al形容词后缀 → fundamental基础的，基本的

funeral.definitionEn: a ceremony, usually a religious one, for burying or cremating (= burning) a dead person
funeral.sentence: They are attending the funeral of the glacier.
funeral.sentenceTrans: 他们正在参加冰川的葬礼。
funeral.mnemonic: funer葬礼 + al表名词 → funeral葬礼

funny.definition: 有趣的，好玩的；好笑的，滑稽的
funny.sentence: It was so funny that he cried with laughter.
funny.sentenceTrans: 这太好笑了，他都笑出眼泪了。
funny.mnemonic: fu趣味 + (n)y形容词后缀 → funny有趣的，好玩的

fur.definitionEn: the soft thick mass of hair that grows on the body of some animals; the skin of an animal with the fur still on it, used especially for making clothes; a piece of clothing, especially a coat or jacket, made of real or artificial fur; an artificial material that looks and feels like fur
fur.sentence: A fur coat is very warm, but very expensive!
fur.sentenceTrans: 毛皮外套很温暖，但也很昂贵！

furnish.definition: （用家具等）布置（房间、公寓等）；供应，提供
furnish.definitionEn: to put furniture in a house, room, etc.
furnish.sentence: We furnished our room with very expensive furniture.
furnish.sentenceTrans: 我们用非常昂贵的家具来装饰我们的房间。

furniture.definitionEn: objects that can be moved, such as tables, chairs and beds, that are put into a house or an office to make it suitable for living or working in
furniture.sentence: All of his furniture came as a set.
furniture.sentenceTrans: 他的所有家具都是成套的。
furniture.mnemonic: furni安置 + ture表名词 → furniture家具

further.definition: 更远地；进一步；  adj.更多的，附加的；  v.促进，推动
further.definitionEn: (comparative of far) at or to a greater distance; to a greater degree or extent
further.sentence: Combined with advanced robotic technology, I can see further.
further.sentenceTrans: 与先进的机器人技术结合，我能看得更远。
further.mnemonic: furth=forth向前，向前方 + er比较级 → 更前面的 → further更远的

furthermore.definitionEn: in addition to what has just been stated
furthermore.sentence: He broke his leg in the forest, furthermore, some strange creatures were watching him.
furthermore.sentenceTrans: 他在森林中摔断了腿，此外，一些奇怪的生物正盯着他。
furthermore.mnemonic: further更远的 + more更多的 → furthermore此外，而且

future.definition: 未来，将来；前途；  adj.将来的，未来的
future.definitionEn: the period of time that will come after the present time
future.sentence: I can see your future from this ball!
future.sentenceTrans: 我能从这个球里看见你的未来！

gain.definitionEn: the act or process of acquiring something; an increase in the amount of something, especially in wealth or weight; financial profit
gain.sentence: We can gain valuable knowledge by reading books.
gain.sentenceTrans: 我们能通过阅读获得宝贵的知识。

gallery.definitionEn: a room or building for showing works of art, especially to the public
gallery.sentence: Many people come to this gallery to see the famous pieces of art.
gallery.sentenceTrans: 很多人来到美术馆欣赏这些著名的艺术作品。

game.definitionEn: an activity or a sport with rules in which people or teams compete against each other
game.sentence: We had a good time playing the board game together.
game.sentenceTrans: 我们一起玩桌游玩得很开心。

gap.definitionEn: a space between two things or in the middle of something, especially because there is a part missing; a difference that separates people, or their opinions, situation, etc.; a space where something is missing; a period of time when something stops, or between two events
gap.sentence: Please mind the gap between the train and the platform!
gap.sentenceTrans: 请当心列车与站台之间的间隙！

garage.definitionEn: a place where vehicles are repaired and where you can buy a car or buy petrol/gas and oil
garage.sentence: There is a car parked in the garage.
garage.mnemonic: gar掩盖，保护 + age名词后缀 → 遮挡和维修的地方 → garage车库，维修厂

garbage.definitionEn: waste food, paper, etc. that you throw away; a place or container where waste food, paper, etc. can be placed; something stupid or not true
garbage.sentence: A few bags of garbage are left on the street.
garbage.sentenceTrans: 好几袋垃圾被丢在街上。

garden.definition: 花园，菜园；  v.从事园艺
garden.definitionEn: a piece of land next to or around your house where you can grow flowers, fruit, vegetables, etc., usually with a lawn
garden.sentence: There are many flowers in the garden.

gas.definitionEn: any substance like air that is neither a solid nor a liquid, for example hydrogen and oxygen are both gases
gas.sentence: A cloud of gas is coming out from the chimney.
gas.sentenceTrans: 一团气体正从烟囱里冒出来。

gasoline.definitionEn: a liquid obtained from petroleum, used as fuel in car engines, etc.
gasoline.sentence: She is filling up her car with gasoline.
gasoline.sentenceTrans: 她正在给自己的车加油。
gasoline.mnemonic: gasol液化气 + ine名词后缀 → gasoline(美)汽油

gate.definitionEn: a place in a wall or a fence that has a movable part which can be opened or closed like a door
gate.sentence: The gate was closed, so we couldn't go in.
gate.sentenceTrans: 大门关上了，所以我们进不去。

gather.definitionEn: to come together, or bring people together, in one place to form a group; to collect plants, fruit, etc. from a wide area; to reach a conclusion often intuitively from hints or through inferences
gather.sentence: People gather around to listen to the girl's beautiful singing.
gather.sentenceTrans: 人们聚在一块，听女孩美妙的演唱。

gay.definition: 同性恋的；  n.同性恋者
gay.definitionEn: a person who is homosexual, especially a man
gay.sentence: This gay-themed movie tells the story of the emotional relationship between two men.
gay.sentenceTrans: 这部电影以同性恋为主题，讲述了两个男人之间的情感关系。

gene.definitionEn: a unit inside a cell which controls a particular quality in a living thing that has been passed on from its parents
gene.sentence: DNA consists of a large number of genes.

general.definition: 普遍的，总的；大体的，大致的，笼统的；首席的，总管的；  n.将军
general.definitionEn: affecting all or most people, places or things;  normal; usual; including the most important aspects of something; not exact or detailed; approximately, but not exactly, the direction/area mentioned; not limited to a particular subject, use or activity; not limited to one part or aspect of a person or thing; highest in rank; chief
general.sentence: In general, trees are tall, green, and have brown bark.
general.sentenceTrans: 一般来说，树木是又高又绿的，而且还有棕色的树皮。

generally.definition: 一般地，通常；笼统地，概括地
generally.sentence: The weather this week will be generally rainy.
generally.sentenceTrans: 这个星期的天气普遍有雨。
generally.mnemonic: gener出生 + ally……地 → 出生具有普遍性 → 通常地；通常强调普遍性

generate.sentence: A man is riding the bicycle to generate electricity.
generate.sentenceTrans: 一个男人骑着自行车来发电。
generate.mnemonic: gener出生，产生 + ate做，造成 → generate发生，引起

generation.definitionEn: all the people who were born at about the same time;  the average time in which children grow up, become adults and have children of their own, (usually considered to be about 30 years)
generation.sentence: My family includes three generations of people.
generation.mnemonic: generate 产生，发生 + ion表名词 → 产生出的一代人 → generation一代；一代人

generous.definition: 慷慨大方的；充裕的，宽厚的
generous.definitionEn: giving or willing to give freely; given freely
generous.sentence: The generous guy just gave the poor man some money.
generous.sentenceTrans: 这个慷慨大方的人刚给了这个穷人一些钱。
generous.mnemonic: gener出生，产生 + ous形容词后缀 → [不断]产生 → generous丰富的，慷慨的

genetic.definitionEn: connected with genes (= the units in the cells of a living thing that control its physical characteristics) or genetics (= the study of genes )
genetic.sentence: Once I saw her mother, I realized that her blonde hair must be genetic.
genetic.sentenceTrans: 一看到她母亲，我就明白了她的金发是遗传的。
genetic.mnemonic: gen出生，产生 + etic与……相关的 → 与出生相关的 → genetic基因的，遗传学的

genius.definitionEn: a person who is unusually intelligent or artistic, or who has a very high level of skill, especially in one area
genius.sentence: The musical genius was a composer even in childhood.
genius.sentenceTrans: 这位音乐天才小时候就是作曲家了。
genius.mnemonic: gen=gene出生 + ius  → 出生就有  → genius天才

gentle.definitionEn: calm and kind; doing things in a quiet and careful way; (of weather, temperature, etc.) not strong or extreme; having only a small effect; not strong or violent; not steep or sharp
gentle.sentence: He was very gentle and gave me his coat.
gentle.sentenceTrans: 他很绅士，把他的外套给我了。

gentleman.definitionEn: a man who treats other people in a proper and polite way
gentleman.sentence: "Thank you. You are really a gentleman."
gentleman.mnemonic: gentle温和的 + man人 → gentleman绅士；有教养的人

gently.definitionEn: With a mild, kind, or tender manner
gently.sentenceTrans: 孩子们对他们的玩具很温柔。
gently.mnemonic: gent温和的 + ly...地 → gently轻轻地；温柔地，温和地

genuine.definitionEn: real; exactly what it appears to be; not artificial
genuine.sentence: Which one is the genuine painting of the famous artist?
genuine.sentenceTrans: 哪一幅才是这位著名画家的真迹？
genuine.mnemonic: genu导致，产生 + ine形容词后缀 → 确实产生出的东西 → genuine真的，真正的

genuinely.definitionEn: in accordance with truth or fact or reality
genuinely.sentence: She was genuinely happy to see her old friend after so many years.
genuinely.sentenceTrans: 见到多年未见的老朋友，她由衷地感到高兴。

geography.definitionEn: (uncountable) the scientific study of the earth's surface, physical features, divisions, products, population, etc.
geography.sentence: Geography can help us know the world better.
geography.sentenceTrans: 学习地理可以让我们更好地了解世界。
geography.mnemonic: geo地球 + graphy写，图 → geography地理，地理学

geometry.definitionEn: the branch of mathematics that deals with the measurements and relationships of lines, angles, surfaces and solids
geometry.sentence: The little boy is so good at solving the mathematical problems of geometry.
geometry.sentenceTrans: 这个小男孩很擅长解决几何类的数学问题。
geometry.mnemonic: geo地 + metry计量，测量 → 测量地面 → geometry几何学

gesture.definitionEn: a movement of your body (especially of your hands and arms) that shows or emphasizes an idea or a feeling
gesture.sentence: This gesture means they think you are very good.
gesture.sentenceTrans: 这种手势表示他们认为你很棒。
gesture.mnemonic: gest带来，产生 + ure名词后缀 → 带来信息的动作 → gesture手势

get.definition: 得到，获得，赢得；收到，接到
get.sentence: They all get what they want.
get.sentenceTrans: 他们都得到了他们想要的。

ghost.definitionEn: the soul of a dead person thought of as living in an unseen world or as appearing to living people
ghost.sentence: There are ghosts in movies and stories, but I don't think they are real.
ghost.sentenceTrans: 电影和故事里有鬼魂，但我认为它们（在现实生活中）不是真的。

giant.definition: 巨大的，特大的；  n.伟人
giant.definitionEn: very large; much larger or more important than similar things usually are
giant.sentence: The giant rock is naturally balanced.
giant.sentenceTrans: 这块巨大的石头保持着天然的平衡。

gift.sentence: She has a gift for math.

girl.definitionEn: a young woman; a female child
girl.sentence: The girl with brown hair is so cute.
girl.sentenceTrans: 这个棕色头发的女孩太可爱了。

give.definitionEn: to hand something to somebody so that they can look at it, use it or keep it for a time
give.sentence: The child is giving the old man a piece of bread.
give.sentenceTrans: 小孩给了那个老人一块面包。

given.definition: 考虑到；  adj.指定的，特定的；  v.给，给予（give的过去分词）
given.definitionEn: an assumption that is taken for granted
given.sentence: Given that she is only three years old, she can draw very well.
given.sentenceTrans: 考虑到她只有三岁，她已经画得很好了。

glad.sentence: I am glad to be sharing my speech with you today.
glad.sentenceTrans: 很高兴今天能给大家做演讲。

glance.sentence: I glanced at her, but she didn't notice.
glance.sentenceTrans: 我瞥了她一眼，但是她没有注意到。
glance.mnemonic: glanc冰，光滑 + ance表名词，性质，状况 → 像冰上划过的光线 → glance一瞥，扫视

glass.definitionEn: (often in compounds) a container made of glass, used for drinking out of
glass.sentence: She is drinking water from the glass.

glimpse.definitionEn: a look at somebody/something for a very short time, when you do not see the person or thing completely
glimpse.sentence: Alice caught a quick glimpse of Wonderland through the tiny door.
glimpse.sentenceTrans: 爱丽丝透过小小的门匆匆瞥见了仙境。

global.definitionEn: covering or affecting the whole world
global.sentence: With the Internet, we can have a global network of friends.
global.sentenceTrans: 有了互联网，我们可以和全世界的朋友联系。
global.mnemonic: glob地球 + al……的 → global全球的

globe.definitionEn: the world (used especially to emphasize its size)
globe.sentence: Airplanes fly all over the globe, even over the poles.
globe.sentenceTrans: 飞机在全世界飞行，甚至会飞过两极上空。

glorious.definition: 辉煌的，壮丽的；光荣的，荣耀的
glorious.sentence: The sunrise in the countryside is quite glorious.
glorious.mnemonic: glori=glory光荣 + ous形容词后缀 → glorious光荣的

glory.definitionEn: fame, praise or honour that is given to somebody because they have achieved something important
glory.sentence: The pupil is completely immersed in the glory of receiving a red scarf.
glory.sentenceTrans: 这个小学生完完全全沉浸在佩戴上红领巾的光荣感中。

glove.definitionEn: a covering for the hand, made of wool, leather, etc. with separate parts for each finger and the thumb
glove.sentence: Gloves keep my fingers warm in winter.
glove.sentenceTrans: 手套使我的手指在冬天很暖和。

glow.definition: 微弱稳定的光；喜悦，满足的心情；  v.发光，发出微光
glow.definitionEn: a gold or red colour; a dull steady light, especially from a fire that has stopped producing flames; the pink colour in your face when you have been doing exercise or feel happy and excited; a gold or red colour
glow.sentence: The orange glow of the sunset is so beautiful!
glow.sentenceTrans: 夕阳的橘色光芒太美了！

go.definitionEn: to move or travel from one place to another

goal.definitionEn: the act of kicking or hitting the ball into the goal; a point that is scored for this
goal.sentence: The boy's goal is to become as strong as the man in the poster.
goal.sentenceTrans: 男孩的目标是变得像海报里的男人一样强壮。

goat.definitionEn: an animal with horns and a coat of hair, that lives wild in mountain areas or is kept on farms for its milk or meat
goat.sentence: I love my pet goat even though it eats everything.
goat.sentenceTrans: 我爱我的宠物山羊，尽管它什么都吃。

god.definitionEn: (in some religions) a being or spirit who is believed to have power over a particular part of nature or who is believed to represent a particular quality
god.sentence: Poseidon was the God of the sea in ancient Greek myths.
god.sentenceTrans: 波塞冬是古希腊神话中的海神。

gold.definitionEn: a chemical element. Gold is a yellow precious metal used for making coins, jewellery, decorative objects, etc.; money, jewellery, etc. that is made of gold
gold.sentence: The boy made a lot of gold with his magic powers.
gold.sentenceTrans: 爱德华用炼金术做出了许多金子。

golden.definition: 金黄色的；金色的；特别的，美好的
golden.definitionEn: having the deep yellow color of gold
golden.mnemonic: gold金子 + en由…制成的 → golden金色的

good.definitionEn: of high quality or an acceptable standard
good.sentence: She has figured out a good idea.

goodbye.definition: 再见（也作good bye）；  n.再见

goodness.definition: 善良，美德；精髓；  int.天哪，哎呀
goodness.definitionEn: the quality of being good; the part of something that has a useful effect on somebody/something, especially somebody’s health
goodness.sentence: Taking care of the injured kittens shows her goodness.
goodness.sentenceTrans: 照顾受伤的小猫展现了她善良的一面。
goodness.mnemonic: good好的 + ness表名词 → goodness善行，优良

goods.definitionEn: things that are produced to be sold
goods.sentence: The goods are sent to us every day.
goods.sentenceTrans: 每天，这些货物都会被寄送给我们。

goose.sentence: We can tell from the shape of its head that this is a goose.
goose.sentenceTrans: 我们可以根据它头部的形状断定这是一只鹅。

govern.definitionEn: to legally control a country or its people and be responsible for introducing new laws, organizing public services, etc.

government.definitionEn: a particular system used for controlling a country, state, etc.
government.sentence: The offices of the local government are in this building.
government.sentenceTrans: 当地政府的办公室就在这栋楼里。
government.mnemonic: govern统治 + ment表名词 → 政府

governor.definitionEn: a person who is chosen to be in charge of the government of a state in the US
governor.sentence: The governor is giving a speech.
governor.sentenceTrans: 这位州长正在发表演讲。
governor.mnemonic: govern管理 + or名词后缀：人 → governor总督

grab.definition: 抓住，抓取；  v.抓住；攫取
grab.definitionEn: to take or hold somebody/something with your hand suddenly, firmly or roughly; to try to take hold of something
grab.sentence: Babies love to grab your fingers.
grab.sentenceTrans: 婴儿喜欢抓住你的手指。

grace.definitionEn: an attractive quality of movement that is smooth, elegant and controlled
grace.sentence: She moves with the natural grace of a ballerina.
grace.sentenceTrans: 她的动作具有芭蕾舞演员的自然优雅。

graceful.definitionEn: moving in a controlled, attractive way or having a smooth, attractive form; polite and kind in your behaviour, especially in a difficult situation
graceful.sentence: She is such a graceful and beautiful actress!
graceful.sentenceTrans: 她是一个如此优雅美丽的演员！
graceful.mnemonic: grace优雅 + ful形容词后缀：…的 → graceful优雅的

grade.definition: 年级；  v.给……分等级；给（试卷或作业）评分
grade.definitionEn: a mark given in an exam or for a piece of school work
grade.sentence: I am in Class one, Grade three.

gradual.definitionEn: happening or developing slowly and by degrees; not sudden; (of a slope) not steep
gradual.sentence: The graph shows a gradual increase.
gradual.sentenceTrans: 图表显示出了逐步的增长。
gradual.mnemonic: grad(e)等级 + ual形容词后缀 → gradual逐步的

gradually.definitionEn: slowly, over a long period of time
gradually.sentence: Gradually, he becomes stronger and stronger.
gradually.sentenceTrans: 渐渐地，他变得越来越强壮。
gradually.mnemonic: gradual逐步的 + ly…...地 → gradually逐步地

graduate.definitionEn: to get a degree, especially your first degree, from a university or college
graduate.sentence: She graduated from university after four years' unforgettable life.
graduate.sentenceTrans: 经过四年难忘的大学生活，她毕业了。
graduate.mnemonic: grad步 + uate使 → 完成所有步骤 → graduate毕业

graduation.definitionEn: the act of successfully completing a university degree, or studies at an American high school
graduation.sentence: Graduation day is finally here! It’s time to celebrate our achievements.
graduation.sentenceTrans: 毕业典礼终于到了！是时候庆祝我们的成就了。
graduation.mnemonic: grad步，级 + uat=ate做… + ion名词后缀 → 使升级并走出 → graduation毕业

grain.definitionEn: the small hard seeds of food plants such as wheat, rice, etc.
grain.sentence: There is a bag of grains on the table.

grammar.definitionEn: the rules in a language for changing the form of words and joining them into sentences; a book containing a description of the rules of a language
grammar.sentence: The English teacher is teaching grammar now.
grammar.sentenceTrans: 英语老师现在正在教语法。
grammar.mnemonic: gramm=gram写，图 + ar表物 → 写的(规则） → grammar语法

grand.definition: 壮丽的，宏伟的，宏大的；  n.一千美元；大钢琴
grand.sentence: The hotel lobby was very impressive and grand.
grand.sentenceTrans: 这家酒店大堂气势宏伟，令人印象深刻。

grandfather.definitionEn: the father of your father or mother
grandfather.sentence: "Grandfather is the father of your parent," the boy said.
grandfather.sentenceTrans: “祖父就是你爸爸或你妈妈的父亲。”男孩说道。
grandfather.mnemonic: grand宏伟的 + father父亲 → grandfather祖父，外祖父

grandmother.definitionEn: the mother of your father or mother
grandmother.sentence: My grandmother gave me a candy cane.
grandmother.sentenceTrans: 我祖母给了我一个拐杖糖。
grandmother.mnemonic: grand显赫的，最高的 + mother母亲 → grandmother祖母，外祖母

grant.definition: 允许，同意，准允；  n.拨款；补助金
grant.definitionEn: to agree to give somebody what they ask for, especially formal or legal permission to do something
grant.sentence: The Subway Committee grants the blind permission to bring guide dogs on board.
grant.sentenceTrans: 地铁委员会允许盲人携带导盲犬上地铁。

graph.definitionEn: a planned drawing, consisting of a line or lines, showing how two or more sets of numbers are related to each other
graph.sentence: He is sitting in front of a computer and reading a lot of graphs.
graph.sentenceTrans: 他正坐在电脑前看各种图表。

grasp.definition: 抓住，抓紧；领会，理解；  n.紧握
grasp.definitionEn: to take a firm hold of somebody/something
grasp.sentence: The baby grasped his mother's finger.
grasp.sentenceTrans: 婴儿抓住了母亲的手指。

grass.definition: 草，牧草；<俚>大麻；告密的人；  v.喂草，以牧草喂养；放牧；告发
grass.definitionEn: an area of ground covered with grass
grass.sentence: It feels great to lie down on the grass.

grateful.definitionEn: feeling or showing thanks because somebody has done something kind for you or has done as you asked
grateful.sentence: Everyone was so grateful to the medical team that they lined the road, waving goodbye thankfully.
grateful.sentenceTrans: 每个人都非常感谢医疗队。他们站在路边，满怀感激地挥手告别。
grateful.mnemonic: grate感激，高兴 + ful多…...的 → grateful感谢的；愉快的

gratitude.definitionEn: the feeling of being grateful and wanting to express your thanks
gratitude.sentence: In the speech, she expressed great gratitude to her mother.
gratitude.sentenceTrans: 她在演讲中表达了对母亲的无限感激。
gratitude.mnemonic: grat(e)感谢 + itude名词后缀 → gratitude感激，感恩

grave.definition: 墓；  adj.严肃的，庄重的；严重的
grave.definitionEn: serious in manner, as if something sad, important or worrying has just happened
grave.sentence: He went down on his knee in front of the two graves.
grave.sentenceTrans: 夏尔跪在爱德华兄弟的墓碑前。
grave.mnemonic: grav重 + e → grave严重的；庄重的

gravity.definitionEn: the force that attracts objects in space towards each other, and that on the earth pulls them towards the centre of the planet, so that things fall to the ground when they are dropped
gravity.sentence: Things fall down because of gravity.
gravity.mnemonic: grav重 + ity名词后缀 → gravity庄重；地心吸力

gray.definition: 灰色的；暗淡的；  n.灰色，暗淡
gray.definitionEn: having a color between black and white; having a color that is like the color of smoke; dull; full of clouds
gray.sentence: My grandmother has a full head of gray hair.

great.definition: 伟大的；极好的，极棒的；非常好的；  adv.（口语）好极了，很好地
great.definitionEn: very large; much bigger than average in size or quantity
great.sentence: Vincent van Gogh is one of the greatest painters in the history of Western art.
great.sentenceTrans: 梵高是西方艺术史上最伟大的画家之一。

greedy.definitionEn: wanting more money, power, food, etc. than you really need
greedy.sentence: The greedy dog also wants the bone in the water.
greedy.sentenceTrans: 这只贪婪的狗狗还想要水里的骨头。
greedy.mnemonic: greed贪婪 + y…的 → greedy贪吃的，贪婪的，贪心的

green.definition: 绿色的，青的，草绿色的；缺乏经验的；生的，未熟的；  n.绿色
green.definitionEn: having the colour of grass or the leaves of most plants and trees; covered with grass or other plants

greenhouse.definitionEn: a building with glass sides and a glass roof for growing plants in
greenhouse.sentence: Greenhouses are the best place to grow plants quickly.
greenhouse.sentenceTrans: 温室是快速栽种植物的最好地方。
greenhouse.mnemonic: green绿色 + house屋子 → 温室，暖房

greet.definitionEn: to say hello to somebody or to welcome them
greet.sentence: This gentleman takes his hat off to greet people.
greet.sentenceTrans: 这位绅士摘下他的帽子，向人们问好。

greeting.definitionEn: something that you say or do to greet somebody
greeting.sentence: He exchanged greetings with his neighbor.
greeting.mnemonic: greet问候 + ing名词后缀 → greeting问候，招呼，致敬

grey.definitionEn: having a color between black and white :having a color that is like the color of smoke
grey.sentence: The grey T-shirt is more popular than the white one.
grey.sentenceTrans: 灰色的衬衫比白色的更受欢迎。

grip.definition: 紧握，握力；握力；  v.握紧，抓牢
grip.definitionEn: to hold something tightly; to hold onto or to move over a surface without slipping
grip.sentence: You'd better not lose your grip on the rock for your safety.
grip.sentenceTrans: 安全起见，你最好紧紧抓住那块石头。

grocer.definitionEn: a person who owns, manages or works in a shop/store selling food and other things used in the home; a shop/store that sells these things
grocer.sentence: This grocer is very nice, he always gives me a discount.
grocer.sentenceTrans: 这个食品杂货商超好，他总是给我打折。

grocery.definitionEn: a shop/store that sells food and other things used in the home. In American English ‘grocery store’ is often used to mean ‘supermarket’.
grocery.sentence: The man works happily in this grocery store.
grocery.sentenceTrans: 这个男人在这家杂货店工作得很开心。

gross.definition: 总的，毛重的；令人恶心的
gross.definitionEn: being the total amount of something before anything is taken away; very unpleasant; very rude
gross.sentence: The gross cost for all these things is very high.
gross.sentenceTrans: 这些东西的总成本很高。

ground.sentence: The man is lying on the ground.

group.definitionEn: a number of people or things that are together or in the same place
group.sentence: A group of people are sitting over here.

grow.definitionEn: to exist and develop in a particular place; to make plants grow
grow.sentence: If you wait, you can watch a plant grow.
grow.sentenceTrans: 你如果等待，你能看到一颗植物的成长。

growth.definitionEn: (of people, animals or plants) the process of growing physically, mentally or emotionally; something that has grown
growth.sentenceTrans: 植物需要阳光才能生长。
growth.mnemonic: grow成长 + th名词后缀 → growth生长，增长

guarantee.definitionEn: a firm promise that you will do something or that something will happen
guarantee.sentence: To secure the loan John needs to find a third party who will guarantee his repayment.
guarantee.sentenceTrans: 为了获得贷款，约翰需要找到一个第三方来担保。

guard.definition: 警戒，保卫；  v.警惕；  v.保卫，守护
guard.definitionEn: a person, such as a soldier, a police officer or a prison officer, who protects a place or people, or prevents prisoners from escaping
guard.sentence: Guard is necessary if we want to catch the criminal.
guard.sentenceTrans: 如果我们想抓罪犯，保持警戒很有必要。

guess.definition: 猜测，估计；  n.猜测，猜想
guess.definitionEn: to try and give an answer or make a judgement about something without being sure of all the facts
guess.sentence: The daughter wants her mother to guess the fruit by smell.
guess.sentenceTrans: 女儿想让她妈妈凭气味猜水果。

guest.definition: 客人，宾客；  v.做特邀嘉宾
guest.definitionEn: a person that you have invited to your house or to a particular event that you are paying for
guest.sentence: We are waiting at the door for the arrival of our guests.
guest.sentenceTrans: 我们在门口等待客人的到来。

guidance.definitionEn: help or advice that is given to somebody, especially by somebody older or with more experience
guidance.sentence: The coach is giving the players some guidance.
guidance.sentenceTrans: 教练正在给球员们提供指导。
guidance.mnemonic: guid(e)指南 + ance名词后缀 → guidance指导

guide.definition: 引导，指导；  n.指南，手册；向导；导游
guide.definitionEn: to direct or influence somebody’s behaviour; to help somebody to move in a particular direction; to move something in a particular direction
guide.sentence: The woman is guided by a guide dog.
guide.sentenceTrans: 这个女人正被导盲犬带着走。

guilt.definitionEn: the unhappy feelings caused by knowing or thinking that you have done something wrong
guilt.sentence: The boy is filled with guilt because he has broken the glass.
guilt.sentenceTrans: 那个小男孩很内疚，因为他打碎了玻璃杯。

guilty.definitionEn: feeling ashamed because you have done something that you know is wrong or have not done something that you should have done
guilty.sentence: The dog felt very guilty for destroying the living room.
guilty.sentenceTrans: 这只狗因为破坏了客厅而感到很内疚。
guilty.mnemonic: guilt内疚 + y...的 → guilty内疚的；有罪的

gum.definitionEn: a sweet/candy that you chew but do not swallow
gum.sentence: My breath smells terrible. I need some gum.
gum.sentenceTrans: 我口气很难闻，我需要嚼点口香糖。

gun.definitionEn: a weapon that shoots bullets or shells
gun.sentence: The man looks cool with a gun in his hand.
gun.sentenceTrans: 这个拿枪的男人看起来太酷了。

gym.definition: 体育馆，健身房；体育，体操
gym.definitionEn: a room or hall with equipment for doing physical exercise, for example in a school
gym.sentence: There are many people exercising in the gym.
gym.sentenceTrans: 有很多人正在体育馆里运动。

gymnasium.definitionEn: a room or hall with equipment for doing physical exercise, for example in a school
gymnasium.sentence: The most popular facility in that gymnasium is the treadmill.
gymnasium.sentenceTrans: 跑步机是那家健身房里最受欢迎的器材。
gymnasium.mnemonic: gymn裸体的 + asium脱衣服锻炼的地方 → gymnasium体育馆

habit.definitionEn: a thing that you do often and almost without thinking, especially something that is hard to stop doing
habit.sentence: Make a habit of washing your hands after using the bathroom!
habit.sentenceTrans: 要养成上完厕所就洗手的习惯。

habitual.definitionEn: (of an action) done, often in a way that is annoying or difficult to stop
habitual.sentence: He is a habitual early riser who always gets up at 6 o'clock.
habitual.sentenceTrans: 他习惯在清晨六点早起。
habitual.mnemonic: habit习惯 + ual形容词后缀 → habitual习惯的，惯常的

hair.definitionEn: the substance that looks like a mass of fine threads growing especially on the head; one of these threads growing on the body of people and some animals
hair.sentence: How did you get your hair so straight?
hair.sentenceTrans: 你是如何让你的头发这么直的？

half.definitionEn: one of two equal or nearly equal parts into which something can be divided
half.sentence: I drank half of the orange juice.

halfway.definitionEn: in the middle of a place or between two points, at an equal distance from each of them
halfway.sentence: He is halfway up the stairs.

hall.definitionEn: a building or large room for public meetings, meals, concerts, etc.
hall.sentence: The conference hall with red chairs is empty.
hall.sentenceTrans: 这个配有红色椅子的会堂空空荡荡的。

halt.definitionEn: to stop; to make somebody/something stop
halt.sentence: The teacher halted the discussion to address a student's question.
halt.sentenceTrans: 老师暂停讨论来回答一个学生的问题。

hammer.definitionEn: a tool with a handle and a heavy metal head, used for breaking things or hitting nails
hammer.sentence: I used a big hammer to push in the nail.
hammer.sentenceTrans: 我用锤子来把钉子敲进去。

hand.definitionEn: the part of the body at the end of the arm, including the fingers and thumb
hand.sentence: She handed the gift to her friend.
hand.sentenceTrans: 她把礼物交给了她的朋友。

handicap.definition: 残疾，生理缺陷；障碍，阻碍；  v.使不利，妨碍
handicap.definitionEn: a permanent physical or mental condition that makes it difficult or impossible to use a particular part of your body or mind
handicap.sentence: The soldier who has a handicap proudly stands with the others.
handicap.sentenceTrans: 这位残疾士兵骄傲地和其他士兵站在一起。

handkerchief.definitionEn: a small piece of material or paper that you use for blowing your nose, etc.
handkerchief.sentence: These handkerchiefs have flowers on them.

handle.definitionEn: the part of a door, drawer, window, etc. that you use to open it; the part of an object, such as a cup, a bag or a tool, that you use to hold it or carry it
handle.sentence: Turn the handle and the door will open.
handle.mnemonic: hand手 + le表示做某种动作时所使用的东西 → handle柄，把手

handsome.definition: 英俊的，帅气的；（金额）相当大的，可观的，优厚的
handsome.sentence: The handsome man posed for pictures.
handsome.sentenceTrans: 这位英俊的男子摆好姿势准备照相。
handsome.mnemonic: hand操作 + some一些 → 易于操作的，可用的 → handsome合适的，外形好的

handwriting.sentence: His beautiful handwriting is easy to read.
handwriting.sentenceTrans: 他漂亮的笔迹清晰易读。
handwriting.mnemonic: hand手 + writing写 → handwriting笔迹，书法

handy.definitionEn: easy to use or to do
handy.sentence: My daddy has many handy tools.
handy.sentenceTrans: 我爸爸有很多简便的工具。
handy.mnemonic: hand手 + y形容词后缀 → handy手巧的，伸手可及的

hang.definition: 悬挂，吊起；  n.悬挂；绞刑
