hang.definitionEn: to kill somebody, usually as a punishment, by tying a rope around their neck and allowing them to drop; to attach something, or to be attached, at the top so that the lower part is free or loose
hang.sentence: A luxurious drop lamp is hanging on the ceiling.
hang.sentenceTrans: 一盏奢华的吊灯挂在天花板上。

happen.definitionEn: to take place, especially without being planned
happen.sentence: How did this horrible accident happen?
happen.sentenceTrans: 这次可怕的事故是如何发生的？
happen.mnemonic: happ出现，是这种情况 + en动词后缀 → happen发生

happening.definition: 意外事件；偶然发生的事；  v.动词happen的现在分词形式
happening.sentence: The police are asking her about the happening.
happening.sentenceTrans: 警察们正在向她询问事件。

happy.sentence: Look at her big smile! She is so happy.
happy.sentenceTrans: 快看她那大大的笑容，她真的很快乐。
happy.mnemonic: happ机会，运气 + y...的 → 有运气的 → happy幸福的

harbor.definitionEn: an area of water on the coast, protected from the open sea by strong walls, where ships can shelter
harbor.sentence: There are many boats in the harbor.
harbor.sentenceTrans: 这个海港停靠着许多船只。
harbor.mnemonic: har军队，队伍 + bor保护，庇护所 → 保护地 → harbor避风港，海港

harbour.definition: 海港；  v.包庇，庇护；窝藏
harbour.definitionEn: an area of water on the coast, protected from the open sea by strong walls, where ships can shelter
harbour.sentence: The ships dock at the harbour.

hard.definition: 坚硬的；困难的；  adv.努力地，艰难地，费力地
hard.definitionEn: solid, firm or stiff and difficult to bend or break
hard.sentence: This climb's pretty hard—I hope I don't fall off.
hard.sentenceTrans: 攀岩好难，希望我别掉下去。

hardly.definitionEn: almost no; almost not; almost none
hardly.sentence: The man always stays at home and hardly goes out.
hardly.sentenceTrans: 这个男人整天待在家，几乎不出门。
hardly.mnemonic: hard艰难 + ly...地 → ad.几乎不，简直不

hardship.definitionEn: a situation that is difficult and unpleasant because you do not have enough money, food, clothes, etc.
hardship.sentence: An orphan faces a life of great hardship.
hardship.sentenceTrans: 孤儿总要面对一个艰难的人生。
hardship.mnemonic: hard艰难的 + ship表情况 → 苦难

hardware.definitionEn: things (such as tools or parts of machines) that are made of metal; the machinery and electronic parts of a computer system
hardware.sentence: He bought a lot of hardware from that store.
hardware.sentenceTrans: 他从那家店买了很多五金器具。
hardware.mnemonic: hard硬 + ware物件 → hardware五金器具

harm.definitionEn: damage or injury that is caused by a person or an event
harm.sentence: Spending too much time on his smartphone may harm his eyes.
harm.sentenceTrans: 过度使用手机会伤害他的眼睛。

harmful.definitionEn: causing damage or injury to somebody/something, especially to a person’s health or to the environment
harmful.sentence: Poor posture can be very harmful to one's back.
harmful.sentenceTrans: 错误的坐姿对人的背部非常有害。
harmful.mnemonic: harm伤害 + ful形容词后缀 → harmful有害的

harmonious.definitionEn: (of sounds) very pleasant when played or sung together; arranged together in a pleasing way so that each part goes well with the other; (of relationships, etc.) friendly, peaceful and without any disagreement
harmonious.sentence: A harmonious color palette can elevate your entire outfit effortlessly.
harmonious.sentenceTrans: 和谐的色彩搭配可以毫不费力地提升你的整体穿搭。
harmonious.mnemonic: harmon(y)和谐 + ious形容词后缀 → harmonious和谐的

harmony.definitionEn: a state of peaceful existence and agreement
harmony.sentence: The Yin-Yang is a symbol of harmony.
harmony.sentenceTrans: 阴阳是和谐的一种象征。
harmony.mnemonic: harm=ar适合 + ony表名词 → 适合的心态 → harmony和谐

harness.definition: 挽具，马具；  v.利用；治理（河流等）
harness.definitionEn: a set of strips of leather and metal pieces that is put around a horse’s head and body so that the horse can be controlled and fastened to a carriage, etc.; a set of strips of leather, etc. for fastening something to a person’s body or to keep them from moving off or falling
harness.sentence: The construction worker is wearing a safety harness around his body.
harness.sentenceTrans: 这名建筑工人身上拴着安全带。
harness.mnemonic: har军队 + ness供给，供应 → harness提供给士兵的 → harness保护带；挽具

harsh.definition: 刺耳的；严厉的；粗糙的；严酷的
harsh.sentence: The harsh noise woke me up.
harsh.sentenceTrans: 刺耳的噪音把我吵醒了。

harvest.definition: 收成；  v.收割；获得；采集
harvest.definitionEn: the act of cutting and gathering crops, or the amount of crops, cut and gathered
harvest.sentence: The wheat harvest is very good this year.

haste.definitionEn: speed in doing something, especially because you do not have enough time
haste.sentence: They have to make haste to catch the flight.
haste.sentenceTrans: 他们必须赶快才能坐上飞机。

hat.definitionEn: a covering made to fit the head, often with a brim (= a flat edge that sticks out), and worn out of doors a straw
hat.sentence: As it was sunny, she wore a hat while walking on the beach.
hat.sentenceTrans: 因为阳光明媚，她戴着帽子走在沙滩上。

hate.definition: 恨，憎恨；不喜欢，讨厌；  n.恨，憎恶

hatred.definitionEn: a very strong feeling of dislike for somebody/something
hatred.sentence: He has a lot of hatred for this terrible phone.
hatred.sentenceTrans: 他对这个糟糕的手机有极大的怨恨。
hatred.mnemonic: hatr仇恨 + ed名词后缀 → hatred憎恶，憎恨，仇恨

hazard.definition: 危险；  v.使冒险，冒险做
hazard.definitionEn: a thing that can be dangerous or cause damage
hazard.sentence: In big cities, there are always plenty of road hazards to watch out for.
hazard.sentenceTrans: 在大城市里，我们总是有很多道路危险要注意。

he.definitionEn: a male person or animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified
he.sentence: He is filling in his gender on the form.
he.sentenceTrans: 他正在表格上填写他的性别。

head.definition: 头；上端；  v.领导; 主管；  adj.领头的
head.definitionEn: the part of the body containing the brain, eyes, ears, nose, and mouth
head.sentence: My head aches—maybe I think too much.
head.sentenceTrans: 头好痛，也许是我用脑太多了。

headache.definitionEn: a continuous pain in the head
headache.sentence: The man is suffering from a headache.
headache.sentenceTrans: 这位男士正在遭受头痛的折磨。

heading.definition: 标题（用于文章或章节开头）；  v.head的现在分词
heading.definitionEn: a title printed at the top of a page or at the beginning of a section of a book
heading.sentence: The heading of the newspaper is larger in size.
heading.sentenceTrans: 报纸的标题的字号大一些。
heading.mnemonic: head头 + ing表名词 → 文章中在顶头的 → heading标题

headline.definitionEn: the title of a newspaper article printed in large letters, especially at the top of the front page
headline.sentence: I didn't read the story; I only saw the headline.
headline.sentenceTrans: 我没读这个故事，我只看了大字标题。
headline.mnemonic: head头 + line字行 → 头一行字 → headline标题

headmaster.definitionEn: a male teacher who is in charge of a school, especially a private school
headmaster.sentence: The headmaster is responsible for the management of this school.
headmaster.sentenceTrans: 这位校长负责管理这所学校。
headmaster.mnemonic: head头 + master主人 → 学校里最高层的管理者 → headmaster英国中小学校长，男舍监

headquarters.definition: 总部，总局；司令部，指挥部
headquarters.definitionEn: a place from which an organization or a military operation is controlled
headquarters.sentence: The EU headquarters is located in Brussels.
headquarters.mnemonic: head头 + quarter使驻扎 + s表地点 → 头脑聚集的地方 → 司令部；总部

heal.definitionEn: to become healthy again; to make something healthy again
heal.sentence: The doctor's treatment has healed the wounded man.
heal.sentenceTrans: 医生的治疗已经让那个受伤的男人痊愈了。

health.definitionEn: the state of being physically and mentally healthy
health.sentence: Eating lots of fruits and vegetables is good for your health.
health.sentenceTrans: 多吃蔬菜水果对你的健康是有益的。
health.mnemonic: heal未受伤的，完好的 + th抽象名词后缀 → health健康

healthy.definitionEn: having good health and not likely to become ill/sick
healthy.mnemonic: health健康 + y ...的 → 健康的；有益健康的

heap.sentence: Heaps of files are waiting to be classified.
heap.sentenceTrans: 有一大堆文件等待被归类。

hear.sentenceTrans: 他听到了一些让人震惊的事情。

heart.definitionEn: a kind or generous feeling for other people
heart.sentenceTrans: 善良的人们拥有博大的心。

heat.definition: 热度；【物理学】热；  v.加热，变热
heat.definitionEn: hot weather; the hot conditions in a building/vehicle, etc.
heat.sentence: This summer the heat is unusually high.
heat.sentenceTrans: 这个夏天热度真的是离奇的高。

heaven.definitionEn: (in some religions) the place believed to be the home of God where good people go when they die; a place or situation in which you are very happy
heaven.sentence: The cat went to heaven after it died.

heavy.definitionEn: having great weight :difficult to lift or move
heavy.sentenceTrans: 当心别让这些集装箱掉下来，它们很重！

heel.definitionEn: the raised part on the bottom of a shoe, boot, etc. that makes the shoe, etc. higher at the back
heel.sentence: These new shoes are rubbing my heels.
heel.sentenceTrans: 这些新鞋磨我的脚后跟。

height.definitionEn: a measurement of how tall a person or thing is :the distance from the bottom to the top of a person or thing
height.sentence: The woman is measuring her daughter's height.
height.sentenceTrans: 这个女人正在给她女儿量身高。
height.mnemonic: heigh=high高的 + t(h)名词后缀，宽度或深度等 → height高度

heighten.definitionEn: if a feeling or an effect heightens, or something heightens it, it becomes stronger or increases
heighten.sentence: The gloomy weather heightened the horrible atmosphere in the graveyard.
heighten.sentenceTrans: 阴沉的天气增强了墓地的恐怖气氛。
heighten.mnemonic: height高度 + en变成 →加高，提高

hello.definitionEn: used as a greeting when you meet somebody, when you answer the telephone or when you want to attract somebody’s attention

help.definitionEn: to make it easier or possible for somebody to do something by doing something for them or by giving them something that they need
help.sentence: I offered her some help during the mountain climbing.
help.sentenceTrans: 爬山的时候，我向她提供了帮助。

helpful.definition: 有益的，有帮助的，有用的
helpful.definitionEn: (of a person) willing to help somebody
helpful.sentence: It is helpful to use a stick to move the rock.
helpful.sentenceTrans: 用棍子移动这块石头是有帮助的。
helpful.mnemonic: help帮助 + ful形容词后缀 → helpful肯帮忙的，给予帮助的

hen.definitionEn: a female chicken, often kept for its eggs or meat; any female bird
hen.sentence: I want to keep a hen so I can eat fresh eggs.
hen.sentenceTrans: 我想养只母鸡，这样就能吃到新鲜的鸡蛋了。

hence.sentence: There is always someone stealing the corn; hence, a fence has been built.
hence.sentenceTrans: 总是有人偷玉米，因此一个篱笆修了起来。

her.definitionEn: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a woman or girl who has already been mentioned or is easily identified

herd.definition: 兽群，牧群；  v.放牧，群集
herd.definitionEn: a group of animals of the same type that live and feed together
herd.sentence: Look! There is a herd of sheep!

here.definitionEn: used after a verb or preposition to mean ‘in, at or to this position or place’
here.sentenceTrans: 我们在这里随时为你服务。

heritage.definitionEn: (in compounds) used to describe a traditional product, brand, breed of animal or plant variety, especially one that is old-fashioned, rare and of high quality
heritage.sentence: Embroidery is an important part of Chinese cultural heritage whose craft should be retained.
heritage.sentenceTrans: 刺绣是中国文化遗产的重要组成部分，刺绣技艺应该保留下来。
heritage.mnemonic: herit继承 + age场所，物品 → 遗产

hero.definitionEn: a person who is admired for great or brave acts or fine qualities
hero.sentence: He was praised as a hero for saving the child from the river.
hero.sentenceTrans: 他从河里救出了孩子，被大家称赞为英雄。

heroic.definitionEn: showing extreme courage and admired by many people; of or relating to heroes
heroic.sentence: An ordinary man may also make a heroic move.
heroic.sentenceTrans: 一个普通人也能做出英勇的举动。
heroic.mnemonic: hero英雄 + ic形容词后缀 → heroic英雄的

hers.definitionEn: that which belongs to or is connected with her
hers.sentence: It's not my homework; it is hers.
hers.sentenceTrans: 这不是我的作业，是她的。

herself.definitionEn: (the reflexive form of she) used when the woman or girl who performs an action is also affected by it
herself.sentence: She can do everything all by herself.
herself.sentenceTrans: 她能自己搞定所有事情。
herself.mnemonic: her她 + self自己 → herself她自己

hesitate.definitionEn: to be slow to speak or act because you feel uncertain or nervous
hesitate.sentence: She hesitated to take the clothes of her choice.
hesitate.sentenceTrans: 她很犹豫要不要买下自己选的衣服。
hesitate.mnemonic: hes粘+ itate表动词 → hesitate脚被粘住，犹豫

hey.definitionEn: used to attract sb's attention or to express interest, surprise or anger

hi.sentence: We say "hi! " when we meet somebody.
hi.sentenceTrans: 我们在遇到别人的时候说“嗨！”。

hide.definition: 隐藏；躲藏；隐瞒；  n.（尤指买卖用的）兽皮
hide.definitionEn: to go to or stay at a place where you cannot be seen or found
hide.sentence: The boy is hiding inside the big box.
hide.sentenceTrans: 男孩就藏在这个大箱子里。

high.definitionEn: at or to a position or level that is a long way up from the ground or from the bottom

highlight.definitionEn: to emphasize something, especially so that people give it more attention; to mark part of a text with a special coloured pen, or to mark an area on a computer screen, to emphasize it or make it easier to see
highlight.sentence: You should highlight all the most important parts of the text.
highlight.sentenceTrans: 你应该标记出课文中所有最重要的部分。

highly.sentence: I highly recommend you today's special dish.
highly.sentenceTrans: 我强烈向你们推荐今天的特别菜。
highly.mnemonic: high高 + ly表副词  → highly高度地，非常

highway.definitionEn: a main road that connects cities, towns, etc.
highway.sentence: We are enjoying the beautiful scenery as we drive along the highway.
highway.sentenceTrans: 我们沿着高速公路开车，享受着美丽的风景。
highway.mnemonic: high[引]主要的 + way路 → highway公路，大路

hill.definitionEn: an area of land that is higher than the land around it, but not as high as a mountain
hill.sentence: There is a red house on the top of that green hill.
hill.sentenceTrans: 在那绿色小山的山顶上有一所红房子。

him.definitionEn: used as the object of a verb, after the verb be or after a preposition to refer to a male person or animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified
him.sentence: The teacher is pointing at him.

himself.definitionEn: (the reflexive form of he) used when the man or boy who performs an action is also affected by it
himself.sentence: He can do many things all by himself.
himself.sentenceTrans: 他能自己搞定所有事情。
himself.mnemonic: him他 + self自己，反身后缀 → himself他自己

hinder.definitionEn: to make it difficult for somebody to do something or for something to happen
hinder.sentence: The heavy traffic might hinder our arrival at the meeting on time.
hinder.sentenceTrans: 交通堵塞可能会让我们无法准时到达会议。

hint.definitionEn: something that you say or do in an indirect way in order to show somebody what you are thinking
hint.sentence: She made a gesture to hint that there was no problem.
hint.sentenceTrans: 她用手势示意一切都没问题。

hire.sentence: When will the company decide who to hire?
hire.sentenceTrans: 公司什么时候决定要雇用谁？

his.definitionEn: of or belonging to a man or boy who has already been mentioned or is easily identified
his.sentence: He looks really cool next to his sports car.
his.sentenceTrans: 他站在自己的跑车旁边，看起来酷毙了！

historic.definition: 有历史意义的，历史上著名的
historic.sentence: He is reading this book which recounts the historic victory of his country years ago.
historic.sentenceTrans: 他正在看的这本书记录了多年前他的国家取得的历史性胜利。
historic.mnemonic: histor=history历史 + ic形容词，...的 → 有历史意义的

historical.definitionEn: connected with the past; connected with the study of history; (of a book, film/movie, etc.) about people and events in the past
historical.sentence: This book is all about historical buildings in China.
historical.sentenceTrans: 这是一本关于中国历史建筑的书。
historical.mnemonic: histor历史 + ical形容词后缀……的 → historical有关历史的

history.definitionEn: all the events that happened in the past; the past events concerned in the development of a particular place, subject, etc.; the study of past events as a subject at school or university
history.sentence: This poster shows the history of different methods of transportation.
history.sentenceTrans: 这张海报展示了各种交通方式的发展历史。
history.mnemonic: histor过去发生的事 + y表名词 → history历史；个人经历

hit.definition: 打击；碰撞，撞击；袭击；到达（某地）；  n.击打；碰撞
hit.definitionEn: an act of hitting somebody/something with your hand or with an object held in your hand
hit.sentence: He hit him in the face.

hobby.definitionEn: an activity that a person does for pleasure when not working
hobby.sentence: Fishing is my hobby, so I often go to the lake on weekends.
hobby.sentenceTrans: 我的爱好是钓鱼，所以我周末常去湖边。

hold.definition: 举办，举行，召开；持有（观点）；抓住；容纳，包含；  n.控制
hold.definitionEn: to put your arms around (someone) :to embrace or hug (someone)
hold.sentence: Our school is holding a sports meeting.
hold.sentenceTrans: 我们学校正在举办运动会。

hole.definitionEn: a hollow space in something solid or in the surface of something
hole.sentence: A hole in the heart can lead to abnormal blood flow between chambers.
hole.sentenceTrans: 心脏上的孔可能导致心脏腔室间的血流异常。

holiday.definition: 节日，假期，休假日；法定假日，公共节日
holiday.definitionEn: a period of time when you are not at work or school
holiday.sentence: People are enjoying their holiday from work.
holiday.sentenceTrans: 人们享受着他们的假日。
holiday.mnemonic: hol神圣 + i + day日子 → holiday节假日

hollow.definition: 空洞的；中间空的，空心的；  n.洞；孔
hollow.definitionEn: having a hole or empty space inside
hollow.sentenceTrans: 过度工作让他感到空虚。
hollow.mnemonic: hol=kel掩盖，隐藏，保存 + low → 可隐藏的地方 → hollow空心的，洞

home.definition: 家，家庭；  adv.在家，到家；  adj.家的；  v.回家
home.definitionEn: the house or flat/apartment that you live in, especially with your family; a house or flat/apartment, etc., when you think of it as property that can be bought and sold; a place where people who cannot care for themselves live and are cared for by others
home.sentence: The family was happy at home.
home.sentenceTrans: 这家人待在家里很开心。

homeland.definitionEn: the country where someone was born or grew up
homeland.sentence: After settling abroad for many years, he missed his homeland terribly.
homeland.sentenceTrans: 在国外定居多年后，他无比思念自己的故乡。
homeland.mnemonic: home家 + land土地 → homeland 祖国

homeless.sentence: The homeless dog wishes he had a family.
homeless.sentenceTrans: 这只流浪狗希望有个家。
homeless.mnemonic: home家 ＋ less表形容词，无…的 → homeless无家可归的

homework.definitionEn: work that is given by teachers for students to do at home
homework.sentence: The tutor helped the children with their homework.
homework.sentenceTrans: 这个家教辅导孩子们完成了作业。
homework.mnemonic: home家庭 + work工作 → homework家庭作业

honest.definition: 诚实的，正直的；正直的；坦率的
honest.definitionEn: always telling the truth, and never stealing or cheating
honest.sentence: Before giving testimony, the witness has to pledge herself to being honest.
honest.sentenceTrans: 作证之前，证人必须发誓所言皆实。
honest.mnemonic: hon=honor荣誉，尊严 + est → honest诚实的

honey.definition: 蜜，蜂蜜；亲爱的，宝贝（爱称）
honey.definitionEn: a sweet sticky yellow substance made by bees that is spread on bread, etc. like jam
honey.sentence: Add more honey if you have a sweet tooth.
honey.sentenceTrans: 如果你喜欢吃甜的，就多加点蜂蜜。

honor.definitionEn: something that you are very pleased or proud to do because people are showing you great respect
honor.sentence: Receiving the gold medal is my honor.

honorable.definitionEn: showing high moral standards; allowing somebody to keep their good name and the respect of others
honorable.sentence: At this honorable moment, he got his master's degree.
honorable.sentenceTrans: 在这个荣耀时刻，他获得了他的硕士学位。
honorable.mnemonic: honor荣誉 + able…的 → honorable光荣的，高尚的

honour.definition: 荣誉；荣幸；尊敬；  v.尊敬
honour.definitionEn: an award, official title, etc. given to somebody as a reward for something that they have done
honour.sentence: Holding a post graduate degree is a matter of honour and pride.
honour.sentenceTrans: 拿到硕士学位是一件光荣并值得自豪的事情。

honourable.definition: 可敬的，值得钦佩的；荣誉的，光荣的
honourable.sentence: The guy who rides on the horse is an honourable knight.
honourable.sentenceTrans: 骑马的人是一名值得钦佩的骑士。
honourable.mnemonic: honour光荣 + able...的 → 光荣的，诚实的

hope.definition: 希望；期望；  v.希望，期望（某事发生）
hope.definitionEn: to want something to happen and think that it is possible
hope.sentence: My hope is to go to a world-famous university one day.
hope.sentenceTrans: 我希望有一天能上一所世界著名的大学。

hopeful.definitionEn: (of a person) believing that something you want will happen
hopeful.sentence: It is still hopeful for the man in yellow to win.
hopeful.sentenceTrans: 穿黄色衣服的人仍然有希望获胜。
hopeful.mnemonic: hope希望 + ful形容词后缀 → hopeful有希望的

hopeless.definitionEn: if something is hopeless, there is no hope that it will get better or succeed; extremely bad; (of people) very bad (at something); with no ability or skill; feeling or showing no hope
hopeless.sentence: I feel hopeless. This job is not easy.
hopeless.sentenceTrans: 我绝望了，这个工作真不简单。
hopeless.mnemonic: hope希望 + less表形容词，无……的 → hopeless无希望的

horizon.definitionEn: the furthest that you can see, where the sky seems to meet the land or the sea
horizon.sentence: The sun is slowly rising from the horizon.
horizon.sentenceTrans: 太阳从地平线上缓缓升起。

horrible.definitionEn: making you feel very shocked and frightened
horrible.sentence: I did not expect to see such a horrible scene on the phone.
horrible.sentenceTrans: 我没料到会在手机上看到这么恐怖的场景。
horrible.mnemonic: horr发抖，恐惧 + ible......的 → 令人发抖的 → horrible可怕的

horror.definitionEn: a feeling of great shock, fear or disgust
horror.sentence: He screamed in horror when he saw the monster.
horror.sentenceTrans: 看到怪物时，他惊恐地尖叫了起来。
horror.mnemonic: horr（因惊吓或发怒）毛发竖起 + or引申词义厌恶 -> horror惊恐

horse.definitionEn: a large animal that is used for riding and for carrying and pulling things
horse.sentence: The black horse is running on the beach.
horse.sentenceTrans: 这匹黑马正在沙滩上奔跑。

horsepower.definitionEn: a unit used to measure the power of engines
horsepower.sentence: The maximum output of this engine is two hundred horsepower.
horsepower.sentenceTrans: 这台发动机的最大输出功率是200马力。

hospitable.definitionEn: (of a person) pleased to welcome guests; generous and friendly to visitors
hospitable.sentence: He was very hospitable to the guests when they came to his house.
hospitable.sentenceTrans: 有人来访时，他表现得十分好客。
hospitable.mnemonic: hospit客人 ＋ able形容词后缀，…的 → 待客，好客 → hospitable好客的，招待周到的，殷勤的

hospital.definitionEn: a large building where people who are ill/sick or injured are given medical treatment and care
hospital.sentence: The patient was taken to the hospital for treatment.
hospital.sentenceTrans: 病人被带进医院进行治疗。
hospital.mnemonic: hospit客人 + al名词词尾 → 客气对待病人的地方 → hospital医院

host.definition: 宿主，主人；节目主持人；  v.主持，主办
host.definitionEn: a person who invites guests to a meal, a party, etc. or who has people staying at their house
host.sentence: Viruses need a living host to reproduce and cause infection.
host.sentenceTrans: 病毒需要活的宿主来繁殖并引起感染。

hostile.definition: 怀有敌意的；敌对的，敌方的
hostile.definitionEn: very unfriendly or aggressive and ready to argue or fight
hostile.sentence: They're hostile towards each other in the fight for MVP.
hostile.sentenceTrans: 流川枫和樱木为了争夺MVP而对彼此充满了敌意。
hostile.mnemonic: host(=hostis)敌人 + ile……的 → 有敌意的 → hostile敌意的

hostility.definitionEn: unfriendly or aggressive feelings or behaviour
hostility.sentence: The dog shows his hostility to strangers.
hostility.sentenceTrans: 狗狗对陌生人满是敌意。
hostility.mnemonic: host敌人 + ility表名词 → hostility敌对

hot.definitionEn: [(hot up) (informal) to become more exciting or to show an increase in activity
hot.sentence: I enjoy a cup of hot coffee with my breakfast.
hot.sentenceTrans: 早餐我享用了一杯热咖啡。

hotel.definitionEn: a building where people stay, usually for a short time, paying for their rooms and meals
hotel.mnemonic: hot=host客人 ＋ el表名词 → hotel客人住的地方

hour.definitionEn: one of the 24 equal parts of a day; 60 minutes
hour.sentence: I get a break at one o'clock—only an hour to go!
hour.sentenceTrans: 一点的时候我可以休息一下，只有一个小时！

house.definitionEn: a building in which a family lives
house.sentence: I have a small house model in the palm of my hand.
house.sentenceTrans: 我手上放了一个小的房子模型。

household.definition: 家庭；  adj.家庭的；家喻户晓的
household.definitionEn: all the people living together in a house or flat/apartment
household.sentence: I grew up in a large household.
household.sentenceTrans: 我生长在一个大家庭中。
household.mnemonic: house家 + hold持有，拥有 → household家庭

housewife.definitionEn: a woman who stays at home to cook, clean, take care of the children, etc. while her husband or partner goes out to work
housewife.sentence: The housewife is ironing the clothes with her child.
housewife.sentenceTrans: 这个家庭主妇正在和她的孩子一起熨衣服。
housewife.mnemonic: house屋子 + wife妻子 → 家庭主妇 → housewife家庭主妇

how.definition: 如何；怎样；到何种地步；多么
how.sentence: How do you bake a cake？

however.definition: 然而，不过，但是；无论如何，不管多么
however.definitionEn: used with an adjective or adverb to mean ‘to whatever degree’
however.sentence: He got a great test score; however, he's still upset.
however.sentenceTrans: 他考了个好成绩，然而他还是不开心。
however.mnemonic: how怎样 + ever永远，表强调 → however然而；不管怎样

huge.definitionEn: very large :very great in size, amount, or degree
huge.sentence: There is a huge yellow duck floating on the lake.
huge.sentenceTrans: 有一只大黄鸭漂在湖上。

human.definitionEn: a person rather than an animal or a machine
human.sentence: Water is important for the human body.
human.mnemonic: hum 土，地 + an名词后缀：属于...的 → 传说人是由土造出的 → human 人类

humanity.definitionEn: the quality of being kind to people and animals by making sure that they do not suffer more than is necessary; the quality of being humane
humanity.sentence: What binds mankind together is our common humanity.
humanity.sentenceTrans: 将人类联系在一起的是我们共同的人性。
humanity.mnemonic: human人类 + ity名词后缀 → humanity人性，人类

humble.definitionEn: used to suggest that you are not as important as other people, but in a way that is not sincere or not very serious
humble.sentence: She praised him with many compliments, but he was humble and denied them.
humble.sentenceTrans: 她说了很多恭维话赞扬莱纳德，但莱纳德很谦虚地拒绝了。
humble.mnemonic: hum土地 + ble形容词后缀 → 接近地面 → humble谦恭的

humor.definition: 幽默；幽默，诙谐；  v.迎合，迁就，顺应
humor.definitionEn: the quality in something that makes it funny or amusing; the ability to laugh at things that are amusing
humor.sentence: This funny kids' cartoon is full of humor.
humor.sentenceTrans: 这部有趣的儿童卡通片十分幽默。

humorous.definitionEn: funny and entertaining; showing a sense of humour
humorous.sentence: This guy was so humorous and made everyone laugh.
humorous.sentenceTrans: 这个人很幽默，把大家都逗笑了。
humorous.mnemonic: humor幽默 + ous…...的 → humorous富于幽默的，诙谐的

humour.definition: 幽默；诙谐；  v.迁就；迎合
humour.definitionEn: the quality in something that makes it funny or amusing; the ability to laugh at things that are amusing
humour.sentence: This funny kids' cartoon is full of humour.
humour.sentenceTrans: 这部有趣的儿童卡通片十分幽默。

hundred.sentence: Whose face is on the hundred-dollar bill?
hundred.sentenceTrans: 一百元美钞上是谁的头像？

hunger.definitionEn: the state of not having enough food to eat, especially when this causes illness or death
hunger.sentence: He wants a hamburger to satisfy his hunger.
hunger.sentenceTrans: 他想吃个汉堡来缓解饥饿。

hungry.definitionEn: feeling that you want to eat something
hungry.sentence: I'm not really hungry, just a small piece of pizza would be fine for me.
hungry.sentenceTrans: 我不是很饿，给我一小块比萨就好。
hungry.mnemonic: hunger饥饿 + y形容词后缀 → hungry饥饿的

hunt.definitionEn: to chase wild animals or birds in order to catch or kill them for food, sport or to make money
hunt.sentence: The man is hunting a reindeer.
hunt.sentenceTrans: 这名男子正在狩猎驯鹿。

hunter.definitionEn: a person who hunts wild animals
hunter.sentence: The man with a hound is an experienced hunter.
hunter.sentenceTrans: 这个带着猎犬的男人是个经验丰富的猎人。
hunter.mnemonic: hunt打猎 ＋ er名词后缀 → hunter猎人

hurry.definitionEn: to do something more quickly than usual because there is not much time
hurry.sentence: It seems that everyone in this city is always in a hurry.
hurry.sentenceTrans: 在这座城市似乎每个人都总是行色匆匆。

hurt.definition: 使受伤；弄伤，弄痛；感到疼痛；  adj.受伤的，受损的
hurt.definitionEn: to feel pain or to be in pain
hurt.sentence: The girl hurt her leg while running.
hurt.sentenceTrans: 这个女生跑步的时候伤到了腿。

husband.definitionEn: the man that somebody is married to; a married man
husband.sentence: Doesn't my husband look great in his new suit?
husband.sentenceTrans: 我的丈夫穿上了他的新西装，看起来不帅么？
husband.mnemonic: hus=house房屋 + band居住，住户 → husband丈夫

hydrogen.definitionEn: a chemical element. Hydrogen is a gas that is the lightest of all the elements. It combines with oxygen to form water.
hydrogen.sentence: Hydrogen is commonly used as a medical gas in respiratory therapy.
hydrogen.sentenceTrans: 氢气常被作为医疗气体用于呼吸治疗。

ice.definitionEn: water that has frozen and become solid
ice.sentence: She is holding some ice in her hands.

ice-cream.definitionEn: a type of sweet frozen food made from milk fat, flavored with fruit, chocolate, etc. and often eaten as a dessert
ice-cream.sentence: I've ordered two bowls of ice-cream.

idea.definitionEn: a plan, thought or suggestion, especially about what to do in a particular situation
idea.sentence: He came up with a good idea to solve that problem.
idea.sentenceTrans: 他想到了一个好主意来解决那个问题。

ideal.definition: 理想的；完美的；空想的；观念的；  n.理想；典范；目标
ideal.sentence: An ideal weekend is to lie on the sofa, watching TV and eating snacks.
ideal.sentenceTrans: 一个理想周末是躺在沙发上看电视、吃零食。
ideal.mnemonic: ide思想，观点 + al名词后缀 → 对未来的想法 → ideal理想的

idealistic.definitionEn: of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of the reality of ideas
idealistic.sentence: She has an idealistic vision of a world where everyone works together in harmony.
idealistic.sentenceTrans: 她对一个人人和谐合作的世界抱有理想主义的愿景。

identical.definitionEn: similar in every detail; the same
identical.sentence: These two chemical reactions generate identical products.
identical.sentenceTrans: 这两个化学反应生成的产物是相同的。
identical.mnemonic: ident相同 + ical…的 → identical一样的

identification.definition: 识别；鉴定，验明；身份证明
identification.definitionEn: official papers or a document that can prove who you are
identification.sentence: To unlock this phone, it requires your fingerprint for identification.
identification.sentenceTrans: 需要识别你的指纹才能打开这个手机。
identification.mnemonic: identif=identify鉴定 + ication表名词 → identification鉴定

identify.definitionEn: to recognize somebody or something and be able to say who or what they are
identify.sentence: Your fingerprints are so unique that they can help the police identify you.
identify.sentenceTrans: 你的指纹是独一无二的，所以它们可以帮助警察识别出你的身份。

identity.definitionEn: the characteristics, feelings or beliefs that distinguish people from others
identity.sentence: He took out his identity card to show who he was.
identity.sentenceTrans: 他掏出身份证来表明自己是谁。
identity.mnemonic: ident相同 + ity表名词 → identity一致；身份

idle.sentence: I don't want to idle around. I need a case.
idle.sentenceTrans: 我不想懒懒散散。我需要个案子。

if.definitionEn: used to say that one thing can, will or might happen or be true, depending on another thing happening or being true
if.sentence: If it is a sunny day, I will go out.If not, I will stay at home.
if.sentenceTrans: 如果这是一个晴天，我就出去玩。如果不是，我就呆在家。

ignorance.definitionEn: a lack of knowledge or information about something
ignorance.sentence: I am embarrassed by my complete ignorance of history.
ignorance.sentenceTrans: 我对历史一无所知，这让我很难堪。
ignorance.mnemonic: i不 ＋ gnor知道 ＋ ance名词后缀 → ignorance无知，愚昧

ignorant.definitionEn: lacking knowledge or information about something; not educated; with very bad manners
ignorant.sentence: He remains ignorant of these reports and tables.
ignorant.sentenceTrans: 他对这些报表一无所知。
ignorant.mnemonic: i不 + gnor知道 + ant形容词后缀 → ignorant无知的

ignore.definitionEn: to pay no attention to something
ignore.sentence: The boy's parents ignored him as they were doing their own things.
ignore.sentenceTrans: 男孩的父母忽略了他，只顾着自己的事。

ill.definition: 生病的，不适的；坏的，不好的
ill.definitionEn: not well or healthy; sick or unhealthy
ill.sentence: The girl is ill; she is resting on the sofa.
ill.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩生病了，她正在沙发上休息。

illegal.sentence: Occupying a bus lane is illegal.
illegal.sentenceTrans: 占用公交车道是违法的。
illegal.mnemonic: il不，无 + legal合法的 → illegal非法的

illness.definitionEn: the state of being physically or mentally ill
illness.sentence: He has an illness, but he still has to work.
illness.sentenceTrans: 他生病了，但仍然要工作。
illness.mnemonic: ill有病的 + ness名词后缀 → illness疾病

illustrate.definitionEn: to make the meaning of something clearer by using examples, pictures, etc.
illustrate.sentence: Our manager illustrated the sales with colorful charts.
illustrate.sentenceTrans: 我们的经理用一些彩色的图表解释了我们的销售量。
illustrate.mnemonic: il=in在内，进入 + lustr照亮 + ate表动词  → 照亮内部（大脑） → illustrate举例说明，阐明

illustration.definitionEn: a picture or drawing in a book, magazine, etc.
illustration.sentence: The book's illustrations of fruits help me to recognize them.
illustration.sentenceTrans: 这本书里的水果插图帮我认出那些水果。
illustration.mnemonic: il 使 + lustr =light光亮 + ation表名词 → 使...光亮 → 说明

image.sentence: He is describing the image of the thief to the police.
image.sentenceTrans: 他正在向警方描述小偷的形象。
image.mnemonic: imag=imagine想象 ＋ e → 头脑里想象的 → image像；形象

imaginary.definitionEn: existing only in your mind or imagination
imaginary.sentence: In my imaginary world, I am a princess who lives in a big castle.
imaginary.sentenceTrans: 在我的幻想世界里，我是一个住在大城堡里的公主。
imaginary.mnemonic: imagin想象 + ary形容词后缀 → imaginary想象中的

imagination.definitionEn: the ability to create pictures in your mind; the part of your mind that does this; the ability to have new and exciting ideas
imagination.sentence: Writers need a great imagination to create wonderful stories.
imagination.sentenceTrans: 作家需要很好的想象力才能创造出美妙的故事。
imagination.mnemonic: imagin想象 + ation名词后缀 → imagination想象

imagine.definition: 想象，幻想；设想，猜想；认为
imagine.definitionEn: to form a picture in your mind of what something might be like
imagine.sentence: The girl imagines a universe in the book.
imagine.sentenceTrans: 小女孩想象书中有宇宙。
imagine.mnemonic: imag=image图像 + ine……的 → 有关图像的 → imagine想象

imaging.definitionEn: the ability to form mental images of things or events
imaging.sentence: Imaging technology is vital in modern medical practice.
imaging.sentenceTrans: 成像技术在现代医学实践中非常重要。

imitate.definitionEn: to copy the way a person speaks or behaves, in order to amuse people; to copy somebody/something
imitate.sentence: The boy is imitating the signature move of his favorite character.
imitate.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩在模仿他最喜欢的角色标志动作。
imitate.mnemonic: imit想象，相象 + ate做 → 做得相象 → imitate模仿

imitation.sentence: The girl applies the lipstick in imitation of her mother.
imitation.sentenceTrans: 这个小女孩模仿她妈妈抹口红。
imitation.mnemonic: imit表示“想象，相像” + ation 名词后缀 → 想象后制造出的 → 仿制品

immediate.definition: 立刻的；紧邻的；紧迫的，当下的
immediate.sentence: You should take immediate action when facing problems.
immediate.sentenceTrans: 面对问题时，你应该立即采取行动。
immediate.mnemonic: im不 + mediate间接的 → immediate直接的

immediately.mnemonic: immediate立即的 + ly…地 → immediately立即，马上

immense.definitionEn: extremely large in size or amount
immense.sentence: Compared with the immense universe, our planet is so small.
immense.sentenceTrans: 与浩瀚无垠的宇宙相比，我们的星球是如此渺小。
immense.mnemonic: im不 + mense测量 → 无法测量的 → immense巨大的

immigrant.definitionEn: a person who has come to live permanently in a country that is not their own
immigrant.sentenceTrans: 移民带来了文化多样性。
immigrant.mnemonic: im向内，进入 + migr迁移 + ant表示人；形容词 → immigrant外来的移民；移入国内的

immigrate.definitionEn: to come and live permanently in a country after leaving your own country
immigrate.sentence: He is filling in the visa application form and plans to immigrate.
immigrate.sentenceTrans: 他正在填写签证申请表，准备移民。
immigrate.mnemonic: im向内 + migrate移居 → immigrate移居国内

immune.definitionEn: that cannot catch or be affected by a particular disease or illness
immune.sentence: People who exercise often are proven to have stronger immune systems.
immune.sentenceTrans: 经常锻炼的人被证实会有更强的免疫系统。
immune.mnemonic: im不 + mun服务 + e  → 免除服务  → immune免疫的

impact.definition: 影响；冲击力；碰撞，冲击（读作/ˈɪmˌpækt/）；  v.有影响（读作/ɪmˈpækt/）
impact.definitionEn: the act of one object hitting another; the force with which this happens
impact.sentence: The continuous heavy rain had a big impact on transport.
impact.sentenceTrans: 持续的暴雨对交通造成了严重的影响。
impact.mnemonic: im进入 + pact紧的 → 紧紧进入人心的力量 → impact影响力

impartial.definitionEn: not supporting one person or group more than another
impartial.sentence: A judge should guarantee that the trial is impartial.
impartial.sentenceTrans: 法官应该保证审判是公平的。
impartial.mnemonic: im不，无，非 + partial不公平的 → impartial公平的

impatience.sentence: Her impatience is growing as she's already waited for an hour.
impatience.sentenceTrans: 她已经等了一个小时，所以变得越来越不耐烦了。

impatient.definitionEn: annoyed or irritated by somebody/something, especially because you have to wait for a long time
impatient.sentence: He had been waiting for twenty minutes and he was getting impatient.
impatient.sentenceTrans: 他已经等了二十分钟，有点不耐烦了。
impatient.mnemonic: im不 + patient有耐心的 → impatient不耐烦的

implement.definition: 实施，执行；  n.工具，器具
implement.definitionEn: a tool or an instrument, often one that is quite simple and that is used outdoors
implement.sentence: The hospital decided to implement a new infection control protocol.
implement.sentenceTrans: 医院决定实施一项新的感染控制方案。
implement.mnemonic: im进 + ple满，填满 + ment指动作本身 → 装入并填满 → implement完成，实施

implication.definitionEn: something that is suggested without being said directly; something that is implied
implication.sentence: She expressed her desire for the cookie by implication.
implication.sentenceTrans: 她含蓄地表达了想吃饼干的想法。
implication.mnemonic: im进 + plic重叠，折叠 + ation名词后缀 → [说话]进入重叠 → implication连累；含蓄

implicit.sentenceTrans: 这些表情符号具有隐含意义。
implicit.mnemonic: im向内，进入 + plicit重叠 → 不直说 → implicit含蓄的，不讲明的

imply.definitionEn: to express (something) in an indirect way :to suggest (something) without saying or showing it plainly
imply.sentence: The light implies that there is somebody in the house.
imply.mnemonic: im进入 + ply重叠，折叠 → 重叠表达 → imply 暗示，意味

import.definition: 进口；  n.进口；含义，意义；重要性（读作/ˈɪmˌpɔrt/）
import.definitionEn: to bring a product, a service, an idea, etc. into one country from another
import.sentence: The goods on this ship were imported from overseas.
import.sentenceTrans: 这艘船上的货物是从海外进口的。
import.mnemonic: im向内，进入 + port拿，运 → 拿进港口 → import进口

importance.sentence: Wi-Fi is of great importance to people as it becomes a basic need.
importance.sentenceTrans: Wi-Fi对人们很重要，它已经成了一项基本需求。
importance.mnemonic: im进 + port拿，运 + ance名词后缀 → 带有意义的状态 → importance重要性

important.definitionEn: having a great effect on people or things; of great value
important.mnemonic: import重要的 + ant具有…性质的 → important重要的；有势力的

impose.definition: 把……强加给；强制实行，强迫接受
impose.definitionEn: to force somebody/something to have to deal with something that is difficult or unpleasant
impose.sentence: The government imposed a ban on single-use plastics to protect the environment.
impose.sentenceTrans: 政府为保护环境强加了对一次性塑料的禁令。

impossible.definitionEn: that cannot exist or be done; not possible
impossible.sentence: It's almost impossible for her to push that massive rock.
impossible.sentenceTrans: 她要推动那块巨大的石头几乎不可能。
impossible.mnemonic: im不，无，非 + possible可能的 → impossible不可能的

impress.definition: 给……留下深刻印象；使牢记，使铭记
impress.definitionEn: if a person or thing impresses you, you feel admiration for them or it; to make somebody understand how important, serious, etc. something is by emphasizing it; to have a great effect on something, especially somebody’s mind, imagination, etc.
impress.sentence: She impressed the foreigners with her costume.
impress.sentenceTrans: 身着古装的她给外国人留下了深刻印象。
impress.mnemonic: im入，向内 + press挤压 → 压进去 → 印入头脑 → impress 使有印象，使铭记

impression.definitionEn: an idea, a feeling or an opinion that you get about somebody/something, or that somebody/something gives you; the effect that an experience or a person has on somebody/something
impression.sentence: She left a good impression on the interviewer.
impression.sentenceTrans: 她给这位面试官留下了好印象。
impression.mnemonic: im在...内 + press压 + ion名词后缀 -> impression印象

impressive.definitionEn: (of things or people) making you feel admiration, because they are very large, good, skilful, etc.
impressive.sentence: The acrobatic performance left an impressive impact on the audience.
impressive.sentenceTrans: 杂技表演给观众留下了很深刻的印象。
impressive.mnemonic: impress印象 + ive形容词后缀 → 有印象的 → impressive印象深刻的

improve.definitionEn: to become better than before; to make something/somebody better than before
improve.sentence: We should keep improving ourselves all the time.
improve.sentenceTrans: 我们应该一直提升自己。
improve.mnemonic: im强化前缀 + prove利润，有利 → 增加有利之处 → improve提高，改善

improvement.definitionEn: an addition or change that makes something better or more valuable
improvement.sentence: I hope our sales show some improvement soon.
improvement.sentenceTrans: 我希望我们的销售很快会有所改善。
improvement.mnemonic: improve改善 + ment名词后缀 → improvement 改善

impulse.definitionEn: a sudden strong wish or need to do something, without stopping to think about the results; a force or movement of energy that causes something else to react; something that causes somebody/something to do something or to develop and make progress
impulse.sentence: These things were an impulse purchase on November 11th by him.
impulse.sentenceTrans: 这些东西是他在“双十一”那天一时冲动买下来的。
impulse.mnemonic: im向内，进入 + pulse跳动 → 冲动

in.definitionEn: at a point within an area or a space
in.sentence: I usually read books in the evening.

inadequate.definition: 不足够的，不充分的，不适当的；不够好的
inadequate.definitionEn: not enough; not good enough; (of people) not able, or not confident enough, to deal with a situation
inadequate.sentence: The small amount of food is inadequate for two people.
inadequate.sentenceTrans: 食物太少了，不够两个人吃。
inadequate.mnemonic: in不 + ad加强意义 + equ平均 + ate……的 → 不充足的，不适当的

incentive.definitionEn: something that encourages you to do something; a payment or concession (= a reduction in the amount of money that has to be paid) that encourages somebody to do something
incentive.sentence: It is becoming increasingly common for companies to use their shares, or the right to acquire them, as a form of incentive.
incentive.sentenceTrans: 公司将股份或获得股份的权利作为一种激励形式的做法越来越普遍。
incentive.mnemonic: in向内，进入 + cent唱歌 + ive名词后缀 → 把精神唱进去 → incentive激励

inch.definitionEn: a unit for measuring length, equal to 2.54 centimetres
inch.sentence: An inch is about two and a half centimeters.

incident.definitionEn: something that happens, especially something unusual or unpleasant
incident.sentence: The headmaster is talking to the two boys about the classroom incident.
incident.sentenceTrans: 校长正在和这两个男孩谈论教室事件。
incident.mnemonic: in进入 + cid降临 + ent表名词 → incident偶然事件

incline.definition: 倾斜，斜坡，斜面（读作/ˈɪnˌklaɪn/）；  v.使倾斜，使倾向于（读作/ɪnˈklaɪn/）
incline.sentence: The small ball is on an incline and could hit the big ball.
incline.sentenceTrans: 小球在斜面的一端，可能会撞向大球。
incline.mnemonic: in使 + clin倾斜 + e → incline 倾斜，斜坡

inclined.sentence: They installed a new inclined access ramp for wheelchairs.
inclined.sentenceTrans: 他们为了方便轮椅通行安装了一个新的斜坡道。
inclined.mnemonic: inclin=incline趋势+ed形容词后缀 → 趋向于…的

include.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) if one thing includes another, it has the second thing as one of its parts; to make somebody/something part of something
include.sentence: Elephants, frogs and birds can be included in the category of "animals".
include.sentenceTrans: 大象、青蛙和鸟可以列入“动物”这个类别里。
include.mnemonic: in进入 + clude关闭 → 关进去 → include包括

inclusion.sentence: The inclusion of a first-aid kit in the trip supplies was essential.
inclusion.sentenceTrans: 将急救箱纳入出行用品中是很有必要的。

inclusive.definition: 包含全部费用的；包容的
inclusive.definitionEn: having the total cost, or the cost of something that is mentioned, contained in the price; including all the days, months, numbers, etc. mentioned; including a wide range of people, things, ideas, etc.
inclusive.sentence: This tour is inclusive of all tickets.
inclusive.sentenceTrans: 这次旅游包含所有门票。
inclusive.mnemonic: in进入 + clus关闭 + ive形容词后缀 → 包括在内的

income.definitionEn: the money that a person, a region, a country, etc. earns from work, from investing money, from business, etc.
income.sentence: The workers' income isn't as much as they expected.
income.sentenceTrans: 工人们的工资没有他们预期的高。
income.mnemonic: in 向内，进入 + come来 → 收入；收益；进款

inconsistent.sentence: His views about her were always changing, so inconsistent!
inconsistent.sentenceTrans: 他对她的感情总是在变化，太前后矛盾了！

incorporate.definitionEn: to include something so that it forms a part of something
incorporate.sentence: The app update incorporates many new features and improvements.
incorporate.sentenceTrans: 这款应用程序的更新加入了许多新功能和改进。
incorporate.mnemonic: in向内，进入 + corpor团体 + ate动词后缀 → 成为团体 → incorporate合并，并入

increase.definition: 增加，增长，增多；  n.增强，提高（读作/ˈɪŋkriːs/）；增加
increase.definitionEn: to become or to make something greater in amount, number, value, etc.
increase.sentence: The population has increased dramatically in recent years.
increase.mnemonic: in向内 + crease生长 → increase增加

increasingly.definitionEn: more and more; to an increasing degree
increasingly.sentence: Snow increasingly accumulated on the ground.
increasingly.mnemonic: in加强 ＋ creas=grow增长 ＋ ing...的 ＋ ly...地 → increasingly日益，越来越多地

indeed.definitionEn: used to emphasize a positive statement or answer; used to add information to a statement
indeed.sentence: I indeed lost sleep last night.
indeed.mnemonic: in在...内 + deed行为 → indeed的确

indefinite.definition: 不清楚的，模糊的；无限的
indefinite.definitionEn: not clearly defined; lasting for a period of time that has no fixed end
indefinite.sentence: Which door should he go through? The answer is indefinite.
indefinite.sentenceTrans: 他应该通过哪扇门？答案是不确定的。
indefinite.mnemonic: in无 + defin=define确定 + ite形容词后缀 → 不确定的

independence.definitionEn: (of a country) freedom from political control by other countries
independence.sentence: It is from Britain that America gained its independence.
independence.sentenceTrans: 美国是从英国获得独立的。
independence.mnemonic: in不 + depend依靠 + ence名词后缀 → 不依靠 → independence独立，自主

independent.definition: 独立的，自立的；  n.无党派者
independent.definitionEn: confident and free to do things without needing help from other people
independent.sentence: He is learning to be independent in the face of a challenge.
independent.sentenceTrans: 他在学习独立面对挑战。
independent.mnemonic: in不 + depend依靠 + ent……的 → 不依靠的 → independent独立的

index.definitionEn: a system that shows the level of prices and wages, etc. so that they can be compared with those of a previous date
index.sentence: The stock index rises and falls all the time. Invest cautiously.
index.sentenceTrans: 股票指数总是起伏不定，投资请谨慎。
index.mnemonic: in进入 + dex显示，宣告 → index指数

indicate.definitionEn: to make somebody notice somebody/something, especially by pointing or moving your head
indicate.sentence: Can you guess what the line chart indicates?
indicate.sentenceTrans: 你能猜到这张折线图说明了什么吗？
indicate.mnemonic: in进入 + dic说话，断言 + ate使，造成 → 说进去 → indicate指示，指明

indication.definitionEn: a remark or sign that shows that something is happening or what somebody is thinking or feeling
indication.sentence: The green arrow is an indication showing that you're allowed to turn left.
indication.sentenceTrans: 绿箭头表明你可以往左拐。
indication.mnemonic: in向内，进入 + dic说话，断言 + ation名词后缀 → 指示，指出，表示

indifference.definitionEn: a lack of interest, feeling or reaction towards somebody/something
indifference.sentence: He rolled his eyes to show his indifference.
indifference.sentenceTrans: 他翻了翻白眼来显示他的冷淡。
indifference.mnemonic: indiffer=indifferent漠不关心的 + ence名词后缀 → 不关心

indifferent.definitionEn: not interested in or concerned about something
indifferent.sentence: The staff were indifferent about the new plan put forward by their boss.
indifferent.sentenceTrans: 员工们对老板提出的新计划漠不关心。
indifferent.mnemonic: in不，无，非 + different不同的 → 与众不同的 → indifferent冷漠的

indispensable.sentence: He has become an indispensable member of our project group.
indispensable.sentenceTrans: 他已成为我们项目组不可缺少的一员。
indispensable.mnemonic: in表否定 + dis向外 + pens=pense称重 + able能...的 → 不能够按重量向外分发的 → indispensable必不可少的

individual.definition: 个别的；个人的；  n.个人
individual.definitionEn: a person considered separately rather than as part of a group
individual.sentence: The teacher is the individual person not wearing a uniform in this graduation photo.
individual.sentenceTrans: 老师是这张毕业照里唯一没穿校服的人。
individual.mnemonic: in不，非 + divid分开，分割 + ual → 不可分割的 → individual个人，独立的个体

indoors.sentence: This golf course also allows you to play golf indoors.
indoors.sentenceTrans: 这种高尔夫球场让你在室内也能打高尔夫。
indoors.mnemonic: in进入 + door门 + s表副词 → indoors在屋内

induce.definitionEn: to persuade or use influence on
induce.sentence: The leader gave a speech to induce his staff to work harder.
induce.sentenceTrans: 领导发表讲话，引导员工更加努力地工作。
induce.mnemonic: in进入+duce引导，带来→引进去→劝诱，诱导

industrial.definitionEn: connected with industry; used by industries; having many industries
industrial.sentence: The industrial area gives out lots of smoke every day.
industrial.sentenceTrans: 这个工业区每天排放大量浓烟。
industrial.mnemonic: industrial=industry工业 + ial有...性质的 → a.工业的；产业的

industrialise.definitionEn: organize the production of into an industry
industrialise.sentence: They wanted to industrialise their nation.

industrialize.definitionEn: organize the production of into an industry
industrialize.sentence: The big city has been completely industrialized.
industrialize.sentenceTrans: 这个大城市已经实现了工业化。

industry.definitionEn: the production of goods from raw materials, especially in factories; the quality of working hard
industry.sentence: Heavy industry is important for our economy.
industry.sentenceTrans: 重工业对于我们的经济很重要。
industry.mnemonic: indu在..中 + stry构建，传播 → 在...中建设 → industry工业，勤劳

inevitable.definitionEn: that you cannot avoid or prevent
inevitable.sentence: It is inevitable for people to get old.
inevitable.mnemonic: in不 + evit避免 + able形容词后缀, 可...的 → 不可避免的，必然的

infant.definition: 幼儿，婴儿；  adj.婴儿的；初期的，初创的
infant.definitionEn: a baby or very young child
infant.sentence: The infant in the duck towel is laughing happily.
infant.sentenceTrans: 裹在鸭子毛巾里的小婴儿笑得真开心。
infant.mnemonic: in不 + fant说话 →不能说话的 → infant婴儿的

infect.definitionEn: to cause (someone or something) to become sick or affected by disease
infect.sentence: You are sick! Put the mask on, or you will infect others.
infect.sentenceTrans: 你生病了！ 把口罩戴上，不然你会传染给别人的。
infect.mnemonic: in进入 + fect做 → 做进去，传染进去 → infect传染，感染

infection.definitionEn: the act or process of causing or getting a disease
infection.sentence: This poor guy has a really terrible lung infection.
infection.sentenceTrans: 这个可怜的家伙受到了很严重的肺部感染。
infection.mnemonic: infect传染 + ion表名词 → infection传染

infectious.definition: 有传染性的，易传染的；具有感染力的
infectious.definitionEn: if a person or an animal is infectious, they have a disease that can be spread to others
infectious.sentence: The disease is highly infectious and spreads rapidly among children.
infectious.sentenceTrans: 这种疾病传染性很强，在儿童中传播很快。
infectious.mnemonic: in进入 + fect做 + infect做进去=传染 + ious……的 → infectious传染的

infer.definitionEn: to reach an opinion or decide that something is true on the basis of information that is available
infer.sentence: He infers from the thick black smoke that there is a fire.
infer.sentenceTrans: 他根据滚滚黑烟推断出这里发生了火灾。
infer.mnemonic: in进入+ fer带来，拿来 → 带进[意义] → 推理，推断

inference.definitionEn: the act or process of forming an opinion, based on what you already know; something that you can find out indirectly from what you already know
inference.sentence: By applying mathematical inferences, students can solve complex problems more effectively.
inference.sentenceTrans: 通过应用数学推理，学生们可以更有效地解决复杂问题。
inference.mnemonic: in在...内 + fer携带 + ence名词后缀 -> inference推断

inferior.sentence: He makes me feel I'm inferior to him.
inferior.sentenceTrans: 他让我感觉在他面前低人一等。
inferior.mnemonic: infer推断 + ior表形容词，较…的 → 轻易推断出的 → inferior低下的

infinite.sentence: We live in an infinite universe that might have no boundaries.
infinite.sentenceTrans: 我们生活在一个可能没有边界的无限宇宙中。
infinite.mnemonic: in无 + fin结束，范围 + ite有……的 → 没有范围的 → 无限的

inflation.definitionEn: a general rise in the prices of services and goods in a particular country, resulting in a fall in the value of money; the rate at which this happens
inflation.sentence: Because of the inflation, we could buy less fruit with the same money.
inflation.sentenceTrans: 因为通货膨胀，我们用同样的钱只能买到更少的水果。
inflation.mnemonic: in进 + flat吹 + ion表名词 → 充气；通货膨胀

influence.definition: 影响，作用；  v.影响，作用
influence.definitionEn: the effect that somebody/something has on the way a person thinks or behaves or on the way that something works or develops; the power that somebody/something has to make somebody/something behave in a particular way
influence.sentence: His mother was a main influence on his becoming a pianist.
influence.sentenceTrans: 他成为一名钢琴家主要是受了他母亲的影响。
influence.mnemonic: in进入 + flu流动 + ence名词后缀 → 流入 → influence影响

influential.definitionEn: having a lot of influence on somebody/something
influential.sentence: He is such an influential star that many people copy his look.
influential.sentenceTrans: 他是一位很有影响力的明星，许多人都在模仿他的穿着。
influential.mnemonic: in进入+flu流动+ent+ial…的→流入，影响现有状态→influential有影响的

inform.sentence: The penguin informed everyone of the rule.
inform.sentenceTrans: 企鹅向所有人宣布了这项规定。
inform.mnemonic: in进 + form形状 → 进入形式 → inform正式通知

information.sentence: The Internet is my main source of getting information about other countries.
information.sentenceTrans: 因特网是我获取其他国家信息的主要来源。
information.mnemonic: inform通知 + ation动作化名词后缀 → information 信息

infrastructure.definitionEn: the basic systems and services that are necessary for a country or an organization to run smoothly, for example buildings, transport and water and power supplies
infrastructure.sentence: A good infrastructure includes transport, communications, etc.
infrastructure.sentenceTrans: 完善的基础设施包括交通、通信等。
infrastructure.mnemonic: infra下，低 ＋ struct建立 ＋ ure名词后缀 → infrastructure下部结构，基础设施

ingredient.definition: 成分；【化】成分，配料；成分，构成要素
ingredient.definitionEn: one of the things from which something is made, especially one of the foods that are used together to make a particular dish
ingredient.sentence: The main ingredient in this medication is acetaminophen.
ingredient.sentenceTrans: 这种药的主要成分是对乙酰氨基酚。
ingredient.mnemonic: in进入 + gred走 + ient → 走进去的，成为其中一部分 → ingredient成份，因素

inhabit.definitionEn: to live in a particular place
inhabit.sentence: Primitive tribes used to inhabit these forests.
inhabit.sentenceTrans: 原始部落过去居住在森林里。

inhabitant.definitionEn: a person or an animal that lives in a particular place
inhabitant.sentence: This small town has many inhabitants.
inhabitant.mnemonic: in使 + habit居住 + ant表示人 → 住户，居民

inherent.definition: 生来就有的；内在的，固有的
inherent.definitionEn: that is a basic or permanent part of somebody/something and that cannot be removed
inherent.sentence: Many believe that curiosity is inherent in children.
inherent.sentenceTrans: 很多人认为好奇是儿童的天性。
inherent.mnemonic: in里面 + her粘附 + ent有...性质的 → 天生与身体内连着 → 天赋的，生来的

inherit.definition: 经遗传而得（特性等）；继承
inherit.definitionEn: to have qualities, physical features, etc. that are similar to those of your parents, grandparents, etc.
inherit.sentence: The baby inherited his father's curly hair.
inherit.sentenceTrans: 小宝宝遗传了父亲的卷发。
inherit.mnemonic: in在...内 + herit继承 → inherit经遗传而得

initial.definition: 字首的；最初的，开始的；  n.（单词）首字母；  v.用姓名的首字母签名于
initial.sentence: The initial letter of this word is "a."
initial.mnemonic: in进入 + it行走 + ial形容词后缀 → 走进 → initial开始的，最初的

initially.sentence: People initially lived in caves; now they live in houses.
initially.sentenceTrans: 人们最初住在山洞里，现在住在房子里。
initially.mnemonic: initial最初的 + ly……地 → initially最初，开头

initiate.sentence: The boy initiated the war by launching a missile.
initiate.sentenceTrans: 小男孩发射导弹发动了这场战争。
initiate.mnemonic: in进入 + ire＝iti去 + iate表动词 → initiate开始，发动

initiative.definitionEn: the power or opportunity to act and gain an advantage before other people do
initiative.sentence: Her boyfriend took the initiative and cleaned up after they all had dinner.
initiative.sentenceTrans: 她男朋友在他们吃完晚饭后主动打扫了卫生。
initiative.mnemonic: in进入 + it行走 + iat开始 + ive名词后缀 → initiative主动

inject.definitionEn: to put a drug or other substance into a person’s or an animal’s body using a syringe
inject.sentence: "Does this hurt?" the doctor asked as she injected her patient with antibiotics.
inject.sentenceTrans: “痛吗？”医生一边给患者注射抗生素一边问。
inject.mnemonic: in向内，进入 + ject投掷，扔 → 扔进去 → 注射

injection.definitionEn: the act or process of forcing a liquid medicine or drug into someone or something by using a special needle
injection.sentence: The woman in his arms was ready for her injection.
injection.sentenceTrans: 在美马怀里的灭已经做好了接受注射的准备。
injection.mnemonic: inject注射 + ion名词后缀 → injection 注射

injure.definitionEn: to harm yourself or somebody else physically, especially in an accident
injure.sentence: The worker injured himself at the construction site.
injure.sentenceTrans: 这名工人在工地上受伤了。

injury.definitionEn: harm done to a person’s or an animal’s body, for example in an accident
injury.sentence: The man got a knee injury when playing soccer.
injury.sentenceTrans: 踢足球时，这个男人的膝盖受伤了。
injury.mnemonic: in不，相反 + jur公正，法律 + y表名词 → 违背法律的不公正行为 → injury伤害

ink.definition: 墨水，油墨；  v.给……上油墨
ink.definitionEn: colored liquid that is used for writing or printing
ink.sentence: I used ink to write some nice Spring Festival wishes.
ink.sentenceTrans: 我用墨水写了些春节祝福。

inn.definitionEn: a pub, usually in the country and often one where people can stay the night
inn.sentence: This traditional inn is surrounded by trees.
inn.sentenceTrans: 这个传统的小旅店被绿树环绕。

inner.definitionEn: inside; towards or close to the centre of a place
inner.sentence: The inner core of the Earth is made up of iron and nickel.
inner.sentenceTrans: 地球内部的核心由铁和镍组成。

innocence.definition: 天真无邪，单纯；清白，无罪
innocence.definitionEn: lack of knowledge and experience of the world, especially of evil or unpleasant things
innocence.sentence: Nothing compares to the innocence of a child.
innocence.sentenceTrans: 什么也比不上孩子的天真无邪。
innocence.mnemonic: in无 ＋ noc伤害，毒 ＋ ence名词后缀 → innocence无害；天真

innocent.definition: 天真的，单纯的；无辜的，清白的；无罪的
innocent.definitionEn: lacking experience with the world and the bad things that happen in life
innocent.sentence: The child had an innocent smile that made everyone around her feel happy.
innocent.sentenceTrans: 这孩子有着天真无邪的笑容，让周围的每个人都感到快乐。
innocent.mnemonic: in无 + noc伤害，毒 + ent形容词后缀 → innocent无害的

innovation.definitionEn: the introduction of new things, ideas or ways of doing something; a new idea, way of doing something, etc. that has been introduced or discovered
innovation.sentence: The age of innovation has already come to us.
innovation.sentenceTrans: 创新时代正在向我们走来。（走进新时代~）
innovation.mnemonic: in进入 + nov新 + ation名词后缀 → innovation创新

innovative.definitionEn: introducing or using new ideas, ways of doing something, etc.
innovative.sentence: This girl always comes up with new and innovative ideas!
innovative.sentenceTrans: 这女孩儿总能想出一些具有创新意义的新点子！
innovative.mnemonic: in进入 + nov新的 + ative形容词后缀，…的 → 革新的，创新的

input.definitionEn: the act of putting information into a computer; the information that you put in
input.sentence: The mouse and the keyboard are input devices.
input.sentenceTrans: 鼠标和键盘是输入设备。

inquire.definitionEn: to ask somebody for some information
inquire.sentence: The policeman is inquiring about the escaped prisoner's whereabouts.
inquire.sentenceTrans: 警察正在询问逃犯的行踪。
inquire.mnemonic: in进入 + quire寻求，询问 → 追问到里面去 → inquire盘问，追究

inquiry.definitionEn: the act of asking questions or collecting information about somebody/something
inquiry.sentence: Let's conduct an inquiry into the origin of this question mark.
inquiry.sentenceTrans: 让我们来对问号的由来进行一项调查。
inquiry.mnemonic: inquir询问 + y名词后缀 → inquiry调查

insect.definitionEn: any small creature with six legs and a body divided into three parts. Insects usually also have wings. Ants, bees and flies are all insects.
insect.sentence: There are many kinds of insects, such as butterflies, bees and ants.
insect.sentenceTrans: 昆虫有很多种类，例如蝴蝶、蜜蜂和蚂蚁。
insect.mnemonic: in进入 + sect切，割 → 昆虫一节一节如被切开一样 → insect昆虫

insert.definitionEn: to put something into something else or between two things
insert.sentence: I am inserting my USB flash drive into the laptop.
insert.sentenceTrans: 我正在将我的U盘插入笔记本电脑中。
insert.mnemonic: in进入 + sert加入，插入 → 加入进来 → insert插入

inside.definition: 【数】内部；里面，内部；  adj.里面的；  adv.在（或向）里面，在内部
inside.definitionEn: on or to the inner part of something/somebody; within something/somebody
inside.sentence: Inside the circle is a flower.
inside.sentenceTrans: 这个圆的内部是一朵花。
inside.mnemonic: in向内，进入 + side边 → inside内部，里面

insight.definition: 深刻的理解，洞察力；见识
insight.definitionEn: the ability to see and understand the truth about people or situations; an understanding of what something is like
insight.sentence: He really has an insight into math.
insight.sentenceTrans: 他对数学真的有很深刻的见解。
insight.mnemonic: in进入 + sight眼光 → 眼光看进去 → 洞察力

insist.definitionEn: to demand that something happens or that somebody agrees to do something
insist.sentence: His mother insists that he should put on his warm pants.
insist.sentenceTrans: 男孩的妈妈坚持要他穿秋裤。
insist.mnemonic: in加强 + sist站立 → 一直站 → insist坚持；硬要

inspect.definitionEn: to look closely at something/somebody, especially to check that everything is as it should be
inspect.sentence: He is inspecting the shop for a hygiene check.
inspect.sentenceTrans: 他正在对这家店铺进行卫生检查。
inspect.mnemonic: in内 + spect看 → 看进去 → 视察

inspection.definitionEn: an official visit to a school, factory, etc. in order to check that rules are being obeyed and that standards are acceptable; the act of looking closely at something/somebody, especially to check that everything is as it should be
inspection.sentence: The mechanic gave the car a thorough inspection according to the check list.
inspection.sentenceTrans: 技工根据检查清单对汽车进行了一次全面检查。
inspection.mnemonic: inspect视察 + ion表名词 → 视察；认真看

inspire.definition: 激励，鼓舞；激发灵感；启示
inspire.definitionEn: to give somebody the desire, confidence or enthusiasm to do something well
inspire.sentence: My father inspired my confidence to become an astronaut from an early age.
inspire.sentenceTrans: 父亲从小就激发了我成为宇航员的信心。
inspire.mnemonic: in进 + spir呼吸 + e强调 → 吸气进去，引申为鼓励 → inspire鼓励

instal.definitionEn: to fix equipment or furniture into position so that it can be used; to put a new program onto a computer; to put somebody in a new position of authority, often with an official ceremony; to make somebody/yourself comfortable in a particular place or position
instal.sentence: My dad helped me to instal the new cabinets in the kitchen.
instal.sentenceTrans: 我爸帮我在厨房安装了一个新橱柜。

install.definitionEn: to fix equipment or furniture into position so that it can be used; to put a new program onto a computer; to put somebody in a new position of authority, often with an official ceremony; to make somebody/yourself comfortable in a particular place or position
install.sentence: The man installed a ceiling fan.
install.sentenceTrans: 这个男人把吊扇装上了。
install.mnemonic: in进 + stall放 → 放进去 → install安装

installation.definitionEn: the act of fixing equipment or furniture in position so that it can be used;  a piece of equipment or machinery that has been fixed in position so that it can be used
installation.sentence: The installation of the air conditioning was a little difficult.
installation.mnemonic: install安装 + ation名词后缀 → installation安装

installment.definitionEn: one of a number of payments that are made regularly over a period of time until something has been paid for
installment.sentence: I have to pay for my car in monthly installments.
installment.sentenceTrans: 我用每月分期付款的方式买了车。
installment.mnemonic: in不 + stall停止 + ment名词后缀→ 不停地送钱 → installment分期付款

instalment.definition: 分期付款；（连载作品或分集戏剧等的）一部分
instalment.definitionEn: a part of a broadcast serial
instalment.sentence: We prefer to pay for things over 12 monthly instalments.
instalment.sentenceTrans: 我们更愿意12个月分期付款。

instance.definition: 例子，实例，事例；情况，场合
instance.sentence: Earthquakes, in some instances, can be devastating, whereas in others they might be quite mild.
instance.sentenceTrans: 地震在一些情况下可能是毁灭性的，但在另一些情况下则影响较小。
instance.mnemonic: in=inside在里面 ＋ st=stand站立 ＋ ance构成名词：表性质、状况等 → 站在里面，属于某事物内，以身为例 → instance例子

instant.definitionEn: a very short period of time; a particular point in time
instant.sentence: The mother caught her baby the instant he fell.
instant.sentenceTrans: 那位母亲在孩子掉下的瞬间接住了他。
instant.mnemonic: in进入 + st站立 + ant…的 → 站进来的 → instant紧急的

instantly.sentence: The beauty of this camera is that the photo is ready instantly.
instantly.sentenceTrans: 这台相机的妙处在于照片立即可得。
instantly.mnemonic: instant立即的 + ly副词后缀 → instantly立即地

instead.sentence: Have some healthy food instead of hamburgers.
instead.sentenceTrans: 吃点健康的食品，别吃汉堡包了。
instead.mnemonic: in进入，使 + stead位置 → instead代替

instinct.definition: 本能，天性；天分，天资；直觉
instinct.definitionEn: a natural tendency for people and animals to behave in a particular way using the knowledge and abilities that they were born with rather than thought or training
instinct.sentence: Even well-fed cats will kill mice because of their hunting instincts.
instinct.sentenceTrans: 即使喂得很饱的猫也会捉老鼠，因为它们有捕食老鼠的天性。
instinct.mnemonic: in内 + stinct刺激 → 内在的刺激 → instinct本能

institute.definition: 学院，专科学院，研究院（或所）；学会；机构；  v.建立，设立，制定
institute.definitionEn: an organization that has a particular purpose, especially one that is connected with education or a particular profession; the building used by this organization
institute.sentence: A lot of top scientists are working in this institute of medical biology.
institute.sentenceTrans: 许多顶尖的科学家在这家医用生物学的研究院工作。
institute.mnemonic: in内部 + stitut建立 + e → 建立在内部的 → 学院；制定，设立

institution.definitionEn: an organization founded and united for a specific purpose
institution.sentence: This English language training institution is very popular with parents and their children alike.
institution.sentenceTrans: 这家英语培训机构很受家长和孩子们的欢迎。
institution.mnemonic: in在......里 + stitut建立 + ion名词后缀 → institution机构

instruct.definitionEn: to teach somebody something, especially a practical skill
instruct.sentence: My mom instructs me how to play golf.
instruct.sentenceTrans: 我妈妈教我怎么打高尔夫球。
instruct.mnemonic: in进 + struct建立 → 把知识建立进去 → instruct指导

instruction.definition: 说明，说明书；指导；指令，命令；指示
instruction.definitionEn: the action or process of teaching; the act of instructing someone
instruction.sentence: She follows the instructions to take her medicine.
instruction.sentenceTrans: 她按照说明书的指示服药。
instruction.mnemonic: instruct指导 + ion名词后缀 → instruction指导

instructive.definitionEn: giving a lot of useful information
instructive.sentence: The little boy learned from this instructive book that it is wrong to lie.
instructive.sentenceTrans: 这个小男孩从这本有教育意义的书中学到了说谎是错误的。
instructive.mnemonic: in进 + struct建立 + ive形容词后缀 → 把知识建立进去 → instructive有益的；教育性的

instrument.definitionEn: an object used for producing musical sounds, for example a piano or a drum
instrument.sentence: Guitar, violin, drum, and piano are all musical instruments.
instrument.sentenceTrans: 吉他、小提琴、鼓和钢琴都是乐器。
instrument.mnemonic: in内 + stru=struct建立 + ment表名词 → 内部结构 → instrument仪器；工具

insult.definition: 侮辱；  n.侮辱的言辞或行为
insult.definitionEn: to say or do something that offends somebody
insult.sentence: The customer insulted the ice cream seller by throwing the money to the ground.
insult.sentenceTrans: 这个顾客把钱丢在地上，以此来侮辱卖冰激凌的小贩。
insult.mnemonic: in进入 + sult跳 → 踩到别人的脸上 → insult侮辱

insurance.definitionEn: an arrangement with a company in which you pay them regular amounts of money and they agree to pay the costs, for example, if you die or are ill/sick, or if you lose or damage something
insurance.sentence: Insurance can offer financial protection against loss as a result of an accident.
insurance.sentenceTrans: 保险能够提供经济上的保护，赔偿因事故造成的损失。
insurance.mnemonic: insur保证 + ance名词后缀 → insurance保险

insure.definitionEn: to buy insurance so that you will receive money if your property, car, etc. gets damaged or stolen, or if you get ill/sick or die
insure.sentence: I insure my car against accident and theft.
insure.sentenceTrans: 我为我的车上了事故险和偷盗险。
insure.mnemonic: in进入 + sure肯定 → 进入肯定 → 保险

integrate.definition: （使）成为一体，（使）合并；（使）加入，融入群体
integrate.definitionEn: to combine two or more things so that they work together; to combine with sth else in this way
integrate.sentence: Our department's four teams must integrate together to work on new projects.
integrate.sentenceTrans: 我们部门的四个小组必须合力推进新项目。
integrate.mnemonic: integr完整 ＋ ate使… → 使…完整 → integrate使一体，使结合

integrity.definitionEn: the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles
integrity.sentence: The judge has a strong sense of integrity.
integrity.sentenceTrans: 这位法官有强烈的正直感。
integrity.mnemonic: integr完整 + ity表名词 → integrity完整，完全

intellectual.definition: 聪明的；需用智力的；  n.知识分子
intellectual.definitionEn: a person who is well educated and enjoys activities in which they have to think seriously about things
intellectual.sentence: The intellectual girl is familiar with all the math formulas.
intellectual.sentenceTrans: 这个聪明的女孩熟知所有的数学公式。
intellectual.mnemonic: intel在...之间 + lectu选，挑选 + al形容词后缀 -> intellectual聪明的

intelligence.definitionEn: the ability to learn, understand and think in a logical way about things; the ability to do this well
intelligence.sentence: Einstein was a man of great intelligence.
intelligence.sentenceTrans: 爱因斯坦是一个智商很高的人。
intelligence.mnemonic: intel在…中间 + lig选择，收集 + ence名词后缀 → 从中选出好的 → 智力

intelligent.definitionEn: good at learning, understanding and thinking in a logical way about things; showing this ability; (of an animal, a being, etc.) able to understand and learn things
intelligent.sentence: If you are as intelligent as this scientist, you may change the world.
intelligent.sentenceTrans: 如果你像这位科学家那么聪明，你就有可能改变世界。
intelligent.mnemonic: intellig知识界 + ent表示具有……性质的 → intelligent智能型的，聪明的

intend.definitionEn: to have a plan, result or purpose in your mind when you do something
intend.sentence: The boy intends to use the money he saved to buy a new skateboard.
intend.sentenceTrans: 男孩打算用存下来的钱买一块新的滑板。
intend.mnemonic: in内 + tend伸展；扩大 → 内心伸出 → intend打算

intense.definitionEn: serious and often involving a lot of action in a short period of time; very great; very strong
intense.sentence: People are having an intense training in the gym.
intense.sentenceTrans: 人们正在健身房里进行着高强度的的训练。
intense.mnemonic: in使 + tense延伸 → 使拉长，绷紧 → intense剧烈的，强烈的

intensify.definitionEn: to increase in degree or strength; to make something increase in degree or strength
intensify.sentence: The microphone intensifies the loudness of my voice.
intensify.sentenceTrans: 麦克风能扩大我说话的音量。
intensify.mnemonic: in使 + tens延伸 + ify动词后缀 → intensify变猛烈；加强

intensity.definitionEn: the strength of something, for example light, that can be measured
intensity.sentence: Light of high intensity may blind your eyes.
intensity.sentenceTrans: 强光线可能会闪瞎你的双眼。
intensity.mnemonic: in 加强 + tens伸展 + ity表名词 → 拉紧 → 强烈，剧烈

intensive.definitionEn: giving force or emphasis to a statement
intensive.sentence: The intensive study for the college entrance exam made him exhausted.
intensive.sentenceTrans: 高考强化训练让他精疲力竭。
intensive.mnemonic: intens强烈的 + ive形容词后缀 → intensive加强的

intensively.sentence: He studied intensively for the exam to ensure he would pass.
intensively.sentenceTrans: 他为考试进行了密集的复习，以确保能够通过。

intention.definitionEn: what you intend or plan to do; your aim
intention.sentence: I have an intention of buying a house, so I must start saving money now.
intention.sentenceTrans: 我一心想买房，所以我现在必须开始存钱了。
intention.mnemonic: intent意图 + ion表名词 → 有意图做某事 → intention有意图，故意

interact.definition: 交流，互动；互相作用，互相影响
interact.definitionEn: to communicate with somebody, especially while you work, play or spend time with them
interact.sentence: You need to interact with people in business.
interact.sentenceTrans: 做生意，你就得与人交流。
interact.mnemonic: inter互相 + act行动 → interact交流，沟通

interaction.definitionEn: the act of communicating with somebody, especially while you work, play or spend time with them
interaction.sentence: The interaction between students and teachers is important in teaching.
interaction.sentenceTrans: 师生之间的相互作用在教学中很重要。
interaction.mnemonic: inter相互 + action行动 → 相互行动 → interaction互动

interest.definitionEn: the feeling that you have when you want to know or learn more about somebody/something
interest.sentence: His interest is to read comics.
interest.mnemonic: inter表示“在…之间，相互 + est表示最高级“最……” → 兴趣；利益；利息

interested.definitionEn: giving your attention to something because you enjoy finding out about it or doing it; showing interest in something and finding it exciting
interested.sentence: The baby seems to be interested in the school bus.
interested.sentenceTrans: 小宝宝似乎对这辆校车很感兴趣。
interested.mnemonic: interest兴趣 ＋ ed形容词后缀 → 感觉有兴趣的 → interested感兴趣的

interesting.definitionEn: attracting your attention because it is special, exciting or unusual
interesting.sentence: Watching cartoons is more interesting for the little baby.
interesting.sentenceTrans: 对于这个小宝宝来说，看动画片更有趣。
interesting.mnemonic: interest对...有兴趣 + ing形容词或现在分词后缀 → interesting有趣的

interfere.definitionEn: to get involved in and try to influence a situation that does not concern you, in a way that annoys other people
interfere.sentence: Let it fall. Don't interfere with the process.
interfere.sentenceTrans: 让它倒下去。别去干涉这个过程。
interfere.mnemonic: inter在…之间 + fer带来，拿来 + e → interfere干涉，干预；妨碍

interference.sentenceTrans: 干涉指的是不必要的打扰。
interference.mnemonic: interfere干涉 + ence表名词 → interference干涉

interior.definitionEn: connected with the inside part of something
interior.sentence: The interior furnishing of the living room is very delicate.
interior.sentenceTrans: 客厅的内部装潢十分精致。
interior.mnemonic: inter内 + ior表形容词，较...的 → interior内部的

intermediate.definitionEn: located between two places, things, states, etc.
intermediate.sentence: The toy in the middle is of intermediate size.
intermediate.mnemonic: inter在…之间，相互 + medi中间 + ate做、造成 → intermediate中间的；中级的

internal.definition: 体内的，内部的；  n.内部器官
internal.sentence: The picture shows humans' major internal organs.
internal.sentenceTrans: 这张图展示了人体主要的内脏器官。
internal.mnemonic: intern=inter在…之内 + al属于...的 → internal内的；国内的

internally.sentence: The engine has been internally inspected and ready for takeoff.
internally.sentenceTrans: 发动机已经通过内部检查，准备起飞。

international.definitionEn: connected with or involving two or more countries
international.sentence: All of them are international students from different countries.
international.sentenceTrans: 他们都是来自不同国家的国际学生。
international.mnemonic: inter在…之间，相互 + national国家的 → international国际的

internet.definitionEn: an international computer network connecting other networks and computers from companies, universities, etc.
internet.sentence: We can get news on the Internet.
internet.sentenceTrans: 我们可以在互联网上获取新闻。

interpret.definition: 口译；解读；解释；  v.把……理解（解释）为
interpret.definitionEn: to translate one language into another as you hear it
interpret.sentence: I interpreted his words into English.
interpret.sentenceTrans: 我把他的话口译成了英文。
interpret.mnemonic: inter相互 + pret表达 → 语言之间相互表达 → interpret口译

interpretation.definitionEn: the act or result of explaining or interpreting something
interpretation.sentence: His English-Chinese interpretation is strange; I doubt if it is correct.
interpretation.sentenceTrans: 他将英文翻译成了很奇怪的中文，我怀疑他翻得不对。
interpretation.mnemonic: inter在…之间，相互 + pret预先 + ation名词后缀 → 相互之间预先了解 → interpretation口译；解释

interrupt.definitionEn: to say or do something that makes somebody stop what they are saying or doing
interrupt.sentence: Their conversation was interrupted by a knock at the door.
interrupt.sentenceTrans: 他们的谈话被敲门声打断了。
interrupt.mnemonic: inter在…中间 + rupt断裂 → 在讲话中间打断 → interrupt打断

interruption.definitionEn: the act of interrupting sb./sth. and of stopping them from speaking
interruption.sentence: He wore a pair of headphones to prevent his friend's interruption.
interruption.sentenceTrans: 他戴了一副耳机，防止他朋友的打扰。
interruption.mnemonic: inter 从中间 + rupt 打破 + ion 名词后缀 → interruption 打扰

interval.definition: 间隔；中场休息，幕间休息
interval.definitionEn: a period of time between events
interval.sentence: This clock only shows fifteen-second intervals.
interval.sentenceTrans: 这个表只能显示15秒的时间间隔。
interval.mnemonic: inter在内，中间 + val墙 → 两堵墙之间的空间 → interval间隔，间歇

intervene.definitionEn: to become involved in a situation in order to improve or help it; to exist between two events or places; to happen in a way that delays something or prevents it from happening
intervene.sentence: They only stopped fighting when the teacher intervened.
intervene.sentenceTrans: 当老师介入时，他们才停止打架。
intervene.mnemonic: inter在…之间，相互 + ven走 + e → 走在二者之间 → intervene干涉

intervention.definitionEn: action taken to improve or help a situation
intervention.sentence: The man's intervention stops the dominos.
intervention.sentenceTrans: 这名男子的干预阻止了多米诺骨牌。
intervention.mnemonic: inter在…之间，相互 + ven走 + tion名词后缀 → intervention干涉，干预

interview.definitionEn: a formal meeting at which somebody is asked questions to see if they are suitable for a particular job, or for a course of study at a college, university, etc.; a meeting (often a public one) at which a journalist asks somebody questions in order to find out their opinions
interview.sentence: During the job interview, the man seemed nervous.
interview.sentenceTrans: 在求职面试过程中，这位男士似乎很紧张。
interview.mnemonic: inter互相 + view看见 → interview会见

interviewer.definitionEn: a person who is asking someone questions at an interview.
interviewer.sentence: The interviewer is looking at his resume to ask questions.
interviewer.sentenceTrans: 面试官正看着他的简历提问。
