sea.definitionEn: the salt water that covers much of the Earth's surface
sea.sentence: The sea looks so calm today.
sea.sentenceTrans: 今天，这片海看起来很平静。

seal.definition: 印章；海豹；  v.封（信封）；密封
seal.definitionEn: to close an envelope, etc. by sticking the edges of the opening together
seal.sentence: He pressed the official seal onto the envelope and nobody else could open it.
seal.sentenceTrans: 他在信封上盖上了火漆印，没有其他人可以打开它。

search.definitionEn: to look carefully for something/somebody; to examine a particular place when looking for somebody/something
search.sentence: The policeman is carrying out a search for the lost item.
search.sentenceTrans: 这名警察正在进行搜索，寻找遗失的物品。

season.definition: 季（节）；  v.给……调味；风干（木柴）
season.definitionEn: one of the four periods (spring, summer, autumn, and winter) into which the year is commonly divided
season.sentence: There are four seasons in a year.
season.mnemonic: sea播种 + son → 影响播种的时间 → season季节

seat.definitionEn: a place where you can sit, for example a chair
seat.sentence: This theater only has sixty seats.
seat.sentenceTrans: 这个电影院只有六十个座椅。

second.definition: 第二名；秒；片刻；  adj.第二的；  adv.第二，其次
second.definitionEn: happening or coming next after the first in a series of similar things or people; 2nd
second.sentence: The second got a silver medal.
second.sentenceTrans: 第二名获得了一枚银牌。

secondary.sentence: He took the silver medal, which is secondary in importance.
secondary.sentenceTrans: 他获得了银牌，位列第二。
secondary.mnemonic: second第二 + ary…的 → secondary第二的；次要的

secret.definition: 秘密；  adj.秘密的，保密的
secret.definitionEn: something that is known about by only a few people and not told to others
secret.sentence: She is telling her friend a surprising secret!
secret.sentenceTrans: 她正在告诉她朋友一个惊人的秘密！
secret.mnemonic: se分开 + cret区别 → 分开来放 → secret秘密

secretary.definitionEn: a person who works in an office, working for another person, dealing with letters and telephone calls, typing, keeping records, arranging meetings with people, etc.
secretary.sentence: As a secretary, she is responsible for answering phone calls and taking notes.
secretary.sentenceTrans: 作为一名秘书，她负责接听电话和做记录。

section.definitionEn: any of the parts into which something is divided
section.sentence: This chart can be divided into six sections of different sizes.
section.sentenceTrans: 这个图表可以分成六个大小不同的部分。
section.mnemonic: sect切，割 + ion名词后缀 → 切开；部门

sector.definition: （经济等的）行业；部门；扇形，扇区
sector.definitionEn: a part of an area of activity, especially of a country’s economy
sector.sentence: This country's economy has three different sectors: manufacturing, agriculture, and services.
sector.sentenceTrans: 这个国家的经济有三个不同的行业：制造业、农业和服务业。
sector.mnemonic: sect切 + or名词后缀 → sector部门

secure.definition: 保护；使安全；（经过努力）获得；  adj.安全的；有把握的，确切的
secure.definitionEn: to protect something so that it is safe and difficult to attack or damage
secure.sentence: The anti-virus software can secure our computers.
secure.sentenceTrans: 防毒软件可以保护我们的电脑。
secure.mnemonic: se免于 + cure忧虑 → secure保护

security.definition: 安全；保护措施；债券；抵押物；保障，保护
security.definitionEn: a place at an airport where you go after your passport has been checked so that officials can find out if you are carrying illegal drugs or weapons
security.sentence: You must go through the security check at the airport.
security.sentenceTrans: 在机场，你必须通过安全检查。
security.mnemonic: secur安全的 + ity名词后缀 → security安全；证券

see.definitionEn: to become aware of somebody/something by using your eyes

seed.definition: 【生】种子；种子，籽；  v.播种，结籽
seed.definitionEn: a small object produced by a plant from which a new plant can grow
seed.sentence: A seed contains the genetic information of a plant.
seed.sentenceTrans: 一颗种子包含了植物的遗传信息。

seem.definitionEn: (not used in the progressive tenses) to give the impression of being or doing something; used to make what you say about your thoughts, feelings or actions less strong; used to suggest that something is true when you are not certain or when you want to be polite
seem.sentence: Judging by the clouds, it seems that it will rain.
seem.sentenceTrans: 根据这云层判断，似乎要下雨。

seize.definitionEn: to take somebody/something in your hand suddenly and using force; to arrest or capture somebody; to be quick to make use of a chance, an opportunity, etc.; to take control of a place or situation, often suddenly and violently
seize.sentence: They seized one another by the wrist.
seize.sentenceTrans: 他们相互抓住了对方的手腕。

seldom.definition: 很少，不常；  adj.不常的；稀少的
seldom.sentence: It seldom rains in the desert.

select.definition: 选择，挑选；  adj.精选的，选择的
select.definitionEn: to choose somebody/something from a group of people or things, usually according to a system; to mark something on a computer screen; to choose something, especially from a menu
select.sentence: Which dress do you think I should select?
select.sentenceTrans: 你觉得我应该选哪条裙子？
select.mnemonic: se分开 + lect选 → 选出分开 → select选择

selection.definitionEn: a number of people or things that have been chosen from a larger group; a collection of things from which something can be chosen
selection.sentence: Our nursery offers a selection of spring flowers of many different colors.
selection.sentenceTrans: 我们的苗圃里有各种颜色的春季花卉可供挑选。
selection.mnemonic: se分开 + lect选择，收集 → select分开选=选择 + ion表名词 → 选择

self.definitionEn: the type of person you are, especially the way you normally behave, look or feel; a person’s personality or character that makes them different from other people; used to refer to a person
self.sentence: She thinks she can find her true self in the mirror.
self.sentenceTrans: 她认为她在镜子里能找到真正的自己。

selfish.definitionEn: caring only about yourself rather than about other people
selfish.sentence: He's so selfish, always hogging the toys.
selfish.sentenceTrans: 他太自私了，总是独占着玩具。
selfish.mnemonic: self自己 + ish形容词后缀 → selfish自私的

sell.sentence: She sells eggs on the street.

semester.definitionEn: one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into
semester.sentence: A school year often contains two semesters.
semester.sentenceTrans: 一学年通常包含两个学期。
semester.mnemonic: se=sex六 + mester=mensis月  → 六个月（约一个学期）  → semester学期

semiconductor.definitionEn: a solid substance that conducts electricity in particular conditions, better than insulators but not as well as conductors; a device containing a semiconductor used in electronics
semiconductor.sentence: Semiconductor is an important material to make chips.
semiconductor.sentenceTrans: 半导体是做芯片的重要材料。
semiconductor.mnemonic: semi半 ＋ conduct传导＋ or名词后缀，表物 → semiconductor半导体

seminar.definitionEn: a meeting in which you receive information on and training in a particular subject
seminar.sentence: A teacher and some students are holding a math seminar.
seminar.sentenceTrans: 一位老师和一些学生正在开数学研讨会。

senate.definitionEn: one of the two groups of elected politicians who make laws in some countries, for example in the US, Australia, Canada and France. The Senate is smaller than the other group but higher in rank. Many state parliaments in the US also have a Senate.
senate.sentence: Several politicians are talking in front of the United States Senate.
senate.sentenceTrans: 几个政治家在美国参议院前面交谈。
senate.mnemonic: sen老 + ate名词后缀  → 参议院，上议院，古罗马的元老院议员

send.definitionEn: to cause (a letter, an e-mail, a package, etc.) to go or to be carried from one place or person to another
send.sentence: She sends a message to her friend.
send.sentenceTrans: 她给她的朋友发了一条信息。

senior.definition: 资格老的，地位较高的；年长的；  n.（大学或高中）毕业生；长辈；上司
senior.definitionEn: high in rank or status; higher in rank or status than others
senior.sentence: He is saluting the senior officer.
senior.mnemonic: sen年老 + ior表示人 → 上年纪的人 → senior长辈

sensation.definitionEn: a feeling that you get when something affects your body; a general feeling or impression that is difficult to explain; an experience or a memory
sensation.sentence: The hot sun is causing a burning sensation on her shoulders.
sensation.sentenceTrans: 炙热的太阳让她的肩膀产生了灼热感。
sensation.mnemonic: sens感觉 + ation 表示行为、状态、结果 → sensation（感官的）感觉能力

sense.definitionEn: one of the five powers (sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch) that your body uses to get information about the world around you
sense.sentence: I'm blind, but I can read this book by using my sense of touch.
sense.sentenceTrans: 我是盲人，但是我能用我的触觉来读这本书。

sensible.definition: 明智的，理智的；可觉察的；合理的
sensible.definitionEn: (of people and their behaviour) able to make good judgements based on reason and experience rather than emotion; practical
sensible.sentence: It's a sensible choice to take only a few things when going climbing.
sensible.sentenceTrans: 轻装上阵去爬山是一个明智的选择。
sensible.mnemonic: sens感觉 + ible形容词后缀，能…的 → sensible能感觉的，明智的

sensitive.definitionEn: easily offended or upset; reacting quickly or more than usual to something
sensitive.sentence: His teeth are sensitive to ice cream.
sensitive.sentenceTrans: 他的牙齿对冰淇淋很敏感。
sensitive.mnemonic: sens感觉 + itive形容词后缀 → sensitive敏感的

sentence.definitionEn: to say officially in court that somebody is to receive a particular punishment
sentence.sentence: The judge sentenced him to life in prison.
sentence.mnemonic: sent（感觉/判断） + ence（名词化） → 原指“思想表达”，后分化为“句子”和“判决”两义

separate.definition: 分开的；独立的；  v.使分开，分离
separate.definitionEn: to divide into different parts or groups; to divide things into different parts or groups;  to move apart; to make people or things move apart; to be between two people, areas, countries, etc. so that they are not touching or connected; to stop living together as a couple with your husband, wife or partner
separate.sentence: They stood in separate places, facing away from each other.
separate.sentenceTrans: 他们站在分开的地方，背对着彼此。
separate.mnemonic: separ分离 + ate形容词后缀具有...的 → separate分离的；个别的

september.sentence: September 5th is my birthday. It's coming soon!
september.sentenceTrans: 9月5日是我的生日，就快要到了！
september.mnemonic: Septem七 + ber → 古罗马的七月，历法修改后沿用成了九月 → September公历九月

sequence.definitionEn: the order that events, actions, etc. happen in or should happen in
sequence.mnemonic: sequ跟随 + ence名词后缀 → sequence连续发生，连续

series.definition: 一连串；系列，系列节目；系列片；连续比赛，系列比赛
series.definitionEn: several events or things of a similar kind that happen one after the other; a set of radio or television programmes that deal with the same subject or that have the same characters
series.sentence: A series of coinciding incidents resulted in the glass-breaking.
series.sentenceTrans: 一连串巧合的事件导致玻璃被打碎。

serious.definition: 认真的，严肃的；严重的；庄重的
serious.definitionEn: needing to be thought about carefully; not only for pleasure; sincere about something; not joking or meant as a joke
serious.sentence: He is always very serious while working.

servant.definitionEn: a person who is hired to do household or personal duties such as cleaning and cooking
servant.sentence: The servant served them with drinks.
servant.sentenceTrans: 这个佣人给他们送上了饮料。
servant.mnemonic: serv服务，保持 ＋ ant表示人 → servant仆人；公务员

serve.definitionEn: to work or perform duties for a person, an organization, a country, etc.
serve.sentence: Wearing a smile, the man served us a plate of Chinese pancake.
serve.sentenceTrans: 那名男子面带微笑，为我们端上了一盘中式煎饼。

service.definition: 服务；公共服务事业（或系统）；维修保养
service.definitionEn: a system that provides something that the public needs, organized by the government or a private company
service.sentence: The cleaning lady provides a range of cleaning services.
service.sentenceTrans: 这位清洁女工提供一系列清洁服务。
service.mnemonic: serv服务 + ice表名词，行为，状态 → service服务

session.definition: 会议；会期；（法庭的）开庭；一段时间的（活动）
session.definitionEn: a formal meeting or series of meetings of a court, a parliament, etc.; a period of time when such meetings are held; a period of time that is spent doing a particular activity
session.sentence: An important session was held on investment policies.
session.sentenceTrans: 一个关于投资政策的重要会议召开了。
session.mnemonic: ses=sed坐下 + sion名词后缀 → 需要坐下的情况 → session会议

set.definition: 设置；（小心地）放置；  n.一套，一副，一批；【数】集合；  adj.固定的，规定的，固执的
set.definitionEn: a group of similar things that belong together in some way
set.sentence: She set the alarm for 7 a.m. before going to bed.
set.sentenceTrans: 她在睡觉前把闹钟设置到了早上7点。

settle.definition: 安顿；结束（争论）；解决；调停
settle.definitionEn: to make a place your permanent home
settle.sentence: He built himself a house and decided to settle there.
settle.sentenceTrans: 他给自己修建了一所房子，并决定在那里安顿下来。

settlement.definitionEn: an official agreement that ends an argument between two people or groups
settlement.sentence: The two sides shook hands on the settlement.
settlement.mnemonic: settle解决，安居 + ment表示行为、行为的过程或结果 → settlement解决

seven.sentence: The candle on the birthday cake is in the shape of a seven.
seven.sentenceTrans: 蛋糕上的蜡烛是7的形状。

seventeen.sentence: I need the ball number seventeen to win the lottery.
seventeen.sentenceTrans: 要想赢得彩票大奖，我还需要一个17号球。

seventy.sentence: Seventy years is a long time.
seventy.sentenceTrans: 七十年是很长的一段时间。

several.definition: 几个，一些；  adj.各自的，分别的
several.definitionEn: more than two but not very many
several.sentence: I have several apples for you!
several.sentenceTrans: 我给你准备了几个苹果！
several.mnemonic: se分离 + veral准备好 → several各自的

severe.definition: 极为恶劣的；严重的；严厉的；艰难的
severe.sentence: It's hard for people to walk in such severe weather conditions.
severe.sentenceTrans: 在如此恶劣的天气条件下，人们走得很艰难。
severe.mnemonic: sever诚恳 + e → severe严肃的，严厉的

sew.definitionEn: to use a needle and thread to make stitches in cloth
sew.sentence: She uses the machine to sew a new dress.
sew.sentenceTrans: 她用机器缝制一条新裙子。

sex.definitionEn: physical activity between two people in which they touch each other’s sexual organs, and which may include sexual intercourse
sex.sentence: The application form asks for your sex.
sex.sentenceTrans: 这张申请表需要填上您的性别。

shade.definition: 阴凉处；遮光物；阴影；  v.遮蔽（光线）
shade.definitionEn: an area that is dark and cool under or behind something, for example a tree or building, because the sun’s light does not get to it
shade.sentence: I am standing in the shade of a tree. It's cooler here.
shade.sentenceTrans: 我站在树荫下，这儿凉快些。

shadow.definition: 影子；阴影；  v.把影子投在……；盯梢
shadow.definitionEn: the dark shape that somebody/something’s form makes on a surface, for example on the ground, when they are between the light and the surface
shadow.sentence: I could see the boy's shadow on the ground as he played soccer.
shadow.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩踢球的时候，我能看到他在地上的影子。
shadow.mnemonic: shade阴影，影子 + ow后缀 → shadow影子

shake.definitionEn: to move or have parts of your body move in short, quick movements and in a way that you are not able to control
shake.sentence: Shake the bottle well before drinking.

shall.definition: 提供建议或征求意见，要不要？
shall.definitionEn: used in questions with I and we for making offers or suggestions or asking advice

shallow.definitionEn: not having much distance between the top or surface and the bottom
shallow.sentence: The boy is swimming in the shallow pool.
shallow.sentenceTrans: 这个男孩在浅水池里游泳。

shame.definition: 羞愧；  v.使羞愧（或惭愧）
shame.definitionEn: a feeling of guilt, regret, or sadness that you have because you know you have done something wrong
shame.sentence: He felt a deep sense of shame because he cheated in the exam.
shame.sentenceTrans: 他因考试作弊而深感羞愧。

shameless.sentence: It is shameless to shout loudly in public.
shameless.sentenceTrans: 在公众场合大声吼叫是无耻的行为

shape.definition: 形状，样子；身材；  v.使形成，塑造
shape.definitionEn: the form or outline of an object
shape.sentence: Put your hands together to make a heart shape.
shape.sentenceTrans: 把你的手放在一起比个心形。

share.definition: 分享，共享；分配，均分；  n.股份，股东
share.definitionEn: to have or use something at the same time as somebody else
share.sentence: Would you like to share some ice cream with me?
share.sentenceTrans: 你想和我一起分享冰激凌吗？

shareholder.definitionEn: an owner of shares in a company or business
shareholder.sentence: A significant decision, it requires the approval of our shareholders.
shareholder.sentenceTrans: 这是一个重大决定，需要得到我们股东的批准。
shareholder.mnemonic: share股份 + holder持有人 → shareholder股东

sharp.definition: 锋利的，尖锐的；敏锐的；  adv.锐利地
sharp.definitionEn: having a fine edge or point, especially of something that can cut or make a hole in something
sharp.sentence: This knife is so sharp that it can easily slice the apple.
sharp.sentenceTrans: 这把刀好锋利啊，切苹果超级容易。

shave.definition: 剃（须发），刮脸；  n.剃须，修面
shave.definitionEn: to cut hair from the skin, especially the face, using a razor
shave.sentence: The man is shaving in front of the mirror.
shave.sentenceTrans: 这个男人正在镜子前刮胡子。

she.definitionEn: (used as the subject of a verb) a female person or animal that has already been mentioned or is easily identified

sheep.definitionEn: an animal with a thick coat, kept on farms for its meat (called mutton or lamb ) or its wool
sheep.sentence: Sheep are raised to produce wool.
sheep.sentenceTrans: 人们养羊是为了产羊毛。

sheer.sentence: She answered these questions correctly by sheer luck.
sheer.sentenceTrans: 她这几道题是全凭运气答对的。

sheet.definitionEn: a large piece of thin cloth used on a bed to lie on or lie under
sheet.sentence: I like the white sheet since it looks clean.
sheet.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢这个白床单，因为它看起来很干净。

shelf.definitionEn: a flat board which is attached to a wall, frame, etc., and on which objects can be placed
shelf.sentence: There are many books on the shelf.

shell.definition: 壳，外壳；炮弹；  v.剥壳；炮击；给……去壳
shell.definitionEn: the hard outer part of eggs, nuts, some seeds and some animals; any object that looks like the shell of a snail or sea creature
shell.sentence: The egg shell broke in half.

shelter.definition: 避难所；遮蔽物；庇护处；  v.遮蔽，庇护
shelter.definitionEn: a building, usually owned by a charity, that provides a place to stay for people without a home, or protection for people or animals who have been badly treated
shelter.sentence: Someone used branches to make a shelter in the woods.
shelter.sentenceTrans: 有人用树枝在树林里搭了个躲避处。
shelter.mnemonic: shel盾 + ter群，队 → shelter躲避处

shield.definitionEn: a large piece of metal or leather carried by soldiers in the past to protect the body when fighting
shield.sentence: The knight fights with a sword and shield.
shield.sentenceTrans: 骑士挥舞着宝剑和盾牌战斗。

shift.definition: 换挡；改换，替换；转移；  n.轮班
shift.definitionEn: to change the gears when you are driving a vehicle
shift.sentence: You have to shift gears as you drive around the corner.
shift.sentenceTrans: 你开车驶过拐角时要换挡。

shine.sentence: The sun is shining in the sky.
shine.sentenceTrans: 太阳在天空中熠熠闪光。

ship.definitionEn: a large boat that carries people or goods by sea
ship.sentence: The ship is carrying a lot of goods.

shipment.definitionEn: a load of goods that are sent from one place to another
shipment.sentence: I'm waiting for the shipment coming from India.
shipment.sentenceTrans: 我在等待从印度运来的货物。
shipment.mnemonic: ship船 + ment表名词 → shipment装船，装运

shirt.definitionEn: a piece of clothing for the upper body that has sleeves and usually a collar and buttons down the front
shirt.sentence: He always has to wear a shirt and tie to work.
shirt.sentenceTrans: 他总是穿衬衫打领带去工作。

shock.definition: 使……震惊，使惊讶；使……震动；  n.震惊；震动；休克
shock.definitionEn: to surprise and upset somebody; (of bad language, immoral behaviour, etc.) to make somebody feel offended or disgusted
shock.sentence: She was shocked to see how much her stock value had fallen.
shock.sentenceTrans: 看到股票跌了这么多，她真是惊呆了！

shocking.definition: 令人震惊的，骇人听闻的
shocking.definitionEn: very surprising and upsetting or causing a sudden feeling of horror or disgust
shocking.sentence: My mobile phone bill this month was shocking!
shocking.sentenceTrans: 我这个月的电话账单太令人震惊了！

shoe.definitionEn: one of a pair of outer coverings for your feet, usually made of leather or plastic
shoe.sentence: There are two pairs of sports shoes on the floor.

shoot.definitionEn: to fire a gun or other weapon; to fire something from a weapon; to kill or wound a person or an animal with a bullet, etc.
shoot.sentence: The instructor taught the girl how to shoot a pistol.
shoot.sentenceTrans: 教练教了女孩儿怎样用手枪射击。

shop.definitionEn: (British English, informal) an act of going shopping, especially for food and other items needed in the house
shop.sentence: We are buying fruits in a shop.
shop.sentenceTrans: 我们正在商店里买水果。

shore.definitionEn: the land along the edge of an area of water (such as an ocean, lake, etc.)

short.definitionEn: measuring or covering a small length or distance, or a smaller length or distance than usual; (of a person) small in height; lasting or taking a small amount of time or less time than usual; (of a period of time) seeming to have passed very quickly; not having enough of something; lacking something; being a shorter form of a name or word; (of a person) speaking to somebody using few words in a way that seems rude
short.sentence: Short hair is in style now.

shortage.definitionEn: a state in which there is not enough of something that is needed
shortage.sentence: The child is experiencing a shortage of water.
shortage.sentenceTrans: 这个孩子正面临水的短缺。
shortage.mnemonic: short短 + age名词形式 → 不足，缺少

shortcoming.definitionEn: a fault in somebody’s character, a plan, a system, etc.
shortcoming.sentence: A shortcoming of this kind of dog is that their legs are too short.
shortcoming.sentenceTrans: 这种狗的缺点是它们的腿太短了。
shortcoming.mnemonic: short短的 + coming来到 → shortcoming短处，缺点

shortly.definitionEn: a short time; not long; soon
shortly.sentence: The note on the door said that they would be back shortly.
shortly.sentenceTrans: 门上的纸条写着他们不久就会回来。
shortly.mnemonic: short短的 + ly……地 → 立刻，马上，不久；简单；

shorts.definitionEn: trousers that end at or above the knee
shorts.sentence: When the weather is warm, it's time to wear shorts.
shorts.sentenceTrans: 天气暖和时，就是穿短裤的时候了。

shot.definitionEn: the action of hitting, kicking or throwing the ball in order to score a point or goal in a game
shot.sentence: "Nice shot!" I said as she hit the ball.

should.definitionEn: used to show what is right, appropriate, etc., especially when criticizing somebody’s actions
should.sentence: When you are working, you should sit up straight.
should.sentenceTrans: 工作时，你应该挺身坐直。

shoulder.definitionEn: either of the two parts of the body between the top of each arm and the neck
shoulder.sentence: The old man has pain in his shoulder.

shout.definitionEn: to say something in a loud voice; to speak loudly/angrily to somebody
shout.sentence: He cupped his hands around his mouth and shouted loudly.
shout.sentenceTrans: 他将双手拢在嘴边，大声呼喊。

show.definition: 展示；（提供事实、信息）证明，表明；  n.演出；节目；展览；显示，表现
show.definitionEn: a theatre performance, especially one that includes singing and dancing; a programme on television or the radio
show.sentence: The girl is showing the photocards she's collected.
show.sentenceTrans: 这个女生在展示她收集的小卡。

shower.definition: 淋浴，淋浴器；阵雨；  v.淋浴，淋湿
shower.definitionEn: the act of washing your body with a shower
shower.sentence: The cat is happy to take a shower.

shrink.definitionEn: to become or to make something smaller in size or amount
shrink.sentence: The girl shrank back, covering her face because of the horror movie.
shrink.sentenceTrans: 女孩因为害怕恐怖片，挡住脸向后缩。
shrink.mnemonic: shr扭转，弯曲 + ink → shrink收缩

shut.definition: 关上，闭上；  adj.关闭的，合拢的
shut.definitionEn: to make something close; to become closed

shy.definition: 羞怯的；腼腆的；胆怯的，迟疑的
shy.definitionEn: feeling nervous and uncomfortable about meeting and talking to people; afraid of doing something or being involved in something
shy.sentence: They are both shy on the first date.
shy.sentenceTrans: 第一次约会时，他们俩都很害羞。

sick.definition: 生病的，有病的；不舒服的；恶心的，想吐的
sick.definitionEn: affected with a disease or illness
sick.sentence: The sick boy fell asleep in the bed.
sick.sentenceTrans: 这个生病的男孩在床上睡着了。

side.definitionEn: either of the two halves of a surface, an object or an area that is divided by an imaginary central line
side.sentence: There are many trees on both sides of the river.
side.sentenceTrans: 小河两边的岸上有许多树。

sideways.definitionEn: to, towards or from the side
sideways.sentence: I am sliding the curtain open sideways.
sideways.sentenceTrans: 我正在将窗帘向侧面拉开。
sideways.mnemonic: side边 + ways方向 → 斜向一边地

sigh.definition: 叹息，叹气；  n.叹气，叹息
sigh.definitionEn: to take and then let out a long deep breath that can be heard, to show that you are disappointed, sad, tired, etc.
sigh.sentence: He sighed with relief after a whole day's busy work.
sigh.sentenceTrans: 经过一天繁忙的工作，他舒了一口气。

sight.definition: 视力；景象，情景；  v.看见
sight.definitionEn: someone or something that is seen
sight.sentence: My dog's sight is better with these binoculars.
sight.sentenceTrans: 用了望远镜，我的狗视力更好了。

sightseeing.definitionEn: the activity of visiting the famous or interesting places of an area
sightseeing.sentence: I like to go sightseeing around seaside towns.
sightseeing.mnemonic: sight眼光 + see看 + ing名词后缀 → 用眼看 → 观光，游览

sign.definition: 记号，符号；标志；标牌，指示牌；手势；迹象；  v.签名；签字；使眼色；做暗号；做手势；签署
sign.definitionEn: to write your name on a document, letter, etc. to show that you have written it, that you agree with what it says, or that it is genuine
sign.sentence: Rick left the sign for him so that he could follow up.
sign.sentenceTrans: 瑞克给他留下了记号让他能够跟上队伍。

signal.definition: 信号；标志；  v.标志；发信号
signal.definitionEn: a movement or sound that you make to give somebody information, instructions, a warning, etc.; a series of electrical waves that carry sounds, pictures or messages, for example to a radio, television or mobile/cell phone; a piece of equipment that uses different coloured lights to tell drivers to go slower, stop, etc., used especially on railways/railroads and roads
signal.sentence: There's no signal in the mountains.
signal.mnemonic: sign标志 + al名词/形容词后缀 → signal信号/显要的

signature.definitionEn: your name as you usually write it, for example at the end of a letter
signature.sentence: The boy wrote his father's signature at the bottom of paper.
signature.sentenceTrans: 男孩在试卷下面签下了他爸爸的名字。
signature.mnemonic: signa=sign记号 + ture表名词 → 签名

significance.definitionEn: the importance of something, especially when this has an effect on what happens in the future
significance.sentence: The wedding anniversary is of great significance to the couple.
significance.sentenceTrans: 结婚纪念日对这对夫妻来说意义重大。
significance.mnemonic: signific=signify有重要性的 + ance名词后缀 → significance重要性；意义

significant.definition: 有重大意义的，重要的；意味深长的；显著的
significant.definitionEn: large or important enough to have an effect or to be noticed; having a special or hidden meaning
significant.sentence: It was a significant day because we got married on that day.
significant.sentenceTrans: 那是一个具有重大意义的日子，因为我们在那天结婚了。
significant.mnemonic: signify使...闻名 + icant表形容词 -> significant有重大意义的

significantly.definitionEn: in a way that is large or important enough to be noticed or have an effect
significantly.sentence: The company's profits have significantly increased in the last two years.
significantly.sentenceTrans: 这家公司的利润在过去两年里显著增加了。
significantly.mnemonic: sign记号，信号 ＋ ific产生…的 ＋ ant形容词后缀 ＋ ly副词后缀 → significant有象征意义的 ＋ ly副词后缀 → significantly意味深长地

silence.definition: 寂静，无声，沉默；  v.使沉默
silence.definitionEn: a complete lack of noise or sound; a situation when nobody is speaking
silence.sentence: They sat face to face in silence.

silent.definition: 沉默的，不说话的；  n.无声电影
silent.sentence: We should keep silent in the library.
silent.sentenceTrans: 在图书馆里我们应当保持安静。

silk.definitionEn: a type of fine smooth cloth made from silk thread; fine soft thread produced by silkworms
silk.sentence: The white silk looks so soft.
silk.sentenceTrans: 这块白色丝绸看上去真柔软。

silly.definition: 傻的，愚蠢的；（尤指像小孩一样）可笑的，荒唐的
silly.definitionEn: showing a lack of thought, understanding or judgement
silly.sentence: Silly to wear a down coat on a hot summer day.
silly.sentenceTrans: 大热天穿羽绒服，太傻了。

silver.definition: 银；银器；  adj.银色的；  v.镀银于，使……成银色
silver.definitionEn: a soft grayish-white metal that is very valuable and is used to make jewelry, coins, knives, forks, etc.
silver.sentence: The silver necklace tarnished over time.
silver.sentenceTrans: 银项链随着时间流逝变暗了。

similar.definitionEn: like somebody/something but not exactly the same
similar.sentence: They are wearing the similar hats.
similar.mnemonic: simil一样 + ar……的 → similar同样的，相似的

similarity.definitionEn: the state of being like somebody/something but not exactly the same; a feature that things or people have that makes them like each other
similarity.sentence: The similarity between water and hydrogen peroxide is that both are made up of hydrogen and oxygen.
similarity.sentenceTrans: 水和过氧化氢的相似点在于，它们都是由氢和氧构成的。
similarity.mnemonic: similar相似的 + ity名词后缀 → similarity类似

similarly.definitionEn: in almost the same way; used to say that two facts, actions, statements, etc. are like each other
similarly.sentence: The group of teenagers are dressed similarly.
similarly.sentenceTrans: 这群年轻人的穿着很相似。
similarly.mnemonic: similar相似的 + ly表副词 → similarly相似地

simple.definition: 简单的，易于理解的；朴素的
simple.definitionEn: not complicated; easy to understand or do
simple.sentence: You can solve this problem—it's simple!
simple.sentenceTrans: 你可以解决这个问题的，它很简单！
simple.mnemonic: sim一个，一起 + ple重叠 → 只有一个重叠在一起 → simple简单的

simplify.definitionEn: to make something easier to do or understand
simplify.sentence: The process of photosynthesis can be simplified into two stages: light-dependent reactions and light-independent reactions.
simplify.sentenceTrans: 光合作用的过程可以简化为两个阶段：依赖光的反应和不依赖光的反应。
simplify.mnemonic: simple简单 + -fy动词词尾 → 使简化

simply.definition: 简单地；仅仅，只不过；简直
simply.definitionEn: in a way that is natural and plain
simply.sentence: My room is just simply furnished because I'm not at home very often.
simply.sentenceTrans: 我的房间陈设简单，因为我不常在家。
simply.mnemonic: simpl=simple简单的 + (l)y表副词 → simply简单地

simulate.definitionEn: to be made to look like something else
simulate.sentence: The playful child simulates his cat's movements.
simulate.sentenceTrans: 顽皮的小孩模仿猫咪的动作。
simulate.mnemonic: simul相类似，一样 + ate动词后缀 → 做得相像 → simulate模仿

simultaneous.definitionEn: happening or done at the same time as something else
simultaneous.sentence: I'm good at handling simultaneous tasks to improve my work efficiency.
simultaneous.sentenceTrans: 我擅长处理同时进行的任务以提高我的工作效率。
simultaneous.mnemonic: simult=simul一样，相同 + aneous有……性质的 → [时间]相同的

simultaneously.definitionEn: at the same time as something else
simultaneously.sentence: The file has been simultaneously sent to all team members.
simultaneously.sentenceTrans: 文件被同时发送给所有的组员。
simultaneously.mnemonic: simultaneous同时发生的 + ly副词后缀 → simultaneously同时发生地

since.definitionEn: from a time in the past until a later past time, or until now
since.sentence: The ground is quite wet since it rained yesterday.
since.sentenceTrans: 由于昨天下雨了，所以地面非常潮湿。

sincere.definitionEn: (of feelings, beliefs or behaviour) showing what you really think or feel; (of a person) saying only what you really think or feel
sincere.sentence: She bowed to show her sincere thanks to her classmate.
sincere.sentenceTrans: 她鞠躬表示她对同学的诚挚的谢意。
sincere.mnemonic: sin同样的 + cere成长 -> 一同成长，关系密切 -> 真诚的

sincerely.definitionEn: in a way that shows what you really feel or think about somebody/something
sincerely.sentence: The robot sincerely hopes to make friends with humans.
sincerely.sentenceTrans: 这个机器人真心希望和人类做朋友。
sincerely.mnemonic: sincere真实的 + ly副词后缀 → sincerely真诚地

singer.definitionEn: a person who sings, or whose job is singing, especially in public
singer.sentence: The singer is recording a song in the recording studio.
singer.sentenceTrans: 歌手正在录音棚里录歌。
singer.mnemonic: sing唱歌 + er人 → singer歌唱家

single.definition: 单个的，单独的；未婚的；单身的；  n.单程票
single.definitionEn: (of a person) not married or having a romantic relationship with somebody
single.sentence: There is a single shoe on the ground.

singular.definitionEn: being a single and separate person or thing
singular.sentence: There is a singular red flower amongst a bed of yellow ones.
singular.sentenceTrans: 在黄色的花丛中有一朵红色的花。
singular.mnemonic: singul=single单一 + ar……的 → singular单独的

sink.definition: 水槽，洗碗池；  v.（使）下沉，（使）降低，（使）沉没
sink.definitionEn: a large open container in a kitchen that has taps/faucets to supply water and that you use for washing dishes in
sink.sentence: I am washing the dishes in the sink.
sink.sentenceTrans: 我正在洗水槽里的餐具。

sir.definitionEn: used as a polite way of addressing a man whose name you do not know, for example in a shop/store or restaurant, or to show respect
sir.sentence: Please call me "Sir" when you talk to me!
sir.sentenceTrans: 当你跟我说话时，请称呼“先生”。

sister.definitionEn: a girl or woman who has the same mother and father as another person
sister.sentence: The girl is the little boy's sister.
sister.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩是小男孩的姐姐。
sister.mnemonic: sis自己的 + ter女性 → 与自己关系密切的女性 → sister姐妹

sit.definitionEn: to rest your weight on your bottom with your back vertical, for example on/in a chair
sit.sentence: The little girl is sitting on the ground.

site.definitionEn: a place where a building, town, etc. was, is or will be located
site.sentence: Builders are working at the construction site.
site.sentenceTrans: 建筑工人们正在工地上干活。

situation.definitionEn: all the circumstances and things that are happening at a particular time and in a particular place
situation.sentence: It's hard to choose which way to go in this situation.
situation.sentenceTrans: 这种情形下很难选择该走哪条路。
situation.mnemonic: situat位于 + ion名词后缀 → situation地理位置

six.sentence: These are my six favorite drinks.
six.sentenceTrans: 这是我最喜爱的六种饮品。

sixteen.sentence: She got a special gift when she turned sixteen years old.
sixteen.sentenceTrans: 当她年满16岁时，收到了一份特殊的礼物。

sixty.sentence: My grandmother turned sixty years old today.

size.definitionEn: how large or small a person or thing is
size.sentence: These shoes come in different sizes: medium, small and large.
size.sentenceTrans: 这些鞋子有不同的尺寸：中号、小号和大号。

skate.definition: 滑冰，溜冰，滑（滑板）；  n.冰鞋
skate.definitionEn: to move on skates (usually referring to ice skating, if no other information is given)
skate.sentence: The little boy is skating by himself.
skate.sentenceTrans: 这个小男孩一个人在滑冰。

skeptical.definitionEn: having doubts that a claim or statement is true or that something will happen
skeptical.sentence: I'm skeptical that the weasel did not come here merely to extend his greetings.
skeptical.sentenceTrans: 我怀疑那只黄鼠狼不仅是来这里表达问候的。
skeptical.mnemonic: skept怀疑 + ical表形容词 → skeptical怀疑的

skepticism.definitionEn: an attitude of doubting the truth of something (such as a claim or statement)
skepticism.sentence: My skepticism of other people's motives has almost always been well-founded!
skepticism.sentenceTrans: 我对他人动机的怀疑基本都是有依据的！
skepticism.mnemonic: skeptic怀疑者 + ism...主义 → skepticism怀疑论

sketch.definition: 素描；速写；  v.速写；简述
sketch.definitionEn: a simple picture that is drawn quickly and does not have many details; a short report or story that gives only basic details about something; a short funny scene on television, in the theatre, etc.
sketch.sentence: The artist is doing a sketch of the living room.
sketch.sentenceTrans: 这位画家正在画一幅客厅的素描。

sketchy.sentence: Your agenda for the meeting today is a little sketchy.
sketchy.sentenceTrans: 今天你的会议日程有点儿粗略。
sketchy.mnemonic: sketch略图 ＋ y...的 → sketchy粗略的

skilful.definitionEn: (of a person) good at doing something, especially something that needs a particular ability or special training; made or done very well
skilful.sentenceTrans: 你是一个娴熟的（扔球）杂技人。

skill.definition: 技能；技巧；技巧，技术，能力
skill.definitionEn: a particular ability or type of ability
skill.sentence: I have many skills - juggling balls is just one of them.
skill.sentenceTrans: 我有很多技能，杂耍球仅仅是其中之一。

skilled.definitionEn: having enough ability, experience and knowledge to be able to do something well
skilled.sentence: The man is skilled at dealing with all kinds of things.
skilled.sentenceTrans: 这个男人可以熟练地处理各种事务。
skilled.mnemonic: skill技术 + ed有……的 → 有技术的 → 熟练的

skillful.definitionEn: having the training, knowledge, and experience that is needed to do something well; having a lot of skill
skillful.sentenceTrans: 他们是技术极其娴熟的滑板运动员！
skillful.mnemonic: skill技术 + ful…的 → 有技术的 → skillful熟练的

skim.definitionEn: to move quickly or lightly along, above, or near the surface of something; to read something quickly in order to find a particular point or the main points; to remove fat, cream, etc. from the surface of a liquid
skim.sentence: There are 100 different ways to skim off the top.
skim.sentenceTrans: 有上百种不同的方法能够从中获利。

skin.definition: 【医】皮肤；兽皮，毛皮；皮，外皮；  v.剥皮
skin.definitionEn: the layer of tissue that covers the body
skin.sentence: Exposure to the sun's ultraviolet rays can damage the skin and increase the risk of skin cancer.
skin.sentenceTrans: 暴露在太阳的紫外线下会损害皮肤，增加患皮肤癌的风险。

skirt.definitionEn: a piece of clothing worn by women and girls that hangs from the waist down
skirt.sentence: She looks great in that skirt.

sky.definitionEn: the space above the earth that you can see when you look up, where clouds and the sun, moon and stars appear
sky.sentence: There are white clouds in the blue sky.
sky.sentenceTrans: 蓝蓝的天空中飘着白色的云朵。

slam.definitionEn: to shut, or to make something shut, with a lot of force, making a loud noise
slam.sentence: He slams the door as he leaves.
slam.sentenceTrans: 他走的时候，砰的一声把门关上了。

slave.definition: 奴隶；  v.奴隶般地工作，苦干
slave.definitionEn: a person who is owned by another person and is forced to work for them; a person who is so strongly influenced by something that they cannot live without it, or cannot make their own decisions; a device
slave.sentenceTrans: 这几个奴隶被锁在了一起。

slavery.definitionEn: the system by which people are owned by other people as slaves
slavery.sentence: Lincoln announced that slavery should be abolished.
slavery.sentenceTrans: 林肯宣布奴隶制应被废除。
slavery.mnemonic: slav=slave奴隶 + ery表行为，身份 → slavery奴隶身份

sleep.definitionEn: to rest with your eyes closed and your mind and body not active
sleep.sentence: Adequate sleep is essential for patient recovery.
sleep.sentenceTrans: 充足的睡眠对患者的康复至关重要。

sleeve.definitionEn: the part of a shirt, jacket, etc. that covers all or part of your arm
sleeve.sentence: In winter, I prefer shirts with long sleeves.
sleeve.sentenceTrans: 冬天，我比较喜欢穿长袖衬衫。

slice.definition: 切片；薄片；份额，部分；  v.把……切成片
slice.definitionEn: a thin flat piece of food that has been cut off a larger piece
slice.sentence: A thin slice of the tissue was examined under the microscope.
slice.sentenceTrans: 一小片组织切片在显微镜下进行了检查。

slide.definition: 使滑动；滑落；  n.幻灯片；滑梯
slide.definitionEn: to move easily over a smooth or wet surface; to make something move in this way
slide.sentence: You can slide your finger across the screen to unlock your phone.
slide.sentenceTrans: 你可以在屏幕上滑动手指来解锁你的手机。

slight.definition: 轻微的，微小的；纤细的，瘦弱的；少量的；  n.轻视，蔑视
slight.definitionEn: very small in degree or amount
slight.sentence: There's a slight imperfection on this antique teapot.
slight.sentenceTrans: 这个古董茶壶上面有一个小瑕疵。

slightly.definitionEn: in a very small amount or degree; a little
slightly.sentence: She is slightly taller than her brother.
slightly.sentenceTrans: 她比她弟弟略微高一点。
slightly.mnemonic: slight轻微的 + ly ...地 →  些微地，轻微地；纤细地

slim.definitionEn: (of a person) thin, in a way that is attractive
slim.sentence: Ever since she started eating a healthy diet, she has had a very slim figure.
slim.sentenceTrans: 自从开始健康饮食，她的身材就变得很苗条了。

slip.definition: 滑倒，跌落；滑落；溜走；  n.溜走；滑倒；疏忽，小错误
slip.definitionEn: to slide a short distance by accident so that you fall or nearly fall
slip.sentence: The floor is wet—make sure you don't slip and fall.
slip.sentenceTrans: 地板很湿，请注意不要滑倒。

slippery.definitionEn: difficult to hold or to stand or move on, because it is smooth, wet or polished
slippery.sentence: Watch out! The ground is slippery!
slippery.mnemonic: slip滑（重读闭音节，双写p） + er名词词尾 + y形容词词尾→ slippery滑的，使人滑跤的

slope.definition: 斜坡；斜度；坡度；  v.倾斜；成斜坡
slope.definitionEn: a surface or piece of land that slopes (= is higher at one end than the other); an area of land that is part of a mountain or hill
slope.sentence: This little slope is for people in wheelchairs.
slope.sentenceTrans: 这个小斜坡是供坐轮椅的人使用的。

slow.definitionEn: (used especially in the comparative and superlative forms, or in compounds) at a slow speed
slow.sentence: The video loading speed is very slow.

small.definitionEn: the slender part of the back
small.sentence: This is a small model of my real house.
small.sentenceTrans: 这是我房子的一个小模型。

smart.definition: 聪明的，机灵的；时髦的，衣着讲究的；  v.难过，烦恼
smart.sentence: The girl is so smart that she can solve very difficult physics problems.
smart.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩很聪明，她能解很难的物理题。

smell.definition: 气味；嗅觉；  v.嗅，闻（......的气味），闻到
smell.definitionEn: the quality of a thing that you can sense with your nose; an unpleasant smell; the ability to sense things with the nose
smell.sentence: The smell of this flower is so good.

smile.definitionEn: an expression on your face that makes the corners of your mouth turn up and that shows happiness, amusement, pleasure, affection, etc.

smoke.definitionEn: the cloud of black, gray, or white gases and dust that is produced by burning something
smoke.sentence: The man is smoking and blowing smoke into the air.
smoke.sentenceTrans: 那个人正在抽烟，向空中吐烟。

smooth.definition: 光滑的，平滑的；平稳的；  v.使......光滑；使......平稳
smooth.definitionEn: completely flat and even, without any lumps, holes or rough areas
smooth.sentence: She said the taste of the chocolate is as smooth as silk. Give me some!
smooth.sentenceTrans: 她说这种巧克力的口感如丝绸般柔滑，给我一点儿尝尝！

smuggle.definitionEn: to take, send or bring goods or people secretly and illegally into or out of a country, etc.
smuggle.sentence: They often smuggle things at night.
smuggle.sentenceTrans: 他们常常在夜晚走私物品。

snack.definitionEn: a small meal or amount of food, usually eaten in a hurry
snack.sentence: Besides snacks, this place has coffee.
snack.sentenceTrans: 除了小吃，这里还有咖啡。

snake.definitionEn: a reptile with a very long thin body and no legs.
snake.sentence: This is a cute cartoon snake.
snake.sentenceTrans: 这是一条可爱的卡通蛇。

snow.definitionEn: soft, white pieces of frozen water that fall to the ground from the sky in cold weather
snow.sentence: She opened the door and it was snowing outside.
snow.sentenceTrans: 小樱打开了大门，外面正飘着雪。

snowy.definitionEn: when a lot of snow falls; covered with snow; very white, like new snow
snowy.sentence: Today is a snowy day, Children are building a snowman together
snowy.sentenceTrans: 今天是个多雪的日子，小朋友们正在一起堆雪人
snowy.mnemonic: snow雪 + y形容词后缀 → snowy下雪的

so.definition: 如此，这么，那么；  conj.所以；  adj.真的，事实如此的，如此的，整齐的

so-called.definitionEn: used to show that you do not think that the word or phrase that is being used to describe somebody/something is appropriate; used to introduce the word that people usually use to describe something
so-called.sentenceTrans: 他们提供所谓的中国菜。
so-called.mnemonic: so用这种方式 + called称呼的 → so-called所谓的

soak.definition: 浸泡；吸收，吸入；  n.浸泡
soak.definitionEn: to put something in liquid for a time so that it becomes completely wet; to become completely wet in this way
soak.sentence: Before cooking dried beans, don't forget to soak them in water for a few hours.
soak.sentenceTrans: 在烹饪干豆子之前，不要忘了将它们浸泡在水中几个小时。

soap.definitionEn: a substance that you use with water for washing your body
soap.sentence: I use a piece of soap to wash my hands.

soar.definitionEn: to fly very high in the air or remain high in the air
soar.sentence: It's wonderful to soar in the sky like a bird.
soar.sentenceTrans: 像小鸟一样在天空中翱翔真是太棒了。
soar.mnemonic: s=ex向外 + oar空气 → 升至空中 → soar高飞

social.definition: 社交的；社会的；  n.社交聚会
social.definitionEn: relating to activities that involve meeting and communicating with other people
social.sentence: People chat and post things on social media platforms.
social.sentenceTrans: 人们在社交媒体上聊天和发照片。
social.mnemonic: soc社会 + ial形容词后缀 → 社会的

society.definitionEn: people in general, living together in communities
society.sentence: In a modern society many people can live peacefully.
society.sentenceTrans: 在现代社会中，许多人都可以和平地生活。
society.mnemonic: socie=social社会 + ty表名词 → society社会，社团

sociologist.sentence: Sociologists study the development of human society and human interactions.
sociologist.sentenceTrans: 社会学家研究人类社会的发展和人际交往。
sociologist.mnemonic: soci=social社会的 ＋ ologist...学家 → sociologist社会学家

sock.definitionEn: a piece of clothing that is worn on your foot and that covers your ankle and sometimes the lower part of your leg
sock.sentence: She is wearing socks of two different colors on her feet.
sock.sentenceTrans: 她脚上穿着两只不同颜色的袜子。

soda.definitionEn: a drink made of soda water, flavoring, and often ice cream
soda.sentence: Soda water is good for your health.

sofa.definitionEn: a long comfortable seat with a back and arms, for two or more people to sit on
sofa.sentence: She lies on the sofa, reading a book.

soft.definition: 软的，柔软的；细嫩的，光滑的；  n.柔软的东西；  adv.柔软地，柔和地
soft.sentenceTrans: 这种材质看起来很柔软。

software.definitionEn: the programs, etc. used to operate a computer
software.sentence: I have a lot of software on my smart phone.
software.sentenceTrans: 我手机上装了很多软件。
software.mnemonic: soft软的 + ware物件 → software软件

soil.definitionEn: the top layer of the earth in which plants, trees, etc. grow
soil.sentence: He is holding some soil in his hands.

soldier.definitionEn: a member of an army, especially one who is not an officer
soldier.sentence: The soldier stands on the watchtower looking into the distance.
soldier.sentenceTrans: 士兵站在瞭望塔上眺望远方。

sole.definition: 脚底，鞋底，袜底；  adj.独有的
sole.definitionEn: the bottom surface of the foot
sole.sentence: She is having the sole of her foot massaged.
sole.mnemonic: sol单独 ＋ e → sole单独的，唯一的

solemn.definitionEn: done, said, etc. in a very serious and sincere way; (of a person) not happy or smiling
solemn.sentence: He gave a salute with a solemn expression.
solemn.sentenceTrans: 他在敬礼时，脸上神情严肃。
solemn.mnemonic: sol全部 + emn=ann年  → 每年都发生的（节日） → solemn庄重的，隆重的

solid.definition: 坚固的；固体的；可靠的；  n.立方体；固体
solid.sentence: This turtle’s shell is solid enough to protect itself.
solid.sentenceTrans: 这个乌龟(龙龟)的背壳相当坚硬，足以保护她自己。

solution.definition: 解决办法；答案，解答；溶液；溶解
solution.definitionEn: a way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation
solution.sentence: I think the other plan is a better solution.
solution.sentenceTrans: 我觉得另一个方案是更好的解决办法。
solution.mnemonic: solut解开；溶解 + ion名词后缀，构成抽象名词 → 溶解；解决

solve.definitionEn: to find a way of dealing with a problem or difficult situation
solve.sentence: He helped the girl solve the math problem.
solve.sentenceTrans: 他帮女孩解答了这道数学题。
solve.mnemonic: so反身代词 + lv松开，分开 + e → solve解决

some.definitionEn: used with uncountable nouns or plural countable nouns to mean ‘an amount of’ or ‘a number of’, when the amount or number is not given
some.sentence: The woman is putting some sugar in her coffee.
some.sentenceTrans: 女人正往她的咖啡里加入一些糖。

somebody.definitionEn: a person who is not known or mentioned by name
somebody.sentence: Somebody sends me the flowers, but I don't know who he is.
somebody.sentenceTrans: 某人给我送了花，可是我不知道他是谁。
somebody.mnemonic: some有些 + body人 → somebody某人，有人

somehow.definition: 出于某种原因，不知怎么地；以某种方式
somehow.definitionEn: in a way that is not known or certain; for a reason that you do not know or understand
somehow.sentenceTrans: 不知怎么的，他看上去变了。

someone.sentence: Someone left the pen on the desk.
someone.mnemonic: some某些 + one一个 → someone某人

someplace.definitionEn: in or at or to some place
someplace.sentence: His playmates are planning to hide someplace.
someplace.sentenceTrans: 他的玩伴正打算躲到某处去。

something.definitionEn: a thing that is not known or mentioned by name
something.sentence: Here, there is something in the box for you.
something.sentenceTrans: 给，盒子里有给你的一些东西。
something.mnemonic: some有些 + thing事 → 一些事情 → something某事，某物

sometime.definition: 在某一时候；  adj.以前的
sometime.definitionEn: at a time that you do not know exactly or has not yet been decided
sometime.sentence: Although I failed the exam, I believe that I will make it sometime.
sometime.sentenceTrans: 虽然我考试失败了，但我相信总有一天我会成功的。
sometime.mnemonic: some某 + time时间 → sometime在某一时侯

sometimes.definitionEn: occasionally rather than all of the time
sometimes.sentence: Sometimes, the weather will change every day.
sometimes.sentenceTrans: 有的时候，天气每天都在变。
sometimes.mnemonic: sometime某一时间的 ＋ s表副词 → 某一时间 → sometimes有时

somewhat.definitionEn: to indicate that something is the case to a limited extent or degree.
somewhat.sentence: The old-style restaurant is somewhat pricier than the street ones.
somewhat.sentenceTrans: 这家老字号饭店的价格比街边饭店的稍贵。

somewhere.definitionEn: in, at or to a place that you do not know or do not mention by name
somewhere.sentence: My pen must be somewhere in this classroom.
somewhere.sentenceTrans: 我的笔一定在教室的某个地方。
somewhere.mnemonic: some某个 + where哪里 → somewhere在某处

song.definitionEn: a short piece of music with words that you sing
song.sentence: We all sang a song together on New Year's Day.
song.sentenceTrans: 在元旦我们一起唱了一首歌。

soon.definitionEn: in a short time from now; a short time after something else has happened
soon.sentence: It'll soon be the New Year.

sophisticated.definitionEn: having a lot of experience of the world and knowing about fashion, culture and other things that people think are socially important
sophisticated.sentenceTrans: 这台机器是非常精密的。
sophisticated.mnemonic: soph智慧 + istic……的 + at＝ate做，造成 + ed……的 → 有智慧的 → sophisticated老于世故的，精致复杂的

sore.definition: 疼痛的，酸痛的；恼火的；  n.痛处
sore.definitionEn: if a part of your body is sore, it is painful, and often red, especially because of infection or because a muscle has been used too much
sore.sentence: Ugh! My back feels so sore!

sorrow.definitionEn: a feeling of great sadness because something very bad has happened
sorrow.sentence: Her tears are full of sorrow.

sorrowful.definition: 充满悲伤的，悲哀的，伤心的
sorrowful.sentence: The girl by the window looked very sorrowful.
sorrowful.sentenceTrans: 窗边的女孩看起来充满悲伤。
sorrowful.mnemonic: sorrow悲伤 + ful形容词后缀 → sorrowful悲哀的

sorry.definition: 抱歉的，歉疚的；  int.对不起，很抱歉
sorry.sentence: I'm sorry I called you fat - you're hardly fat at all, please forgive me!
sorry.sentenceTrans: 很抱歉我说你胖，你一点都不胖，请原谅我！

sort.definition: 把……分类，整理，挑选；  n.种类，类别
sort.definitionEn: to arrange things in groups or in a particular order according to their type, etc.; to separate things of one type from others
sort.sentence: I sorted the books into piles of big ones and small ones.
sort.sentenceTrans: 我将书按大小分成了几摞。

soul.definitionEn: the spiritual part of a person, believed to exist after death
soul.sentence: Piano and drum are the core musical instruments in soul music.
soul.sentenceTrans: 钢琴和鼓是灵魂乐的核心乐器。

sound.definition: 声音，声响；  v.听起来；  adj.健全的，完好的；合理的；可靠的
sound.definitionEn: what you can hear coming from a television, radio, etc., or as part of a film/movie
sound.sentence: The sound coming from the speakers was very loud.
sound.sentenceTrans: 喇叭里传出来的声音很大。

soup.definitionEn: a food made by cooking vegetables, meat, or fish in a large amount of liquid
soup.sentence: This is a bowl of chicken soup.

source.definition: 来源；出处；河的源头；知情人士，提供消息者
source.definitionEn: the place where a river or stream starts; a person or thing that causes something, especially a problem; a place, person or thing that you get something from
source.sentence: The lake is the source of the river.
source.sentenceTrans: 这片湖是这条河的发源地。
source.mnemonic: sou=sub从下往上 + rce引导 → source来源；出处

south.definition: 南；南方；  adj.南方的，南部的；  adv.向南方，在南方
south.sentence: Penguins live in the far south.
south.sentenceTrans: 企鹅生活在遥远的南方。

southern.definitionEn: located in or toward the south
southern.sentence: He lives in the southern part of the city.
southern.mnemonic: south南 + ern...方向的 → 南方的

souvenir.definitionEn: a thing that you buy and/or keep to remind yourself of a place, an occasion or a holiday/vacation; something that you bring back for other people when you have been on holiday/vacation
souvenir.sentence: I bought a handmade bell as a souvenir for my friend.
souvenir.sentenceTrans: 我给朋友买了一个手工铃铛作为纪念品。

sow.definitionEn: to plant or spread seeds in or on the ground
sow.sentence: He is sowing seeds into the soil.

space.definitionEn: the amount of an area, room, surface, etc., that is empty or available for use
space.sentence: In nursing, it's important to maintain personal space.
space.sentenceTrans: 在护理中，保持个人空间非常重要。

spacecraft.definitionEn: a vehicle that travels in space
spacecraft.sentence: The spacecraft is used to explore the unknown area in space.
spacecraft.sentenceTrans: 宇宙飞船是用来探索宇宙中的未知区域的。
spacecraft.mnemonic: space宇宙 + craft小船 → spacecraft航天器，宇宙飞船

spade.definitionEn: a garden tool with a broad metal blade and a long handle, used for digging
spade.sentence: He used a spade to dig a hole for the new tree.
spade.sentenceTrans: 他用铁锹挖了个坑来种新树。

span.definition: 跨度；时间段；持续时间；小范围，短距离；  v.持续，贯穿（时间）；横跨；包括
span.definitionEn: the width of something from one side to the other
span.sentence: The bridge's span is about half a kilometer.
span.sentenceTrans: 这座大桥的跨距大约是500米。

spare.definition: 备用的；多余的，空闲的；瘦的；  n.备用品；  v.抽出，腾出
spare.definitionEn: kept in case you need to replace the one you usually use; extra
spare.sentence: Prepare a spare pen for your exam.
spare.sentenceTrans: 为考试准备一支备用的笔。

sparingly.definitionEn: to a meager degree or in a meager manner
sparingly.sentence: One way of becoming rich is to spend money sparingly.
sparingly.sentenceTrans: 一个致富方式就是节俭开支。

spark.definition: 火花，火星；  v.发出火花
spark.definitionEn: a very small burning piece of material that is produced by something that is burning or by hitting two hard substances together; a small flash of light produced by an electric current
spark.sentence: There are many sparks coming out during the work.
spark.sentenceTrans: 在作业时有很多火星飞溅出来。

speak.definitionEn: to talk to somebody about something; to have a conversation with somebody
speak.sentence: When he speaks, everybody else listens carefully.
speak.sentenceTrans: 他说话的时候别人都在认真地听。

special.definitionEn: different from what is normal or usual
special.sentence: Their wedding anniversary was a very special day to them.
special.sentenceTrans: 结婚纪念日对他们来说是特别的一天。
special.mnemonic: speci种类 + al…的 → 比其他种类好的 → special特别的

specialisation.definitionEn: (biology) the structural adaptation of some body part for a particular function
specialisation.sentence: Excessive specialisation isolates the individual in his or her work and inhibits not only social contacts with work mates, but knowledge generation.
specialisation.sentenceTrans: 过度的专业化使个人在工作中孤立无援，不仅阻碍了与同事的社会交往，也阻碍了知识的创造。

specialise.definitionEn: to become an expert in a particular area of work, study or business; to spend more time on one area of work, etc. than on others
specialise.sentence: We specialise in studying the characteristics of different plants.
specialise.sentenceTrans: 我们专门研究不同植物的特性。
specialise.mnemonic: special特别的 + ise动词后缀 → specialise专门研究

specialist.definitionEn: a person who is an expert in a particular area of work or study
specialist.sentence: They are the specialists in our hospital.
specialist.sentenceTrans: 他们是我们医院的专家。
specialist.mnemonic: special特别的 + ist表示人 → 特殊的人，有特别专长的人 → specialist专家

specialization.definitionEn: a particular area of work, study or business which somebody spends more time on than on other areas
specialization.sentence: The scientist's specialization is in physics.
specialization.sentenceTrans: 这个科学家的特长是物理。
specialization.mnemonic: special特殊的 + ization……化 → specialization特殊化

specialize.definitionEn: to become an expert in a particular area of work, study or business; to spend more time on one area of work, etc. than on others
specialize.sentence: The store specializes in selling hiking gear.
specialize.sentenceTrans: 这家店专门卖登山设备。
specialize.mnemonic: special特别的 + ize……化 → 特殊化

specially.definitionEn: for a particular purpose, person,etc; more than usual or more than other things
specially.sentence: The door was specially made for the giraffe.
specially.sentenceTrans: 这个门是专门为长颈鹿做的。
specially.mnemonic: special特别的 + ly副词后缀 → specially特别地，专门地

species.definitionEn: a class of things of the same kind and with the same name
species.sentence: There are tens of thousands of different species of birds in the world.
species.sentenceTrans: 世界上有数万种各不相同的鸟。

specific.sentence: The teacher asked for a specific example to illustrate the concept.
specific.sentenceTrans: 老师要求举一个具体的例子来说明这个概念。
specific.mnemonic: speci种类 + fic制造，做 → 做某种东西 → specific具体的

specification.definitionEn: a detailed description of how something is, or should be, designed or made
specification.sentence: The product does not match the specification listed on your website.
specification.sentenceTrans: 产品与你们网站上列出的规格不符。
specification.mnemonic: specific具体的 + ation表名词 → specification具体说明

specify.definitionEn: to state something, especially by giving an exact measurement, time, exact instructions, etc.
specify.sentence: If you want to achieve your goals, it's important to specify them clearly.
specify.sentenceTrans: 如果你想达到目标，清晰详细地说明这些目标很重要。
specify.mnemonic: speci外观，种类+ fy表动词 → 归类 →  指定，详细说明

specimen.definitionEn: a small amount of something that shows what the rest of it is like
specimen.sentence: This exhibit contains various specimens of butterfly.
specimen.sentenceTrans: 这件展览品中包含了各种蝴蝶标本。
specimen.mnemonic: speci仔细看 + men人 → 需要人仔细观察的东西 → specimen样本

spectator.definitionEn: a person who is watching an event, especially a sports event
spectator.sentence: Thousands of spectators watched the tennis match.
spectator.sentenceTrans: 成千上万的观众观看了这场网球比赛。
spectator.mnemonic: spect看 + ator名词后缀：人 → 看的人 → spectator观众

speculate.definition: 推测，猜测；投机，做投机买卖
speculate.definitionEn: to form an opinion about something without knowing all the details or facts
speculate.sentence: He speculated about future trends in the stock market.
speculate.sentenceTrans: 他推测了股市的未来趋势。
speculate.mnemonic: specul环顾 + ate动词后缀 → 看准了 → speculate思考，投机

speech.definitionEn: a spoken expression of ideas, opinions, etc., that is made by someone who is speaking in front of a group of people
speech.sentence: The public speaker looks confident during his speech.
speech.sentenceTrans: 这位发言人在他演讲时看上去胸有成竹。

speechless.sentence: She was speechless after seeing the countdown of the pop-up ad.
speechless.sentenceTrans: 在看到广告倒计时后，她无语了。

speed.definitionEn: the rate at which someone or something moves or travels; the rate at which something happens or is done; the quality of being quick or rapid
speed.sentence: The train is traveling at a speed of 300 km/h.
speed.sentenceTrans: 列车的运行速度是每小时300千米。

spell.definition: 拼写；招致；意味着；  n.一段时间；魅力
spell.definitionEn: to say or write the letters of a word in the correct order; to form words correctly from individual letters; to form words when they are put together in a particular order
spell.sentence: Sometimes we can play word games to learn how to spell.
spell.sentenceTrans: 有时候我们能通过玩拼字游戏来学会拼写。

spelling.definitionEn: the act of forming words correctly from individual letters; the way that a particular word is written
spelling.sentence: The spelling of that word is so easy. B-O-Y, boy!
spelling.sentenceTrans: 那个单词的拼写很简单，B-O-Y，boy！
spelling.mnemonic: spell拼写 + ing名词后缀 → spelling拼写法，拼法

spend.definitionEn: to give money to pay for goods, services, etc.
spend.sentence: I spend too much money on clothes!
spend.sentenceTrans: 我在买衣服上花了太多的钱。

spending.definitionEn: the act of spending or disbursing money
spending.sentence: The girl is planning her spending in detail.
spending.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩正在详细计划她的开支。

sphere.definitionEn: any object that is completely round, for example a ball
sphere.sentence: The world is not flat; it is a sphere.
sphere.sentenceTrans: 世界不是平的，而是一个球体。

spill.definition: 使流出，涌流；（人群）涌出；  n.溢出，溅出
spill.definitionEn: to cause or allow (something) to fall, flow, or run over the edge of a container usually in an accidental way
spill.sentence: Oh no! I've spilled the green nail polish.
spill.sentenceTrans: 哦不！我把这瓶绿色的指甲油弄洒了。

spin.definition: （使）旋转；疾驰；纺织；  n.高速旋转
spin.definitionEn: to turn or cause someone or something to turn around repeatedly
spin.sentence: The top spins across the floor.

spirit.definition: 精神，心灵；情绪；烈酒（spirits）；灵魂；  v.（秘密地或神秘地）带走
spirit.definitionEn: the soul thought of as separate from the body and believed to live on after death; a ghost
spirit.sentence: The dove with olive branch symbol captures the spirit of peace and friendship.
spirit.sentenceTrans: 鸽子衔橄榄枝的标志象征和平友爱的精神。
spirit.mnemonic: spir呼吸 + it名词 → spirit精神

spiritual.definitionEn: of or relating to a person's spirit
spiritual.sentence: Watching the sun set peacefully was a spiritual experience.
spiritual.sentenceTrans: 平静地看着太阳落下是一种很好的精神体验。
spiritual.mnemonic: spirit精神 + ual形容词后缀  → spiritual精神的

spite.definition: 恶意，怨恨；  v.刁难，欺侮
spite.definitionEn: a feeling of wanting to hurt or upset somebody
spite.sentence: The dog peed on his master's bed out of spite.
spite.sentenceTrans: 出于怨恨，这只狗尿在了主人的床上。

splash.definitionEn: (of liquid) to fall noisily onto a surface
splash.sentence: The man's dancing makes the water splash everywhere.
splash.sentenceTrans: 世勋跳起舞来水花四溅。

splendid.definition: 壮观的，辉煌的，华丽的；极好的，出色的
splendid.sentence: The palace looks really splendid at night.
splendid.sentenceTrans: 这座宫殿在夜晚看起来格外壮丽。
splendid.mnemonic: splend光辉 + id形容词后缀 → splendid辉煌的，华丽的

split.definition: 裂缝；劈裂，劈开；碎片；  v.分开
split.definitionEn: to divide, or to make a group of people divide, into smaller groups that have very different opinions; to divide something into two or more parts and share it between different people, activities, etc.
split.sentence: There's a split on the wall.

spoil.definition: 溺爱；毁坏；  v.（食物）变质；  n.战利品，赃物
spoil.definitionEn: to give a child everything that they ask for and not enough discipline in a way that has a bad effect on their character and behaviour
spoil.sentence: The grandparents spoil their grandchild by doing everything for him.
spoil.sentenceTrans: 爷爷奶奶太宠他们的孙子了，恨不得替他把所有事都做了。

sponsor.definitionEn: a person or company that pays for a radio or television programme, or for a concert or sporting event, usually in return for advertising
sponsor.sentence: The sponsors are threatening to rip up their contracts!
sponsor.sentenceTrans: 赞助商威胁要取消合约！

spontaneous.definitionEn: not planned but done because you suddenly want to do it; often doing things without planning to, because you suddenly want to do them
spontaneous.sentence: Remote work during the pandemic, which took away opportunities to have spontaneous discussions, led to meeting creep.
spontaneous.sentenceTrans: 在疫情期间的远程工作，由于无法进行自发讨论，导致了会议的过度增多。
spontaneous.mnemonic: spont=spond承诺 + aneous表形容词 → 自内心承诺 → 自愿的

spoon.definitionEn: a tool that has a handle with a shallow bowl at the end, used for stirring, serving and eating food
spoon.sentence: Could you please pass me the spoon?

sport.definitionEn: activity that you do for pleasure and that needs physical effort or skill, usually done in a special area and according to fixed rules
sport.mnemonic: s远离 + port带走，越过 → 不思考严肃的问题 → sport运动，娱乐

sportsman.definitionEn: a man who plays a lot of sport, especially as a professional
sportsman.sentence: Your father was quite a sportsman in his younger days.
sportsman.sentenceTrans: 你父亲年轻的时候是个运动健将。
sportsman.mnemonic: sports运动 + man人 → sportsman运动员

spot.definition: 点，斑点；（通常为圆形的）斑点，斑块；污点；  v.看见，注意到，发现
spot.definitionEn: a small area of a surface that is different from other areas
spot.sentence: This type of dog has many black spots.
spot.sentenceTrans: 这种狗的身上有很多黑色的斑点。

spouse.sentence: The young spouses planned to travel abroad.
spouse.sentenceTrans: 这对年轻夫妇计划去国外旅行。

spray.definitionEn: (especially in compounds) a substance that is forced out of a container such as an aerosol, in very small drops
spray.sentence: The girl uses a pepper spray to protect herself.
spray.sentenceTrans: 女孩用辣椒水喷雾来防身。

spread.definition: 抹，敷；伸开，伸展；  n.散布，传播
spread.definitionEn: to open something that has been folded so that it covers a larger area than before; to arrange objects so that they cover a large area and can be seen easily
spread.sentence: I like to spread butter on the bread before making a sandwich.
spread.sentenceTrans: 做三明治之前，我喜欢在面包上涂点黄油。

spring.definition: 春天；弹簧；泉，泉源；  v.反弹，跳，跃
spring.sentence: In China, the flying swallows are the sign of spring.
spring.sentenceTrans: 在中国，飞燕是春天的标志。

spur.definitionEn: to encourage a horse to go faster, especially by pushing the spurs on your boots into its side
spur.sentence: My colleagues always spur me to work harder.
spur.sentenceTrans: 我的同事们经常激励我工作更努力。

spy.definition: 暗中监视（或侦察）；发现；  n.间谍，密探
spy.definitionEn: to collect secret information about another country, organization or person; to suddenly see or notice somebody/something
spy.sentence: The man was hiding in the bush to spy on them.
spy.sentenceTrans: 这个男人正躲在灌木丛里监视他们。

square.definition: 广场；正方形；  v.把……弄成正方形；  adj.正方形的；直角的；平方的
square.definitionEn: an open area in a town, usually with four sides, surrounded by buildings
square.sentence: This square is a nice, quiet place to take a walk.
square.sentenceTrans: 这个广场安静宜人，是个散步的好地方。

squeeze.definition: （常指用手）挤压；挤进，塞进；  n.压榨
squeeze.definitionEn: to press something firmly, especially with your fingers; to force somebody/something/yourself into or through a small space
squeeze.sentence: She squeezes the toothpaste onto the toothbrush.

stabilise.definitionEn: support or hold steady and make steadfast, with or as if with a brace
stabilise.sentence: A student placed sandbags to stabilise the display board before the presentation.
stabilise.sentenceTrans: 一名学生在展示前放置沙袋使展板稳固。

stability.definitionEn: the quality or state of being steady and not changing or being disturbed in any way (= the quality of being stable)
stability.sentence: Walking a tightrope requires extreme stability.
stability.sentenceTrans: 走钢丝需要极强的稳定性。
stability.mnemonic: st=stable稳定的 + ability能力 → stability稳定性

stabilize.definitionEn: to become or to make something become firm, steady and unlikely to change; to make something stable
stabilize.sentence: The meat prices stabilized after a volatile first half of the year.
stabilize.sentenceTrans: 经历上半年的动荡之后，肉类价格稳定了下来。
stabilize.mnemonic: stabil=stable稳定的 + ize使成为… → stabilize（使）稳定，（使）稳固

stable.definition: 稳定的；安定的；稳重的；  n.马厩
stable.definitionEn: firmly fixed; not likely to move, change or fail
stable.sentence: The price finally became stable after some ups and downs.
stable.sentenceTrans: 物价在一阵起伏后终于变稳定了。
stable.mnemonic: st站立 + able能…的 → 能站的 → stable稳定的

staff.definition: 工作人员，全体职员；拐杖；  v.为……配备职员
staff.definitionEn: all the workers employed in an organization considered as a group
staff.sentence: The doctors and nurses are important members of the hospital staff.
staff.sentenceTrans: 医生和护士都是重要的医院职员。

stage.definition: 舞台；阶段；  v.举行；上演
stage.definitionEn: a raised area, usually in a theatre, etc. where actors, dancers, etc. perform
stage.sentence: The students are playing music on the stage.
stage.sentenceTrans: 学生们正在舞台上演奏音乐。
stage.mnemonic: sta表示“站，立” + ge表名词 → stage舞台；戏剧；阶段

stagger.definitionEn: to walk with weak unsteady steps, as if you are about to fall
stagger.sentence: The old woman staggered toward the hospital.
stagger.sentenceTrans: 老妇人蹒跚地走向医院。

stagnant.definitionEn: water or air is not moving and therefore smells unpleasant
stagnant.sentence: The stagnant pond is covered by algae.
stagnant.sentenceTrans: 死水池塘被藻类所覆盖。
stagnant.mnemonic: stagn站 + ant形容词后缀 → 站着不走 → 停滞的

stain.definition: 污渍，污迹；  v.弄脏；玷污；染色
stain.definitionEn: a dirty mark on something, that is difficult to remove
stain.sentence: Oh dear! Look at that big red stain on his shirt.
stain.sentenceTrans: 天哪！看他衬衫上那一大块红色的污渍。

stair.definitionEn: a series of steps that go from one level or floor to another
stair.sentence: The stairs ascend in a graceful curve.
stair.sentenceTrans: 这个楼梯呈优美的曲线上升。

stamp.definition: 印，章；邮票；跺脚；  v.盖印；跺脚
stamp.definitionEn: a design or words made by stamping something onto a surface
stamp.sentence: The stamp on the pig shows the acceptable quality of it.
stamp.sentenceTrans: 猪身上盖的章表示猪的质量合格。

stand.definitionEn: to be on your feet; to be in a vertical position
stand.sentence: My dog can stand on two feet and she can even put on her own shoes!
stand.sentenceTrans: 我的狗能双脚站立，它甚至能自己穿鞋！

standard.definition: 标准，规格；  adj.标准的，规范的
standard.definitionEn: a level of quality, especially one that people think is acceptable;  a level of quality that is normal or acceptable for a particular person or in a particular situation
standard.sentenceTrans: 护照照片有着严格的标准。
standard.mnemonic: stand站立 + ard=hard坚硬的 → standard标准

standardisation.definitionEn: the condition in which a standard has been successfully established
standardisation.sentenceTrans: 标准化让工作空间变得井然有序。

standardise.definitionEn: evaluate by comparing with a standard
standardise.sentence: We should standardise the testing process.
standardise.sentenceTrans: 我们应该把测试流程标准化。

standardization.definitionEn: the condition in which a standard has been successfully established
standardization.sentence: The standardization of education means that every child has the same education.
standardization.sentenceTrans: 教育标准化意味着每个孩子都能接受同样的教育。

standardize.definitionEn: to make objects or activities of the same type have the same features or qualities; to make something standard
standardize.sentence: The factory standardized the shape of the products on the conveyor belt.
standardize.sentenceTrans: 工厂对传送带上的产品的形状进行标准化加工。
standardize.mnemonic: standard标准 + ize使成为 → 使标准化

standpoint.definitionEn: an opinion or a way of thinking about ideas or situations
standpoint.sentence: The two ministers held conflicting standpoints on war issue.
standpoint.sentenceTrans: 两位大臣在战争问题上持有相反的观点。
standpoint.mnemonic: stand立 + point点 → standpoint立场，观点

star.definition: 星，恒星；明星，名角；  v.主演
star.definitionEn: a large ball of burning gas in space that we see as a point of light in the sky at night; an object, a decoration, a mark, etc., usually with five or six points, whose shape represents a star; a famous and excellent singer, performer, sports player, etc.;  a person who has the main part, or one of the main parts, in a film/movie, play, etc.
star.sentenceTrans: 这里有很多快乐的星星。

stare.definitionEn: to look at somebody/something for a long time
stare.sentence: She secretly stared at others from behind the window.
stare.sentenceTrans: 她在窗户后面偷偷地盯着别人。

start.definitionEn: to begin doing or using something
start.sentence: With so much homework to do, I'd better get started right now!
start.sentenceTrans: 有那么多作业要做，我最好马上就开始！

starvation.definitionEn: suffering or death caused by having nothing to eat or not enough to eat :the condition of someone who is starving
starvation.sentence: The drought resulted in the starvation of many animals.
starvation.sentenceTrans: 干旱导致许多动物挨饿。
starvation.mnemonic: starv使挨饿 + ation名词后缀 → starvation饥饿

starve.definitionEn: to suffer or die because you do not have enough food to eat; to make somebody suffer or die in this way
starve.sentence: This polar bear is starving because it doesn't have enough food to eat.
starve.sentenceTrans: 这只北极熊快饿死了，因为它没有足够的食物吃。

state.definition: 【化】状态；国家，政府；州，邦；  v.说明，陈述；  adj.国家的，州的，邦的
state.definitionEn: an organized political community forming part of a country
state.sentence: The state of an atom in a molecule refers to its electron configuration.
state.sentenceTrans: 分子中原子的状态是指其电子配置。
state.mnemonic: stat站立 + e强调 → state国家，状态

statement.definitionEn: a printed record of money paid, received, etc.
statement.sentence: The company made a statement confirming that the couple would be fired.
statement.sentenceTrans: 这家公司发表声明，确定这对情侣将被辞退。
statement.mnemonic: state陈述 + ment表名词 → 站着说话 → statement声明立场

static.definition: 静电的；静态的；静止的；  n.静电，静电干扰
static.definitionEn: not moving, changing or developing; (physics) (of a force) acting as a weight but not producing movement
static.sentence: Her hair was full of static electricity.

station.definitionEn: a place where trains stop so that passengers can get on and off; the buildings connected with this
station.sentence: The train at the station is about to leave.
station.sentenceTrans: 车站里停着的火车快要出发了。

statistic.definitionEn: a number that represents a piece of information (such as information about how often something is done, how common something is, etc.)
statistic.sentence: These statistics can help analyze the stock market.
statistic.sentenceTrans: 这些数据有助于分析股市。
statistic.mnemonic: stat站 + istic名词后缀，学科 → 站着去计算数据的学科 → statistic统计学

statistical.definitionEn: connected with or based on statistics
statistical.sentence: The statistical data shows that most people cannot afford a house.
statistical.sentenceTrans: 这项统计数据表明大多数人买不起房子。
statistical.mnemonic: stat站，立 + istical……的 → 统计的，统计学的

statue.definitionEn: a figure of a person or an animal in stone, metal, etc., usually the same size as in real life or larger
statue.sentence: The angel statue is carved out of stone.
statue.sentenceTrans: 这座天使雕像由石头雕刻而成。

status.definitionEn: the legal position of a person, group or country
status.sentence: Cats held a high status in ancient Egypt.
status.sentenceTrans: 猫在古埃及有很高的地位。
status.mnemonic: stat站着 + us名词后缀 → 站着 → status地位

stay.definition: 保持；继续是；  n.停留，逗留 ；逗留，延缓
stay.definitionEn: to continue to be in a particular place for a period of time without moving away
stay.sentence: Some shops stay open 24 hours a day.

steady.definition: 坚定的，扎实的；稳定的，平稳的；稳重的，可靠的
steady.definitionEn: firmly fixed, supported or balanced; not shaking or likely to fall down
steady.sentence: The stone house is quite steady under the extreme weather.
steady.sentenceTrans: 石屋在极端天气下非常稳固。
steady.mnemonic: stead稳定 + y表形容词  → steady坚定的

steal.definitionEn: to take (something that does not belong to you) in a way that is wrong or illegal; to move secretly and quietly so that other people do not notice you
steal.sentence: The thief is trying to steal his wallet.
steal.sentenceTrans: 小偷正试图偷他的钱包。

steam.definitionEn: the hot gas that is created when water is boiled
steam.sentence: Steam is coming from the pot. Turn off the stove!
steam.sentenceTrans: 水蒸气正在往锅外冒，关火吧！

steamer.definitionEn: a metal container with small holes in it, that is placed over a pan of boiling water in order to cook food in the steam
steamer.sentence: These yummy baozi are being cooked in the steamer.
steamer.sentenceTrans: 美味的包子在蒸笼里蒸着。
steamer.mnemonic: steam蒸汽 + er名词后缀 → 汽船

steel.definitionEn: a strong hard metal that is made of a mixture of iron and carbon; the industry that produces steel; a long thin straight piece of steel with a rough surface, used for rubbing knives on to make them sharp
steel.sentence: Steel can be used to reinforce concrete in the construction of buildings.
steel.sentenceTrans: 在建造房屋时，钢铁可以用于加固混凝土。

steep.definition: 急剧的；陡峭的；  v.浸，泡
steep.definitionEn: (of a slope, hill, etc.) rising or falling quickly, not gradually
steep.sentence: There was a steep rise in prices.

steer.definition: 驾驶；控制，引导；掌握方向盘，掌舵
steer.definitionEn: to control the direction in which a boat, car, etc. moves; (of a boat, car, etc.) to move in a particular direction; to take control of a situation and influence the way in which it develops
steer.sentence: Be cautious when you steer a car.

stem.definition: 茎，（树）干；  v.阻止；起源于
stem.definitionEn: the main long thin part of a plant above the ground from which the leaves or flowers grow; a smaller part that grows from this and supports flowers or leaves
stem.sentence: The boy is climbing along the stem to reach the clouds.
stem.sentenceTrans: 爬上花茎，男孩儿就可以触摸到云朵了。

step.definition: 脚步，脚步声；步骤，阶段；台阶；步伐；  v.踩；走，举步
step.definitionEn: the act of lifting your foot and putting it down in order to walk or move somewhere; the sound this makes
step.sentence: He's so excited to see his baby girl take her first step.
step.sentenceTrans: 看到他的宝贝女儿迈出第一步，他激动极了。

stereo.definition: 立体声（装置）；  adj.立体声的
stereo.definitionEn: using a sound system that has two separate speakers so that you hear different sounds from each; produced by a system of this type
stereo.sentence: You must listen to the song in stereo to really appreciate the music.
stereo.sentenceTrans: 你一定要用立体声设备听歌，这样才能真正地欣赏音乐。

stereotype.definition: 刻板印象；老套的模式，陈规
stereotype.definitionEn: a fixed idea or image that many people have of a particular type of person or thing, but which is often not true in reality
stereotype.sentence: There is a stereotype about successful business man: dark suit and fancy watch.
stereotype.sentenceTrans: 人们对于成功商人有种刻板印象：深色西装和昂贵的手表。
stereotype.mnemonic: stereo立体 + type模式 → stereotype陈规，老套

stick.definition: 粘贴；刺，戳，扎；  n.棍，棒，条
stick.definitionEn: to fix something to something else, usually with a sticky substance; to become fixed to something in this way
stick.sentence: The woman is sticking a paper-cut on the window.
stick.sentenceTrans: 这位女士正将一张剪纸贴在窗户上。

sticky.definitionEn: (of paper, labels, etc.) with glue on one side so that you can stick it to a surface; made of or covered in a substance that sticks to things that touch it
sticky.sentence: The glue on her hand is so sticky.
sticky.mnemonic: stick粘，粘 + y…的 → sticky粘性的

stiff.sentence: "My back is so stiff!" the athlete complained.
stiff.sentenceTrans: “我的背好酸痛啊！” 这位运动员抱怨道。

still.definition: 还，仍；(虽然…）还是；  adj.静止的
still.sentence: He has been exercising for 3 months, but he still weighs over 90 kilograms.
still.sentenceTrans: 他锻炼了三个月，但体重还是超过90公斤。

stimulate.definition: 刺激（身体部位等）；激励，鼓舞
stimulate.definitionEn: to make somebody interested and excited about something; to make something develop or become more active; to encourage something
stimulate.sentence: The onions stimulate my eyes to tear up.
stimulate.sentenceTrans: 洋葱刺激了我的眼睛使其流泪。

sting.definition: 叮；刺；  n.（因被刺而引起的）疼痛；刺
sting.definitionEn: (of an insect or plant) to touch your skin or make a very small hole in it so that you feel a sharp pain
sting.sentence: A bee stung me on the arm and it really hurt!
sting.sentenceTrans: 一只蜜蜂叮了我的胳膊一下，真疼！

stir.definitionEn: to mix something by making circular movements in it with a spoon or similar object
stir.sentence: The lady is stirring the coffee.
stir.sentenceTrans: 这位女士正在搅拌咖啡。

stock.definition: 股票；库存，存货清单；家畜；  v.储存；存货
stock.definitionEn: the value of the shares in a company that have been sold; a share that somebody has bought in a company or business
stock.sentence: Many types of stocks are displayed on the large screen.
stock.sentenceTrans: 大屏幕上显示着多种类型的股票。

stocking.definitionEn: either of a pair of thin pieces of clothing that fit closely over a woman’s legs and feet
stocking.sentence: Stockings can be a great way to keep warm.
stocking.sentenceTrans: 长筒袜可以起到很好的保暖作用。
stocking.mnemonic: stock树干，筒状物 + ing名词后缀 → stock腿 + ing名词后缀 → stocking长筒袜

stomach.definition: 胃，胃口；  v.吃得下；忍受
stomach.definitionEn: the organ inside the body where food goes when you swallow it; the front part of the body below the chest
stomach.sentence: We should eat healthy food if we want a strong stomach.
stomach.sentenceTrans: 想拥有强健的胃，我们就应该健康饮食。

stone.definitionEn: a hard substance that comes from the ground and is used for building, carving, etc.
stone.sentence: These stones come from a river and have been rounded by the water.
stone.sentenceTrans: 这些石头是从河里捞出来的，已经被流水打磨圆润了。

stop.definition: 停止；阻止；  n.停止；车站
stop.definitionEn: to not do something that you have been doing before; to not continue doing something
stop.sentence: The road worker held up his hand to stop the car.
stop.sentenceTrans: 修路工人举手让车停下来。

storage.definitionEn: the process of keeping something in a particular place until it is needed; the space where things can be kept; space where you put things when they are not being used
storage.sentence: The huge refrigerator has lots of storage space!
storage.sentenceTrans: 这台大冰箱有很多储存空间！
storage.mnemonic: stor=store保存 + age行为 → 贮存，保管

store.definition: 商店；仓库；储存品；  v.贮藏，储存，积蓄
store.definitionEn: a large shop that sells many different types of goods
store.sentence: I took my son to the grocery store to buy some food.
store.sentenceTrans: 我带着儿子去杂货店买了一些食物。

storey.definitionEn: a level of a building; a floor

storm.definitionEn: very bad weather with strong winds and rain, and often thunder and lightning

story.definitionEn: an account, often spoken, of what happened to somebody or of how something happened
story.sentence: She is reading a story to her kids.
story.sentenceTrans: 她正给自己的孩子们讲故事呢。

stove.definitionEn: a large piece of equipment for cooking food, containing an oven and gas or electric rings on top
