stove.sentence: Turn off the stove, or the food will be overcooked.
stove.sentenceTrans: 快把炉子关掉，不然食物要煮过头了。

straight.definition: 直的；坦诚的；  adv.直接地
straight.definitionEn: without a bend or curve; going in one direction only

strain.definition: 负担，压力；  v.拉紧，使......变紧张
strain.definitionEn: pressure on somebody/something because they have too much to do or manage, or something very difficult to deal with; the problems, worry or anxiety that this produces
strain.sentence: The long working hours were a strain on my neck.
strain.sentenceTrans: 长时间工作让我的脖子感到有压力。

strange.definitionEn: unusual or surprising, especially in a way that is difficult to understand
strange.sentence: The rock has a strange shape.

stranger.definitionEn: someone who you have not met before or do not know
stranger.sentence: Kids, be careful of strangers offering candy!
stranger.sentenceTrans: 小朋友，小心拿糖给你吃的陌生人！
stranger.mnemonic: strang陌生的 + er人 → stranger陌生人；新来者

strategic.definition: 战略（上）的，对全局有重要意义的，关键的
strategic.definitionEn: done as part of a plan that is meant to achieve a particular purpose or to gain an advantage; connected with getting an advantage in a war or other military situation
strategic.sentence: Shanghai is of strategic importance to the international trade of China.
strategic.sentenceTrans: 上海这座城市对中国的国际贸易具有重要的战略意义。
strategic.mnemonic: strateg战略 + ic形容词后缀 → strategic战略(上)的

strategy.definitionEn: a plan that is intended to achieve a particular purpose; the skill of planning the movements of armies in a battle or war; an example of doing this
strategy.sentence: I like strategy games that require deep thinking, like chess.
strategy.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢需要深思熟虑的策略性游戏，比如国际象棋。
strategy.mnemonic: strat军队 + egy名词后缀 → 军队需要战略 → strategy战略；策略

straw.definitionEn: a thin tube of plastic or paper that you suck a drink through
straw.sentence: Why do you need two straws for one drink?
straw.sentenceTrans: 你一杯饮料为什么要两根吸管？

stream.sentence: There is a small stream running through the forest.
stream.sentenceTrans: 有一条小溪从森林中流过。

street.definitionEn: a road in a city or town that has houses or other buildings on one or both sides
street.sentence: There are no people on the street at night.
street.sentenceTrans: 到了晚上，街上就空无一人。

strength.definition: 体力，力气，力量；长处；实力
strength.definitionEn: the quality or state of being physically strong
strength.sentence: The man is flipping a heavy tire to build his strength.
strength.sentenceTrans: 这名男子翻转沉重的轮胎来增强力量。
strength.mnemonic: streng=strong强壮的 + th抽象名词 → strength力量

strengthen.definitionEn: to become stronger; to make somebody/something stronger
strengthen.sentence: She keeps training every day to strengthen her arms.
strengthen.sentenceTrans: 她每天坚持锻炼来使手臂变强壮。
strengthen.mnemonic: strength力量 + en动词后缀  → strengthen加强

stress.definition: 压力；紧张；强调；重读，重音；  v.强调
stress.definitionEn: a state of mental tension and worry caused by problems in your life, work, etc.
stress.sentence: The business team is under great stress from work.
stress.sentenceTrans: 这个商务团队因工作压力很大。

stretch.definition: 伸展，延伸，张开；  n.伸展，张开
stretch.definitionEn: to make something longer, wider or looser, for example by pulling it; to become longer, etc. in this; (of cloth) to become bigger or longer when you pull it and return to its original shape when you stop; to put your arms or legs out straight and contract your muscles; to put out an arm or a leg in order to reach something;
stretch.sentence: He stretches his arm out while singing.
stretch.sentenceTrans: 他一边唱歌一边把手臂伸展开。
stretch.mnemonic: stre=str扭转，拉紧 + tch动词后缀 → 向不同方向发力 → stretch伸展，张开

strict.definition: 严厉的；（条例、法规等）严格的
strict.definitionEn: demanding that rules, especially rules about behaviour, should be obeyed
strict.sentence: The teacher is strict during the exam.

strike.definition: 击打；袭击；罢工；  n.罢工；打击；袭击
strike.definitionEn: to hit somebody/something hard or with force; to hit somebody/something with your hand or a weapon
strike.sentence: Strike the ball flat and hard to knock it out of the stadium.
strike.sentenceTrans: 用力朝水平方向击球，就能把球打出场外。

striking.definition: 吸引人的，容貌出众的；显著的，突出的
striking.definitionEn: interesting and unusual enough to attract attention
striking.sentence: The most striking feature of this cat is its long snow-white hair.
striking.sentenceTrans: 这只猫最吸引人的是它雪白的长毛。
striking.mnemonic: strik=strike攻击 + ing形容词后缀 → 攻击 → striking惹人注目的

string.definitionEn: a tightly stretched piece of wire, nylon, or catgut on a musical instrument, that produces a musical note when the instrument is played

strip.definitionEn: to take off all or most of your clothes or another person’s clothes
strip.sentence: Please strip off your clothes for the medical exam.
strip.sentenceTrans: 请脱掉你的衣服配合体检。

stripe.definitionEn: a long narrow line of colour, that is a different colour from the areas next to it
stripe.sentence: The zebra has black and white stripes on its body.
stripe.sentenceTrans: 斑马身上有黑白相间的条纹。

strive.definitionEn: to try very hard to achieve something
strive.sentence: They will strive for what they want.
strive.sentenceTrans: 他们会为自己想要的东西而奋斗。

stroke.definition: 击打；中风；  v.击打；轻抚
stroke.definitionEn: to move your hand gently and slowly over a surface, somebody’s hair or an animal’s fur or hair, etc.
stroke.sentence: He hit the ball cleanly with a beautiful stroke.
stroke.sentenceTrans: 他利落地击球，打出漂亮的一击。

strong.definitionEn: (of people, animals, etc.) having a lot of physical power so that you can lift heavy weights, do hard physical work, etc.
strong.sentence: The strong man has a muscular body.
strong.sentenceTrans: 这个强壮的男人有着一身健壮的肌肉。

structure.definition: 建筑物；结构；  v.精心组织；系统安排
structure.definitionEn: something (such as a house, tower, bridge, etc.) that is built by putting parts together and that usually stands on its own
structure.sentence: There are so many new structures going up.
structure.sentenceTrans: 许多新的建筑正在兴建。
structure.mnemonic: struct建立 + ure表名词 → structure构造；结构

struggle.definition: 奋斗，拼搏；挣扎；  n.奋斗；斗争
struggle.definitionEn: something that is difficult for you to do or achieve
struggle.sentence: She's struggling to reach the top of the cliff.
struggle.sentenceTrans: 她为了自己登顶的目标而奋斗。

stubborn.definition: 顽固的；倔强的；难对付的
stubborn.definitionEn: determined not to change your opinion or attitude
stubborn.sentence: The stubborn man covered his ears and refused to listen.
stubborn.sentenceTrans: 这个顽固的男人捂着耳朵拒绝听人讲话。
stubborn.mnemonic: stub树桩、树墩 + orn形容词后缀 → stubborn顽固的，执拗的

student.definitionEn: a person who is studying at a school, especially a secondary school

studio.definition: 摄影棚；录音室，录像室；工作室
studio.definitionEn: a place where films/movies are made or produced
studio.sentence: In the studio, the model and the photographer are working.
studio.sentenceTrans: 摄影棚里模特和摄影师正在工作。
studio.mnemonic: studi=study学习 + o表名词，物 → 工作室

study.definition: 学习；研究；  n.学习；研究；书房
study.definitionEn: to spend time learning about a subject by reading, going to college, etc.
study.sentence: Sorry I can't go out with you, I have to study for the exam.
study.sentenceTrans: 抱歉我不能跟你出去玩，我还要准备考试呢。

stuff.definition: 东西；原料；  v.把……塞进；装满
stuff.definitionEn: used to refer to a substance, material, group of objects, etc. when you do not know the name, when the name is not important or when it is obvious what you are talking about
stuff.sentence: We keep all of the baby's stuff in his bedroom.
stuff.sentenceTrans: 我们把婴儿的所有东西都放在他的卧室里。

stupid.definitionEn: not intelligent: having or showing a lack of ability to learn and understand things
stupid.sentence: The donkey made a stupid mistake.
stupid.sentenceTrans: 这头驴犯了一个愚蠢的错误。
stupid.mnemonic: stup笨，麻木 ＋ id形容词，“如…的” → stupid笨的

style.definitionEn: a particular design of something, especially clothes; the quality of being fashionable in the clothes that you wear
style.sentence: She dresses in a cozy and sunny style.
style.sentenceTrans: 她的穿衣风格休闲又阳光。

stylish.sentence: Even a dog can be very stylish.
stylish.mnemonic: styl=style风格 + ish形容词后缀 → 有风格的 → stylish流行的

subject.definition: 学科，科目；实验对象；主题；话题，主题
subject.definitionEn: an area of knowledge that is studied in school; a thing or person that is being discussed, described or dealt with
subject.sentence: English was my favorite subject in school.
subject.sentenceTrans: 英语是我上学时最喜欢的科目。
subject.mnemonic: sub在…下面 + ject投掷，扔 → 扔下去 → 服从的，扔下去让大家讨论的主题 → subject主题

submarine.definition: 潜水艇；  adj.水底的，海底的
submarine.definitionEn: a ship that can travel underwater
submarine.sentenceTrans: 潜水艇可以在水下航行。
submarine.mnemonic: sub在下面 + marine海洋的 → 在海下面 → submarine海底的；潜水艇

submerge.definitionEn: to go under the surface of water or liquid; to put something or make something go under the surface of water or liquid
submerge.sentence: The car was almost submerged by the floodwater!
submerge.sentenceTrans: 汽车就快被洪水淹没了！
submerge.mnemonic: sub在下面 + merge沉 → submerge淹没

submission.definitionEn: the act of accepting that somebody has defeated you and that you must obey them
submission.sentence: The knight kneeled and handed over his sword to show his submission.
submission.sentenceTrans: 这位骑士单膝跪地并交出自己的宝剑以示屈服。
submission.mnemonic: sub下面 + miss送，放出 + ion名词后缀 → 放在下面 → submission屈服

submit.definitionEn: to give a document, proposal, etc. to somebody in authority so that they can study or consider it
submit.sentence: The man is submitting the report to his boss.
submit.sentenceTrans: 这个男人正在把报告递交给他的老板。
submit.mnemonic: sub下面 + mit放出，发送 → 从下面送出 → submit提交、呈递

subsequent.definitionEn: happening or coming after something else
subsequent.sentence: The giant wave was responsible for the subsequent sinking of the ship.
subsequent.sentenceTrans: 巨浪是船随后沉没的主要原因。
subsequent.mnemonic: sub在后面 + sequ跟随 + ent形容词后缀 → subsequent随后的

subsidy.definitionEn: money that is paid by a government or an organization to reduce the costs of services or of producing goods so that their prices can be kept low
subsidy.sentence: The government provided a subsidy for the entrepreneurs.
subsidy.sentenceTrans: 政府为创业者提供了补贴。
subsidy.mnemonic: subsid减弱 + y名词后缀 → 拨款以减低公共事业消费 → subsidy补贴

substance.definitionEn: a type of solid, liquid or gas that has particular qualities
substance.sentence: Substances like water have three different forms.
substance.sentenceTrans: 像水这样的物质们有三种不同的形态。
substance.mnemonic: sub下面 + st站立 + ance表名词 → 站在下面的东西 → substance物质；本质

substantial.sentence: The store provided substantial discounts on all clothes.
substantial.sentenceTrans: 这家店给所有衣服都打了大幅度的折扣。
substantial.mnemonic: sub下面 + stan站立 + tial形容词后缀 → 作为基本存在的 → substantial重大的，大量的

substitute.definition: 代替；  n.替代物；替代者
substitute.definitionEn: to take the place of somebody/something else; to use somebody/something instead of somebody/something else
substitute.sentence: You should substitute fruits for sweets.
substitute.sentenceTrans: 你应该用水果代替甜食。
substitute.mnemonic: sub在下面，副手，次一等 + stitute创建，建立 → 建在下面 → substitute代替，候补

subtle.sentence: There is a subtle change in his weight.
subtle.sentenceTrans: 他的体重有细微的变化。
subtle.mnemonic: sub在...下面 + tle网 → subtle不明显的

subtract.definitionEn: to take a number or an amount away from another number or amount
subtract.sentence: If you subtract 3 from 5, you get 2.
subtract.mnemonic: sub在下面 + tract抽 → 抽去 → 减去，去掉

suburb.definitionEn: an area where people live that is outside the centre of a city
suburb.sentence: In the suburbs, there are fewer houses and more trees.
suburb.mnemonic: sub在下面，次一等 + urb城市 → suburb郊区，郊外

subway.definitionEn: an underground railway/railroad system in a city; a path that goes under a road, etc. which people can use to cross to the other side
subway.sentence: He takes the subway to work every day.
subway.mnemonic: sub在下 + way道路 → subway地下通道，地铁

succeed.definitionEn: to achieve something that you have been trying to do or get; to have the result or effect that was intended; to be successful in your job, earning money, power, respect, etc.
succeed.sentence: I succeeded in shooting three arrows in the center of the target.
succeed.sentenceTrans: 我成功地将三支箭射中了靶心。
succeed.mnemonic: suc在…下面 + ceed走 → 从下走到上面 → succeed成功

success.definitionEn: the fact that you have achieved something that you want and have been trying to do or get; the fact of becoming rich or famous or of getting a high social position
success.sentence: The success of reaching the top of the mountain brought him great joy.
success.sentenceTrans: 成功登上山顶让他无比喜悦。
success.mnemonic: suc在……下面 + cess行走 → 在后面跟着前人走 → success成功；胜利

successful.sentence: He was a successful businessman and brought great changes to our phones.
successful.sentenceTrans: 他是一位成功的商人，给我们的手机带来了极大的变化。
successful.mnemonic: suc在下面 + cess行走，前进 + ful…的 → success成功 + ful…的 → successful成功的，有成就的

succession.definition: 一连串；连续，继续；继承权
succession.definitionEn: a number of people or things that follow each other in time or order
succession.sentence: A succession of horses passed us in the forest.
succession.sentenceTrans: 森林中，一匹匹马从我们身边经过。
succession.mnemonic: suc紧接着 + cess前进 + ion名词后缀 → succession接连，一系列

successive.definitionEn: following immediately one after the other
successive.sentence: Dominoes fall down in a successive way.
successive.sentenceTrans: 多米诺骨牌接二连三地倒下了。
successive.mnemonic: suc在…下面 + cess行走 + ive形容词后缀 → 接着后面走的 → 连续的

suck.definitionEn: to take liquid, air, etc. into your mouth by using the muscles of your lips; to keep something in your mouth and pull on it with your lips and tongue; to take liquid, air, etc. out of something
suck.sentence: The newborn began to suck milk from the bottle immediately.
suck.sentenceTrans: 新生儿立刻开始用奶瓶吸吮牛奶。

sudden.definitionEn: happening or done quickly and unexpectedly
sudden.sentence: The boy was scared by the sudden burst of the balloon.
sudden.sentenceTrans: 气球突然爆了，吓了男孩一跳。
sudden.mnemonic: sud达到 + den去 → 突然到来的事情 → sudden立即，突然

suddenly.sentence: Suddenly, my friend surprised me from behind.
suddenly.sentenceTrans: 我的朋友突然从后面给我来了个惊喜。
suddenly.mnemonic: sudden突然的 ＋ ly...地 → suddenly突然地

suffer.definitionEn: to be badly affected by a disease, pain, sadness, a lack of something, etc.; to experience something unpleasant, such as injury, defeat or loss;  to become worse
suffer.sentence: He suffers from a bad toothache.
suffer.mnemonic: suf在下 + fer负重 → suffer承受

suffering.sentence: My father’s suffering is getting serious.
suffering.sentenceTrans: 爸爸的痛苦越来越严重。
suffering.mnemonic: suf在下面 + fer带 + ing表名词 → suffer带到下面去受苦 + ing表名词 → suffering受难

sufficient.definitionEn: enough for a particular purpose; as much as you need
sufficient.sentence: The animal has sufficient food for the winter.
sufficient.sentenceTrans: 这只动物有充足的食物来过冬。
sufficient.mnemonic: suffic足以 + ient形容词后缀 → sufficient 足够的

sugar.definitionEn: a sweet substance usually in the form of white or brown crystals or white powder that comes from plants and is used to make foods sweeter
sugar.sentence: I'd like a spoonful of sugar in my coffee.
sugar.sentenceTrans: 我想在我的咖啡里放一勺糖。

suggest.definition: 建议，提议；使人想起；暗示
suggest.definitionEn: to put forward an idea or a plan for other people to think about
suggest.sentence: You look terrible! I suggest you go to see a doctor.
suggest.sentenceTrans: 你看起来糟透了！我建议你去看医生。
suggest.mnemonic: sug在下面 + gest带来，产生 → 从下面带上来 → suggest建议

suggestion.definitionEn: an idea or a plan that you mention for somebody else to think about
suggestion.sentence: The shopping guide gives her some suggestions about the skirt.
suggestion.sentenceTrans: 导购给了她一些选裙子的建议。
suggestion.mnemonic: sug=sub在下面 + gest带来，产生 + ion表名词 → 从下面产生的建议 → suggestion建议，意见

suit.definition: 西服，套装；服装；诉讼；  v.适合；相配
suit.definitionEn: a set of clothes made of the same cloth, including a jacket and trousers/pants or a skirt
suit.sentence: The businessman is wearing a gray suit.
suit.sentenceTrans: 这位商人穿着一套灰色的西装。

suitable.definitionEn: right or appropriate for a particular purpose or occasion
suitable.sentence: That's a suitable dress for the party.
suitable.sentenceTrans: 那件裙子适合参加派对。
suitable.mnemonic: suit适合 + able……的 → suitable合适的，适宜的

suite.definitionEn: a set of rooms, especially in a hotel
suite.sentence: This suite is big enough for a whole family to live in.
suite.sentenceTrans: 这间套房足够一家人住了。

sum.definition: 全部，总和；算术；  v.概括
sum.sentence: The sum of one and one is two.

summarise.definitionEn: to give a summary of something (= a statement of the main points)
summarise.sentence: I think the speaker summarised the theory quite nicely.
summarise.sentenceTrans: 我认为发言人很好的概括了这个原理。

summarize.definitionEn: to give a summary of something (= a statement of the main points)
summarize.sentence: I don’t want to read the whole thing. Could you just summarize the book for me?
summarize.sentenceTrans: 我不想再看这个东西了，你能就帮我概括一下这本书吗？
summarize.mnemonic: summar总，加 + ize动词后缀 → summarize概括

summary.definitionEn: a short statement that gives only the main points of something, not the details
summary.sentence: I made a summary of this article.
summary.sentenceTrans: 我对这篇文章做了一下总结。
summary.mnemonic: summ总数 + ary表名词 → 内容总和 → summary摘要

summer.definitionEn: the warmest season of the year that is after spring and before autumn
summer.sentence: It's fun to relax at the beach in the summer.
summer.sentenceTrans: 夏天在沙滩上放松很有趣。

summit.definition: 山顶，顶点；  adj.最高级的；政府首脑的
summit.definitionEn: the highest point of something, especially the top of a mountain
summit.sentence: He eventually climbed to the summit of the mountain.

sun.definitionEn: the star that shines in the sky during the day and gives the earth heat and light

sunday.definitionEn: the day of the week after Saturday and before Monday, thought of as either the first or the last day of the week
sunday.sentence: We don't have to go to school on Sunday. Let's play!
sunday.sentenceTrans: 周日不上学，咱们去玩儿吧！

sunlight.sentence: The sunlight brightens the green field.
sunlight.mnemonic: sun太阳 + light光亮 → sunlight日光

sunny.definition: 阳光充足的，阳光明媚的
sunny.definitionEn: with a lot of bright light from the sun
sunny.sentence: The blue sky means that today is a sunny day.
sunny.sentenceTrans: 蓝蓝的天空表明今天是个晴天。
sunny.mnemonic: sun太阳 + n + y形容词后缀 → sunny晴朗的

sunrise.definitionEn: the time when the sun first appears in the sky in the morning
sunrise.sentence: I got up early today and saw a beautiful sunrise.
sunrise.sentenceTrans: 我今天早起看了美丽的日出。
sunrise.mnemonic: sun太阳 + rise升起 → 太阳升起来 → sunrise日出

sunset.definitionEn: the time when the sun goes below the horizon in the evening
sunset.sentence: The sunset on the river looks amazing tonight.
sunset.sentenceTrans: 今天傍晚，河上的日落美不胜收。
sunset.mnemonic: sun太阳 + set落 → sunset 日落

sunshine.definitionEn: the sun's light or rays; warmth and light from the sun
sunshine.sentence: The sunshine broke through the clouds.
sunshine.mnemonic: sun太阳 + shine光亮 → sunshine日光，日照

super.sentence: Superman has all kinds of super powers, like flying and super strength!
super.sentenceTrans: 超人有各种各样的超能力，比如飞行和超级力量。

superficial.definitionEn: not studying or looking at something thoroughly; seeing only what is obvious
superficial.sentence: The house may look new, but it's all superficial.
superficial.sentenceTrans: 这栋房子看起来很新，但这只是表面现象。
superficial.mnemonic: super在…上面 + fic做 + ial形容词后缀 → 在表面上做 → 肤浅

superior.definition: 上级；  adj.（级别/重要性）更高的；更好的
superior.definitionEn: a person of higher rank, status or position; used in titles for the head of a religious community
superior.sentence: The people on the left have to listen to their superior.
superior.sentenceTrans: 左边的人得听从他们的上司。
superior.mnemonic: super在上面 + ior表形容词，较…的 → superior在上面的，超越的

supermarket.definitionEn: a large shop/store that sells food, drinks and goods used in the home, where people choose what they want from the shelves and pay for it as they leave
supermarket.sentence: You can buy a lot of things in the supermarket.
supermarket.sentenceTrans: 你可以在超市买到很多东西。
supermarket.mnemonic: super超级 + market市场 → supermarket超市

supervise.definitionEn: to be in charge of somebody/something and make sure that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.
supervise.sentence: It is absurd to supervise the students studying in the classroom like this.
supervise.sentenceTrans: 像这样监督教室里学习的学生是荒唐可笑的。
supervise.mnemonic: super在…上面 + vise看 → 在上面看 → 临视 → supervise监督

supervision.definitionEn: the work or activity involved in being in charge of somebody/something and making sure that everything is done correctly, safely, etc.; a meeting between a student and their tutor or supervisor that involves teaching and discussion of the student's work
supervision.sentence: The young staff member worked hard under the supervision of his boss.
supervision.sentenceTrans: 这位年轻的职员在老板的监督下努力工作。
supervision.mnemonic: supervis监督 + ion名词后缀 → supervision监督

supper.definitionEn: the last meal of the day, either a main meal, usually smaller and less formal than dinner, or a snack eaten before you go to bed

supplement.definition: 增补，补充物，保健品；附录，增刊；  v.补充（读作/ˈsʌpləˌmɛnt/）
supplement.definitionEn: a thing that is added to something else to improve or complete it; a pill that you take or a special kind of food that you eat in order to improve your health; a book or a section at the end of a book that gives extra information or deals with a special subject
supplement.sentence: You should take these herbal supplements once a day.
supplement.sentenceTrans: 你应该一天服用一次这些草本保健品。
supplement.mnemonic: sup在下面，次要 + ple满，填满 + ment名词后缀 → 增加次要的心填满 → 增补

supply.definition: 供应，供应量；供给；  v.供给
supply.definitionEn: an amount of something that is provided or available to be used
supply.sentence: The farmer has an adequate supply of milk.
supply.sentenceTrans: 农场主有充足的牛奶供应。
supply.mnemonic: sup在下面 + ply填充，充满 → 填充下去 → 供应[下去]，补给

support.definition: 支援；支撑；  n.支持；支撑物
support.definitionEn: encouragement and help that you give to somebody/something because you approve of them and want them to be successful
support.sentence: Doctors and resources are being sent from other areas to support this province.
support.sentenceTrans: 其他地区派遣医生、运送物资来支援这个省。
support.mnemonic: sup在…下面 + port带 → 带来支持 → support支持

suppose.definitionEn: to think or believe that something is true or possible (based on the knowledge that you have)
suppose.sentence: I suppose that I can be back before nine o'clock.
suppose.mnemonic: sup在……下面 + pose放 → 放下去想 → suppose猜想，推测

supreme.definitionEn: very great or the greatest in degree
supreme.sentence: The king is the supreme leader of the country.
supreme.sentenceTrans: 国王是国家里至高无上的领导者。

sure.definition: （表示同意）当然，确实地，无疑地；  adj.肯定的；确信的
sure.definitionEn: used to say ‘yes’ to somebody; used to emphasize something that you are saying
sure.sentence: I am sure that the tortoise can win because the rabbit is still asleep.
sure.sentenceTrans: 我确信乌龟可以赢得这场比赛，因为兔子还在睡觉呢。

surface.definitionEn: the top layer of an area of water or land
surface.sentence: There is some oil on the surface of the soup.
surface.mnemonic: sur超过，在上面 + face脸面 → surface表面

surgeon.definitionEn: a doctor who is trained to perform surgery (= medical operations that involve cutting open a person’s body)
surgeon.sentence: My surgeon decided to give me an operation.
surgeon.sentenceTrans: 我的外科医生决定给我动手术。
surgeon.mnemonic: sur手 + geon工作，去做 → surgeon外科医生

surgery.definitionEn: medical treatment of injuries or diseases that involves cutting open a person’s body and often removing or replacing some parts; the branch of medicine connected with this treatment
surgery.sentence: They are performing surgery on a patient now.
surgery.sentenceTrans: 他们正在给一位病人做外科手术。
surgery.mnemonic: surger=surgeon外科医生 + y名词后缀 → surgery外科，外科手术

surpass.definitionEn: to do or be better than somebody/something
surpass.sentence: The turtle surpassed the rabbit in the running race.
surpass.sentenceTrans: 乌龟在跑步比赛中超过了兔子。
surpass.mnemonic: sur超过，在上面 + pass通过 → 在上面通过 → surpass超过

surprise.definition: 使惊奇，使诧异，使感到意外
surprise.definitionEn: an event, a piece of news, etc. that is unexpected or that happens suddenly
surprise.sentence: She was extremely surprised at the size of the woman's muscles.
surprise.sentenceTrans: 麦克斯看到那个女人的肌肉，整个人都方（huang）了！
surprise.mnemonic: sur突然 + prise拿住，抓住 → 突然被抓住 → surprise吃惊

surrender.definitionEn: to admit that you have been defeated and want to stop fighting; to allow yourself to be caught, taken prisoner, etc.
surrender.sentence: Surrender your worries and embrace the joy of the present.
surrender.sentenceTrans: 放下焦虑，拥抱当下的美好。
surrender.mnemonic: sur下面 + render给予 → 给到下面 → [把枪]放下 → surrender投降

surround.sentenceTrans: 高大的树木环绕着湖泊。
surround.mnemonic: sur在···上 + round圆的 → surround围绕

surroundings.definitionEn: everything that is around or near somebody/something
surroundings.sentence: The village's surroundings are mostly forests and green lands.
surroundings.sentenceTrans: 村庄的周围主要是森林和绿地。
surroundings.mnemonic: sur随后 + round圆圈 + ings表名词 → surroundings周围的事物，环境

survey.definition: 调查；  v.鉴定；测量，勘测
survey.definitionEn: an investigation of the opinions, behaviour, etc. of a particular group of people, which is usually done by asking them questions
survey.sentence: The old lady is taking a survey.
survey.sentenceTrans: 这位年老的女士正在做调查。
survey.mnemonic: sur在上面 + vey看 → 从上面看 → survey调查

survival.definitionEn: the state of continuing to live or exist, often despite difficulty or danger
survival.sentence: She taught me survival skills in the wild, like how to start a fire in the forest.
survival.sentenceTrans: 她教了我野外求生的技能，比如如何在森林里生火。
survival.mnemonic: survive幸存 + al名词后缀 → survival生存，存活

survive.definition: 幸存，存活；存活；  v.生存，活着
survive.definitionEn: to continue to live or exist
survive.sentenceTrans: 这个女孩在海难中幸存了下来。

survivor.definitionEn: a person who continues to live after an accident, illness, war, etc.
survivor.sentence: Most of the survivors of the Titanic disaster were women and children.
survivor.sentenceTrans: 泰坦尼克号沉没事件中的大多数幸存者是女性和儿童。
survivor.mnemonic: surviv=survive幸存，生还 + or 名词后缀,表示人 → 生还者, 残存

suspect.definition: 犯罪嫌疑人，可疑分子；  v.怀疑，猜疑；  adj.可疑的
suspect.definitionEn: a person who is suspected of a crime or of having done something wrong
suspect.sentence: The suspect is talking with his lawyer.
suspect.sentenceTrans: 犯罪嫌疑人正在和他的律师谈话。
suspect.mnemonic: sus在…下面 + pect看 → (偷偷地)在下面看 → suspect怀疑；嫌疑犯，可疑分子

suspend.definitionEn: to hang something so that it is free on all sides except at the point of support
suspend.sentence: These lights are suspended on the ceiling.
suspend.sentenceTrans: 这些灯被吊在天花板上。
suspend.mnemonic: sus在…下 + pend挂 → 挂在下面 → suspend吊，悬挂

suspicion.definitionEn: a feeling that somebody has done something wrong, illegal or dishonest, even though you have no proof; the feeling that you cannot trust somebody/something
suspicion.sentence: The two men raised the suspicion of the policeman.
suspicion.sentenceTrans: 这两个人引起了警察的怀疑。
suspicion.mnemonic: su=sus下面 + spic环顾，检查 + ion表名词 → 在下面看 → 怀疑

suspicious.definitionEn: feeling that somebody has done something wrong, illegal or dishonest, without having any proof; making you feel that something is wrong, illegal or dishonest
suspicious.sentence: The policeman found the man's behavior suspicious.
suspicious.sentenceTrans: 警察发现这个人的行为很可疑。
suspicious.mnemonic: suspici怀疑 + ous形容词后缀 → suspicious猜疑的

sustain.definition: 支撑，承受；维持（生命）；使保持
sustain.definitionEn: to support a weight without breaking or falling
sustain.sentence: Get up! The chair can't sustain your weight anymore!
sustain.sentenceTrans: 快起来！这把椅子快承受不住你的重量了！
sustain.mnemonic: sus在…下面 + tain握住 → 在下面握住 → 支撑，承受

sustainable.definitionEn: involving the use of natural products and energy in a way that does not harm the environment; that can continue or be continued for a long time
sustainable.sentence: We promote sustainable jewelry practices, using recycled materials.
sustainable.sentenceTrans: 我们倡导可持续的珠宝制作实践，使用回收材料。
sustainable.mnemonic: sustain支持 + able可…的 → sustainable可以忍受的；足可支撑的

swallow.definition: 吞下；相信；  n.吞咽；燕子
swallow.definitionEn: to make food, drink, etc. go down your throat into your stomach
swallow.sentence: She always lifts her head when swallowing pills.
swallow.sentenceTrans: 她总是会在吞药片的时候抬起头。

swear.definition: 发誓，郑重地说，保证；咒骂
swear.definitionEn: to make a serious promise to do something; to promise that you are telling the truth; to make a public or official promise, especially in court; to make somebody promise not to tell something to anyone
swear.sentence: I swear I'm telling the truth.

sweat.definitionEn: when you sweat, drops of liquid appear on the surface of your skin, for example when you are hot, ill/sick or afraid
sweat.sentence: I sweat a lot whenever I get to work.
sweat.sentenceTrans: 每次去上班，我都会出很多汗。

sweater.definition: 毛衣，厚运动衫，羊毛衫，针织套衫
sweater.definitionEn: a knitted piece of clothing made of wool or cotton for the upper part of the body, with long sleeves. In British English the word is used to describe a piece of clothing with no buttons. In American English a sweater can have buttons and be like a jacket.
sweater.sentence: She likes this red sweater. It can keep her warm.
sweater.sentenceTrans: 她喜欢这件红色毛衣。它能帮她保暖。
sweater.mnemonic: sweat汗 + er表物 → 穿着会出汗的 → sweater厚运动衫

sweep.definition: 扫，打扫，清扫；席卷，迅速传播；  n.清扫；打扫范围
sweep.definitionEn: to clean a room, surface, etc. using a broom (= a type of brush on a long handle); to remove something from a surface using a brush, your hand, etc.
sweep.sentence: The floor is so dirty! I need to sweep it.
sweep.sentenceTrans: 地板太脏了！我需要扫扫。

sweet.definitionEn: containing, or tasting as if it contains, a lot of sugar; having a pleasant smell; having a pleasant sound; (especially of children or small things) attractive; having or showing a kind character
sweet.sentence: I'm savouring a sweet and fruity cocktail.
sweet.sentenceTrans: 我正在品尝一款甜而果味浓郁的鸡尾酒。

swift.definition: 迅速的，敏捷的，立刻的；敏捷的；  n.雨燕
swift.definitionEn: happening or done quickly and immediately; doing something quickly
swift.sentence: The cheetah is the swiftest land animal.
swift.sentenceTrans: 猎豹是跑得最快的陆地动物。

swim.definitionEn: (of a person) to move through water in a horizontal position using the arms and legs
swim.sentence: Two girls swam in the pool.
swim.sentenceTrans: 小丸子和小玉在游泳池里面游了泳。

swing.definition: 摇荡，摆动；使摇摆，使转动，使转向；  n.秋千
swing.definitionEn: to move backwards or forwards or from side to side while hanging from a fixed point; to make something do this
swing.sentence: He swings in the forest from tree to tree.
swing.sentenceTrans: 他在丛林的树间荡来荡去。

switch.definitionEn: a small device that you press or move up and down in order to turn a light or piece of electrical equipment on and off
switch.sentence: There are so many switches in your home! Which one turns on the lights?
switch.sentenceTrans: 你家有这么多开关，哪一个能把灯打开？

sword.definitionEn: a weapon with a long metal blade and a handle
sword.sentence: He is holding his wooden sword to the air.

symbol.definitionEn: a person, an object, an event, etc. that represents a more general quality or situation
symbol.sentence: Doves are the symbol of peace.
symbol.mnemonic: sym共同，相同 + bol抛 → 共同抛出的标志 → 象征

symbolic.definitionEn: relating to or being used as a symbol
symbolic.sentence: The red cross is symbolic of medical care.
symbolic.sentenceTrans: 红十字标志象征着医疗援救。
symbolic.mnemonic: symbol标志 + ic形容词后缀 → symbolic 象征的

symbolise.definitionEn: represent or identify by using a symbol; use symbols
symbolise.sentence: This gesture symbolises that you did a good job.
symbolise.sentenceTrans: 该手势象征着你干的不错。

symbolize.sentence: These three icons symbolize unhappiness for most young people.
symbolize.sentenceTrans: 这三个图标对大多数年轻人来说象征着不快乐。
symbolize.mnemonic: symbol符合 ＋ ize动词后缀 → 共同抛出标志 → symbolize用符号表示；象征

sympathise.definitionEn: to feel sorry for somebody; to show that you understand and feel sorry about somebody’s problems
sympathise.sentence: I really sympathised with him who was depressed for failing the exam.
sympathise.sentenceTrans: 他考试不及格心情十分沮丧，我十分感同身受。

sympathize.definitionEn: to feel sorry for somebody; to show that you understand and feel sorry about somebody’s problems
sympathize.sentence: I sympathize with him, patting him on the shoulder.
sympathize.sentenceTrans: 我很同情他，拍了拍他的肩膀。
sympathize.mnemonic: sym共同 + path感情 + ize动词后缀 → sympathize情感共鸣

sympathy.definitionEn: the feeling that you care about and are sorry about someone else's trouble, grief, misfortune, etc.
sympathy.sentence: He felt a lot of sympathy for the dog and gave it a bone.
sympathy.sentenceTrans: 他很同情那条狗并给了它一根骨头。
sympathy.mnemonic: sym共同 + pathy感情 → sympathy同情

symptom.definitionEn: a change in your body or mind that shows that you are not healthy
symptom.sentence: Flu symptoms include a headache, a sore throat, and a fever.
symptom.sentenceTrans: 流感的症状包括头痛、嗓子痛和发烧。
symptom.mnemonic: sym一起 + ptom落下 → symptom症状

synthetic.definitionEn: artificial; made by combining chemical substances rather than being produced naturally by plants or animals
synthetic.sentence: This sweater is made of synthetic fibers.
synthetic.sentenceTrans: 这件毛衣是由合成纤维制成的。
synthetic.mnemonic: syn共同 + the=thesis放置 + tic形容词后缀 → 放一起 → synthetic合成的

system.definitionEn: an organized set of ideas or theories or a particular way of doing something
system.sentence: There are eight planets in our solar system.
system.sentenceTrans: 我们的太阳系中有八大行星。
system.mnemonic: sy一起 + stem使立住 → system系统

systematic.definition: 系统的，有条理的；成体系的
systematic.definitionEn: done according to a system or plan, in a thorough, efficient or determined way
systematic.sentence: The building has a very systematic design, with every part repeated.
systematic.sentenceTrans: 这个建筑有系统化的设计，每个部分都有重复。
systematic.mnemonic: system系统 + atic…的 → 有系统的

table.definition: 桌子，台子；表格；  v.搁置
table.definitionEn: a piece of furniture that consists of a flat top supported by legs
table.sentence: The meeting room had a large table big enough for fifteen people to sit around.
table.sentenceTrans: 这间会议室有一个大桌子，足够坐下十五个人。

tablet.definitionEn: a flat piece of stone that has words written on it, especially one that has been fixed to a wall in memory of an important person or event
tablet.sentence: I take a tablet when I have a headache.
tablet.sentenceTrans: 我一头痛就会吃一片药。

tackle.definition: 对付，处理，解决（难题）；（足球等比赛中）阻截；  n.阻截，阻截队员
tackle.definitionEn: to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem or situation
tackle.sentence: The firefighters are tackling the blaze.
tackle.sentenceTrans: 消防队员们正在努力扑灭大火。

tag.definitionEn: a small piece of cloth, paper, metal, etc., that is attached to something and that has information written on it
tag.sentence: I always look for a sale tag to get a lower price.
tag.sentenceTrans: 我总是在寻找降价标签以得到更低的价格。

tail.definitionEn: the part that sticks out and can be moved at the back of the body of a bird, an animal or a fish
tail.sentence: The horse's long tail lifted up into the air as it ran.
tail.sentenceTrans: 马的长尾巴随着其奔跑的步伐甩向空中。

tailor.definition: 裁缝；  v.调整……使适应；定做
tailor.definitionEn: a person whose job is to make men’s clothes, especially somebody who makes suits, etc. for individual customers
tailor.sentence: The tailor measured him for a new suit.
tailor.sentenceTrans: 裁缝为他量身定做了一套新西装。
tailor.mnemonic: tail剪，割 + or表名词 → tailor裁缝

take.definition: 带；接受；花费（时间），占用……时间
take.definitionEn: to carry or move something from one place to another

tale.definitionEn: a story about imaginary events :an exciting or dramatic story
tale.sentence: He stayed up late at night just to finish reading the tale.
tale.sentenceTrans: 他晚上熬夜，就是为了能看完这个故事。

talent.definitionEn: a special ability that allows someone to do something well;  people or a person with a natural ability to do something well
talent.sentence: This baby showed great talent as he was playing the piano.
talent.sentenceTrans: 这个宝宝弹钢琴的时候展现出超强的天赋。

talk.definitionEn: to say things; to speak in order to give information or to express feelings, ideas, etc.
talk.sentence: They are talking to each other to share ideas.
talk.sentenceTrans: 他们正在聊天以分享想法。

tall.definitionEn: (of a person, building, tree, etc.) having a greater than average height
tall.sentence: How did you grow so tall?
tall.sentenceTrans: 你是怎么长到这么高的？

tame.definition: 驯服的，温顺的；  v.驯服
tame.definitionEn: (of animals, birds, etc.) not afraid of people, and used to living with them
tame.sentence: Don't worry, this lion is tame—it won't hurt you.
tame.sentenceTrans: 别担心，这只狮子很温驯，它不会伤害你的。

tank.definition: 大容器，大罐；坦克；水槽，池塘
tank.definitionEn: a container for holding a liquid or gas; the contents of a tank or the amount it will hold
tank.sentence: The man is checking the large yellow tank.
tank.sentenceTrans: 这个人正在检查这个黄色的大罐子。

tap.definition: 水龙头；轻敲；  v.监听，窃听 (电话)；轻叩，轻敲；刷（卡）
tap.definitionEn: a device for controlling the flow of water from a pipe into a bath/ bathtub or sink; a device for controlling the flow of liquid or gas from a pipe or container

tape.definition: 磁带；胶带，胶条；带子；  v.录音；用胶带粘贴
tape.definitionEn: to fasten, tie, or cover (something) with tape
tape.sentence: I'm using a pencil to rewind the tape.

target.definitionEn: an object that people practise shooting at, especially a round board with circles on it
target.sentence: Yes! I hit the target, right in the center!
target.sentenceTrans: 太好了！我击中了靶子，正中靶心！

task.definitionEn: a piece of work that has been given to someone; a job for someone to do
task.sentence: I'm so happy—there isn't a single task on my to-do list!
task.sentenceTrans: 我很高兴，我的任务列表上已经没有任务了！

taste.definition: 品尝，尝（......的味道），尝起来；有……的味道；  n.味道；鉴赏力；品味；爱好，志趣
taste.definitionEn: to test the flavour of something by eating or drinking a small amount of it
taste.sentence: She always tastes the soup before serving it to others.
taste.sentenceTrans: 她上汤之前总要先尝一尝。

tax.definition: 税，税款；  v.征税；使负重担
tax.definitionEn: money that you have to pay to the government so that it can pay for public services
tax.sentence: The amount of tax people pay to the government depends on their income.
tax.sentenceTrans: 人们向政府纳税的数额取决于他们的收入。

taxi.definition: 出租车，计程车；  v.用出租车运送
taxi.definitionEn: a car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere. Taxis usually have meters which show how much money you have to pay.
taxi.sentence: The man is waiting for a taxi.
taxi.sentenceTrans: 这位男士正等着出租车。

tea.definitionEn: a hot drink made by pouring boiling water onto tea leaves. It may be drunk with milk or lemon and/or sugar added.
tea.sentence: Would you like a cup of tea?

teach.definitionEn: to give lessons to students in a school, college, university, etc.; to help somebody learn something by giving information about it
teach.sentence: My mother taught me the importance of waste segregation.
teach.sentenceTrans: 妈妈教我了解了垃圾分类的重要性。

teacher.definitionEn: a person whose job is teaching, especially in a school
teacher.sentence: Our teacher showed us where America and China were in the world.
teacher.sentenceTrans: 老师指给我们看了美国和中国在地球上的位置。

team.definitionEn: a group of people who play a particular game or sport against another group of people
team.sentence: The superheroes formed a team to fight together.
team.sentenceTrans: 超级英雄们组成一个团队一起战斗。

tear.definition: 撕裂，撕碎（读作/ter/ ）；  n.眼泪（读作/tɪr/）
tear.definitionEn: to damage something by pulling it apart or into pieces or by cutting it on something sharp; to become damaged in this way
tear.sentence: The broken-hearted man is tearing the photo into pieces.
tear.sentenceTrans: 这个心碎的男人正在把照片撕成碎片。

technical.definitionEn: connected with the practical use of machinery, methods, etc. in science and industry; connected with the skills needed for a particular job, sport, art, etc.; connected with a particular subject and therefore difficult to understand if you do not know about that subject
technical.sentence: She is responsible for answering technical questions.
technical.mnemonic: techn技术，能力 + ical形容词后缀 → technical技术上的

technician.definitionEn: a person who is very skilled at the technical aspects of an art, a sport, etc.
technician.sentence: We brought the technician in to repair our computers.
technician.sentenceTrans: 我们把技术员叫来修电脑。
technician.mnemonic: techn技术 + ician表专家，从事某职业的人 → technician技术员

technique.definitionEn: a particular way of doing something, especially one in which you have to learn special skills
technique.sentence: The musician combines different techniques in the performance.
technique.sentenceTrans: 这位音乐家在表演中结合了不同的技巧。
technique.mnemonic: techni技术 + que后缀 -> 技术

technological.sentence: Communication is much easier nowadays thanks to technological advancements.
technological.sentenceTrans: 由于技术的进步，现今通信更容易了。

technology.definition: 科技；技术，工艺，工程技术
technology.definitionEn: the use of science in industry, engineering, etc. to invent useful things or to solve problems; machinery or equipment designed using technology
technology.sentence: Now there are more and more technology products in our lives.
technology.sentenceTrans: 现在我们的生活中科技产品越来越多。
technology.mnemonic: techno技术，能力 + logy学说 → 技术，科技

tedious.definitionEn: lasting or taking too long and not interesting
tedious.sentence: It is really tedious to look at the screen all day long.
tedious.sentenceTrans: 整天看着屏幕非常枯燥。
tedious.mnemonic: ted厌倦 + ious表形容词 → 冗长沉闷的

teenager.definitionEn: a person who is between 13 and 19 years old
teenager.sentence: Teenagers are always full of energy.
teenager.sentenceTrans: 青少年总是充满了能量。
teenager.mnemonic: teen青少年 + age年龄 + r=er表人 → teenager青少年

telegram.definitionEn: a message sent by telegraph and then printed and given to somebody
telegram.sentence: She sent a telegram upon her arrival in Beijing.
telegram.sentenceTrans: 她一抵达北京就发了一封电报。
telegram.mnemonic: tele远，传送 + gram写，画 → telegram电报

telephone.definitionEn: a system for talking to somebody else over long distances, using wires or radio; a machine used for this; the part of the telephone that you hold in your hand and speak into
telephone.sentence: The telephone rang while she was sleeping.
telephone.sentenceTrans: 电话在她睡觉的时候响了起来。
telephone.mnemonic: tele远，传送 + phone声音 → 远方声音传过来 → 电话

telescope.definitionEn: a piece of equipment shaped like a tube, containing lenses, that you look through to make objects that are far away appear larger and nearer
telescope.sentence: You can see many distant stars through the telescope.
telescope.sentenceTrans: 通过望远镜，你可以看到许多遥远的星星。
telescope.mnemonic: tele远，传送 + scope看 → 看远方 → 望远镜

television.definition: 电视（机）；电视节目；电视行业
television.definitionEn: a piece of electrical equipment with a screen on which you can watch programmes with moving pictures and sounds; the system, process or business of broadcasting television programmes
television.sentence: We can watch the games on television.
television.sentenceTrans: 我们可以通过电视看球赛。
television.mnemonic: tele电 + vis看 + ion表名词 → television电视（机）

tell.sentence: She is telling a story to her two children.
tell.sentenceTrans: 她在给两个孩子讲故事。

teller.definitionEn: an official appointed to count the votes (especially in legislative assembly)
teller.sentence: Tellers deal with customers face-to-face in the bank, including giving and receiving cash.
teller.sentenceTrans: 银行出纳员与客户面对面打交道，包括给出和收取现金。

temper.definitionEn: if somebody has a temper, they become angry very easily
temper.sentence: Stuck in traffic for over an hour, the man began to lose his temper.
temper.sentenceTrans: 堵车一个多小时了，这个男人开始发火了。
temper.mnemonic: temper=tempor时间；节制；调节 → 不同的时间不同的心情 → temper脾气；心情；调和

temperature.definition: 温度；气温；某人的体温（尤指用来检测是否生病）
temperature.definitionEn: the measurement in degrees of how hot or cold a thing or place is
temperature.sentence: The temperature of my phone is high enough to cook eggs.
temperature.sentenceTrans: 我的手机温度好高，都可以煎蛋了。
temperature.mnemonic: tempera克制自己 + ture名词后缀 → 可管控自己的 → temperature气温；体温

temple.definition: 庙宇，寺院；圣殿，神殿；太阳穴
temple.definitionEn: a building used for the worship of a god or gods, especially in religions other than Christianity
temple.sentence: People usually go to temples to pray for good fortune.
temple.sentenceTrans: 人们经常去寺庙祈求好运。
temple.mnemonic: tem切割，隔断 + ple → 被独立隔断的地方 → temple庙宇

temporary.definitionEn: lasting or intended to last or be used only for a short time; not permanent
temporary.sentence: The tent on the car is a temporary home for us.
temporary.sentenceTrans: 车顶上的帐篷是我们的临时居所。
temporary.mnemonic: tempor时间 + ary形容词后缀 → 有时间性的 → temporary临时的

tempt.definitionEn: to attract somebody or make somebody want to do or have something, even if they know it is wrong
tempt.sentence: The squirrel is easily tempted by the acorn.
tempt.sentenceTrans: 这只松鼠很容易被一颗橡子引诱。

temptation.definitionEn: the desire to do or have something that you know is bad or wrong
temptation.sentence: He gave in to his temptation to try the desserts.
temptation.sentenceTrans: 他没能抵抗住这些甜点的诱惑。
temptation.mnemonic: tempt诱惑 + ation名词后缀 → temptation诱惑，引诱

ten.sentence: There are ten girls standing together.

tend.definition: 照顾，照料；往往会发生某事
tend.sentence: They tend the tree with care.
tend.sentenceTrans: 他们小心地照料这棵树。

tendency.definitionEn: an inclination of something or to do something
tendency.sentence: There is an increasing tendency in our sales.
tendency.sentenceTrans: 我们的销量有增长的趋势。
tendency.mnemonic: tend倾向 + ency名词后缀；状态 → tendency倾向

tender.definition: 温柔的；柔弱的，脆弱的；嫩的；  n.煤水车；  v.提出（希望对方接受的意见等）
tender.sentence: You have to be soft and tender with the baby.
tender.mnemonic: tend伸，伸出 + er形容词后缀 → 刚伸出的嫩芽 → tender嫩的，柔软的，温柔的

tennis.definitionEn: a game that is played by two people or two pairs of people on a special court (called a tennis court) where they hit a small ball back and forth over a net using rackets
tennis.sentence: My father taught me how to play tennis.
tennis.sentenceTrans: 我父亲教我怎样打网球。

tense.definition: 紧张的；拉紧的；  n.时态
tense.definitionEn: (of a person) nervous or worried, and unable to relax; (of a situation, an event, a period of time, etc.) in which people have strong feelings such as worry, anger, etc. that often cannot be expressed openly
tense.sentence: I feel really tense about the coming exam.
tense.sentenceTrans: 我真的对即将来临的考试感到紧张。
tense.mnemonic: tense=tens伸展 → 绷紧的，紧张的

tension.definitionEn: a feeling of nervousness that makes you unable to relax; a situation in which people do not trust each other, or feel unfriendly towards each other, and which may cause them to attack each other
tension.sentence: There was tension in the air as they waited to be interviewed.
tension.sentenceTrans: 他们等候面试时，空气中弥漫着紧张的气氛。
tension.mnemonic: tens=tense拉紧的，紧张的 + ion状态 → 紧张

tent.definitionEn: a shelter made of a large sheet of canvas, nylon, etc. that is supported by poles and ropes fixed to the ground, and is used especially for camping
tent.sentence: The couple put up a tent beside the river.
tent.sentenceTrans: 那对夫妇在河边支起了帐篷。

term.definition: 学期；术语；期限；（pl.）条款；  v.把……称为
term.definitionEn: each of the various parts in a series, an equation, etc.
term.sentence: The autumn term in China begins from September 1st.
term.sentenceTrans: 中国的秋季学期是从9月1日开始的。

terminal.definition: 终点站；  adj.末端的；晚期的
terminal.definitionEn: a building or set of buildings at an airport where air passengers arrive and leave
terminal.sentence: Our bus will arrive at the terminal around 6 pm.
terminal.sentenceTrans: 我们的公交车将在晚上6点左右到达终点站。
terminal.mnemonic: termin终端 + al形容词词尾 → terminal终端的；末端的

terminate.definitionEn: to end; to make something end
terminate.sentence: We terminated the contract to end our cooperation.
terminate.sentenceTrans: 我们终止了合同来结束合作。
terminate.mnemonic: termin终端 + ate动词后缀 → terminate终结

terrible.definition: 非常严重的，糟糕的；极糟的；可怕的，骇人的
terrible.sentence: Thousands of eggs were broken in the terrible traffic accident.
terrible.sentenceTrans: 在这场严重的车祸中，数以千计的鸡蛋碎了。

terrific.definition: 极好的；（尺寸或程度）极其巨大的，大得惊人的
terrific.sentence: The little girl feels terrific about the picnic.
terrific.sentenceTrans: 这个小女孩对这次野餐感觉棒极了。
terrific.mnemonic: terr怕 + ific……的 → 好到了让人害怕的地步 → terrific极好的

territory.definitionEn: an area that one person, group, animal, etc. considers as their own and defends against others who try to enter it
territory.sentence: The dog's pee helps to mark its territory.
territory.sentenceTrans: 狗狗通过撒尿来标记自己的领土。
territory.mnemonic: territ=terr土地 + ory场所、范围 → 地的范围 → territory领土

terror.definitionEn: a feeling of extreme fear; a person, situation or thing that makes you very afraid
terror.sentence: They shouted in terror when they saw the spider.
terror.sentenceTrans: 当看见蜘蛛时，他们吓得尖叫起来。
terror.mnemonic: terr战栗 + or名词后缀 → terror恐怖

terrorism.definitionEn: the use of violent action in order to achieve political aims or to force a government to act
terrorism.sentence: Their acts of terrorism have caused great pain and loss to this country.
terrorism.sentenceTrans: 他们的恐怖主义行径给这个国家造成了巨大的痛苦和损失。
terrorism.mnemonic: terr恐，怕 ＋ or人 ＋ ism...主义 → terrorism恐怖主义，恐怖行动

terrorist.definitionEn: a person who takes part in terrorism
terrorist.sentence: The durian terrorist is trying to attack other fruits.
terrorist.sentenceTrans: 榴莲恐怖分子正试图攻击其他水果。
terrorist.mnemonic: terror恐怖 + ist名词后缀：人 → terrorist恐怖分子

test.definition: 试验；测验，测试；  n.试验；测验，测试
test.definitionEn: a set of questions or problems that are designed to measure a person's knowledge, skills, or abilities
test.sentence: I will collect some soil to test later.
test.sentenceTrans: 稍后我会取一些土壤进行试验。

text.definitionEn: the main printed part of a book or magazine, not the notes, pictures, etc.; any form of written material; the written form of a speech, a play, an article, etc.
text.sentence: Processing and analyzing text data is a common task in natural language processing and sentiment analysis.
text.sentenceTrans: 处理和分析文本数据是自然语言处理和情感分析中的常见任务。

than.definitionEn: used for comparing amounts, numbers, distances, etc.
than.sentence: As you can see, I'm heavier than my little sister.
than.sentenceTrans: 如你看到的那样，我比妹妹要重一些。

thank.definitionEn: to tell somebody that you are grateful for something

that.definitionEn: used for referring to a person or thing that is not near the speaker or as near to the speaker as another
that.sentence: Do you want this book or that one?
that.sentenceTrans: 你想要这本书还是那一本？

the.definition: 这（表示特指），那 (指已提到或易领会到的人或事物)
the.definitionEn: used to refer to somebody/something that has already been mentioned or is easily understood

theater.definitionEn: a building or an outdoor area where plays and similar types of entertainment are performed
theater.sentence: The theater quickly emptied when the performance ended.
theater.sentenceTrans: 表演结束之后，戏院很快就空了。
theater.mnemonic: thea看见 + ter=tron表地点 → theater剧场

theatre.definitionEn: a building or an outdoor area where plays and similar types of entertainment are performed
theatre.sentence: Let's go to the theatre and watch a play!

their.sentenceTrans: 她们在交换她们的礼物。

theirs.definition: 他们的（所有物），属于他们的（东西）
theirs.definitionEn: (the possessive form of they) of or belonging to them
theirs.sentence: Now, the big house is theirs!
theirs.sentenceTrans: 现在，这栋大房子属于他们了。
theirs.mnemonic: their他们的 + s所有格后缀 → theirs他们的（所有物）

them.definitionEn: used when referring to people, animals or things as the object of a verb or preposition, or after the verb be
them.sentence: Both of them enjoy the meal.
them.sentenceTrans: 两个孩子都很喜欢这顿饭。

themselves.definitionEn: used when people or animals performing an action are also affected by it
themselves.sentence: The old couple are holding a photo of themselves taken 50 years ago.
themselves.sentenceTrans: 这对老夫妻正拿着一张他们自己在50年前拍的照片。
themselves.mnemonic: them他们+selves自己的复数 → 他们自己,

then.definitionEn: used to refer to a particular time in the past or future
then.sentence: Type in your password, then take out your money.
then.sentenceTrans: 输入你的密码，然后取走你的钱。

theory.definitionEn: a formal set of ideas that is intended to explain why something happens or exists
theory.sentence: It can be inferred from his theory that the universe is expanding.
theory.sentenceTrans: 我们可以从他的理论推测出宇宙在膨胀。
theory.mnemonic: theor思考 + y抽象名词词尾 → theory理论，原理；学说

therapy.definitionEn: the treatment of a physical problem or an illness
therapy.sentence: The man is trying a kind of Chinese therapy.
therapy.sentenceTrans: 这个男人正在尝试一种中医理疗。
therapy.mnemonic: therap治疗 + y表名词 → therapy治疗，理疗

there.definitionEn: in, at or to that place or position
there.sentence: Look! There is a bird in the tree.
there.mnemonic: the去，到 + re状语后缀 → there在那里

thereby.definitionEn: by that means or because of that
thereby.sentence: He ate a lot of junk food and thereby got fat.
thereby.sentenceTrans: 他吃了很多垃圾食品，因此长胖了。
thereby.mnemonic: there在那里 + by后缀 → thereby因此

therefore.definitionEn: used to introduce the logical result of something that has just been mentioned
therefore.sentence: The criminal was caught and therefore went to jail.
therefore.sentenceTrans: 罪犯已经被抓住了，因此他被送入了监狱。
therefore.mnemonic: there这样 + fore因为 → therefore因此

thermometer.definitionEn: an instrument used for measuring the temperature of the air, a person’s body, etc.
thermometer.sentence: The man used a thermometer to take his temperature.
thermometer.sentenceTrans: 这个男人用一支温度计来测量体温。
thermometer.mnemonic: thermo热 + meter计量，测量 → thermometer温度计，寒暑表

these.definitionEn: used to refer to things that have already been mentioned
these.sentence: I bought these items this morning.
these.sentenceTrans: 今天早上我买了这些东西。

thesis.definitionEn: a long piece of writing completed by a student as part of a university degree, based on their own research
thesis.sentence: The latest findings support the thesis of natural selection.
thesis.sentenceTrans: 这些最新发现证实了自然选择这一论点。
thesis.mnemonic: thesis=thet安排，放置 → 放好的研究主题 → thesis论文；命题

they.definitionEn: people, animals or things that have already been mentioned or are easily identified
they.sentence: "Where are your parents?" "They went on a trip."
they.sentenceTrans: “你父母在哪儿？” “他们去旅游了。”

thick.definitionEn: having a larger distance between opposite sides or surfaces than other similar objects or than normal
thick.sentence: The study material for the final exam is surprisingly this thick!
thick.sentenceTrans: 期末考试要复习的资料居然有这么厚！

thief.sentence: A thief is stealing the girl's phone.
thief.sentenceTrans: 一个小偷正在偷这个女孩的手机。

thin.definitionEn: (sometimes disapproving) (of a person or part of the body) not covered with much flesh
thin.sentence: He became very thin due to work stress.
thin.sentenceTrans: 他因工作压力变得很瘦。

thing.definition: 东西，事物；事情，事件，事态
thing.definitionEn: objects, clothing or tools that belong to somebody or are used for a particular purpose
thing.sentence: These are different things that people need in daily life.
thing.sentenceTrans: 这些都是人们在日常生活中所需的不同物品。

think.definitionEn: to have an opinion about someone or something
think.sentence: The person is thinking about a question.
think.sentenceTrans: 这个人正在考虑一个问题。

third.definitionEn: occupying the number three position in a series
third.sentence: One third of the pie chart is orange.
third.sentenceTrans: 饼图的三分之一是橘色的。

thirsty.sentence: The girl is so thirsty wandering in the desert.
thirsty.sentenceTrans: 女孩在沙漠里漫无目的地走着，渴极了。
thirsty.mnemonic: thirst口渴 + y……的 → thirsty口渴的，渴望的

thirteen.sentence: There's a number thirteen on my shirt.

thirty.sentence: The chef was thirty years old.

this.definitionEn: used to refer to a particular person or thing, thing or event that is close to you, especially compared with another

thorough.definition: 彻底的，完全的；详尽的，细致的
thorough.definitionEn: done completely; with great attention to detail; (of a person) doing things very carefully and with great attention to detail; used to emphasize how bad or annoying somebody/something is
thorough.sentence: A thorough brushing will give you fresh breath.
thorough.sentenceTrans: 彻底的刷牙可以使你口气清新。

thoroughly.definitionEn: in a complete and thorough manner (`good' is sometimes used informally for `thoroughly')
thoroughly.sentence: You need wash the hair thoroughly after using shampoo.
thoroughly.sentenceTrans: 每次用洗发剂洗发后都要彻底冲干净。

those.definitionEn: used for referring to somebody/something that have already been mentioned or are already known about
those.sentence: Look, those birds are flying high in the sky.
those.sentenceTrans: 看，那些鸟正在天空中展翅高飞。

though.sentence: Even though life is not entirely satisfactory, we still need to maintain optimism.
though.sentenceTrans: 尽管生活不尽人意，但我们还是要保持乐观。

thought.definition: 思想，想法；  v.想，以为（think的过去式和过去分词）；思考
thought.definitionEn: an idea, plan, opinion, picture, etc., that is formed in your mind; something that you think of
thought.sentence: He has many thoughts about his future.
thought.sentenceTrans: 他对自己的未来有很多想法。

thoughtful.definitionEn: showing concern for the needs or feelings of other people
thoughtful.mnemonic: thought想法，思考 + ful形容词后缀 → thoughtful体贴的，沉思的

thread.definition: 线；头绪，线索，思路；  v.穿线于；穿过
thread.definitionEn: a thin string of cotton, wool, silk, etc. used for sewing or making cloth
thread.sentence: I can use these colorful threads to make knitted scarves.
thread.sentenceTrans: 我能用这些五颜六色的线织成围巾。

threat.definition: 威胁，恐吓；凶兆，坏事发生的可能
threat.definitionEn: a statement in which you tell somebody that you will punish or harm them, especially if they do not do what you want
threat.sentence: The big guy is making a threat to the man in blue.
threat.sentenceTrans: 这个大块头正在威胁那个穿蓝衣服的人。

threaten.definitionEn: to say that you will cause trouble, hurt somebody, etc. if you do not get what you want
threaten.sentence: The landlord threatened to kick out the tenant if he didn't pay the rent.
threaten.sentenceTrans: 房东威胁租客，如果不付房租就把他赶出去。
threaten.mnemonic: threat威胁 + en动词后缀 → threaten威胁，恐吓

three.sentence: This hand gesture represents the number three.

thrill.definition: 兴奋；震颤；引起激动的事物；  v.激动；（使）非常兴奋
thrill.definitionEn: to excite or please somebody very much
thrill.sentence: It's quite a thrill to play with a virtual reality headset.
thrill.sentenceTrans: 玩VR头盔是一件令人兴奋不已的事情。

thrive.definitionEn: to become, and continue to be, successful, strong, healthy, etc.
thrive.sentence: Today, this city continues to thrive.
thrive.sentenceTrans: 如今，这座城市继续繁荣发展。

throat.definitionEn: a passage in the neck through which food and air pass on their way into the body; the front part of the neck
throat.sentence: I had a sore throat after I caught a cold.

throne.definitionEn: a special chair used by a king or queen to sit on at ceremonies
throne.sentence: The king is sitting on the throne.

through.definition: 通过；  adv.彻底；  adj.直通的
through.definitionEn: from one end or side of something/somebody to the other
through.sentence: I can run through brick walls—what can you do?
through.sentenceTrans: 我能奔跑着穿过砖墙——你能干什么？

throughout.definition: 到处；到处；全部；贯穿，遍及；自始至终
throughout.definitionEn: during the whole period of time of something
throughout.sentence: The Internet's base stations have been built throughout the world.
throughout.sentenceTrans: 互联网的基站遍布世界各地。
throughout.mnemonic: through通过 + out在外部 → 走到底最后到外面 → throughout遍及，到处

throw.definitionEn: to cause (something) to move out of your hand and through the air by quickly moving your arm forward
throw.sentence: The two kids are throwing balls to each other.
throw.sentenceTrans: 这两个孩子在互相扔球。

thumb.definitionEn: the short thick finger at the side of the hand, slightly apart from the other four
thumb.sentence: The fracture of the thumb can affect the grip strength.
thumb.sentenceTrans: 大拇指的骨折会影响握力。

thunder.definition: 雷，雷声；轰隆声；  v.大声斥责
thunder.definitionEn: the loud noise that you hear after a flash of lightning, during a storm
thunder.sentence: Don't stand under a tree when there is thunder. Lightning might strike you.
thunder.sentenceTrans: 打雷时不要站在树下，闪电可能会击中你。

thursday.definitionEn: the day of the week after Wednesday and before Friday

thus.definitionEn: as a result of something just mentioned
thus.sentence: He exercises every day and thus has managed to lose some weight.
thus.sentenceTrans: 他每天都锻炼，因此减肥成功了。

ticket.definitionEn: a printed piece of paper that gives you the right to travel on a particular bus, train, etc. or to go into a theatre, etc.
ticket.sentence: They got two tickets to fly back.
ticket.sentenceTrans: 他们有两张返程的机票。

tide.definitionEn: the regular upward and downward movement of the level of the ocean that is caused by the pull of the Sun and the Moon on the Earth
tide.sentence: The tide is going out, leaving the beach soft and clean.
tide.sentenceTrans: 潮水退去了，海滩变得柔软又干净。

tidy.definitionEn: arranged neatly and with everything in order; keeping things neat and in order
tidy.sentence: The living room looked so tidy after mom cleaned it.
tidy.sentenceTrans: 妈妈打扫后，客厅看起来如此干净整洁。
tidy.mnemonic: tid=tide季节，时间 + y形容词后缀 → 符合季节和时间规律 → tidy整洁的

tie.definition: 领带；联系，关系，纽带；平局；  v.绑，捆；系
tie.definitionEn: a thing that limits somebody’s freedom of action
tie.sentence: I finally learned how to wear my tie.
tie.sentenceTrans: 我终于学会了如何系领带。

tiger.definitionEn: a large wild animal of the cat family, that has yellowish fur with black lines (= stripes) and lives in parts of Asia
tiger.sentence: The tiger is a large wild animal.
tiger.sentenceTrans: 老虎是一种大型野生动物。

tight.definition: 紧身的，紧的；  adv.紧紧地，牢固地
tight.definitionEn: fitting closely to your body and sometimes uncomfortable
tight.sentence: Oh no, this sweater is too tight for me.
tight.sentenceTrans: 哦不，这件线衣对我来说太紧了。

till.definitionEn: to prepare and use land for growing crops

time.definition: 时间；次数；时期，时代，年代；  v.计时，定时；安排……的时间；  adj.时间的；定时的；分期的
time.definitionEn: what is measured in minutes, hours, days, etc.
time.sentence: Look at the time! I'm late again! My boss is going to kill me.
time.sentenceTrans: 看看时间！我又迟到了！我老板会杀了我的。

timing.definitionEn: Timing is about choosing the right moment for something to happen.
timing.sentence: With perfect timing, he captured the perfect shot of the smile.
timing.sentenceTrans: 他在完美的时机抓拍下了完美的笑容。

tin.definitionEn: a metal container in which food and drink is sold; the contents of one of these containers; a metal container used for cooking food in
tin.sentence: The kids like using tins as telephones.
tin.sentenceTrans: 孩子们喜欢拿罐子当电话。

tiny.definition: 微小的，很小的；极小的；微量的
tiny.definitionEn: very small in size or amount
tiny.sentence: The tiny girl sat on his shoulder.
tiny.sentenceTrans: 袖珍的爱丽丝坐在疯帽子的肩上。（《爱丽丝梦游仙境》）
tiny.mnemonic: tin=tine尖齿 + y表形容词 → tiny微小的

tip.definition: 小费；诀窍，建议；指示，指点；尖端；  v.给小费
tip.definitionEn: a small amount of extra money that you give to somebody, for example somebody who serves you in a restaurant
tip.sentence: He gave the porter a 5-dollar tip.
tip.sentenceTrans: 他给了那名行李员五美元的小费。

tire.definitionEn: to become tired and feel as if you want to sleep or rest; to make somebody feel this way
tire.sentence: The strange guy rolls a tire out into the road.
tire.sentenceTrans: 狂鼠扔出了一个轮胎（其实是炸弹）。

tired.definitionEn: feeling that you would like to sleep or rest; needing rest
tired.mnemonic: tire使...劳累 + d → tired疲劳的

tissue.definition: 纸巾；（人、动植物细胞的）组织
tissue.definitionEn: a piece of soft paper that absorbs liquids, used especially as a handkerchief; a collection of cells that form the different parts of humans, animals and plants; very thin paper used for wrapping and packing things that break easily
tissue.sentence: The little girl uses a tissue when she sneezes.
tissue.sentenceTrans: 打喷嚏时，小女孩用了一张纸巾。

title.definitionEn: the name of a book, poem, painting, piece of music, etc.
title.sentence: She read a book whose title shows it's about a woman born in 1982.
title.sentenceTrans: 她读了一本书，书名表明这本书和一位在1982年出生的女性有关。

to.definitionEn: in the direction of something; towards something

toast.definition: 敬酒；干杯；  v.为……干杯；烤；烘
toast.definitionEn: the act of a group of people wishing somebody happiness, success, etc. by drinking a glass of something, especially alcohol, at the same time
toast.sentence: He made a toast at the wedding.
toast.sentenceTrans: 夏洛克在华生的婚礼上说了祝酒词。

tobacco.definitionEn: the dried leaves of the tobacco plant that are used for making cigarettes, smoking in a pipe or chewing
tobacco.sentence: Tobacco is made up of dried leaves.
tobacco.sentenceTrans: 烟草是由干叶片制成的。

today.sentence: Today is the day for me to pay my taxes.
today.sentenceTrans: 今天是我要交税的日子。

toe.definitionEn: one of the five small parts that stick out from the foot
toe.sentence: When I drop a rock on my foot, every single toe hurts.
toe.sentenceTrans: 当我把石头砸到脚上的时候，每个脚趾都疼。

together.sentence: This place is even more beautiful to me because we're here together.
together.sentenceTrans: 因为我们在一起，所以这个地方变得分外美丽。
together.mnemonic: to去 + gether聚集 → 聚集在一起 → together一起

toilet.definitionEn: a large bowl attached to a pipe that is used for getting rid of bodily waste and then flushed with water
toilet.sentence: The boy is cleaning the toilet.
toilet.sentenceTrans: 那个男孩正在清洗马桶。
toilet.mnemonic: toil网 + et小词后缀 → 用作梳妆台台布的小块薄麻布 → 梳洗引申到马桶

tolerance.definitionEn: the ability to suffer something, especially pain, difficult conditions, etc. without being harmed
tolerance.sentence: I've had to develop a tolerance for loud noise at home.
tolerance.sentenceTrans: 我不得不在家养成耐受巨大噪声的能力。
tolerance.mnemonic: toler容忍 + ance表示状态、情况、性质、行为 → tolerance忍受，容忍

tolerant.definitionEn: willing to accept feelings, habits, or beliefs that are different from your own
tolerant.sentence: He is tolerant of his naughty cat.
tolerant.sentenceTrans: 他对他淘气的小猫很容忍。
tolerant.mnemonic: toler容忍 + ant形容词后缀 → tolerant心胸宽大的

tolerate.definitionEn: to accept somebody/something that is annoying, unpleasant, etc. without complaining
tolerate.sentence: They have to tolerate the bad smell in the elevator.
tolerate.sentenceTrans: 他们不得不忍受电梯里的臭味。
tolerate.mnemonic: toler容忍 + ate动词后缀 → tolerate容忍

tomato.definitionEn: a soft fruit with a lot of juice and shiny red skin that is eaten as a vegetable either raw or cooked

tomorrow.definition: 在明天，在明日；  n. 明天
tomorrow.definitionEn: on or during the day after today
tomorrow.sentence: We'll spend the Christmas Day together tomorrow.
tomorrow.sentenceTrans: 明天我们会一起过圣诞节。
tomorrow.mnemonic: to在...时 + morrow早晨 → 到下一个早晨 → tomorrow明天

ton.definitionEn: a unit for measuring weight that equals 2,240 pounds (1,016 kilograms)
ton.sentence: One ton is equal to 1,000 kilograms.

tone.definition: 语气；语调；色调；  v.使更健壮
tone.definitionEn: the quality of a sound, especially the sound of a musical instrument or one produced by electronic equipment
tone.sentence: The little boy learned to use a more polite tone when speaking to his mother.
tone.sentenceTrans: 这个小男孩学会用更礼貌的语气和母亲说话。

tongue.definitionEn: the soft part in the mouth that moves around, used for tasting, swallowing, speaking, etc.
tongue.sentence: The boy sticks out his tongue to make a face to me.
tongue.sentenceTrans: 男孩伸出舌头来对我做鬼脸。

tonight.definitionEn: this night or the night following this day
tonight.sentence: He is watching the news tonight.

too.definitionEn: used before adjectives and adverbs to say that something is more than is good, necessary, possible, etc.

tool.definitionEn: something (such as a hammer, saw, shovel, etc.) that you hold in your hand and use for a particular task
tool.sentence: We have all kinds of useful tools.
tool.sentenceTrans: 我们有各种各样的实用工具。

tooth.definitionEn: one of the hard white objects inside the mouth that are used for biting and chewing
tooth.sentence: Every tooth was straight and white.

top.definition: 顶部，顶端；  v.胜过；  adj.（位置、级别或程度）最高的
top.definitionEn: the highest part or point of something
top.sentence: He stands on the top of the mountain.

topic.definitionEn: a subject that you talk, write or learn about
topic.sentence: He wrote down a topic for us to discuss.
topic.sentenceTrans: 他写下一个主题供我们讨论。

torch.definitionEn: a small electric lamp that uses batteries and that you can hold in your hand; a long piece of wood that has material at one end that is set on fire and that people carry to give light;
torch.sentence: He is holding up a flaming torch to throw light on the wall.
torch.sentenceTrans: 他正举着燃烧的火把将墙面照亮。

torture.definition: 折磨；对……施以酷刑，拷问；  n.酷刑，折磨
torture.definitionEn: to cause severe physical pain as a form of punishment or as a way to force someone to do or say something
torture.sentence: My friend tortured us with her terrible singing.
torture.sentenceTrans: 我朋友用她糟糕的歌声折磨我们。
torture.mnemonic: tort扭转 + ure表名词 → 扭曲别人 → torture 折磨

total.definition: 整个的，总体的；  n.总数；  v.合计，总共
total.definitionEn: being the amount or number after everyone or everything is counted or added together
total.sentence: What's the total number of ducks in the pond?
total.sentenceTrans: 池塘里一共有多少只鸭子呢？
total.mnemonic: tot全部 + al表形容词 → total总体的

totally.sentence: The moon is totally blocking the sun's light.
totally.sentenceTrans: 月球完全阻挡了射到地面的阳光。
totally.mnemonic: tot合计 + ally...地 → totally完全地

touch.definitionEn: to put your hand, fingers, etc., on someone or something
touch.sentence: He is touching her belly to feel the baby moving.
touch.sentenceTrans: 他想摸摸她的肚子来感受宝宝的移动。

tough.definitionEn: physically strong and likely to be violent
tough.sentence: She is a tough and ambitious athlete.
tough.sentenceTrans: 她是一位健壮且有抱负的运动员。

tour.definition: 旅游；做巡回演出；  n.巡游
tour.definitionEn: to travel around a place, for example on holiday/vacation, or to perform, to advertise something, etc.
tour.sentence: The family is planning to tour around the world together.
tour.sentenceTrans: 这家人正计划一起环游世界。
tour.mnemonic: tour=turn旋转；迂回 → 转着玩 → tour旅游

tourism.definitionEn: the business activity connected with providing accommodation, services and entertainment for people who are visiting a place for pleasure
tourism.sentence: The beach is a popular location for tourism.
tourism.mnemonic: tour旅行 + ism名词后缀  → tourism 旅游

tourist.definitionEn: a person who travels to a place for pleasure
tourist.sentence: The tourists enjoyed traveling to new places.
tourist.sentenceTrans: 这些旅行者喜欢去新地方旅行。
tourist.mnemonic: tour旋转；迂回 ＋ ist表示人 → tourist旅游者

toward.sentence: The little girl is walking toward her father.
toward.sentenceTrans: 这个小女孩正向爸爸走去。
toward.mnemonic: to朝，向 + ward副词后缀，表方向 → toward向

towards.definitionEn: move, look, or point in a certain direction
towards.sentence: He is running towards his goal.
towards.sentenceTrans: 他正向着他的目标奔去。

towel.definitionEn: a piece of cloth or paper used for drying things, especially your body
towel.sentence: She uses a blue towel to dry her hair.
towel.sentenceTrans: 她用一条蓝色的毛巾擦头发。

tower.definition: 塔，楼塔；  v.高耸；胜过；高于，超过
tower.definitionEn: a tall, narrow building or structure that may stand apart from or be attached to another building or structure
tower.sentence: All the lights of this tower will be on at night.
tower.sentenceTrans: 一到晚上，这座塔的灯就会被全部点亮。

town.definitionEn: a place with many houses, shops/stores, etc. where people live and work. It is larger than a village but smaller than a city
town.sentence: I grew up in a seaside town.
town.sentenceTrans: 我在一个海滨小镇长大。

toy.definitionEn: an object for children to play with; an object that you have for enjoyment or pleasure rather than for a serious purpose
toy.sentence: I like this toy. It can be used to scare others.
toy.sentenceTrans: 我喜欢这个玩具，它可以用来吓人。

trace.definitionEn: to find or discover somebody/something by looking carefully for them/it
trace.sentence: The police dog traced the scent and located the stolen money.
trace.sentenceTrans: 这只警犬循着气味找到了被偷走的钱款。

track.definition: 跟踪，追赶；  n.足迹；轨道；小路，小径；跑道
track.definitionEn: to find somebody/something by following the marks, signs, information, etc., that they have left behind them; tow (a boat) along a waterway from the bank
track.sentence: He follows the footprints to track the bad guy.
track.sentenceTrans: 他跟着脚印追踪那个坏蛋。

tractor.definitionEn: a powerful vehicle with two large and two smaller wheels, used especially for pulling farm machinery
tractor.mnemonic: tract拉 + or名词后缀，物 → 拉东西 → tractor拖拉机

trade.definition: 贸易，商业；职业，行业；  v.经商，交易；做买卖，交易
trade.definitionEn: the activity or process of buying, selling, or exchanging goods or services
trade.sentence: International trade has become a major source of income for this company.
trade.sentenceTrans: 国际贸易成了这家公司的一项主要收入来源。

trademark.definitionEn: to register something as a trademark
trademark.sentence: This is the trademark of a popular APP.
trademark.sentenceTrans: 这是一款很火的应用的商标。
trademark.mnemonic: trade贸易 + mark记号，符号 → trademark商标

tradition.definitionEn: a belief, custom or way of doing something that has existed for a long time among a particular group of people; a set of these beliefs or customs
tradition.sentence: Dragon Boat Festival has many different traditions.
tradition.sentenceTrans: 端午节有许多不同的传统习俗。
tradition.mnemonic: tra过 + di给 + tion名词后缀 → 一代一代地传递 → tradition传统

traditional.definitionEn: being part of the beliefs, customs or way of life of a particular group of people, that have not changed for a long time
traditional.sentence: The kid is dressing in traditional clothing.
traditional.sentenceTrans: 这个小朋友穿着传统的服饰。

traffic.definition: 交通，车流；信息流量；非法买卖，非法交易；  v.买卖
traffic.definitionEn: the vehicles that are on a road at a particular time; the movement of ships, trains, aircraft, etc. along a particular route
traffic.sentence: The cars are hardly moving in the traffic jam.
traffic.sentenceTrans: 车子在交通堵塞中艰难地移动着。
traffic.mnemonic: tra=trans穿过 + ffic摩擦 → 在相互摩擦中穿过 → traffic交通，车流，流量

tragedy.definitionEn: a very sad event or situation, especially one that involves death; a serious play with a sad ending, especially one in which the main character dies; plays of this type
tragedy.sentence: The car accident was a tragedy for the man.
tragedy.sentenceTrans: 这场车祸对这个男人来说是场悲剧。

trail.sentence: The cyclist is riding on the forest trail.
trail.sentenceTrans: 自行车手正在森林小径上骑行。

train.definition: 火车，列车；行列；  v.训练；培训
train.definitionEn: a railway/railroad engine pulling a number of coaches/cars or trucks, taking people and goods from one place to another
train.sentence: The train is about to travel through the building.

trainer.definitionEn: a person who teaches people or animals to perform a particular job or skill well, or to do a particular sport
trainer.sentence: His personal trainer is teaching him how to use the fitness equipment correctly.
trainer.sentenceTrans: 他的私人教练正在教他如何正确使用健身器材。

training.definitionEn: the process of preparing to take part in a sports competition by doing physical exercises
training.sentence: We use train_test_split function to split the dataset into training and testing sets, with 80% of the data used for training.
training.sentenceTrans: 我们使用train_test_split函数将数据集分为训练集和测试集，其中80%的数据用于训练。

trait.definitionEn: A trait is a particular characteristic, quality, or tendency that someone or something has.
trait.sentence: The most obvious trait of his appearance is his big nose.
trait.sentenceTrans: 他最明显的外貌特征就是他的大鼻子。

transaction.definitionEn: a piece of business that is done between people, especially an act of buying or selling
transaction.sentence: I paid him and he gave me the house—it was an easy transaction.
transaction.sentenceTrans: 我给他钱，他给我房子——这是一笔轻松的交易。
transaction.mnemonic: trans变换，转移 + action行动 → 交换行动 → 交易

transfer.definition: 转移；调任；换乘；  n.转让；转移；汇兑（读作/ˈtrænsfər/）
transfer.definitionEn: to move from one place to another; to move something/somebody from one place to another
transfer.sentence: The worker transferred the box to another place.
transfer.sentenceTrans: 工人把箱子转移到了另一个地方。
transfer.mnemonic: trans横过，越过 + fer带来 → transfer转移

transform.definitionEn: to completely change the appearance or character of something, especially so that it is better; to change the form of something
transform.sentence: Makeup transformed him into a strikingly handsome man.
transform.sentenceTrans: 这个男人化妆爆改后变得很帅。
transform.mnemonic: trans变换，转移 + form形状 → 改变形状 → transform变形

transformation.definitionEn: a complete change in somebody/something; used in South Africa to describe the process of making institutions and organizations more democratic
transformation.sentence: The transformation of reactants into products is the key in chemical reactions.
transformation.sentenceTrans: 反应物转化为生成物是化学反应的关键。
transformation.mnemonic: trans变 + form形状 + ation名词后缀 → 转变，变形

transformer.definitionEn: a device for reducing or increasing the voltage of an electric power supply, usually to allow a particular piece of electrical equipment to be used
transformer.sentence: These transformers help to send electricity across the grid.
transformer.sentenceTrans: 这些变压器把电传输到整个电网中。
transformer.mnemonic: trans转变 + form形状 + er表人/物 → 变压器，转换器，变形金刚

transit.definition: 运输；运送；  v.穿过，经过
transit.definitionEn: the process of being moved or carried from one place to another
transit.sentence: This truck is used for transit between the two cities.
transit.sentenceTrans: 这辆卡车用于在这两个城市之间运输货物。
transit.mnemonic: trans越过 + it走 → 越过……走 → transit 运送，通行

translate.definitionEn: to express the meaning of speech or writing in a different language; to be changed from one language to another
translate.sentence: The girl used a phone app to translate this phrase into English.
translate.sentenceTrans: 女孩用一款手机应用程序把这个短语翻译成了英文。
translate.mnemonic: trans交换 + late拿出，带出 → 交换拿出 → translate翻译；转化

translation.definitionEn: a text or work that has been changed from one language into another
translation.sentence: The little boy is trying to do some translation exercises.
translation.sentenceTrans: 这个小男孩正尝试着做一些翻译练习。
translation.mnemonic: translat=translate翻译 + ion表行为，状态 → 翻译

transmission.definitionEn: the act or process of passing something from one person, place or thing to another; the act or process of sending out an electronic signal or message or of broadcasting a radio or television programme; a radio or television message or broadcast; the system in a vehicle by which power is passed from the engine to the wheels
transmission.sentence: This tower was built for mobile phone signal transmission.
transmission.sentenceTrans: 这座塔是用来传输手机信号的。
transmission.mnemonic: trans横 + miss送 + ion表名词  → 横着送  → transmission传输，发射

transmit.definitionEn: to send an electronic signal, radio or television broadcast, etc.
transmit.sentence: The tower transmits the TV signal.
transmit.mnemonic: trans横过，超过 + mit送 → 横着送消息 → transmit传播，传送

transparent.definitionEn: (of glass, plastic, etc.) allowing you to see through it
transparent.sentence: The transparent sterile dressing allows for continuous wound observation without the need for frequent removal.
transparent.sentenceTrans: 透明的无菌敷料允许持续观察伤口，而无需频繁更换。
transparent.mnemonic: trans横过，超过 + par出现 + ent形容词后缀 → 横穿某物能看见 → transparent透明的

transplant.definitionEn: to take an organ, skin, etc. from one person, animal, part of the body, etc. and put it into or onto another; to move a growing plant and plant it somewhere else; to move somebody/something to a different place or environment
transplant.sentence: The gardener transplanted the flowers to a sunnier spot.
transplant.sentenceTrans: 园丁将花移植到更阳光的地方。
transplant.mnemonic: trans转移 + plant种植 → transplant移植

transport.definitionEn: to take something/somebody from one place to another in a vehicle
transport.sentence: Airplanes, ships, trains and trucks are means of transporting goods.
transport.sentenceTrans: 飞机、轮船、火车和卡车是运输货物的方式。

transportation.definition: 运输工具；运输系统；交通；运输
transportation.definitionEn: a system for carrying people or goods from one place to another using vehicles, roads, etc.; a vehicle or method of travel; the activity or business of carrying goods from one place to another using lorries/trucks, trains, etc.
transportation.sentence: The common forms of transportation include bus, plane, ship and train.
transportation.sentenceTrans: 常见的运输工具有：汽车、飞机、轮船和火车。
transportation.mnemonic: trans转移 + port拿，运 + ation名词后缀 → 运输，运输业

trap.definition: 陷阱；险境；圈套；  v.使陷入圈套；困住
trap.definitionEn: a clever plan designed to trick somebody, either by capturing them or by making them do or say something that they did not mean to do or say
trap.sentence: The man is about to fall into the trap!
trap.sentenceTrans: 这个男人就要陷入圈套了！

travel.definition: 旅行；行走；  n.旅行，旅游
travel.definitionEn: to go on a trip or journey :to go to a place and especially one that is far away
travel.sentence: My girlfriend and I travelled all over the world.

tray.definitionEn: a flat piece of wood, metal or plastic with raised edges, used for carrying or holding things, especially food; a shallow plastic box, used for various purposes
tray.sentence: He brought three glasses of water on a tray.
tray.sentenceTrans: 他用托盘端过来三杯水。

treasure.definition: 金银财宝；不可多得的人才；  v.珍视，珍爱
treasure.definitionEn: a collection of valuable things such as gold, silver and jewellery
treasure.sentence: These treasures will make me rich.

treat.definition: 治疗；请客，款待；对待；  n.款待
treat.definitionEn: to give medical care or attention to a person, an illness, an injury, etc.
